paragraphs.en: Caddy came to the door and stood there, looking at Father and Mother. Her eyes flew at me, and away. I began to cry. It went loud and I got up. Caddy came in and stood with her back to the wall, looking at me. I went toward her, crying, and she shrank against the wall and I saw her eyes and I cried louder and pulled at her dress. She put her hands out but I pulled at her dress. Her eyes ran.
paragraphs.zh: 凯蒂来到门口，站在那里，看着爸爸和妈妈。她的目光扫向我，然后又移开。我开始哭泣。声音很大，我站了起来。凯蒂进来，背靠墙站着，看着我。我哭着走向她，她缩在墙上，我看到了她的眼睛，我哭得更大声，拉扯她的衣服。她伸出双手，但我拉着她的衣服。她的眼睛转动着。

paragraphs.en: Versh said, Your name Benjamin now. You know how come your name Benjamin now. They making a bluegum out of you. Mammy say in old time your granpa changed nigger’s name, and he turn preacher, and when they look at him, he bluegum too. Didn’t use to be bluegum, neither. And when family woman look him in the eye in the full of the moon, chile born bluegum. And one evening, when they was about a dozen them bluegum chillen running round the place, he never come home. Possum hunters found him in the woods, et clean. And you know who et him. Them bluegum chillen did.
paragraphs.zh: 弗许说，你现在叫本杰明。你现在知道你的名字本杰明是怎么来的了吧。他们把你变成了蓝桉树。妈妈说，从前，你爷爷改了黑鬼的名字，他变成了传教士，当他们看着他时，他也喝了蓝口香糖。以前也不是蓝胶唱片。当家庭妇女在满月时看着他的眼睛时，智利出生的蓝桉。一天晚上，当他们大约有十几只蓝桉树到处跑时，他再也没有回家。负鼠猎人在树林里发现了他，而且他很干净。你知道谁吃了他。他们蓝桉辣椒做到了。

paragraphs.en: We were in the hall. Caddy was still looking at me. Her hand was against her mouth and I saw her eyes and I cried. We went up the stairs. She stopped again, against the wall, looking at me and I cried and she went on and I came on, crying, and she shrank against the wall, looking at me. She opened the door to her room, but I pulled at her dress and we went to the bathroom and she stood against the door, looking at me. Then she put her arm across her face and I pushed at her, crying.
paragraphs.zh: 我们在大厅里。凯蒂仍然看着我。她的手捂着嘴，我看到她的眼睛，我哭了。我们走上楼梯。她又停了下来，靠在墙上，看着我，我哭了，她继续前行，我也继续前行，哭着，她缩在墙上，看着我。她打开了她房间的门，但我拉着她的衣服，我们去了卫生间，她站在门边看着我。然后她用手臂捂住脸，我推着她哭。

paragraphs.en: What are you doing to him, Jason said. Why cant you let him alone.
paragraphs.zh: “你对他做什么？”杰生说。为什么你不能放过他。

paragraphs.en: I aint touching him, Luster said. He been doing this way all day long. He needs whipping.
paragraphs.zh: 我不会碰他，勒斯特说。他一整天都是这样做的。他需要鞭打。

paragraphs.en: He needs to be sent to Jackson, Quentin said. How can anybody live in a house like this.
paragraphs.zh: 昆丁说，他需要被送到杰克逊。怎么会有人住在这样的房子里。

paragraphs.en: If you dont like it, young lady, you’d better get out, Jason said.
paragraphs.zh: “小姐，如果你不喜欢，你最好滚出去。”杰生说道。

paragraphs.en: I’m going to, Quentin said. Dont you worry.
paragraphs.zh: “我去。”昆丁说。别担心。

paragraphs.en: Versh said, “You move back some, so I can dry my legs off.” He shoved me back a little. “Dont you start bellering, now. You can still see it. That’s all you have to do. You aint had to be out in the rain like I is. You’s born lucky and dont know it.” He lay on his back before the fire.
paragraphs.zh: 弗许说：“你往后退一些，我把腿擦干。”他把我往后推了一点。“现在别开始大喊大叫了。你仍然可以看到它。这就是你所要做的。你不必像我一样在雨中。你生来很幸运，但你不知道这一点。”他仰面躺在火堆前。

paragraphs.en: “You know how come your name Benjamin now.” Versh said. “Your mamma too proud for you. What mammy say.”
paragraphs.zh: “你现在知道你的名字本杰明是怎么来的了吧。”弗许说道。“你妈妈太为你骄傲了。妈妈怎么说呢。”

paragraphs.en: “You be still there and let me dry my legs off.” Versh said. “Or you know what I’ll do. I’ll skin your rinktum.”
paragraphs.zh: “你别动，让我把腿擦干。”弗许说道。“或者你知道我会做什么。我会剥掉你的溜冰场的皮。”

paragraphs.en: We could hear the fire and the roof and Versh.
paragraphs.zh: 我们可以听到火声、屋顶声和弗许声。

paragraphs.en: Versh got up quick and jerked his legs back. Father said, “All right, Versh.”
paragraphs.zh: 弗许迅速站起来，猛地收回双腿。父亲说：“好吧，弗许。”

paragraphs.en: “I’ll feed him tonight.” Caddy said. “Sometimes he cries when Versh feeds him.”
paragraphs.zh: “今晚我喂他。”凯蒂说。“有时弗许喂他吃东西时他会哭。”

paragraphs.en: “Take this tray up,” Dilsey said. “And hurry back and feed Benjy.”
paragraphs.zh: “把这个托盘拿起来，”迪尔西说道。“赶紧回去喂班吉。”

paragraphs.en: “Dont you want Caddy to feed you.” Caddy said.
paragraphs.zh: “你不想让凯蒂喂你吗？”凯蒂说。

paragraphs.en: Has he got to keep that old dirty slipper on the table, Quentin said. Why dont you feed him in the kitchen. It’s like eating with a pig.
paragraphs.zh: “他必须把那只又旧又脏的拖鞋放在桌子上吗？”昆丁说。你为什么不在厨房里喂他呢？就像和猪一起吃饭一样。

paragraphs.en: If you dont like the way we eat, you’d better not come to the table, Jason said.
paragraphs.zh: “如果你不喜欢我们吃的方式，你最好不要到餐桌上来。”杰生说。

paragraphs.en: Steam came off of Roskus. He was sitting in front of the stove. The oven door was open and Roskus had his feet in it. Steam came off the bowl. Caddy put the spoon into my mouth easy. There was a black spot on the inside of the bowl.
paragraphs.zh: 罗斯库斯冒出蒸汽。他坐在炉子前面。烤箱门开着，罗斯库斯把脚伸进去。蒸汽从碗里冒出来。凯蒂轻松地将勺子放进我嘴里。碗的内侧有一个黑点。

paragraphs.en: Now, now, Dilsey said. He aint going to bother you no more.
paragraphs.zh: 现在，现在，迪尔西说。他不会再打扰你了。

paragraphs.en: It got down below the mark. Then the bowl was empty. It went away. “He’s hungry tonight.” Caddy said. The bowl came back. I couldn’t see the spot. Then I could. “He’s starved, tonight.” Caddy said. “Look how much he’s eaten.”
paragraphs.zh: 它跌破了标记。然后碗就空了。它消失了。“他今晚饿了。”凯蒂说。碗又回来了。我看不到那个地方。那我就可以了。“今晚他饿坏了。”凯蒂说。“看看他吃了多少。”

paragraphs.en: Yes he will, Quentin said. You all send him out to spy on me. I hate this house. I’m going to run away.
paragraphs.zh: 是的，他会的，昆丁说。你们都派他出去监视我。我讨厌这个房子。我要逃跑。

paragraphs.en: Roskus said, “It going to rain all night.”
paragraphs.zh: 罗斯库斯说：“整夜都会下雨。”

paragraphs.en: You’ve been running a long time, not to ’ve got any further off than mealtime, Jason said.
paragraphs.zh: 杰生说，你已经跑了很长一段时间了，除了吃饭时间之外就没有其他时间了。

paragraphs.en: See if I dont, Quentin said.
paragraphs.zh: 昆丁说，看我不知道。

paragraphs.en: “Then I dont know what I going to do.” Dilsey said. “It caught me in the hip so bad now I cant scarcely move. Climbing them stairs all evening.”
paragraphs.zh: “那我就不知道自己要做什么了。”迪尔西说道。“它严重击中了我的臀部，现在我几乎无法动弹。整个晚上都在爬楼梯。”

paragraphs.en: Oh, I wouldn’t be surprised, Jason said. I wouldn’t be surprised at anything you’d do.
paragraphs.zh: 哦，我不会感到惊讶，杰生说。我不会对你所做的任何事情感到惊讶。

paragraphs.en: Quentin threw her napkin on the table.
paragraphs.zh: 昆丁把餐巾扔在桌子上。

paragraphs.en: Hush your mouth, Jason, Dilsey said. She went and put her arm around Quentin. Sit down, honey, Dilsey said. He ought to be shamed of hisself, throwing what aint your fault up to you.
paragraphs.zh: “闭嘴，杰生，”迪尔西说。她走过去，用手臂搂住昆丁。坐下，亲爱的，迪尔西说。他应该为自己感到羞耻，把不是你的错的事情都推给你。

paragraphs.en: “She sulling again, is she.” Roskus said.
paragraphs.zh: “她又生闷气了，是吗？”罗斯库斯说道。

paragraphs.en: “Hush your mouth.” Dilsey said.
paragraphs.zh: “闭嘴。”迪尔西说道。

paragraphs.en: Quentin pushed Dilsey away. She looked at Jason. Her mouth was red. She picked up her glass of water and swung her arm back, looking at Jason. Dilsey caught her arm. They fought. The glass broke on the table, and the water ran into the table. Quentin was running.
paragraphs.zh: 昆丁推开迪尔西。她看着杰生。她的嘴红了。她端起水杯，收回手臂，看着杰生。迪尔西抓住了她的手臂。他们打架了。玻璃在桌子上碎了，水流到了桌子上。昆丁正在奔跑。

paragraphs.en: “Mother’s sick again.” Caddy said.
paragraphs.zh: “妈妈又病了。”凯蒂说。

paragraphs.en: “Sho she is.” Dilsey said. “Weather like this make anybody sick. When you going to get done eating, boy.”
paragraphs.zh: “当然，她是。”迪尔西说道。“这样的天气会让任何人生病。当你吃完饭的时候，孩子。”

paragraphs.en: Goddamn you, Quentin said. Goddamn you. We could hear her running on the stairs. We went to the library.
paragraphs.zh: 该死的你，昆丁说。该死的你。我们可以听到她在楼梯上奔跑的声音。我们去了图书馆。

paragraphs.en: Caddy gave me the cushion, and I could look at the cushion and the mirror and the fire.
paragraphs.zh: 凯蒂给了我垫子，我可以看到垫子、镜子和火。

paragraphs.en: “We must be quiet while Quentin’s studying.” Father said. “What are you doing, Jason.”
paragraphs.zh: “昆丁学习的时候一定要安静。”父亲说。“杰生，你在做什么。”

paragraphs.en: “Nothing.” Jason said.
paragraphs.zh: “没什么。”杰生说道。

paragraphs.en: “Suppose you come over here to do it, then.” Father said.
paragraphs.zh: “那么，假设你来这里做这件事。”父亲说。

paragraphs.en: Jason came out of the corner.
paragraphs.zh: 杰生从角落里走了出来。

paragraphs.en: “What are you chewing.” Father said.
paragraphs.zh: “你在嚼什么。”父亲说。

paragraphs.en: “Nothing.” Jason said.
paragraphs.zh: “没什么。”杰生说道。

paragraphs.en: “He’s chewing paper again.” Caddy said.
paragraphs.zh: “他又在嚼纸了。”凯蒂说。

paragraphs.en: “Come here, Jason.” Father said.
paragraphs.zh: “杰生，过来。”父亲说。

paragraphs.en: Jason threw into the fire. It hissed, uncurled, turning black. Then it was gray. Then it was gone. Caddy and Father and Jason were in Mother’s chair. Jason’s eyes were puffed shut and his mouth moved, like tasting. Caddy’s head was on Father’s shoulder. Her hair was like fire, and little points of fire were in her eyes, and I went and Father lifted me into the chair too, and Caddy held me. She smelled like trees.
paragraphs.zh: 杰生扔进火里。它发出嘶嘶声，展开，变成黑色。然后就变成灰色了。然后它就消失了。凯蒂、父亲和杰生坐在母亲的椅子上。杰生的眼睛睁得大大的，嘴巴动了动，像是在品尝。凯蒂的头靠在父亲的肩膀上。她的头发像火一样，她的眼睛里有小火点，我走过去，父亲也把我抱到椅子上，凯蒂抱着我。她闻起来像树。

paragraphs.en: She smelled like trees. In the corner it was dark, but I could see the window. I squatted there, holding the slipper. I couldn’t see it, but my hands saw it, and I could hear it getting night, and my hands saw the slipper but I couldn’t see myself, but my hands could see the slipper, and I squatted there, hearing it getting dark.
paragraphs.zh: 她闻起来像树。角落里很黑，但我可以看到窗户。我蹲在那里，拿着拖鞋。我看不到它，但我的手看到了它，我能听到天黑了，我的手看到了拖鞋，但我看不见自己，但我的手能看到拖鞋，我蹲在那里，听到天黑了。

paragraphs.en: Here you is, Luster said. Look what I got. He showed it to me. You know where I got it. Miss Quentin gave it to me. I knowed they couldn’t keep me out. What you doing, off in here. I thought you done slipped back out doors. Aint you done enough moaning and slobbering today, without hiding off in this here empty room, mumbling and taking on. Come on here to bed, so I can get up there before it starts. I cant fool with you all night tonight. Just let them horns toot the first toot and I done gone.
paragraphs.zh: 给你，勒斯特说。看看我得到了什么。他给我看了。你知道我从哪里得到的。昆丁小姐给我的。我知道他们无法将我拒之门外。你在做什么，就在这里。我以为你已经完事了，溜回门外了。你今天的呻吟和流口水还不够多吗，还没有躲在这个空荡荡的房间里，咕哝着，承担责任。到这里来睡觉吧，这样我就可以在比赛开始前起床了。今晚我不能整夜欺骗你。只要让它们吹响第一声喇叭，我就消失了。

paragraphs.en: We didn’t go to our room.
paragraphs.zh: 我们没有去我们的房间。

paragraphs.en: “This is where we have the measles.” Caddy said. “Why do we have to sleep in here tonight.”
paragraphs.zh: “这就是我们有麻疹的地方。”凯蒂说。“为什么我们今晚要睡在这里？”

paragraphs.en: “What you care where you sleep.” Dilsey said. She shut the door and sat down and began to undress me. Jason began to cry. “Hush.” Dilsey said.
paragraphs.zh: “你在乎你睡在哪里。”迪尔西说道。她关上门，坐下来开始给我脱衣服。杰生哭了。“嘘。”迪尔西说道。

paragraphs.en: “I want to sleep with Damuddy.” Jason said.
paragraphs.zh: “我想和外婆睡。”杰生说道。

paragraphs.en: “She’s sick.” Caddy said. “You can sleep with her when she gets well. Cant he, Dilsey.”
paragraphs.zh: “她病了。”凯蒂说。“等她康复了，你就可以和她一起睡了。不行吗，迪尔西。”

paragraphs.en: “Hush, now.” Dilsey said. Jason hushed.
paragraphs.zh: “嘘，现在。”迪尔西说道。杰生沉默了。

paragraphs.en: “Our nighties are here, and everything.” Caddy said. “It’s like moving.”
paragraphs.zh: “我们的睡衣和一切都在这里。”凯蒂说。“就像移动一样。”

paragraphs.en: “And you better get into them.” Dilsey said. “You be unbuttoning Jason.”
paragraphs.zh: “你最好加入其中。”迪尔西说道。“杰生，你快解开扣子了。”

paragraphs.en: Caddy unbuttoned Jason. He began to cry.
paragraphs.zh: 凯蒂解开了杰生的扣子。他开始哭泣。

paragraphs.en: “You want to get whipped.” Dilsey said. Jason hushed.
paragraphs.zh: “你想被鞭打。”迪尔西说道。杰生沉默了。

paragraphs.en: Quentin, Mother said in the hall.
paragraphs.zh: 昆丁，母亲在大厅里说道。

paragraphs.en: What, Quentin said beyond the wall. We heard Mother lock the door. She looked in our door and came in and stooped over the bed and kissed me on the forehead.
paragraphs.zh: 什么，昆丁在墙外说道。我们听到妈妈锁门的声音。她朝我们的门看了一眼，进来了，弯下腰在我的额头上吻了一下。

paragraphs.en: When you get him to bed, go and ask Dilsey if she objects to my having a hot water bottle, Mother said. Tell her that if she does, I’ll try to get along without it. Tell her I just want to know.
paragraphs.zh: “当你让他上床睡觉时，去问迪尔西她是否反对我用热水袋，”母亲说。告诉她，如果她这样做，我会尝试不这样做也能相处。告诉她我只是想知道。

paragraphs.en: Yessum, Luster said. Come on. Get your pants off.
paragraphs.zh: 是的，勒斯特说。快点。脱掉你的裤子。

paragraphs.en: Quentin and Versh came in. Quentin had his face turned away. “What are you crying for.” Caddy said.
paragraphs.zh: 昆丁和弗许进来了。昆丁扭过脸去。“你哭什么。”凯蒂说。

paragraphs.en: “Hush.” Dilsey said. “You all get undressed, now. You can go on home, Versh.”
paragraphs.zh: “嘘。”迪尔西说道。“现在你们都脱衣服了。弗许，你们可以回家了。”

paragraphs.en: I got undressed and I looked at myself, and I began to cry. Hush, Luster said. Looking for them aint going to do no good. They’re gone. You keep on like this, and we aint going have you no more birthday. He put my gown on. I hushed, and then Luster stopped, his head toward the window. Then he went to the window and looked out. He came back and took my arm. Here she come, he said. Be quiet, now. We went to the window and looked out. It came out of Quentin’s window and climbed across into the tree. We watched the tree shaking. The shaking went down the tree, than it came out and we watched it go away across the grass. Then we couldn’t see it. Come on, Luster said. There now. Hear them horns. You get in that bed while my foots behaves.
paragraphs.zh: 我脱掉衣服，看着自己，然后开始哭泣。嘘，勒斯特说。寻找他们不会有任何好处。他们走了。你再这样下去，我们就不会再给你过生日了。他给我穿上了礼服。我安静下来，然后勒斯特停了下来，他的头朝向窗户。然后他走到窗前向外看去。他回来了，抓住了我的手臂。她来了，他说。安静点，现在。我们走到窗前向外看去。它从昆丁的窗户出来，爬到树上。我们看着树摇晃。震动从树上传下来，然后传出来，我们看着它穿过草地消失。然后我们就看不到了。来吧，勒斯特说。现在就在那里。听到他们的号角声。当我的脚恢复正常时，你就上那张床。

paragraphs.en: There were two beds. Quentin got in the other one. He turned his face to the wall. Dilsey put Jason in with him. Caddy took her dress off.
paragraphs.zh: 有两张床。昆丁坐进了另一辆车。他把脸转向墙壁。迪尔西把杰生安置在他身边。凯蒂脱掉了衣服。

paragraphs.en: “Just look at your drawers.” Dilsey said. “You better be glad your ma aint seen you.”
paragraphs.zh: “看看你的抽屉。”迪尔西说道。“你最好庆幸你妈妈没有看见你。”

paragraphs.en: “I already told on her.” Jason said.
paragraphs.zh: “我已经告诉过她了。”杰生说道。

paragraphs.en: “I bound you would.” Dilsey said.
paragraphs.zh: “我约束你。”迪尔西说道。

paragraphs.en: “And see what you got by it.” Caddy said. “Tattletale.”
paragraphs.zh: “看看你得到了什么。”凯蒂说。“流言蜚语。”

paragraphs.en: “What did I get by it.” Jason said.
paragraphs.zh: “我得到了什么。”杰生说道。

paragraphs.en: “Whyn’t you get your nightie on.” Dilsey said. She went and helped Caddy take off her bodice and drawers. “Just look at you.” Dilsey said. She wadded the drawers and scrubbed Caddy behind with them. “It done soaked clean through onto you.” she said. “But you wont get no bath this night. Here.” She put Caddy’s nightie on her and Caddy climbed into the bed and Dilsey went to the door and stood with her hand on the light. “You all be quiet now, you hear.” she said.
paragraphs.zh: “你为什么不穿上睡衣。”迪尔西说道。她走过去帮凯蒂脱掉紧身胸衣和抽屉。“就看看你吧。”迪尔西说道。她把抽屉塞满，用它们擦洗凯蒂的身后。“它已经把你浸透了。”她说。“但是今晚你不能洗澡。在这里。”她给凯蒂穿上睡衣，凯蒂爬上床，迪尔西走到门口，手放在灯上。“你们现在都安静，听见了。”她说。

paragraphs.en: “All right.” Caddy said. “Mother’s not coming in tonight.” she said. “So we still have to mind me.”
paragraphs.zh: “好吧。”凯蒂说。“妈妈今晚不会回来。”她说。“所以我们还是得管我。”

paragraphs.en: “Yes.” Dilsey said. “Go to sleep, now.”
paragraphs.zh: “是的。”迪尔西说道。“现在去睡觉吧。”

paragraphs.en: “Mother’s sick.” Caddy said. “She and Damuddy are both sick.”
paragraphs.zh: “妈妈病了。”凯蒂说。“她和外婆都病了。”

paragraphs.en: “Hush.” Dilsey said. “You go to sleep.”
paragraphs.zh: “嘘。”迪尔西说道。“你去睡觉吧。”

paragraphs.en: The room went black, except the door. Then the door went black. Caddy said, “Hush, Maury,” putting her hand on me. So I stayed hushed. We could hear us. We could hear the dark.
paragraphs.zh: 房间里一片漆黑，除了门。然后门就黑了。凯蒂说：“嘘，莫里，”她把手放在我身上。所以我保持沉默。我们能听到我们的声音。我们能听到黑暗的声音。

paragraphs.en: It went away, and Father looked at us. He looked at Quentin and Jason, then he came and kissed Caddy and put his hand on my head.
paragraphs.zh: 它消失了，父亲看着我们。他看着昆丁和杰生，然后走过来亲吻了凯蒂，并把手放在了我的头上。

paragraphs.en: “Is Mother very sick.” Caddy said.
paragraphs.zh: “妈妈病得很重吗？”凯蒂说。

paragraphs.en: “No.” Father said. “Are you going to take good care of Maury.”
paragraphs.zh: “不。”父亲说。“你要好好照顾莫里吗？”

paragraphs.en: “Yes.” Caddy said.
paragraphs.zh: “是的。”凯蒂说。

paragraphs.en: Father went to the door and looked at us again. Then the dark came back, and he stood black in the door, and then the door turned black again. Caddy held me and I could hear us all, and the darkness, and something I could smell. And then I could see the windows, where the trees were buzzing. Then the dark began to go in smooth, bright shapes, like it always does, even when Caddy says that I have been asleep.
paragraphs.zh: 父亲走到门口，又看了我们一眼。然后黑暗又回来了，他黑黑地站在门里，然后门又变黑了。凯蒂抱着我，我能听到我们所有人的声音，还有黑暗，还有我能闻到的味道。然后我可以看到窗户，那里的树木在嗡嗡作响。然后黑暗开始变得光滑、明亮，就像往常一样，即使凯蒂说我已经睡着了。

paragraphs.en: When the shadow of the sash appeared on the curtains it was between seven and eight oclock and then I was in time again, hearing the watch. It was Grandfather’s and when Father gave it to me he said, Quentin, I give you the mausoleum of all hope and desire; it’s rather excrutiating-ly apt that you will use it to gain the reducto absurdum of all human experience which can fit your individual needs no better than it fitted his or his father’s. I give it to you not that you may remember time, but that you might forget it now and then for a moment and not spend all your breath trying to conquer it. Because no battle is ever won he said. They are not even fought. The field only reveals to man his own folly and despair, and victory is an illusion of philosophers and fools.
paragraphs.zh: 窗框的影子出现在帘子上时，是七点到八点之间，于是我又进入了时间，听见了表的声音。那是祖父的表，父亲把它给我的时候说，昆丁，我把一切希望和欲望的陵墓送给你；你将用它把全部人生经验推到荒谬的归结，这安排真是贴切得叫人痛苦，那些经验适合你的个人需要，并不比适合他或他父亲的需要多一点。我把它给你，不是要你记住时间，而是要你偶尔有一刻忘掉时间，别耗尽气力去征服它。因为没有一场仗是打赢过的，他说。甚至根本没有打过。战场只向人显示他自己的愚蠢和绝望，而胜利是哲学家和傻瓜的幻觉。

paragraphs.en: It was propped against the collar box and I lay listening to it. Hearing it, that is. I dont suppose anybody ever deliberately listens to a watch or a clock. You dont have to. You can be oblivious to the sound for a long while, then in a second of ticking it can create in the mind unbroken the long diminishing parade of time you didn’t hear. Like Father said down the long and lonely light-rays you might see Jesus walking, like. And the good Saint Francis that said Little Sister Death, that never had a sister.
paragraphs.zh: 它靠在领子盒上，我躺着听它。是听见它，才对。我想从来没有谁会特意去听一只表或一座钟。不必听。你可以很久很久都不理会那声音，可一秒钟的滴答，就能在心里接连不断地唤出那段你没有听见的、绵长而渐渐远去的时间行列。就像父亲说的，沿着悠长而孤独的光线，你仿佛能看见耶稣走着，仿佛。还有那位善良的圣方济各，称死为小妹妹，他却从来没有过妹妹。

paragraphs.en: Through the wall I heard Shreve’s bed-springs and then his slippers on the floor hishing. I got up and went to the dresser and slid my hand along it and touched the watch and turned it face-down and went back to bed. But the shadow of the sash was still there and I had learned to tell almost to the minute, so I’d have to turn my back to it, feeling the eyes animals used to have in the back of their heads when it was on top, itching. It’s always the idle habits you acquire which you will regret. Father said that. That Christ was not crucified: he was worn away by a minute clicking of little wheels. That had no sister.
paragraphs.zh: 透过墙壁，我听到施里夫的弹簧床的声音，然后是他的拖鞋在地板上发出的嘶嘶声。我起身走到梳妆台前，把手滑过梳妆台，触摸手表，然后将其翻面朝下，然后回到床上。但腰带的阴影仍然在那里，我已经学会了几乎准确无误地讲述，所以我不得不背对着它，感觉到动物过去在腰带上时在后脑勺上的眼睛，发痒。你所养成的闲散习惯总是会让你后悔的。父亲这么说。基督没有被钉在十字架上：他被小轮子的轻微咔哒声磨损了。那是没有妹妹的。

paragraphs.en: And so as soon as I knew I couldn’t see it, I began to wonder what time it was. Father said that constant speculation regarding the position of mechanical hands on an arbitrary dial which is a symptom of mind-function. Excrement Father said like sweating. And I saying All right. Wonder. Go on and wonder.
paragraphs.zh: 所以当我知道我看不到它时，我开始想知道现在几点了。父亲说，不断猜测机械指针在任意表盘上的位置是心智功能的症状。粪爷满头大汗的说道。我说好吧。想知道。继续思考吧。

paragraphs.en: If it had been cloudy I could have looked at the window, thinking what he said about idle habits. Thinking it would be nice for them down at New London if the weather held up like this. Why shouldn’t it? The month of brides, the voice that breathed She ran right out of the mirror, out of the banked scent. Roses. Roses. Mr and Mrs Jason Richmond Compson announce the marriage of. Roses. Not virgins like dogwood, milkweed. I said I have committed incest, Father I said. Roses. Cunning and serene. If you attend Harvard one year, but dont see the boat-race, there should be a refund. Let Jason have it. Give Jason a year at Harvard.
paragraphs.zh: 如果是阴天，我就可以看着窗子，思考他所说的关于闲散习惯的事情。我想如果天气一直这样的话，对他们在新伦敦来说会很好。为什么不应该呢？新娘之月，呼吸的声音她从镜子里跑出来，从储存的气味里跑出来。玫瑰。玫瑰。杰生Richmond康普生夫妇宣布结婚。玫瑰。不是山茱萸、马利筋之类的处女。我说我犯了乱伦罪，父亲我说。玫瑰。狡猾而冷静。如果你在哈佛就读一年，但没有看到划船比赛，应该退款。让杰生拥有吧。给杰生在哈佛大学一年的时间。

paragraphs.en: Shreve stood in the door, putting his collar on, his glasses glinting rosily, as though he had washed them with his face. “You taking a cut this morning?”
paragraphs.zh: 施里夫站在门口，套上衣领，眼镜闪着红光，就好像他用脸洗过一样。“你今天早上剪了吗？”

paragraphs.en: “Is it that late?”
paragraphs.zh: “这么晚了吗？”

paragraphs.en: He looked at his watch. “Bell in two minutes.”
paragraphs.zh: 他看了看手表。“两分钟后就响铃。”

paragraphs.en: “I didn’t know it was that late.” He was still looking at the watch, his mouth shaping. “I’ll have to hustle. I cant stand another cut. The dean told me last week—” He put the watch back into his pocket. Then I quit talking.
paragraphs.zh: “我不知道已经这么晚了。”他仍然看着手表，抿着嘴。“我得抓紧时间了。我再也受不了了。院长上周告诉我——”他把手表放回口袋里。然后我就不说话了。

paragraphs.en: “You’d better slip on your pants and run,” he said. He went out.
paragraphs.zh: “你最好穿上裤子跑，”他说。他出去了。

paragraphs.en: I got up and moved about, listening to him through the wall. He entered the sitting-room, toward the door.
paragraphs.zh: 我起身走动，隔着墙听他说话。他走进起居室，朝门口走去。

paragraphs.en: “Aren’t you ready yet?”
paragraphs.zh: “你还没准备好吗？”

paragraphs.en: “Not yet. Run along. I’ll make it.”
paragraphs.zh: “还没有。快跑吧。我会成功的。”

paragraphs.en: He went out. The door closed. His feet went down the corridor. Then I could hear the watch again. I quit moving around and went to the window and drew the curtains aside and watched them running for chapel, the same ones fighting the same heaving coat-sleeves, the same books and flapping collars flushing past like debris on a flood, and Spoade. Calling Shreve my husband. Ah let him alone, Shreve said, if he’s got better sense than to chase after the little dirty sluts, whose business. In the South you are ashamed of being a virgin. Boys. Men. They lie about it. Because it means less to women, Father said. He said it was men invented virginity not women. Father said it’s like death, only a state in which the others are left and I said, But to believe it doesn’t matter and he said, That’s what’s so sad about anything: not only virginity, and I said, Why couldn’t it have been me and not her who is unvirgin and he said, That’s why that’s sad too; nothing is even worth the changing of it, and Shreve said if he’s got better sense than to chase after the little dirty sluts and I said Did you ever have a sister? Did you? Did you?
paragraphs.zh: 他出去了。门关上了。他的脚沿着走廊走去。然后我又听到了手表的声音。我不再四处走动，走到窗前，把窗帘拉到一边，看着他们跑向教堂，同样的人与同样起伏的衣袖作斗争，同样的书和拍打的衣领像洪水中的碎片一样冲过，还有斯波德。称施里夫为我丈夫。啊，别管他了，施里夫说，如果他比追那些肮脏的小荡妇更明智的话，那是他们的事。在南方，你以身为处女为耻。男孩们。男人。他们对此撒谎。因为这对女人来说意义不大，父亲说。他说童贞是男人发明的，而不是女人。父亲说这就像死亡，只是其他人都处于一种状态，我说，但相信这并不重要，他说，这就是任何事情的可悲之处：不仅仅是童贞，我说，为什么不是我而不是她是非处女，他说，这就是为什么这也是可悲的；没有什么值得改变的，施里夫说如果他有更好的理智去追那些肮脏的小荡妇，我说你有过妹妹吗？你有吗？你有吗？

paragraphs.en: Spoade was in the middle of them like a terrapin in a street full of scuttering dead leaves, his collar about his ears, moving at his customary unhurried walk. He was from South Carolina, a senior. It was his club’s boast that he never ran for chapel and had never got there on time and had never been absent in four years and had never made either chapel or first lecture with a shirt on his back and socks on his feet. About ten oclock he’d come in Thompson’s, get two cups of coffee, sit down and take his socks out of his pocket and remove his shoes and put them on while the coffee cooled. About noon you’d see him with a shirt and collar on, like anybody else. The others passed him running, but he never increased his pace at all. After a while the quad was empty.
paragraphs.zh: 斯波德站在他们中间，就像一只水龟在满是飞落的枯叶的街道上，他的衣领围着耳朵，按照他惯常的从容不迫的步伐走着。他来自南卡罗来纳州，是一名大四学生。他的俱乐部夸口说，他从来没有竞选过教堂，也从来没有准时到达那里，四年来从未缺席过，而且从来没有穿着衬衫、脚上穿着袜子去教堂或第一次演讲。大约十点钟，他来到汤普森店，喝了两杯咖啡，坐下来，从口袋里掏出袜子，脱掉鞋子，等咖啡冷却后穿上。中午时分，你会看到他像其他人一样穿着衬衫，戴着领子。其他人都跑过他，但他却没有加快脚步。过了一会儿，四方院就空了。

paragraphs.en: A sparrow slanted across the sunlight, onto the window ledge, and cocked his head at me. His eye was round and bright. First he’d watch me with one eye, then flick! and it would be the other one, his throat pumping faster than any pulse. The hour began to strike. The sparrow quit swapping eyes and watched me steadily with the same one until the chimes ceased, as if he were listening too. Then he flicked off the ledge and was gone.
paragraphs.zh: 一只麻雀斜跨过阳光，飞到窗台上，向我歪着头。他的眼睛又圆又亮。首先他会用一只眼睛看着我，然后轻弹！这将是另一个，他的喉咙跳得比任何脉搏都快。时间开始敲响。麻雀不再交换眼睛，而是用同一只眼睛稳定地看着我，直到钟声停止，仿佛他也在听。然后他从壁架上弹了下来，消失了。

paragraphs.en: It was a while before the last stroke ceased vibrating. It stayed in the air, more felt than heard, for a long time. Like all the bells that ever rang still ringing in the long dying light-rays and Jesus and Saint Francis talking about his sister. Because if it were just to hell; if that were all of it. Finished. If things just finished themselves. Nobody else there but her and me. If we could just have done something so dreadful that they would have fled hell except us. I have committed incest I said Father it was I it was not Dalton Ames And when he put Dalton Ames. Dalton Ames. Dalton Ames. When he put the pistol in my hand I didn’t. That’s why I didn’t. He would be there and she would and I would. Dalton Ames. Dalton Ames. Dalton Ames. If we could have just done something so dreadful and Father said That’s sad too, people cannot do anything that dreadful they cannot do anything very dreadful at all they cannot even remember tomorrow what seemed dreadful today and I said, You can shirk all things and he said, Ah can you. And I will look down and see my murmuring bones and the deep water like wind, like a roof of wind, and after a long time they cannot distinguish even bones upon the lonely and inviolate sand. Until on the Day when He says Rise only the flat-iron would come floating up. It’s not when you realise that nothing can help you—religion, pride, anything—it’s when you realise that you dont need any aid. Dalton Ames. Dalton Ames. Dalton Ames. If I could have been his mother lying with open body lifted laughing, holding his father with my hand refraining, seeing, watching him die before he lived. One minute she was standing in the door
paragraphs.zh: 过了一会儿，最后一次敲击才停止振动。它在空气中停留了很长一段时间，更多的是感觉到而不是听到。就像所有曾经敲响过的钟声，在漫长而消逝的光线中仍然响起，耶稣和圣弗朗西斯谈论着他的妹妹。因为如果只是下地狱的话；如果这就是全部的话。完成的。如果事情就这么结束了。除了她和我，那里没有其他人。如果我们能做一些如此可怕的事情，那么除了我们之外，他们就会逃离地狱。我犯了乱伦我说父亲这是我，不是道尔顿·艾姆斯当他把道尔顿·艾姆斯。道尔顿·艾姆斯。道尔顿·艾姆斯。当他把手枪放在我手里时，我没有。这就是为什么我没有这样做。他会在那里，她会在那里，我也会在那里。道尔顿·艾姆斯。道尔顿·艾姆斯。道尔顿·艾姆斯。如果我们可以做一些如此可怕的事情，父亲说那也很悲伤，人们不能做任何可怕的事情，他们根本不能做任何非常可怕的事情，他们甚至不记得明天今天看起来可怕的事情，我说，你可以逃避所有事情，他说，啊，你可以吗。我低头一看，我的骨头咕咕作响，深水如风，如风的屋顶，过了很长一段时间，他们甚至无法辨认孤独和未受侵犯的沙地上的骨头。直到他说“起来”的那一天，只有扁铁才会浮起来。不是当你意识到没有任何东西可以帮助你时——宗教、骄傲，任何东西——而是当你意识到你不需要任何帮助时。道尔顿·艾姆斯。道尔顿·艾姆斯。道尔顿·艾姆斯。如果我能成为他的母亲，张开身体躺在地上，笑着，用我的手握住他的父亲，看着他在他活着之前死去。前一分钟她还站在门口

paragraphs.en: I went to the dresser and took up the watch, with the face still down. I tapped the crystal on the corner of the dresser and caught the fragments of glass in my hand and put them into the ashtray and twisted the hands off and put them in the tray. The watch ticked on. I turned the face up, the blank dial with little wheels clicking and clicking behind it, not knowing any better. Jesus walking on Galilee and Washington not telling lies. Father brought back a watch-charm from the Saint Louis Fair to Jason: a tiny opera glass into which you squinted with one eye and saw a skyscraper, a ferris wheel all spidery, Niagara Falls on a pinhead. There was a red smear on the dial. When I saw it my thumb began to smart. I put the watch down and went into Shreve’s room and got the iodine and painted the cut. I cleaned the rest of the glass out of the rim with the towel.
paragraphs.zh: 我走到梳妆台前，拿起手表，手表的表盘仍然朝下。我敲了敲梳妆台一角的水晶，接住了手里的玻璃碎片，放进烟灰缸里，又扭开手，放进了托盘里。手表滴答作响。我把表盘翻过来，空白的表盘后面有小轮子，咔哒作响，我不知道还有什么更好的了。耶稣行走在加利利和华盛顿，没有说谎。父亲从圣路易斯集市带回了一件手表饰品给杰生：一个小小的歌剧玻璃，你用一只眼睛眯起眼睛就能看到一座摩天大楼、一个蜘蛛般的摩天轮、针头上的尼亚加拉大瀑布。表盘上有一道红色污迹。当我看到它时，我的拇指开始变聪明。我放下手表，走进施里夫的房间拿了碘酒，给伤口涂了药。我用毛巾把玻璃边缘的其余部分擦干净。

paragraphs.en: I laid out two suits of underwear, with socks, shirts, collars and ties, and packed my trunk. I put in everything except my new suit and an old one and two pairs of shoes and two hats, and my books. I carried the books into the sitting-room and stacked them on the table, the ones I had brought from home and the ones Father said it used to be a gentleman was known by his books; nowadays he is known by the ones he has not returned and locked the trunk and addressed it. The quarter hour sounded. I stopped and listened to it until the chimes ceased.
paragraphs.zh: 我拿出两套内衣、袜子、衬衫、领子和领带，然后收拾行李。我把所有东西都放进去了，除了我的新西装、一套旧西装、两双鞋、两顶帽子和我的书。我把书搬进客厅，堆在桌子上，从家里带来的，父亲说以前是君子的，从书上就知道了；如今，那些没有回来的人都认识他了，他锁上了行李箱并写了地址。刻钟声响起。我停下来听，直到钟声停止。

paragraphs.en: I bathed and shaved. The water made my finger smart a little, so I painted it again. I put on my new suit and put my watch on and packed the other suit and the accessories and my razor and brushes in my hand bag, and wrapped the trunk key into a sheet of paper and put it in an envelope and addressed it to Father, and wrote the two notes and sealed them.
paragraphs.zh: 我洗澡、刮胡子。水让我的手指有点酸，所以我又画了一遍。我穿上新衣服，戴上手表，把另一套衣服和配饰以及剃须刀和刷子装进手提包里，把行李箱钥匙包在一张纸里装进信封里写给父亲，写下两张纸条并密封起来。

paragraphs.en: The shadow hadn’t quite cleared the stoop. I stopped inside the door, watching the shadow move. It moved almost perceptibly, creeping back inside the door, driving the shadow back into the door. Only she was running already when I heard it. In the mirror she was running before I knew what it was. That quick, her train caught up over her arm she ran out of the mirror like a cloud, her veil swirling in long glints her heels brittle and fast clutching her dress onto her shoulder with the other hand, running out of the mirror the smells roses roses the voice that breathed o’er Eden. Then she was across the porch I couldn’t hear her heels then in the moonlight like a cloud, the floating shadow of the veil running across the grass, into the bellowing. She ran out of her dress, clutching her bridal, running into the bellowing where T. P. in the dew Whooey Sassprilluh Benjy under the box bellowing. Father had a V-shaped silver cuirass on his running chest
paragraphs.zh: 阴影还没有完全离开门廊。我在门内停了下来，看着影子移动。它几乎可以被察觉地移动，爬回门内，将影子赶回门内。只是当我听到的时候她已经跑了。我还没反应过来，镜子里的她就开始奔跑了。很快，她的裙裾追上了她的手臂，她像一朵云一样跑出了镜子，她的面纱在长长的闪光中旋转，她的脚跟脆弱，另一只手迅速将衣服抓在肩膀上，从镜子里跑出，玫瑰的气味升起，伊甸园里呼吸的声音升起。然后她穿过门廊，我听不见她的脚后跟，在月光下像一朵云，面纱的浮动影子穿过草地，进入咆哮声。她跑出她的礼服，紧紧抓住她的新娘，跑进蒂·皮在露水里的蒂·皮在盒子下的吼叫声。父亲跑步时的胸前有一个V形的银色胸甲

paragraphs.en: Shreve said, “Well, you didn’t. . . . Is it a wedding or a wake?”
paragraphs.zh: 施里夫说：“好吧，你没有……这是婚礼还是守灵？”

paragraphs.en: “I couldn’t make it,” I said.
paragraphs.zh: “我没能做到，”我说。

paragraphs.en: “Not with all that primping. What’s the matter? You think this was Sunday?”
paragraphs.zh: “没有那么打扮。出什么事了？你以为今天是星期天吗？”

paragraphs.en: “I reckon the police wont get me for wearing my new suit one time,” I said.
paragraphs.zh: “我想警察不会因为我穿了一次新衣服而逮捕我，”我说。

paragraphs.en: “I was thinking about the Square students. Have you got too proud to attend classes too?”
paragraphs.zh: “我在想 Square 的学生。你们是不是也太骄傲而不愿上课了？”

paragraphs.en: “I’m going to eat first.” The shadow on the stoop was gone. I stepped into sunlight, finding my shadow again. I walked down the steps just ahead of it. The half hour went. Then the chimes ceased and died away.
paragraphs.zh: “我先去吃饭了。”门廊上的影子消失了。我走进阳光下，再次找到了自己的影子。我走下它前面的台阶。半个小时过去了。然后钟声停止了，渐渐消失了。

paragraphs.en: Deacon wasn’t at the postoffice either. I stamped the two envelopes and mailed the one to Father and put Shreve’s in my inside pocket, and then I remembered where I had last seen the Deacon. It was on Decoration Day, in a G. A. R. uniform, in the middle of the parade. If you waited long enough on any corner you would see him in whatever parade came along. The one before was on Columbus’ or Garibaldi’s or somebody’s birthday. He was in the Street Sweeper’s section, in a stovepipe hat, carrying a two inch Italian flag, smoking a cigar among the brooms and scoops. But the last time was the G. A. R. one, because Shreve said:
paragraphs.zh: 迪肯也不在邮局。我在两个信封上贴了邮票，将其中一个寄给了父亲，然后把施里夫的信封放进了我的内兜里，然后我记起了我最后一次见到执事的地方。那是在装饰日，穿着 G. A. R. 制服，在游行中间。如果你在任何角落等得足够长，你就会在任何游行队伍中看到他。前一次是在哥伦布或加里波第或某人的生日那天。他在街道清扫工的区域，戴着一顶瘦腿帽，举着一面两英寸的意大利国旗，在扫帚和铲子之间抽着雪茄。但最后一次是G.A.R.那次，因为施里夫说：

paragraphs.en: “There now. Just look at what your grandpa did to that poor old nigger.”
paragraphs.zh: “好了。看看你爷爷对那个可怜的老黑鬼做了什么。”

paragraphs.en: “Yes,” I said, “Now he can spend day after day marching in parades. If it hadn’t been for my grandfather, he’d have to work like whitefolks.”
paragraphs.zh: “是的，”我说，“现在他可以日复一日地参加游行了。如果没有我祖父，他就得像白人一样工作了。”

paragraphs.en: I didn’t see him anywhere. But I never knew even a working nigger that you could find when you wanted him, let alone one that lived off the fat of the land. A car came along. I went over to town and went to Parker’s and had a good breakfast. While I was eating I heard a clock strike the hour. But then I suppose it takes at least one hour to lose time in, who has been longer than history getting into the mechanical progression of it.
paragraphs.zh: 我没有在任何地方看到他。但我从来不知道，当你需要的时候，甚至可以找到一个工作的黑鬼，更不用说一个靠土地肥沃为生的黑鬼了。一辆车开过来了。我进城去帕克家吃了一顿丰盛的早餐。当我吃饭的时候，我听到钟声敲响了。但我想至少要花一个小时才能进入，这比历史上机械进展的时间还要长。

paragraphs.en: When I finished breakfast I bought a cigar. The girl said a fifty cent one was the best, so I took one and lit it and went out to the street. I stood there and took a couple of puffs, then I held it in my hand and went on toward the corner. I passed a jeweller’s window, but I looked away in time. At the corner two bootblacks caught me, one on either side, shrill and raucous, like blackbirds. I gave the cigar to one of them, and the other one a nickel. Then they let me alone. The one with the cigar was trying to sell it to the other for the nickel.
paragraphs.zh: 吃完早餐后，我买了一支雪茄。女孩说五美分的最好，所以我拿了一根点燃，然后走到街上。我站在那里，吸了几口，然后握在手里，朝拐角处走去。我经过一家珠宝店的橱窗，但我及时把目光移开。在拐角处，两个擦鞋匠抓住了我，两边各一个，声音尖利而沙哑，就像乌鸫一样。我把雪茄给了其中一个人，给了另一个人五分钱。然后他们就放过我了。拿着雪茄的那个人试图以五分钱的价格卖给另一个人。

paragraphs.en: There was a clock, high up in the sun, and I thought about how, when you dont want to do a thing, your body will try to trick you into doing it, sort of unawares. I could feel the muscles in the back of my neck, and then I could hear my watch ticking away in my pocket and after a while I had all the other sounds shut away, leaving only the watch in my pocket. I turned back up the street, to the window. He was working at the table behind the window. He was going bald. There was a glass in his eye—a metal tube screwed into his face. I went in.
paragraphs.zh: 太阳高处有一个时钟，我想到，当你不想做一件事时，你的身体会试图欺骗你去做这件事，有点不知不觉。我能感觉到脖子后面的肌肉，然后我能听到手表在口袋里滴答作响，过了一会儿，我把所有其他声音都关掉了，只剩下手表在口袋里。我转身沿着街道，来到窗前。他正在窗后的桌子旁工作。他快秃了。他的眼睛里有一块玻璃——一根金属管拧进他的脸上。我进去了。

paragraphs.en: The place was full of ticking, like crickets in September grass, and I could hear a big clock on the wall above his head. He looked up, his eye big and blurred and rushing beyond the glass. I took mine out and handed it to him.
paragraphs.zh: 这个地方充满了滴答声，就像九月草地上的蟋蟀，我能听到他头顶墙上挂着一个大钟的声音。他抬起头来，他的眼睛又大又模糊，冲向玻璃外面。我把我的拿出来递给他。

paragraphs.en: “I broke my watch.”
paragraphs.zh: “我把手表弄坏了。”

paragraphs.en: He flipped it over in his hand. “I should say you have. You must have stepped on it.”
paragraphs.zh: 他把它在手里翻了个身。“我应该说你有。你一定是踩到了它。”

paragraphs.en: “Yes, sir. I knocked it off the dresser and stepped on it in the dark. It’s still running though.”
paragraphs.zh: “是的，先生。我把它从梳妆台上摔了下来，然后在黑暗中踩到了它。不过它还在运行。”

paragraphs.en: He pried the back open and squinted into it. “Seems to be all right. I cant tell until I go over it, though. I’ll go into it this afternoon.”
paragraphs.zh: 他撬开后背，眯起眼睛往里看。“看来没问题。不过，在我仔细检查之前我无法判断。今天下午我会再讨论。”

paragraphs.en: “I’ll bring it back later,” I said. “Would you mind telling me if any of those watches in the window are right?”
paragraphs.zh: “我稍后再把它带回来。”我说。“你介意告诉我橱窗里的手表是否准确吗？”

paragraphs.en: He held my watch on his palm and looked up at me with his blurred rushing eye.
paragraphs.zh: 他把我的手表放在手掌上，用他那双模糊的、急促的眼睛抬头看着我。

paragraphs.en: “I made a bet with a fellow,” I said, “And I forgot my glasses this morning.”
paragraphs.zh: “我和一个人打赌，”我说，“今天早上我忘记带眼镜了。”

paragraphs.en: “Why, all right,” he said. He laid the watch down and half rose on his stool and looked over the barrier. Then he glanced up at the wall. “It’s twen—”
paragraphs.zh: “好吧，”他说。他放下手表，在凳子上半站起来，朝栅栏外看去。然后他抬头看了一眼墙壁。“已经两点了——”

paragraphs.en: “Dont tell me,” I said, “please sir. Just tell me if any of them are right.”
paragraphs.zh: “请不要告诉我，”我说，“先生，请告诉我他们中是否有一个是对的。”

paragraphs.en: He looked at me again. He sat back on the stool and pushed the glass up onto his forehead. It left a red circle around his eye and when it was gone his whole face looked naked. “What’re you celebrating today?” he said. “That boat race aint until next week, is it?”
paragraphs.zh: 他又看了我一眼。他坐回凳子上，把玻璃杯推到额头上。它在他的眼睛周围留下了一个红圈，当它消失后，他的整张脸看起来都赤裸了。“今天庆祝什么？”他说。“划船比赛要到下周才举行，是吗？”

paragraphs.en: “No, sir. This is just a private celebration. Birthday. Are any of them right?”
paragraphs.zh: “不，先生。这只是一个私人庆祝活动。生日。他们中的任何一个是对的吗？”

paragraphs.en: “No. But they haven’t been regulated and set yet. If you’re thinking of buying one of them—”
paragraphs.zh: “不。但是它们还没有受到监管和设置。如果你想购买其中一个——”

paragraphs.en: “No, sir. I dont need a watch. We have a clock in our sitting room. I’ll have this one fixed when I do.” I reached my hand.
paragraphs.zh: “不，先生。我不需要手表。我们的客厅里有一个钟。等我需要的时候我会修好这个。”我伸手。

paragraphs.en: “Better leave it now.”
paragraphs.zh: “最好现在就离开。”

paragraphs.en: “I’ll bring it back later.” He gave me the watch. I put it in my pocket. I couldn’t hear it now, above all the others. “I’m much obliged to you. I hope I haven’t taken up your time.”
paragraphs.zh: “我稍后再带回来。”他把手表给了我。我把它放进口袋里。我现在听不到，尤其是其他人。“我非常感谢你。希望我没有占用你的时间。”

paragraphs.en: “That’s all right. Bring it in when you are ready. And you better put off this celebration until after we win that boat race.”
paragraphs.zh: “没关系。等你准备好了就把它带进来。你最好把这个庆祝活动推迟到我们赢得划船比赛之后。”

paragraphs.en: “Yes, sir. I reckon I had.”
paragraphs.zh: “是的，先生。我想我已经做到了。”

paragraphs.en: I went out, shutting the door upon the ticking. I looked back into the window. He was watching me across the barrier. There were about a dozen watches in the window, a dozen different hours and each with the same assertive and contradictory assurance that mine had, without any hands at all. Contradicting one another. I could hear mine, ticking away inside my pocket, even though nobody could see it, even though it could tell nothing if anyone could.
paragraphs.zh: 我出去了，随着滴答声关上了门。我回头看向窗外。他越过栅栏看着我。橱窗里大约有十几个手表，十几个不同的时间，每个手表都和我的一样自信而矛盾的保证，但根本没有任何指针。互相矛盾。我能听到我的声音在我的口袋里滴答作响，尽管没有人能看到它，即使它什么也不能告诉任何人。

paragraphs.en: And so I told myself to take that one. Because Father said clocks slay time. He said time is dead as long as it is being clicked off by little wheels; only when the clock stops does time come to life. The hands were extended, slightly off the horizontal at a faint angle, like a gull tilting into the wind. Holding all I used to be sorry about like the new moon holding water, niggers say. The jeweler was working again, bent over his bench, the tube tunnelled into his face. His hair was parted in the center. The part ran up into the bald spot, like a drained marsh in December.
paragraphs.zh: 所以我告诉自己接受那个。因为父亲说钟表可以杀死时间。他说，只要时间还被小轮子转动着，时间就死了。只有当时钟停止时，时间才变得有生命。双手伸出，略微偏离水平线，形成一个微弱的角度，就像一只迎风倾斜的海鸥。黑鬼们说，把我曾经感到遗憾的一切都握在手中，就像新月握着水一样。珠宝商又开始工作了，弯着腰，管子扎进了他的脸上。他的头发从中间分开。这部分伸进了光秃秃的地方，就像十二月干涸的沼泽一样。

paragraphs.en: I saw the hardware store from across the street. I didn’t know you bought flat-irons by the pound.
paragraphs.zh: 我从街对面看到了那家五金店。我不知道你是按磅买熨斗的。

paragraphs.en: The clerk said, “These weigh ten pounds.” Only they were bigger than I thought. So I got two six-pound little ones, because they would look like a pair of shoes wrapped up. They felt heavy enough together, but I thought again how Father had said about the reducto absurdum of human experience, thinking how the only opportunity I seemed to have for the application of Harvard. Maybe by next year; thinking maybe it takes two years in school to learn to do that properly.
paragraphs.zh: 店员说：“这些重十磅。”只是它们比我想象的要大。所以我买了两个六磅重的小东西，因为它们看起来就像一双包起来的鞋子。他们在一起感到很沉重，但我又想起了父亲所说的人类经验的归谬法，想到了我似乎拥有申请哈佛的唯一机会。也许到明年；我想也许需要在学校学习两年才能学会正确地做到这一点。

paragraphs.en: But they felt heavy enough in the air. A street car came. I got on. I didn’t see the placard on the front. It was full, mostly prosperous looking people reading newspapers. The only vacant seat was beside a nigger. He wore a derby and shined shoes and he was holding a dead cigar stub. I used to think that a Southerner had to be always conscious of niggers. I thought that Northerners would expect him to. When I first came East I kept thinking You’ve got to remember to think of them as coloured people not niggers, and if it hadn’t happened that I wasn’t thrown with many of them, I’d have wasted a lot of time and trouble before I learned that the best way to take all people, black or white, is to take them for what they think they are, then leave them alone. That was when I realised that a nigger is not a person so much as a form of behaviour; a sort of obverse reflection of the white people he lives among. But I thought at first that I ought to miss having a lot of them around me because I thought that Northerners thought I did, but I didn’t know that I really had missed Roskus and Dilsey and them until that morning in Virginia. The train was stopped when I waked and I raised the shade and looked out. The car was blocking a road crossing, where two white fences came down a hill and then sprayed outward and downward like part of the skeleton of a horn, and there was a nigger on a mule in the middle of the stiff ruts, waiting for the train to move. How long he had been there I didn’t know, but he sat straddle of the mule, his head wrapped in a piece of blanket, as if they had been built there with the fence and the road, or with the hill, carved out of the hill itself, like a sign put there saying You are home again. He didn’t have a saddle and his feet dangled almost to the ground. The mule looked like a rabbit. I raised the window.
paragraphs.zh: 但他们在空气中感觉足够沉重。一辆街车来了。我上了车。我没看到前面的标语牌。里面挤满了人，大部分都是看起来很富有的人在看报纸。唯一的空座位是在一个黑鬼旁边。他穿着一顶圆顶德比帽，擦得锃亮的鞋子，手里拿着一根已经用完的雪茄烟蒂。我曾经认为南方人必须时刻关注黑人。我以为北方人会期待他这么做。当我第一次来到东部时，我一直在想，你必须记住把他们视为有色人种，而不是黑鬼，如果不是碰巧我没有和他们中的许多人一起被抛弃，我会浪费很多时间和麻烦，然后才明白对待所有人，无论是黑人还是白人，最好的方法就是按照他们认为的样子对待他们，然后别管他们。就在那时我意识到，黑鬼与其说是一个人，不如说是一种行为形式；它是一种行为方式。这是他所生活的白人的正面反映。但一开始我想我应该怀念有很多人在我身边，因为我以为北方人也认为我怀念他们，但我不知道直到那天早上在弗吉尼亚，我才真正想念罗斯库斯和迪尔西和他们。当我醒来时，火车已经停了下来，我拉起窗帘向外看去。汽车挡住了一个路口，两道白色栅栏从山上下来，然后像喇叭骨架的一部分一样向外和向下喷射，僵硬的车辙中间有一个骑着骡子的黑鬼，等待火车开动。我不知道他在那里呆了多久，但他跨坐在骡子上，头裹着一块毯子，仿佛它们是与栅栏和道路一起建在那里的，或者是与山一起建造的，从山上雕刻出来，就像放在那里的一个标志，说你又回家了。他没有马鞍，双脚几乎悬在地上。骡子看起来像兔子。我升起窗户。

paragraphs.en: “Hey, Uncle,” I said, “Is this the way?”
paragraphs.zh: “嘿，叔叔，”我说，“就是这条路吗？”

paragraphs.en: “Suh?” He looked at me, then he loosened the blanket and lifted it away from his ear.
paragraphs.zh: “嗯？”他看着我，然后松开毯子，把它从耳边拿开。

paragraphs.en: “Christmas gift!” I said.
paragraphs.zh: “圣诞礼物！”我说。

paragraphs.en: “Sho comin, boss. You done caught me, aint you?”
paragraphs.zh: “快来吧，老大。你抓住我了，不是吗？”

paragraphs.en: “I’ll let you off this time.” I dragged my pants out of the little hammock and got a quarter out. “But look out next time. I’ll be coming back through here two days after New Year, and look out then.” I threw the quarter out the window. “Buy yourself some Santy Claus.”
paragraphs.zh: “这次我就放过你了。”我把裤子从小吊床上拉出来，取出了一枚硬币。“不过下次小心点。新年后两天我会回来这里，到时候小心点。”我把那枚硬币扔出了窗外。“给自己买点圣诞老人吧。”

paragraphs.en: “Yes, suh,” he said. He got down and picked up the quarter and rubbed it on his leg. “Thanky, young marster. Thanky.” Then the train began to move. I leaned out the window, into the cold air, looking back. He stood there beside the gaunt rabbit of a mule, the two of them shabby and motionless and unimpatient. The train swung around the curve, the engine puffing with short, heavy blasts, and they passed smoothly from sight that way, with that quality about them of shabby and timeless patience, of static serenity: that blending of childlike and ready incompetence and paradoxical reliability that tends and protects them it loves out of all reason and robs them steadily and evades responsibility and obligations by means too barefaced to be called subterfuge even and is taken in theft or evasion with only that frank and spontaneous admiration for the victor which a gentleman feels for anyone who beats him in a fair contest, and withal a fond and unflagging tolerance for whitefolks’ vagaries like that of a grandparent for unpredictable and troublesome children, which I had forgotten. And all that day, while the train wound through rushing gaps and along ledges where movement was only a labouring sound of the exhaust and groaning wheels and the eternal mountains stood fading into the thick sky, I thought of home, of the bleak station and the mud and the niggers and country folks thronging slowly about the square, with toy monkeys and wagons and candy in sacks and roman candles sticking out, and my insides would move like they used to do in school when the bell rang.
paragraphs.zh: “是的，先生，”他说。他蹲下身子，捡起那枚硬币，擦在腿上。“谢谢少爷，谢谢。”然后火车开始行驶。我把身子探出窗外，迎着寒冷的空气，回头望去。他站在一头瘦弱的骡子旁边，两人衣衫褴褛，一动不动，不耐烦。火车绕着弯道行驶，引擎发出短促而沉重的爆炸声，他们顺利地从视线中驶过，他们身上带着一种破旧的、永恒的耐心和静态的宁静：孩子般的、准备好的无能和矛盾的可靠性混合在一起，照顾和保护他们，它毫无理由地爱着他们，稳步地抢劫他们，逃避责任和义务，手段过于赤裸裸，甚至不能被称为诡计，被偷窃或逃避只有对胜利者的坦率而自发的钦佩，就像一位绅士对在公平竞争中击败他的人所怀有的那种钦佩之情，并且对白人的变幻莫测抱有一种亲切而坚定的宽容，就像祖父母对不可预测和麻烦的孩子的宽容一样，而我已经忘记了。整整一天，当火车蜿蜒穿过急流的间隙，沿着壁架行驶时，那里的运动只是排气管和车轮的呻吟声，永恒的山脉矗立在厚重的天空中，渐渐消失，我想到了家，想到了荒凉的车站和泥土，想到了黑人和乡下人慢慢地聚集在广场上，玩具猴子和马车，袋子里装着糖果，罗马蜡烛伸出来，我的内心会像以前一样移动当铃声响起时，在学校做。

paragraphs.en: I wouldn’t begin counting until the clock struck three. Then I would begin, counting to sixty and folding down one finger and thinking of the other fourteen fingers waiting to be folded down, or thirteen or twelve or eight or seven, until all of a sudden I’d realise silence and the unwinking minds, and I’d say “Ma’am?” “Your name is Quentin, isn’t it?” Miss Laura said. Then more silence and the cruel unwinking minds and hands jerking into the silence. “Tell Quentin who discovered the Mississippi River, Henry.” “DeSoto.” Then the minds would go away, and after a while I’d be afraid I had gotten behind and I’d count fast and fold down another finger, then I’d be afraid I was going too fast and I’d slow up, then I’d get afraid and count fast again. So I never could come out even with the bell, and the released surging of feet moving already, feeling earth in the scuffed floor, and the day like a pane of glass struck a light, sharp blow, and my insides would move, sitting still. Moving sitting still. One minute she was standing in the door. Benjy. Bellowing. Benjamin the child of mine old age bellowing. Caddy! Caddy!
paragraphs.zh: 直到时钟敲响三点我才开始数数。然后我会开始，数到六十，折叠一根手指，想着另外十四根手指等待折叠，或者十三根、十二根、八根、七根，直到突然间我意识到沉默和不眨眼的思想，我会说“女士？”“你叫昆丁，是吗？”劳拉小姐说道。然后是更多的沉默，残酷的、不眨眼的思想和双手猛地陷入沉默。“告诉昆丁谁发现了密西西比河，亨利。”“德索托。”然后我的思绪就会消失，过了一会儿，我会担心自己落后了，我会快速数数，然后放下另一个手指，然后我会担心自己走得太快，我会放慢速度，然后我会感到害怕，再次快速数数。所以，即使铃声响了，我也永远无法出来，脚已经开始移动，感觉到磨损的地板上的泥土，而白天就像一块玻璃受到了轻轻的、猛烈的打击，我的内心会动起来，一动不动地坐着。动静坐定。一分钟前她还站在门口。班吉。吼叫。本杰明是我晚年的孩子吼叫。凯蒂！凯蒂！

paragraphs.en: I’m going to run away. He began to cry she went and touched him. Hush. I’m not going to. Hush. He hushed. Dilsey.
paragraphs.zh: 我要逃跑。他开始哭泣，她走过去抚摸他。嘘。我不会的。嘘。他沉默了。迪尔西。

paragraphs.en: He smell what you tell him when he want to. Dont have to listen nor talk.
paragraphs.zh: 当他想闻的时候，他会闻到你告诉他的东西。不必听也不必说。

paragraphs.en: Can he smell that new name they give him? Can he smell bad luck?
paragraphs.zh: 他能闻到他们给他起的新名字吗？他能闻到霉运的味道吗？

paragraphs.en: What he want to worry about luck for? Luck cant do him no hurt.
paragraphs.zh: 他要担心运气做什么？运气不会伤害他。

paragraphs.en: What they change his name for then if aint trying to help his luck?
paragraphs.zh: 如果不是为了帮助他好运的话，他们给他改名字是为了什么？

paragraphs.en: The street car stopped, started, stopped again. Below the window I watched the crowns of people’s heads passing beneath new straw hats not yet unbleached. There were women in the car now, with market baskets, and men in work-clothes were beginning to outnumber the shined shoes and collars.
paragraphs.zh: 街车停下来，启动，又停下来。在窗下，我看到人们的头顶在尚未漂白的新草帽下经过。车里现在有女人了，提着购物篮，穿着工作服的男人开始多于擦得锃亮的鞋子和衣领。

paragraphs.en: The nigger touched my knee. “Pardon me,” he said. I swung my legs out and let him pass. We were going beside a blank wall, the sound clattering back into the car, at the women with market baskets on their knees and a man in a stained hat with a pipe stuck in the band. I could smell water, and in a break in the wall I saw a glint of water and two masts, and a gull motionless in midair, like on an invisible wire between the masts, and I raised my hand and through my coat touched the letters I had written. When the car stopped I got off.
paragraphs.zh: 黑鬼碰了碰我的膝盖。“请原谅，”他说。我把腿摆开，让他过去了。我们正沿着一堵空白的墙走，声音叮当响回到车里，朝着膝盖上放着购物篮的妇女和一个戴着污迹斑斑的帽子、带子里插着烟斗的男人。我能闻到水的味道，在墙上的一个缺口处，我看到了一丝水光和两根桅杆，还有一只海鸥在半空中一动不动，就像在桅杆之间一根看不见的电线上，我举起手，透过外套触摸我写的字母。车停稳后我就下车了。

paragraphs.en: The bridge was open to let a schooner through. She was in tow, the tug nudging along under her quarter, trailing smoke, but the ship herself was like she was moving without visible means. A man naked to the waist was coiling down a line on the fo’c’s’le head. His body was burned the colour of leaf tobacco. Another man in a straw hat without any crown was at the wheel. The ship went through the bridge, moving under bare poles like a ghost in broad day, with three gulls hovering above the stern like toys on invisible wires.
paragraphs.zh: 桥是开放的，可以让一艘纵帆船通过。她被拖着，拖船在她的舱底下轻轻前行，拖着浓烟，但船本身就像在没有任何可见手段的情况下移动。一个赤裸上身的男人正在用一根绳子盘绕在对方的头上。他的身体被烧成烟叶的颜色。驾驶的是另一个戴着草帽、没有戴王冠的男人。船穿过桥，在光秃秃的柱子下移动，就像光天化日之下的幽灵一样，三只海鸥在船尾上方盘旋，就像隐形电线上的玩具。

paragraphs.en: When it closed I crossed to the other side and leaned on the rail above the boathouses. The float was empty and the doors were closed. The crew just pulled in the late afternoon now, resting up before. The shadow of the bridge, the tiers of railing, my shadow leaning flat upon the water, so easily had I tricked it that would not quit me. At least fifty feet it was, and if I only had something to blot it into the water, holding it until it was drowned, the shadow of the package like two shoes wrapped up lying on the water. Niggers say a drowned man’s shadow was watching for him in the water all the time. It twinkled and glinted, like breathing, the float slow like breathing too, and debris half submerged, healing out to the sea and the caverns and the grottoes of the sea. The displacement of water is equal to the something of something. Reducto absurdum of all human experience, and two six-pound flat-irons weigh more than one tailor’s goose. What a sinful waste Dilsey would say. Benjy knew it when Damuddy died. He cried. He smell hit. He smell hit.
paragraphs.zh: 当它关闭时，我走到另一边，靠在船库上方的栏杆上。花车是空的，门也关着。船员们刚刚在下午晚些时候抵达，之前已经休息了。桥的影子，栏杆的层层，我的影子平靠在水面上，我如此轻易地欺骗了它，它不会让我离开。至少有五十英尺，如果我有什么东西把它吸进水里，握住它直到它被淹死，包裹的影子就像两只鞋子包裹着躺在水面上。黑人说，一个溺水者的影子一直在水里注视着他。它闪烁着，像呼吸一样，漂浮物也像呼吸一样缓慢，残骸半淹没在大海中、海中的洞穴和石窟中。水的排量等于某物的某物。还原所有人类经验的荒谬，两个六磅重的熨斗比一只裁缝的鹅还重。迪尔西会说这是多么罪恶的浪费啊。外婆死后，班吉就知道了。他哭了。他闻到了打击的味道。他闻到了打击的味道。

paragraphs.en: The tug came back downstream, the water shearing in long rolling cylinders, rocking the float at last with the echo of passage, the float lurching onto the rolling cylinder with a plopping sound and a long jarring noise as the door rolled back and two men emerged, carrying a shell. They set it in the water and a moment later Bland came out, with the sculls. He wore flannels, a grey jacket and a stiff straw hat. Either he or his mother had read somewhere that Oxford students pulled in flannels and stiff hats, so early one March they bought Gerald a one pair shell and in his flannels and stiff hat he went on the river. The folks at the boathouses threatened to call a policeman, but he went anyway. His mother came down in a hired auto, in a fur suit like an arctic explorer’s, and saw him off in a twenty-five mile wind and a steady drove of ice floes like dirty sheep. Ever since then I have believed that God is not only a gentleman and a sport; He is a Kentuckian too. When he sailed away she made a detour and came down to the river again and drove along parallel with him, the car in low gear. They said you couldn’t have told they’d ever seen one another before, like a King and Queen, not even looking at one another, just moving side by side across Massachusetts on parallel courses like a couple of planets.
paragraphs.zh: 拖船回到下游，水在长长的滚动圆筒中剪切，最后随着通过的回声摇晃着浮标，浮标突然摇晃到滚动圆筒上，发出扑通的声音和长长的刺耳噪音，门向后滚动，两个人带着一个贝壳出现了。他们把它放进水里，过了一会儿，布兰德带着双桨出来了。他穿着法兰绒衣服、灰色夹克、戴着硬挺的草帽。他或他的母亲在某处读到，牛津大学的学生穿着法兰绒衣服，戴着硬帽子，所以三月初，他们给杰拉尔德买了一件贝壳，他穿着法兰绒衣服，戴着硬帽子去河边。船库里的人威胁要报警，但他还是去了。他的母亲开着一辆租来的汽车下来，穿着北极探险家那样的毛皮套装，在二十五英里的狂风和像肮脏的羊一样的连续的浮冰中送他离开。从那时起我就相信上帝不仅是一位绅士、一位运动家；他也是肯塔基人。当他扬帆离开时，她绕道再次来到河边，与他平行行驶，车子挂着低速档。他们说你不可能知道他们以前见过彼此，就像国王和王后一样，甚至没有看对方，只是在平行的轨道上并肩穿过马萨诸塞州，就像两颗行星一样。

paragraphs.en: He got in and pulled away. He pulled pretty well now. He ought to. They said his mother tried to make him give rowing up and do something else the rest of his class couldn’t or wouldn’t do, but for once he was stubborn. If you could call it stubbornness, sitting in his attitudes of princely boredom, with his curly yellow hair and his violet eyes and his eyelashes and his New York clothes, while his mamma was telling us about Gerald’s horses and Gerald’s niggers and Gerald’s women. Husbands and fathers in Kentucky must have been awful glad when she carried Gerald off to Cambridge. She had an apartment over in town, and Gerald had one there too, besides his rooms in college. She approved of Gerald associating with me because I at least revealed a blundering sense of noblesse oblige by getting myself born below Mason and Dixon, and a few others whose geography met the requirements (minimum) Forgave, at least. Or condoned. But since she met Spoade coming out of chapel one He said she couldn’t be a lady no lady would be out at that hour of the night she never had been able to forgive him for having five names, including that of a present English ducal house. I’m sure she solaced herself by being convinced that some misfit Maingault or Mortemar had got mixed up with the lodge-keeper’s daughter. Which was quite probable, whether she invented it or not. Spoade was the world’s champion sitter-around, no holds barred and gouging discretionary.
paragraphs.zh: 他上车后就离开了。他现在拉得很好。他应该这样做。他们说，他的母亲试图让他放弃划船，去做一些班上其他同学不能或不愿做的事情，但这一次他很固执。如果你可以称之为固执的话，他以一种王子般的无聊态度坐着，他卷曲的黄色头发，他的紫罗兰色的眼睛，他的睫毛和他的纽约衣服，而他的妈妈正在告诉我们杰拉尔德的马，杰拉尔德的黑鬼和杰拉尔德的女人。当她把杰拉尔德带到剑桥时，肯塔基州的丈夫和父亲一定非常高兴。她在城里有一套公寓，除了大学里的房间之外，杰拉尔德也在那里拥有一间公寓。她同意杰拉尔德与我交往，因为我至少在梅森和迪克森以及其他一些地理位置满足要求（最低限度）的人之下出生，从而暴露了一种错误的贵族责任感，至少可以原谅。或者纵容。但自从她遇见从一号教堂出来的斯波德以来，他说她不可能是一位女士，没有哪个女士会在晚上的那个时候出去，她永远无法原谅他有五个名字，包括现在的英国公爵家族的名字。我确信，她确信某个不合群的迈格特或莫特马尔与旅馆老板的女儿混在一起了，以此来安慰自己。无论她是否发明，这都是很有可能的。斯波德是世界冠军坐骑，没有任何限制，可以自由裁量。

paragraphs.en: The shell was a speck now, the oars catching the sun in spaced glints, as if the hull were winking itself along. Did you ever have a sister? No but they’re all bitches. Did you ever have a sister? One minute she was. Bitches. Not bitch one minute she stood in the door Dalton Ames. Dalton Ames. Dalton Shirts. I thought all the time they were khaki, army issue khaki, until I saw they were of heavy Chinese silk or finest flannel because they made his face so brown his eyes so blue. Dalton Ames. It just missed gentility. Theatrical fixture. Just papier-mache, then touch. Oh. Asbestos. Not quite bronze. But wont see him at the house.
paragraphs.zh: 贝壳现在变成了一个斑点，桨在阳光下闪烁着间隔的光芒，就好像船体在闪烁着自己。你曾经有过妹妹吗？不，但他们都是婊子。你曾经有过妹妹吗？一分钟后她还这样。母狗。她一分钟都没有站在道尔顿·艾姆斯的门口。道尔顿·艾姆斯。道尔顿衬衫。我一直以为它们是卡其色，军用卡其色，直到我看到它们是厚重的中国丝绸或最好的法兰绒，因为它们使他的脸如此棕色，眼睛如此蓝色。道尔顿·艾姆斯。它只是错过了温柔。戏剧固定装置。只是纸型，然后触摸。哦。石棉。不太青铜。但不会在家里见到他。

paragraphs.en: Caddy’s a woman too, remember. She must do things for women’s reasons, too.
paragraphs.zh: 请记住，凯蒂也是女人。她也必须为女性的利益做事。

paragraphs.en: Why wont you bring him to the house, Caddy? Why must you do like nigger women do in the pasture the ditches the dark woods hot hidden furious in the dark woods.
paragraphs.zh: 你为什么不把他带回家，凯蒂？为什么你一定要像黑鬼女人一样，在牧场、沟渠、黑暗的树林里、在黑暗的树林里炎热、隐藏的愤怒。

paragraphs.en: And after a while I had been hearing my watch for some time and I could feel the letters crackle through my coat, against the railing, and I leaned on the railing, watching my shadow, how I had tricked it. I moved along the rail, but my suit was dark too and I could wipe my hands, watching my shadow, how I had tricked it. I walked it into the shadow of the quai. Then I went east.
paragraphs.zh: 过了一会儿，我听到手表的声音已经有一段时间了，我能感觉到字母在我的外套上噼啪作响，靠在栏杆上，我靠在栏杆上，看着我的影子，我是如何欺骗它的。我沿着栏杆移动，但我的衣服也是深色的，我可以擦手，观察我的影子，看看我是如何欺骗它的。我走进码头的阴影里。然后我就往东走。

paragraphs.en: Harvard my Harvard boy Harvard harvard That pimple-faced infant she met at the field-meet with coloured ribbons. Skulking along the fence trying to whistle her out like a puppy. Because they couldn’t cajole him into the diningroom Mother believed he had some sort of spell he was going to cast on her when he got her alone. Yet any blackguard He was lying beside the box under the window bellowing that could drive up in a limousine with a flower in his buttonhole. Harvard. Quentin this is Herbert. My Harvard boy. Herbert will be a big brother has already promised Jason a position in the bank.
paragraphs.zh: 哈佛，我的哈佛男孩，哈佛，哈佛，她在田野比赛中遇到的那个带着彩带、满脸痘痘的婴儿。像小狗一样沿着栅栏偷偷摸摸地想用口哨把她赶出去。因为他们无法把他哄进餐厅，所以母亲相信，当他单独和她在一起时，他会对她施某种咒语。然而，任何一个恶棍都躺在窗下的箱子旁边，大声吼叫，可以开着一辆纽扣孔里插着一朵花的豪华轿车过来。哈佛。昆丁这是赫伯特。我的哈佛男孩。赫伯特会当大哥已经答应杰生在银行谋得一个职位。

paragraphs.en: Hearty, celluloid like a drummer. Face full of teeth white but not smiling. I’ve heard of him up there. All teeth but not smiling. You going to drive?
paragraphs.zh: 像鼓手一样热情、赛璐珞。满脸牙齿雪白，却没有笑容。我听说过他在那里。满是牙齿，但没有微笑。你要开车吗？

paragraphs.en: Get in Quentin.
paragraphs.zh: 进入昆丁。

paragraphs.en: You going to drive.
paragraphs.zh: 你要开车。

paragraphs.en: It’s her car aren’t you proud of your little sister owns first auto in town Herbert his present. Louis has been giving her lessons every morning didn’t you get my letter Mr and Mrs Jason Richmond Compson announce the marriage of their daughter Candace to Mr Sydney Herbert Head on the twenty-fifth of April one thousand nine hundred and ten at Jefferson Mississippi. At home after the first of August number Something Something Avenue South Bend Indiana. Shreve said Aren’t you even going to open it? Three days. Times. Mr and Mrs Jason Richmond Compson Young Lochinvar rode out of the west a little too soon, didn’t he?
paragraphs.zh: 这是她的车，你不是为你的妹妹拥有镇上第一辆汽车而感到自豪吗？赫伯特是他的礼物。路易斯每天早上都在上课，你没收到我的信吗？杰生·里士满·康普生先生和夫人宣布他们的女儿坎迪斯于 1910 年 4 月 25 日在密西西比州杰斐逊市与西德尼·赫伯特·海德先生结婚。八月一日后在家，号码为Something Something Avenue South Bend Indiana。施里夫说你连打开都不打开吗？三天。次。年轻的洛钦瓦骑马离开西部有点太早了，不是吗？

paragraphs.en: I’m from the south. You’re funny, aren’t you.
paragraphs.zh: 我来自南方。你很有趣，不是吗。

paragraphs.en: O yes I knew it was somewhere in the country.
paragraphs.zh: 哦，是的，我知道那是在乡下的某个地方。

paragraphs.en: You’re funny, aren’t you. You ought to join the circus.
paragraphs.zh: 你很有趣，不是吗。你应该加入马戏团。

paragraphs.en: I did. That’s how I ruined my eyes watering the elephant’s fleas. Three times These country girls. You cant even tell about them, can you. Well, anyway Byron never had his wish, thank God. But not hit a man in glasses. Aren’t you even going to open it? It lay on the table a candle burning at each corner upon the envelope tied in a soiled pink garter two artificial flowers. Not hit a man in glasses.
paragraphs.zh: 我做到了。我就是这样给大象的跳蚤浇水而毁了我的眼睛的。三遍这些乡下姑娘。你甚至无法讲述它们，不是吗？好吧，无论如何，拜伦从未实现他的愿望，感谢上帝。但没有打到戴眼镜的人。你连它都不打开吗？桌上放着一支蜡烛，信封的四角都燃烧着，信封上系着两朵人造花，用脏兮兮的粉色吊袜带绑着。没有打到戴眼镜的人。

paragraphs.en: Country people poor things they never saw an auto before lots of them honk the horn Candace so She wouldn’t look at me they’ll get out of the way wouldn’t look at me your father wouldn’t like it if you were to injure one of them I’ll declare your father will simply have to get an auto now I’m almost sorry you brought it down Herbert I’ve enjoyed it so much of course there’s the carriage but so often when I’d like to go out Mr Compson has the darkies doing something it would be worth my head to interrupt he insists that Roskus is at my call all the time but I know what that means I know how often people make promises just to satisfy their consciences are you going to treat my little baby girl that way Herbert but I know you wont Herbert has spoiled us all to death Quentin did I write you that he is going to take Jason into his bank when Jason finishes high school Jason will make a splendid banker he is the only one of my children with any practical sense you can thank me for that he takes after my people the others are all Compson Jason furnished the flour. They made kites on the back porch and sold them for a nickle a piece, he and the Patterson boy. Jason was treasurer.
paragraphs.zh: 乡下人很可怜，他们以前从未见过汽车，很多人都按喇叭坎迪斯，所以她不会看我，他们会让路，不会看我，如果你伤害他们中的一个，你的父亲不会喜欢它，我会宣布你的父亲现在只需要得到一辆汽车，我几乎很抱歉你把它撞倒了赫伯特，我非常喜欢它，当然有马车，但经常当我想出去的时候康普生先生黑人正在做一些值得我花心思打断的事情，他坚持说罗斯库斯一直在听我的电话，但我知道这意味着什么，我知道人们经常做出承诺，只是为了满足他们的良心，你会这样对待我的小宝贝女儿赫伯特，但我知道你不会，赫伯特把我们都宠坏了昆丁我写信给你了吗，当杰生高中毕业时，他将带杰生进入他的银行杰生将成为一名出色的银行家他是我的孩子中唯一一个有实际意义的人，你可以感谢我，因为他效仿我的人民，其他人都是康普生杰生提供的面粉。他和帕特森男孩在后廊制作了风筝，然后以每枚一分钱的价格出售。杰生是财务主管。

paragraphs.en: There was no nigger in this street car, and the hats unbleached as yet flowing past under the window. Going to Harvard. We have sold Benjy’s He lay on the ground under the window, bellowing. We have sold Benjy’s pasture so that Quentin may go to Harvard a brother to you. Your little brother.
paragraphs.zh: 这辆有轨电车里没有黑人，那些还没有漂白的帽子从车窗下流过。要去哈佛。我们卖掉了班吉的他躺在窗下的地上，吼叫着。我们已经卖掉了班吉的牧场，这样昆丁就可以去哈佛当你的兄弟了。你的小弟弟。

paragraphs.en: You should have a car it’s done you no end of good dont you think so Quentin I call him Quentin at once you see I have heard so much about him from Candace.
paragraphs.zh: 你应该拥有一辆车，这对你有无穷无尽的好处，你不这么认为昆丁吗？我立刻就叫他昆丁，你看，我从坎迪斯那里听说过很多关于他的事。

paragraphs.en: Why shouldn’t you I want my boys to be more than friends yes Candace and Quentin more than friends Father I have committed what a pity you had no brother or sister No sister no sister had no sister Dont ask Quentin he and Mr Compson both feel a little insulted when I am strong enough to come down to the table I am going on nerve now I’ll pay for it after it’s all over and you have taken my little daughter away from me My little sister had no. If I could say Mother. Mother
paragraphs.zh: 为什么你不应该吗？我希望我的孩子们不仅仅是朋友，是的，坎迪斯和昆丁，不仅仅是朋友，父亲，我犯了多么遗憾的事，你没有兄弟姐妹，没有姐妹，没有姐妹，没有姐妹。别问昆丁，当我足够坚强，走到餐桌旁时，他和康普生先生都感到有点被侮辱，我现在很紧张，在一切结束后，你把我的小女儿从我身边带走，我的小妹妹没有。如果我可以说妈妈的话。母亲

paragraphs.en: Unless I do what I am tempted to and take you instead I dont think Mr Compson could overtake the car.
paragraphs.zh: 除非我做我想做的事，带你去，否则我认为康普生先生不可能超越这辆车。

paragraphs.en: Ah Herbert Candace do you hear that She wouldn’t look at me soft stubborn jaw-angle not back-looking You needn’t be jealous though it’s just an old woman he’s flattering a grown married daughter I cant believe it.
paragraphs.zh: 啊赫伯特坎迪斯你听到了吗她不会看着我柔软顽固的下巴角度不回头你不必嫉妒虽然这只是一个老妇人他正在奉承一个已婚的女儿我不敢相信。

paragraphs.en: Nonsense you look like a girl you are lots younger than Candace colour in your cheeks like a girl A face reproachful tearful an odour of camphor and of tears a voice weeping steadily and softly beyond the twilit door the twilight-coloured smell of honeysuckle. Bringing empty trunks down the attic stairs they sounded like coffins French Lick. Found not death at the salt lick
paragraphs.zh: 胡说，你看起来像个女孩，你比坎迪斯年轻得多，你的脸颊颜色像个女孩，一张充满责备泪水的脸，带着樟脑和泪水的气味，一个声音在暮色的门外稳定而轻柔地哭泣，暮色的金银花气味。把空箱子从阁楼楼梯上搬下来，听起来就像是法国利克的棺材。在盐舔处发现没有死亡

paragraphs.en: Hats not unbleached and not hats. In three years I can not wear a hat. I could not. Was. Will there be hats then since I was not and not Harvard then. Where the best of thought Father said clings like dead ivy vines upon old dead brick. Not Harvard then. Not to me, anyway. Again. Sadder than was. Again. Saddest of all. Again.
paragraphs.zh: 帽子不是未漂白的，也不是帽子。三年后我就不能戴帽子了。我不能。曾是。那时会有帽子吗，因为我当时不是哈佛，也不是哈佛。父亲所说的最好的思想就像死去的常春藤蔓一样附着在枯死的砖头上。那时还不是哈佛。无论如何，对我来说不是。再次。比原来更难过了再次。最悲伤的是。再次。

paragraphs.en: Spoade had a shirt on; then it must be. When I can see my shadow again if not careful that I tricked into the water shall tread again upon my impervious shadow. But no sister. I wouldn’t have done it. I wont have my daughter spied on I wouldn’t have.
paragraphs.zh: 斯波德穿着一件衬衫；那么一定是的。当我再次看到我的影子时，如果我不小心被骗进水里，我将再次踩到我不透水的影子。但没有姐姐。我不会这么做的。我不会让我的女儿被监视，我不会。

paragraphs.en: How can I control any of them when you have always taught them to have no respect for me and my wishes I know you look down on my people but is that any reason for teaching my children my own children I suffered for to have no respect Trampling my shadow’s bones into the concrete with hard heels and then I was hearing the watch, and I touched the letters through my coat.
paragraphs.zh: 当你总是教导他们不尊重我和我的愿望时，我怎么能控制他们中的任何一个？我知道你看不起我的人民，但有任何理由去教导我的孩子，我自己的孩子，我因不尊重而受苦，用坚硬的高跟鞋将我影子的骨头踩在混凝土上，然后我听到了手表的声音，我透过外套触摸了字母。

paragraphs.en: I will not have my daughter spied on by you or Quentin or anybody no matter what you think she has done
paragraphs.zh: 我不会让你、昆丁或任何人监视我的女儿，无论你认为她做了什么

paragraphs.en: At least you agree there is reason for having her watched
paragraphs.zh: 至少你同意让她观看是有理由的

paragraphs.en: I wouldn’t have I wouldn’t have. I know you wouldn’t I didn’t mean to speak so sharply but women have no respect for each other for themselves
paragraphs.zh: 我不会的我不会的。我知道你不会，我本来不想说得那么尖锐，但女人之间不尊重彼此

paragraphs.en: But why did she The chimes began as I stepped on my shadow, but it was the quarter hour. The Deacon wasn’t in sight anywhere. think I would have could have
paragraphs.zh: 但为什么她在我踩到影子的时候就开始鸣响，但现在已经是一刻钟了。到处都看不到执事的身影。我想我本来可以

paragraphs.en: She didn’t mean that that’s the way women do things its because she loves Caddy
paragraphs.zh: 她并不是说这就是女人做事的方式，而是因为她喜欢凯蒂

paragraphs.en: The street lamps would go down the hill then rise toward town I walked upon the belly of my shadow. I could extend my hand beyond it. feeling Father behind me beyond the rasping darkness of summer and August the street lamps Father and I protect women from one another from themselves our women Women are like that they dont acquire knowledge of people we are for that they are just born with a practical fertility of suspicion that makes a crop every so often and usually right they have an affinity for evil for supplying whatever the evil lacks in itself for drawing it about them instinctively as you do bedclothing in slumber fertilising the mind for it until the evil has served its purpose whether it ever existed or no He was coming along between a couple of freshmen. He hadn’t quite recovered from the parade, for he gave me a salute, a very superior-officerish kind.
paragraphs.zh: 路灯会从山上下来，然后升向城镇，我踩着影子的肚子行走。我可以把手伸出去。超越夏季和八月的刺耳黑暗，路灯，父亲和我保护女人免受彼此的伤害，我们的女人就像她们不了解我们是谁，因为她们生来就有一种实际的怀疑生育力，这种怀疑常常使农作物时常正确，她们对邪恶有一种亲和力，提供邪恶本身所缺乏的一切，本能地将邪恶吸引到他们身上，就像你在沉睡中做床上用品一样，为它滋养心灵，直到邪恶达到其目的，无论它是否存在过或者不，他是从几个新生中间走过的。他还没有从游行中完全恢复过来，他向我行了一个非常高级军官的敬礼。

paragraphs.en: “I want to see you a minute,” I said, stopping.
paragraphs.zh: “我想见你一下，”我停下来说道。

paragraphs.en: “See me? All right. See you again, fellows,” he said, stopping and turning back; “glad to have chatted with you.” That was the Deacon, all over. Talk about your natural psychologists. They said he hadn’t missed a train at the beginning of school in forty years, and that he could pick out a Southerner with one glance. He never missed, and once he had heard you speak, he could name your state. He had a regular uniform he met trains in, a sort of Uncle Tom’s cabin outfit, patches and all.
paragraphs.zh: “看到我了吗？好吧。再见了，伙计们，”他说着，停下来，转身往回走。“很高兴和你聊天。”那就是执事，一切都结束了。谈谈你的自然心理学家。他们说他四十年来没有错过开学时的火车，而且他一眼就能认出一个南方人。他从来没有错过，一旦他听到你说话，他就能说出你所在的州。他穿着一套在火车上穿的普通制服，类似于汤姆叔叔的机舱服装，还有补丁等等。

paragraphs.en: “Yes, suh. Right dis way, young marster, hyer we is,” taking your bags. “Hyer, boy, come hyer and git dese grips.” Whereupon a moving mountain of luggage would edge up, revealing a white boy of about fifteen, and the Deacon would hang another bag on him somehow and drive him off. “Now, den, dont you drap hit. Yes, suh, young marster, jes give de old nigger yo room number, and hit’ll be done got cold dar when you arrives.”
paragraphs.zh: “是的，先生。对了，少爷，我们就是这样。”拿上你的行李。“嘿，孩子，来吧，握紧这些。”于是，一座移动的行李山就会慢慢上升，露出一个十五岁左右的白人男孩，执事会以某种方式在他身上挂上另一个袋子，然后把他赶走。“现在，丹恩，你别打了。是的，先生，年轻的先生，我给老黑鬼你房间号，等你到达时，打就完成了。”

paragraphs.en: From then on until he had you completely subjugated he was always in or out of your room, ubiquitous and garrulous, though his manner gradually moved northward as his raiment improved, until at last when he had bled you until you began to learn better he was calling you Quentin or whatever, and when you saw him next he’d be wearing a cast-off Brooks suit and a hat with a Princeton club I forget which band that someone had given him and which he was pleasantly and unshakably convinced was a part of Abe Lincoln’s military sash. Someone spread the story years ago, when he first appeared around college from wherever he came from, that he was a graduate of the divinity school. And when he came to understand what it meant he was so taken with it that he began to retail the story himself, until at last he must come to believe he really had. Anyway he related long pointless anecdotes of his undergraduate days, speaking familiarly of dead and departed professors by their first names, usually incorrect ones. But he had been guide mentor and friend to unnumbered crops of innocent and lonely freshmen, and I suppose that with all his petty chicanery and hypocrisy he stank no higher in heaven’s nostrils than any other.
paragraphs.zh: 从那时起，直到他彻底征服你为止，他总是进出你的房间，无所不在，喋喋不休，尽管他的态度随着衣着的改善而逐渐北移，直到最后当他给你流血，直到你开始学得更好时，他才叫你昆丁或其他什么，当你下次看到他时，他会穿着一套废弃的布鲁克斯西装，戴着带有普林斯顿俱乐部的帽子，我忘记了有人给了他哪条乐队，他是令人愉快和坚定不移的确信是亚伯·林肯军用腰带的一部分。几年前，当他第一次从任何地方出现在大学周围时，有人传播了这个故事，说他是神学院的毕业生。当他明白这意味着什么时，他对此非常着迷，以至于他开始自己讲述这个故事，直到最后他必须相信他真的明白了。不管怎样，他讲述了他大学时代的长篇无意义的轶事，熟悉地谈论已故和离任的教授的名字，通常是不正确的名字。但他曾是无数无辜而孤独的新生的导师和朋友，我想，尽管他的小伎俩和虚伪，他在天堂的鼻孔里并不比其他人更臭。

paragraphs.en: “Haven’t seen you in three-four days,” he said, staring at me from his still military aura. “You been sick?”
paragraphs.zh: “已经三四天没见到你了，”他说道，脸上仍然带着军人的气息，盯着我。“你生病了吗？”

paragraphs.en: “No. I’ve been all right. Working, I reckon. I’ve seen you, though.”
paragraphs.zh: “没有。我一直都很好。我想是在工作。不过我见过你。”

paragraphs.en: “Yes?”
paragraphs.zh: “是吗？”

paragraphs.en: “In the parade the other day.”
paragraphs.zh: “前几天的游行中。”

paragraphs.en: “Oh, that. Yes, I was there. I dont care nothing about that sort of thing, you understand, but the boys likes to have me with them, the vet’runs does. Ladies wants all the old vet’runs to turn out, you know. So I has to oblige them.”
paragraphs.zh: “哦，那个。是的，我在那儿。我一点也不关心这类事情，你明白，但是男孩们喜欢我和他们在一起，老兵们也喜欢。女士们希望所有老老兵们都能参加比赛，你知道。所以我必须满足他们。”

paragraphs.en: “And on that Wop holiday too,” I said. “You were obliging the W. C. T. U. then, I reckon.”
paragraphs.zh: “还有那个沃普假期，”我说。“我想，当时你是在向 W.C.T.U. 求助。”

paragraphs.en: “That? I was doing that for my son-in-law. He aims to get a job on the city forces. Street cleaner. I tells him all he wants is a broom to sleep on. You saw me, did you?”
paragraphs.zh: “那个？我是为我女婿做的。他的目标是在城市部队找到一份工作。街道清洁工。我告诉他他想要的只是一把用来睡觉的扫帚。你看到我了，是吗？”

paragraphs.en: “Both times. Yes.”
paragraphs.zh: “两次。是的。”

paragraphs.en: “I mean, in uniform. How’d I look?”
paragraphs.zh: “我是说，穿着制服。我看起来怎么样？”

paragraphs.en: “You looked fine. You looked better than any of them. They ought to make you a general, Deacon.”
paragraphs.zh: “你看起来很好。你看起来比他们中任何一个人都好。他们应该让你成为将军，迪肯。”

paragraphs.en: He touched my arm, lightly, his hand that worn, gentle quality of niggers’ hands. “Listen. This aint for outside talking. I dont mind telling you because you and me’s the same folks, come long and short.” He leaned a little to me, speaking rapidly, his eyes not looking at me. “I’ve got strings out, right now. Wait till next year. Just wait. Then see where I’m marching. I wont need to tell you how I’m fixing it; I say, just wait and see, my boy.” He looked at me now and clapped me lightly on the shoulder and rocked back on his heels, nodding at me. “Yes, sir. I didnt turn Democrat three years ago for nothing. My son-in-law on the city; me—Yes, sir. If just turning Democrat’ll make that son of a bitch go to work. . . . And me: just you stand on that corner yonder a year from two days ago, and see.”
paragraphs.zh: 他轻轻地碰了碰我的手臂，他的手像黑鬼的手一样磨损，温柔。“听着。这不适合在外面说话。我不介意告诉你，因为你和我是同一个人，无论长短。”他稍微靠向我，语速很快，眼睛没有看着我。“我现在就已经做好了准备。等到明年。等着吧。然后看看我将走向何方。我不需要告诉你我是如何解决的；我说，等着瞧吧，我的孩子。”他现在看着我，轻轻拍了拍我的肩膀，然后向后摇晃，对我点点头。“是的，先生。三年前我加入民主党并不是无缘无故的。我在这座城市的女婿；我——是的，先生。只要加入民主党就能让那个王八蛋去工作……还有我：你就站在一年前的那个街角，两天前看看吧。”

paragraphs.en: “I hope so. You deserve it, Deacon. And while I think about it—” I took the letter from my pocket. “Take this around to my room tomorrow and give it to Shreve. He’ll have something for you. But not till tomorrow, mind.”
paragraphs.zh: “我希望如此。你应得的，迪肯。当我想到这一点时——”我从口袋里掏出那封信。“明天把这个带到我的房间交给施里夫。他会给你一些东西。但要等到明天，注意。”

paragraphs.en: He took the letter and examined it. “It’s sealed up.”
paragraphs.zh: 他接过这封信并检查了它。“它被密封了。”

paragraphs.en: “Yes. And it’s written inside, Not good until tomorrow.”
paragraphs.zh: “是的。里面写着，明天才好。”

paragraphs.en: “H’m,” he said. He looked at the envelope, his mouth pursed. “Something for me, you say?”
paragraphs.zh: “嗯，”他说。他看着信封，抿着嘴。“你说有什么东西给我？”

paragraphs.en: “Yes. A present I’m making you.”
paragraphs.zh: “是的。我正在给你做一份礼物。”

paragraphs.en: He was looking at me now, the envelope white in his black hand, in the sun. His eyes were soft and irisless and brown, and suddenly I saw Roskus watching me from behind all his white-folks’ claptrap of uniforms and politics and Harvard manner, diffident, secret, inarticulate and sad. “You aint playing a joke on the old nigger, is you?”
paragraphs.zh: 他现在正看着我，黑色的手里握着白色的信封，在阳光下。他的眼睛是柔和的，没有虹膜，是棕色的，突然我看到罗斯库斯从他那群白人对制服、政治和哈佛风格的夸夸其谈后面看着我，羞怯、神秘、不善言辞和悲伤。“你不会跟那个老黑鬼开玩笑吧？”

paragraphs.en: “You know I’m not. Did any Southerner ever play a joke on you?”
paragraphs.zh: “你知道我不是。有哪个南方人跟你开玩笑过吗？”

paragraphs.en: “You’re right. They’re fine folks. But you cant live with them.”
paragraphs.zh: “你是对的。他们是好人。但你不能和他们一起生活。”

paragraphs.en: “Did you ever try?” I said. But Roskus was gone. Once more he was that self he had long since taught himself to wear in the world’s eye, pompous, spurious, not quite gross.
paragraphs.zh: “你尝试过吗？”我说。但罗斯库斯已经走了。他再次成为了他早已学会在世人眼中展现的那个自己，浮夸、虚伪，但并不粗俗。

paragraphs.en: “I’ll confer to your wishes, my boy.”
paragraphs.zh: “我会满足你的愿望，我的孩子。”

paragraphs.en: “Not until tomorrow, remember.”
paragraphs.zh: “明天之前不行，记住。”

paragraphs.en: “Sure,” he said; “understood, my boy. Well—”
paragraphs.zh: “当然，”他说。“明白了，我的孩子。好吧——”

paragraphs.en: “I hope—” I said. He looked down at me, benignant, profound. Suddenly I held out my hand and we shook, he gravely, from the pompous height of his municipal and military dream. “You’re a good fellow, Deacon. I hope. . . . You’ve helped a lot of young fellows, here and there.”
paragraphs.zh: “我希望——”我说。他低头看着我，慈祥而深邃。突然我伸出了手，我们握手，他严肃地从他的市政和军事梦想的浮夸高度。“你是个好人，迪肯。我希望……你已经帮助了很多年轻人，到处都是。”

paragraphs.en: “I’ve tried to treat all folks right,” he said. “I draw no petty social lines. A man to me is a man, wherever I find him.”
paragraphs.zh: “我试图正确对待所有人，”他说。“我不会划出细微的社交界限。对我来说，男人就是男人，无论我在哪里找到他。”

paragraphs.en: “I hope you’ll always find as many friends as you’ve made.”
paragraphs.zh: “我希望你永远能找到尽可能多的朋友。”

paragraphs.en: “Young fellows. I get along with them. They dont forget me, neither,” he said, waving the envelope. He put it into his pocket and buttoned his coat. “Yes, sir,” he said, “I’ve had good friends.”
paragraphs.zh: “年轻人。我和他们相处融洽。他们也不会忘记我，”他挥舞着信封说道。他把它放进口袋，扣上外套的扣子。“是的，先生，”他说，“我有一些好朋友。”

paragraphs.en: The chimes began again, the half hour. I stood in the belly of my shadow and listened to the strokes spaced and tranquil along the sunlight, among the thin, still little leaves. Spaced and peaceful and serene, with that quality of autumn always in bells even in the month of brides. Lying on the ground under the window bellowing He took one look at her and knew. Out of the mouths of babes. The street lamps The chimes ceased. I went back to the postoffice, treading my shadow into pavement. go down the hill then they rise toward town like lanterns hung one above another on a wall. Father said because she loves Caddy she loves people through their shortcomings. Uncle Maury straddling his legs before the fire must remove one hand long enough to drink Christmas. Jason ran on, his hands in his pockets fell down and lay there like a trussed fowl until Versh set him up. Whyn’t you keep them hands outen your pockets when you running you could stand up then Rolling his head in the cradle rolling it flat across the back. Caddy told Jason Versh said that the reason Uncle Maury didn’t work was that he used to roll his head in the cradle when he was little.
paragraphs.zh: 钟声再次响起，半点钟声响起。我站在影子的深处，聆听着阳光下，细细的、静止的小树叶之间间隔而宁静的敲击声。空间宽敞、平和、宁静，即使在新娘月里，秋天的气息也总是在钟声中响起。趴在窗下的地上吼叫，他一看她就知道了。从辣妹嘴里说出来。路灯钟声停止了。我回到邮局，把我的影子踩在人行道上。他们下了山，然后朝镇上走去，就像墙上的灯笼一个接一个地挂着。父亲说因为她爱凯蒂，所以她爱人们的缺点。莫里舅舅跨坐在火堆前，必须移开一只手，足够长的时间喝圣诞酒。杰生继续跑，双手插在口袋里，像一只被拴住的家禽一样倒在地上，直到弗许把他扶起来。为什么你不让他们的手从你的口袋里，当你跑步时，你可以站起来，然后把他的头放在摇篮里，把它平放在背上。凯蒂告诉杰生弗许说，莫里舅舅不工作的原因是他小时候经常在摇篮里滚动头。

paragraphs.en: Shreve was coming up the walk, shambling, fatly earnest, his glasses glinting beneath the running leaves like little pools.
paragraphs.zh: 施里夫正沿着步道走来，步履蹒跚，极其认真，他的眼镜在像小水池一样的树叶下闪闪发光。

paragraphs.en: “I gave Deacon a note for some things. I may not be in this afternoon, so dont you let him have anything until tomorrow, will you?”
paragraphs.zh: “我给迪肯写了一些事情的纸条。我今天下午可能不在，所以你明天之前不要让他有任何事情，好吗？”

paragraphs.en: “All right.” He looked at me. “Say, what’re you doing today, anyhow? All dressed up and mooning around like the prologue to a suttee. Did you go to Psychology this morning?”
paragraphs.zh: “好吧。”他看着我。“说吧，你今天到底在做什么？全副武装，像苏蒂的序幕一样闲逛。今天早上你去心理学了吗？”

paragraphs.en: “I’m not doing anything. Not until tomorrow, now.”
paragraphs.zh: “我什么也没做。直到明天，现在。”

paragraphs.en: “What’s that you got there?”
paragraphs.zh: “你那儿拿的是什么？”

paragraphs.en: “Nothing. Pair of shoes I had half-soled. Not until tomorrow, you hear?”
paragraphs.zh: “没什么。我的一双半底鞋。明天才到，你听到了吗？”

paragraphs.en: “Sure. All right. Oh, by the way, did you get a letter off the table this morning?”
paragraphs.zh: “当然。好吧。哦，顺便问一下，今天早上你收到一封没有收到的信吗？”

paragraphs.en: “No.”
“It’s there. From Semiramis. Chauffeur brought it before ten o’clock.”
paragraphs.zh: “就在那里。从塞米勒米斯来的。司机在十点钟之前送来的。”

paragraphs.en: “All right. I’ll get it. Wonder what she wants now.”
paragraphs.zh: “好吧。我去拿。不知道她现在想要什么。”

paragraphs.en: “Another band recital, I guess. Tumpty ta ta Gerald blah. ‘A little louder on the drum, Quentin.’ God, I’m glad I’m not a gentleman.” He went on, nursing a book, a little shapeless, fatly intent. The street lamps do you think so because one of our forefathers was a governor and three were generals and Mother’s weren’t
paragraphs.zh: “我猜又是一场乐队演奏会。Tumpty ta ta 杰拉尔德等等。‘昆丁，鼓声大一点。’上帝啊，我很高兴我不是一个绅士。”他继续前行，手里捧着一本书，神情有点不成形，但注意力却很集中。路灯你这么认为是因为我们的祖先之一是州长，三个是将军，而母亲的不是

paragraphs.en: The car came up and stopped. The bells were still ringing the half hour. I got on and it went on again, blotting the half hour. No: the three quarters. Then it would be ten minutes anyway. To leave Harvard your Mother’s dream for sold Benjy’s pasture for
paragraphs.zh: 车子开过来停了下来。半点的钟声仍然响着。我上了车，事情又继续了，浪费了半个小时。不：四分之三。那么无论如何也就十分钟了。离开你母亲的哈佛梦想，卖掉班吉的牧场

I turned my back to it, tramping my shadow into the dust. There was something terrible in me sometimes at night I could see it grinning at me I could see it through them grinning at me through their faces it’s gone now and I’m sick
