paragraphs.zh: 终于看不到烟囱了。路挨着一堵墙。树木斜靠在墙上，洒满阳光。石头很凉。走近它，就能感受到一股凉意。只是我们的国家不像这个国家。只是走过它就有一些东西。一种平静而猛烈的繁殖力，可以满足永远的面包饥饿感。在你周围流动，而不是沉思和护理每一块小气的石头。就像它是临时搭建的，以便有足够的绿色在树林中流动，甚至远处的蓝色也不是那么丰富的奇美拉。告诉我骨头必须再次折断，我内心开始说“啊啊啊”，我开始出汗。我在乎什么，我知道一条腿断了，什么都不是了，什么也不是了，我只需要在屋子里多待一会儿，就这样，我的下巴肌肉开始麻木，我的嘴里流着汗，说等等，等一下啊啊啊，爸爸该死的那匹马，该死的那匹马。等等，都是我的错。每天早上他都会提着篮子沿着栅栏走向厨房，每天早上我都会拖着一根棍子沿着栅栏走去。我把自己拖到窗台前，为他铺上一块煤，迪尔西说你会毁了自己，自从你被撞了几天后，你就没有任何感觉了。等一下，我一会儿就会习惯，等一下，我会习惯的

paragraphs.en: Even sound seemed to fail in this air, like the air was worn out with carrying sounds so long. A dog’s voice carries further than a train, in the darkness anyway. And some people’s. Niggers. Louis Hatcher never even used his horn carrying it and that old lantern. I said, “Louis, when was the last time you cleaned that lantern?”
paragraphs.zh: 就连声音在这空气中都显得失灵，仿佛空气因长时间的声音承载而变得疲惫不堪。无论如何，在黑暗中，狗的声音比火车传得更远。还有一些人的。黑鬼。路易斯·海切尔甚至从未用过他的号角来携带它和那盏旧灯笼。我说：“路易斯，你最后一次清理那个灯笼是什么时候？”

paragraphs.en: “I cleant hit a little while back. You member when all dat floodwatter wash dem folks away up yonder? I cleant hit dat ve’y day. Old woman and me settin fore de fire dat night and she say ‘Louis, whut you gwine do ef dat flood git out dis fur?’ and I say ‘Dat’s a fack. I reckon I had better clean dat lantun up.’ So I cleant hit dat night.”
paragraphs.zh: “我不久前就击中了。你知道那些洪水把那边的人们冲走的时候吗？我那天晚上就击中了。那天晚上我和老妇人在火前放火，她说‘路易斯，如果洪水冲走了你的皮毛，你要做什么？’我说‘那是骗子。我想我最好把那个兰屯清理干净。’所以我击中了那个。晚上。”

paragraphs.en: “That flood was way up in Pennsylvania,” I said. “It couldn’t even have got down this far.”
paragraphs.zh: “宾夕法尼亚州的洪水水位很高，”我说。“根本不可能落到这一步。”

paragraphs.en: “Dat’s whut you says,” Louis said. “Watter kin git des ez high en wet in Jefferson ez hit kin in Pennsylvaney, I reckon. Hit’s de folks dat says de high watter cant git dis fur dat comes floatin out on de ridge-pole, too.”
paragraphs.zh: “这就是你说的，”路易斯说。“我想，杰斐逊的水流在宾夕法尼亚州的水流中也很潮湿。人们说，高水流不能从山脊上飘浮出来。”

paragraphs.en: “Did you and Martha get out that night?”
paragraphs.zh: “那天晚上你和玛莎出去了吗？”

paragraphs.en: “We done jest that. I cleant dat lantun and me and her sot de balance of de night on top o dat knoll back de graveyard. En ef I’d a knowed of aihy one higher, we’d a been on hit instead.”
paragraphs.zh: “我们就这么开玩笑了。我和我以及她在墓地后面的小山丘上清理了夜晚的平衡。如果我知道有一个更高的，我们就会受到打击。”

paragraphs.en: “And you haven’t cleaned that lantern since then.”
paragraphs.zh: “从那以后你就没有清理过那个灯笼了。”

paragraphs.en: “Whut I want to clean hit when dey aint no need?”
paragraphs.zh: “当他们不需要的时候，我为什么要干净利落？”

paragraphs.en: “You mean, until another flood comes along?”
paragraphs.zh: “你是说，直到另一场洪水来临？”

paragraphs.en: “Hit kep us outen dat un.”
paragraphs.zh: “打击让我们摆脱了困境。”

paragraphs.en: “Oh, come on, Uncle Louis,” I said.
paragraphs.zh: “哦，来吧，路易斯叔叔，”我说。

paragraphs.en: “Yes, suh. You do you way en I do mine. Ef all I got to do to keep outen de high watter is to clean dis yere lantun, I wont quoil wid no man.”
paragraphs.zh: “是的，先生。你按照你的方式做，我也按照我的方式做。如果我要做的就是清理兰屯，以防止洪水泛滥，那么我不会在没有人的情况下担心。”

paragraphs.en: “Unc’ Louis wouldn’t ketch nothin wid a light he could see by,” Versh said.
paragraphs.zh: “路易叔叔不会在他看得见的灯光下抓任何东西，”弗许说。

paragraphs.en: “I wuz huntin possums in dis country when dey was still drowndin nits in yo pappy’s head wid coal oil, boy,” Louis said. “Ketchin um, too.”
paragraphs.zh: “我在这个国家狩猎负鼠，当时负鼠还被煤油淹没在你爸爸脑袋里的幼虫中，孩子，”路易斯说。“凯钦，嗯，也是。”

paragraphs.en: “Dat’s de troof,” Versh said. “I reckon Unc’ Louis done caught mo possums than aihy man in dis country.”
paragraphs.zh: “就是这样，”弗许说。“我认为路易叔叔在这个国家抓到的负鼠比抓到的人还要多。”

paragraphs.en: “Yes, suh,” Louis said, “I got plenty light fer possums to see, all right. I aint heard none o dem complainin. Hush, now. Dar he. Whooey. Hum awn, dawg.” And we’d sit in the dry leaves that whispered a little with the slow respiration of our waiting and with the slow breathing of the earth and the windless October, the rank smell of the lantern fouling the brittle air, listening to the dogs and to the echo of Louis’ voice dying away. He never raised it, yet on a still night we have heard it from our front porch. When he called the dogs in he sounded just like the horn he carried slung on his shoulder and never used, but clearer, mellower, as though his voice were a part of darkness and silence, coiling out of it, coiling into it again. WhoOoooo. WhoOoooo. WhoOooooooooooooooo. Got to marry somebody
paragraphs.zh: “是的，先生，”路易斯说，“我有足够多的光线可以让负鼠看到，好吧。我没有听到他们抱怨。嘘，现在。达他。呼。嗯，天啊。”我们坐在干燥的树叶上，随着我们等待的缓慢呼吸、大地缓慢的呼吸和无风的十月，灯笼的恶臭污染了脆弱的空气，听着狗的叫声和路易斯渐渐远去的声音的回声。他从来没有举过它，但在一个寂静的夜晚，我们从前廊听到了它。当他把狗叫进来时，他的声音就像他挂在肩上从未使用过的号角一样，但更清晰、更柔和，仿佛他的声音是黑暗和寂静的一部分，从其中盘旋出来，又盘旋进去。哇噢噢。哇噢噢。谁哦哦哦哦哦哦。一定要和某人结婚

paragraphs.zh: 我必须嫁给弗许告诉我一个男人自残的人。他走进树林，坐在沟里，用剃刀剃了刀。一把破损的剃刀将它们向后甩到肩膀上，同样的动作完成了向后猛烈的血绞，而不是循环。但事实并非如此。并不是没有它们。从来没有拥有过它们，我才能说“哦，那是中国人，我不懂中文”。父亲说那是因为你是处女：你明白吗？女人从来都不是处女。纯洁是一种消极的状态，因此违背自然。伤害你的是自然，而不是凯蒂，我说这只是说说而已，他说童贞也是如此，我说你不知道。你不可能知道，他说是的。当我们意识到悲剧是二手的那一刻。

paragraphs.en: Where the shadow of the bridge fell I could see down for a long way, but not as far as the bottom. When you leave a leaf in water a long time after awhile the tissue will be gone and the delicate fibers waving slow as the motion of sleep. They dont touch one another, no matter how knotted up they once were, no matter how close they lay once to the bones. And maybe when He says Rise the eyes will come floating up too, out of the deep quiet and the sleep, to look on glory. And after awhile the flat irons would come floating up. I hid them under the end of the bridge and went back and leaned on the rail.
paragraphs.zh: 在桥的影子落下的地方，我可以看到很远的地方，但看不到底部。当你把一片叶子放在水中很长一段时间后，一段时间后，组织就会消失，脆弱的纤维会像睡眠一样缓慢地摆动。它们不会互相接触，无论它们曾经多么纠缠在一起，无论它们曾经离骨头有多近。也许当他说“起来”时，眼睛也会浮起，从深深的安静和睡眠中浮现出来，观看荣耀。过了一会儿，熨斗就会浮起来。我把它们藏在桥底下，然后回去靠在栏杆上。

paragraphs.en: I could not see the bottom, but I could see a long way into the motion of the water before the eye gave out, and then I saw a shadow hanging like a fat arrow stemming into the current. Mayflies skimmed in and out of the shadow of the bridge just above the surface. If it could just be a hell beyond that: the clean flame the two of us more than dead. Then you will have only me then only me then the two of us amid the pointing and the horror beyond the clean flame The arrow increased without motion, then in a quick swirl the trout lipped a fly beneath the surface with that sort of gigantic delicacy of an elephant picking up a peanut. The fading vortex drifted away down stream and then I saw the arrow again, nose into the current, wavering delicately to the motion of the water above which the May flies slanted and poised. Only you and me then amid the pointing and the horror walled by the clean flame
paragraphs.zh: 我看不到底部，但在眼睛失去知觉之前，我可以看到很长一段距离，进入水的运动，然后我看到一个影子像一支粗箭头一样悬挂在水流中。蜉蝣在桥面的阴影中飞进飞出。如果这只是一个地狱的话：清洁的火焰让我们两个都死了。然后你就只有我了然后只有我然后我们两个就在干净的火焰之外的指点和恐怖之中箭矢一动不动地增加了，然后在一个快速的旋转中，鳟鱼用嘴唇把一只苍蝇咬到了水面下，就像大象捡起花生一样巨大的美味。逐渐减弱的漩涡顺流而下，然后我又看到了那支箭，它的鼻子伸进了水流中，随着水面的运动而微妙地摇摆，五月蝇在上面倾斜并保持着平衡。那时只有你和我在被洁净的火焰包围的指指点点和恐惧之中

paragraphs.en: The trout hung, delicate and motionless among the wavering shadows. Three boys with fishing poles came onto the bridge and we leaned on the rail and looked down at the trout. They knew the fish. He was a neighbourhood character.
paragraphs.zh: 鳟鱼纤弱地悬挂在摇曳的阴影中，一动不动。三个拿着鱼竿的男孩来到桥上，我们靠在栏杆上低头看着鳟鱼。他们认识这条鱼。他是一个邻里人物。

paragraphs.en: “They’ve been trying to catch that trout for twenty-five years. There’s a store in Boston offers a twenty-five dollar fishing rod to anybody that can catch him.”
paragraphs.zh: “二十五年来，他们一直想钓那条鳟鱼。波士顿有一家商店向任何能钓到这条鳟鱼的人提供一根 25 美元的钓鱼竿。”

paragraphs.en: “Why dont you all catch him, then? Wouldnt you like to have a twenty-five dollar fishing rod?”
paragraphs.zh: “那你们为什么不去抓他呢？你们不想买根二十五美元的鱼竿吗？”

paragraphs.en: “Yes,” they said. They leaned on the rail, looking down at the trout. “I sure would,” one said.
paragraphs.zh: “是的，”他们说。他们靠在栏杆上，低头看着鳟鱼。“我肯定会的，”其中一人说道。

paragraphs.en: “I wouldnt take the rod,” the second said. “I’d take the money instead.”
paragraphs.zh: “我不会接受这根棍子，”第二个说。“我宁愿拿钱。”

paragraphs.en: “Maybe they wouldnt do that,” the first said. “I bet he’d make you take the rod.”
paragraphs.zh: “也许他们不会那样做，”第一个说。“我打赌他会让你接受这根棍子。”

paragraphs.en: “Then I’d sell it.”
paragraphs.zh: “那我就卖掉它。”

paragraphs.en: “You couldnt get twenty-five dollars for it.”
paragraphs.zh: “你拿不到二十五美元。”

paragraphs.en: “I’d take what I could get, then. I can catch just as many fish with this pole as I could with a twenty-five dollar one.” Then they talked about what they would do with twenty-five dollars. They all talked at once, their voices insistent and contradictory and impatient, making of unreality a possibility, then a probability, then an incontrovertible fact, as people will when their desires become words.
paragraphs.zh: “那么，我会拿我能得到的东西。我用这根竿子钓到的鱼和用一根二十五美元的竿子钓到的鱼一样多。”然后他们讨论了要用二十五美元做什么。他们同时说话，他们的声音坚持、矛盾、不耐烦，让不现实成为一种可能性，然后成为一种概率，然后成为无可争议的事实，就像人们在欲望变成言语时所做的那样。

paragraphs.en: “I’d buy a horse and wagon,” the second said.
paragraphs.zh: “我会买一匹马和一辆马车，”第二个说。

paragraphs.en: “Yes you would,” the others said.
paragraphs.zh: “是的，你会的，”其他人说。

paragraphs.en: “I would. I know where I can buy one for twenty-five dollars. I know the man.”
paragraphs.zh: “我愿意。我知道在哪里可以花二十五美元买到一个。我认识那个人。”

paragraphs.en: “Who is it?”
paragraphs.zh: “是谁？”

paragraphs.en: “That’s all right who it is. I can buy it for twenty-five dollars.”
paragraphs.zh: “不管是谁，我都可以花二十五美元买下它。”

paragraphs.en: “Yah,” the others said, “He dont know any such thing. He’s just talking.”
paragraphs.zh: “是的，”其他人说，“他什么都不知道。他只是说说而已。”

paragraphs.en: “Do you think so?” the boy said. They continued to jeer at him, but he said nothing more. He leaned on the rail, looking down at the trout which he had already spent, and suddenly the acrimony, the conflict, was gone from their voices, as if to them too it was as though he had captured the fish and bought his horse and wagon, they too partaking of that adult trait of being convinced of anything by an assumption of silent superiority. I suppose that people, using themselves and each other so much by words, are at least consistent in attributing wisdom to a still tongue, and for a while I could feel the other two seeking swiftly for some means by which to cope with him, to rob him of his horse and wagon.
paragraphs.zh: “你这么认为吗？”男孩说。他们继续嘲笑他，但他什么也没说。他靠在栏杆上，低头看着他已经吃完的鳟鱼，突然间，他们声音中的尖酸刻薄和冲突消失了，仿佛对他们来说，就好像他捕获了鱼，买了他的马和马车，他们也分享了成年人的特征，通过自以为沉默的优越感来相信任何事情。我想，人们如此多地通过言语来利用自己和彼此，至少一致地认为沉默的舌头是智慧的，有一段时间，我能感觉到另外两个人正在迅速寻找某种方法来对付他，抢走他的马和马车。

paragraphs.en: “You couldnt get twenty-five dollars for that pole,” the first said. “I bet anything you couldnt.”
paragraphs.zh: “那根杆子你卖不到二十五美元，”第一个说。“我敢打赌，你不能打赌。”

paragraphs.en: “He hasnt caught that trout yet,” the third said suddenly, then they both cried:
paragraphs.zh: “他还没钓到那条鳟鱼。”第三个突然说道，然后他们都哭了：

paragraphs.en: “Yah, wha’d I tell you? What’s the man’s name? I dare you to tell. There aint any such man.”
paragraphs.zh: “是啊，我告诉你什么了？那个人叫什么名字？我敢说，没有这样的人。”

paragraphs.en: “Ah, shut up,” the second said. “Look, Here he comes again.” They leaned on the rail, motionless, identical, their poles slanting slenderly in the sunlight, also identical. The trout rose without haste, a shadow in faint wavering increase; again the little vortex faded slowly downstream. “Gee,” the first one murmured.
paragraphs.zh: “啊，闭嘴，”第二个说。“你看，他又来了。”它们靠在栏杆上，一动不动，一模一样，杆子在阳光下细长地倾斜着，也一模一样。鳟鱼不慌不忙地升起，影子在微弱地摇曳着增加；小漩涡再次向下游缓缓消退。“哎呀，”第一个低声说道。

paragraphs.en: “We dont try to catch him anymore,” he said. “We just watch Boston folks that come out and try.”
paragraphs.zh: “我们不再试图抓住他，”他说。“我们只是看着波士顿人出来尝试。”

paragraphs.en: “Is he the only fish in this pool?”
paragraphs.zh: “这池子里就只有他一条鱼吗？”

paragraphs.en: “Yes. He ran all the others out. The best place to fish around here is down at the Eddy.”
paragraphs.zh: “是的。他把其他人都赶走了。这附近最好的钓鱼地点是在涡流下面。”

paragraphs.en: “No it aint,” the second said. “It’s better at Bigelow’s Mill two to one.” Then they argued for a while about which was the best fishing and then left off all of a sudden to watch the trout rise again and the broken swirl of water suck down a little of the sky. I asked how far it was to the nearest town. They told me.
paragraphs.zh: “不，不是，”第二个说。“毕格罗磨坊的效果更好，二比一。”然后他们争论了一会儿哪一个钓鱼最好，然后突然停下来，看着鳟鱼再次升起，破碎的水流吸走了一点天空。我问距离最近的城镇有多远。他们告诉我。

paragraphs.en: “But the closest car line is that way,” the second said, pointing back down the road. “Where are you going?”
paragraphs.zh: “但最近的汽车线路就在那边，”第二个说，指着路的另一边。“你要去哪里？”

paragraphs.en: “Nowhere. Just walking.”
paragraphs.zh: “无处可去。只是步行。”

paragraphs.en: “You from the college?”
paragraphs.zh: “你是学院的？”

paragraphs.en: “Yes. Are there any factories in that town?”
paragraphs.zh: “是的。那个镇上有工厂吗？”

paragraphs.en: “Factories?” They looked at me.
paragraphs.zh: “工厂？”他们看着我。

paragraphs.en: “No,” the second said. “Not there.” They looked at my clothes. “You looking for work?”
paragraphs.zh: “不，”第二个说。“不在那里。”他们看了我的衣服。“你在找工作吗？”

paragraphs.en: “How about Bigelow’s Mill?” the third said. “That’s a factory.”
paragraphs.zh: “毕格罗磨坊怎么样？”第三个说。“那是一家工厂。”

paragraphs.en: “Factory my eye. He means a sure enough factory.”
paragraphs.zh: “工厂是我的眼睛。他指的是一家工厂。”

paragraphs.en: “One with a whistle,” I said. “I havent heard any one oclock whistles yet.”
paragraphs.zh: “一个有口哨的，”我说。“我还没听到一点点的口哨声呢。”

paragraphs.en: “Oh,” the second said. “There’s a clock in the Unitarian steeple. You can find out the time from that. Havent you got a watch on that chain?”
paragraphs.zh: “哦，”第二个说。“一神论者的尖塔里有一个钟。你可以从钟表上知道时间。你的链子上没有手表吗？”

paragraphs.en: “I broke it this morning.” I showed them my watch. They examined it gravely.
paragraphs.zh: “今天早上我把它弄坏了。”我给他们看了我的手表。他们严肃地检查了它。

paragraphs.en: “It’s still running,” the second said. “What does a watch like that cost?”
paragraphs.zh: “它还在运行，”第二个说。“这样的手表值多少钱？”

paragraphs.en: “It was a present,” I said. “My father gave it to me when I graduated from high school.”
paragraphs.zh: “这是一份礼物，”我说。“我高中毕业时，我父亲把它送给了我。”

paragraphs.en: “Are you a Canadian?” the third said. He had red hair.
paragraphs.zh: “你是加拿大人吗？”第三个说。他有一头红头发。

paragraphs.en: “Canadian?”
paragraphs.zh: “加拿大人？”

paragraphs.en: “He dont talk like them,” the second said. “I’ve heard them talk. He talks like they do in minstrel shows.”
paragraphs.zh: “他说话不像他们，”第二个说。“我听过他们说话。他说话就像吟游诗人表演中那样。”

paragraphs.en: “Say,” the third said, “Aint you afraid he’ll hit you?”
paragraphs.zh: “喂，”第三个说，“你不怕他打你吗？”

paragraphs.en: “Hit me?”
paragraphs.zh: “打我？”

paragraphs.en: “You said he talks like a coloured man.”
paragraphs.zh: “你说他说话像个有色人种。”

paragraphs.en: “Ah, dry up,” the second said. “You can see the steeple when you get over that hill there.”
paragraphs.zh: “啊，擦干，”第二个说。“当你翻过那座山时，你就能看到尖塔了。”

paragraphs.en: I thanked them. “I hope you have good luck. Only dont catch that old fellow down there. He deserves to be let alone.”
paragraphs.zh: 我向他们表示感谢。“我希望你好运。只是别在那儿抓住那个老家伙。他不值得打扰。”

paragraphs.en: “Cant anybody catch that fish,” the first said. They leaned on the rail, looking down into the water, the three poles like three slanting threads of yellow fire in the sun. I walked upon my shadow, tramping it into the dappled shade of trees again. The road curved, mounting away from the water. It crossed the hill, then descended winding, carrying the eye, the mind on ahead beneath a still green tunnel, and the square cupola above the trees and the round eye of the clock but far enough. I sat down at the roadside. The grass was ankle deep, myriad. The shadows on the road were as still as if they had been put there with a stencil, with slanting pencils of sunlight. But it was only a train, and after a while it died away beyond the trees, the long sound, and then I could hear my watch and the train dying away, as though it were running through another month or another summer somewhere, rushing away under the poised gull and all things rushing. Except Gerald. He would be sort of grand too, pulling in lonely state across the noon, rowing himself right out of noon, up the long bright air like an apotheosis, mounting into a drowsing infinity where only he and the gull, the one terrifically motionless, the other in a steady and measured pull and recover that partook of inertia itself, the world punily beneath their shadows on the sun. Caddy that blackguard that blackguard Caddy
paragraphs.zh: “没人能钓到那条鱼吗？”第一个说。他们靠在栏杆上，俯视水中，三根柱子在阳光下就像三根倾斜的黄色火线。我踩着自己的影子，再次将它踩进斑驳的树荫里。道路弯曲，远离水面。它穿过山丘，然后蜿蜒而下，带着眼睛和心灵在一条静谧的绿色隧道下方、树木上方的方形圆顶和圆形的钟眼上行走，但距离足够远。我在路边坐下。草丛深及脚踝，无数。路上的影子一动不动，仿佛是用模板画出来的，阳光斜斜地照射着。但这只是一列火车，过了一会儿，它在树林后面消失了，那悠长的声音，然后我能听到我的手表和火车渐渐消失，仿佛它正在某个地方运行另一个月或另一个夏天，在泰然自若的海鸥和所有事物的奔腾下疾驰而去。除了杰拉尔德。他也会很伟大，在中午的时候以孤独的状态拉动，从中午划船出来，像神化一样在漫长而明亮的空气中上升，上升到一个令人昏昏欲睡的无限，那里只有他和海鸥，一个一动不动，另一个稳定而有节制地拉动，恢复了惯性本身，世界在太阳的阴影下微不足道。凯蒂那个恶棍那个恶棍凯蒂

paragraphs.en: Their voices came over the hill, and the three slender poles like balanced threads of running fire. They looked at me passing, not slowing.
paragraphs.zh: 他们的声音从山那边传来，三根细长的杆子就像平衡的火线。他们看着我经过，没有放慢速度。

paragraphs.en: “Well,” I said, “I dont see him.”
paragraphs.zh: “嗯，”我说，“我没有看到他。”

paragraphs.en: “We didnt try to catch him,” the first said. “You cant catch that fish.”
paragraphs.zh: “我们并没有试图抓住他，”第一个人说。“你钓不到那条鱼。”

paragraphs.en: “There’s the clock,” the second said, pointing. “You can tell the time when you get a little closer.”
paragraphs.zh: “那儿有钟，”第二个指着说。“靠近一点就能知道时间了。”

paragraphs.en: “Yes,” I said, “All right.” I got up. “You all going to town?”
paragraphs.zh: “是的，”我说，“好吧。”我起身。“你们都去城里吗？”

paragraphs.en: “We’re going to the Eddy for chub,” the first said.
paragraphs.zh: “我们要去艾迪河抓鲢鱼，”第一个说。

paragraphs.en: “You cant catch anything at the Eddy,” the second said.
paragraphs.zh: “你在涡流上什么也抓不到，”第二个说。

paragraphs.en: “I guess you want to go to the mill, with a lot of fellows splashing and scaring all the fish away.”
paragraphs.zh: “我猜你想去磨坊，那里有很多人在泼水，把所有的鱼都吓跑了。”

paragraphs.en: “You cant catch any fish at the Eddy.”
paragraphs.zh: “你在涡流钓不到鱼。”

paragraphs.en: “We wont catch none nowhere if we dont go on,” the third said.
paragraphs.zh: “如果我们不继续前进，我们就什么也抓不到，”第三个说。

paragraphs.en: “I dont see why you keep on talking about the Eddy,” the second said. “You cant catch anything there.”
paragraphs.zh: “我不明白你为什么一直谈论涡流，”第二个说。“你在那里抓不到任何东西。”

paragraphs.en: “You dont have to go,” the first said. “You’re not tied to me.”
paragraphs.zh: “你不必走，”第一个说。“你与我无关。”

paragraphs.en: “Let’s go to the mill and go swimming,” the third said.
paragraphs.zh: “我们去磨坊去游泳吧，”第三个说。

paragraphs.en: “I’m going to the Eddy and fish,” the first said. “You can do as you please.”
paragraphs.zh: “我要去涡流钓鱼。”第一个说。“你可以随心所欲。”

paragraphs.en: “Say, how long has it been since you heard of anybody catching a fish at the Eddy?” the second said to the third.
paragraphs.zh: “请问，你有多久没有听说有人在涡流钓到鱼了？”第二个对第三个说。

paragraphs.en: “Let’s go to the mill and go swimming,” the third said. The cupola sank slowly beyond the trees, with the round face of the clock far enough yet. We went on in the dappled shade. We came to an orchard, pink and white. It was full of bees; already we could hear them.
paragraphs.zh: “我们去磨坊去游泳吧，”第三个说。冲天炉慢慢地沉入树林之外，而钟面的圆面还足够远。我们在斑驳的树荫下继续前行。我们来到了一片果园，粉红色和白色的。里面全是蜜蜂。我们已经能听到他们的声音了。

paragraphs.en: “Let’s go to the mill and go swimming,” the third said. A lane turned off beside the orchard. The third boy slowed and halted. The first went on, flecks of sunlight slipping along the pole across his shoulder and down the back of his shirt. “Come on,” the third said. The second boy stopped too. Why must you marry somebody Caddy
paragraphs.zh: “我们去磨坊去游泳吧，”第三个说。果园旁边有一条小路拐弯。第三个男孩放慢了速度并停了下来。第一个还在继续，阳光沿着杆子滑过他的肩膀，落在他的衬衫后面。“来吧，”第三个说。第二个男孩也停了下来。为什么你一定要嫁给凯蒂

paragraphs.en: Do you want me to say it do you think that if I say it it wont be
paragraphs.zh: 你想让我这么说吗？你认为如果我这么说就不会了吗

paragraphs.en: “Let’s go up to the mill,” he said. “Come on.”
paragraphs.zh: “我们去磨坊吧，”他说。“快点。”

paragraphs.en: The first boy went on. His bare feet made no sound, falling softer than leaves in the thin dust. In the orchard the bees sounded like a wind getting up, a sound caught by a spell just under crescendo and sustained. The lane went along the wall, arched over, shattered with bloom, dissolving into trees. Sunlight slanted into it, sparse and eager. Yellow butterflies flickered along the shade like flecks of sun.
paragraphs.zh: 第一个男孩继续说道。他光着的脚没有发出任何声音，落在薄薄的尘土里，比树叶还要柔软。果园里蜜蜂的叫声就像一阵风吹过，这种声音被咒语捕捉到，声音正逐渐增强并持续下去。小巷沿着墙延伸，呈拱形，花朵碎裂，融入树木。阳光斜射进来，稀疏而渴望。黄色的蝴蝶在树荫下翩翩起舞，就像阳光的斑点。

paragraphs.en: “What do you want to go to the Eddy for?” the second boy said. “You can fish at the mill if you want to.”
paragraphs.zh: “你去艾迪做什么？”第二个男孩说道。“如果你愿意的话，可以去工厂钓鱼。”

paragraphs.en: “Ah, let him go,” the third said. They looked after the first boy. Sunlight slid patchily across his walking shoulders, glinting along the pole like yellow ants.
paragraphs.zh: “啊，让他走吧。”第三个说道。他们照顾第一个男孩。阳光斑驳地洒在他行走的肩膀上，像黄色的蚂蚁一样沿着杆子闪闪发光。

paragraphs.en: “Kenny,” the second said. Say it to Father will you I will am my fathers Progenitive I invented him created I him Say it to him it will not be for he will say I was not and then you and I since philoprogenitive
paragraphs.zh: “肯尼，”第二个说。对父亲说吧，你会吗？我会是我父亲的后代，我发明了他，创造了我他，对他说，不会，因为他会说我不是，然后你和我，因为 philoprogenitive

paragraphs.en: “Ah, come on,” the boy said, “They’re already in.” They looked after the first boy. “Yah,” they said suddenly, “go on then, mamma’s boy. If he goes swimming he’ll get his head wet and then he’ll get a licking.” They turned into the lane and went on, the yellow butterflies slanting about them along the shade.
paragraphs.zh: “啊，来吧，”男孩说，“他们已经进来了。”他们照顾第一个男孩。“是的，”他们突然说道，“继续吧，妈妈的孩子。如果他去游泳，他的头就会被淋湿，然后他就会被舔。”他们拐进小巷继续前行，黄色的蝴蝶沿着树荫在他们周围倾斜。

paragraphs.en: it is because there is nothing else I believe there is something else but there may not be and then I You will find that even injustice is scarcely worthy of what you believe yourself to be He paid me no attention, his jaw set in profile, his face turned a little away beneath his broken hat.
paragraphs.zh: 这是因为没有别的东西了，我相信还有别的东西，但可能没有，然后我你会发现，即使是不公正也几乎不值得你相信自己是怎样的。

paragraphs.en: “Why dont you go swimming with them?” I said. that blackguard Caddy
paragraphs.zh: “你为什么不和他们一起去游泳呢？”我说。那个恶棍凯蒂

paragraphs.en: Were you trying to pick a fight with him were you
paragraphs.zh: 你是想跟他吵架吗？

paragraphs.en: A liar and a scoundrel Caddy was dropped from his club for cheating at cards got sent to Coventry caught cheating at midterm exams and expelled
paragraphs.zh: 骗子和恶棍凯蒂因打牌作弊被俱乐部除名，被送往考文垂，在期中考试中作弊被抓并被开除

paragraphs.en: Well what about it I’m not going to play cards with
paragraphs.zh: 好吧，那我不打算和他一起打牌怎么样？

paragraphs.en: “Do you like fishing better than swimming?” I said. The sound of the bees diminished, sustained yet, as though instead of sinking into silence, silence merely increased between us, as water rises. The road curved again and became a street between shady lawns with white houses. Caddy that blackguard can you think of Benjy and Father and do it not of me
paragraphs.zh: “比起游泳，你更喜欢钓鱼吗？”我说。蜜蜂的声音减弱了，但仍然持续着，仿佛我们之间的沉默并没有陷入沉默，而是随着水的上涨而增加。道路又拐了个弯，变成了一条街道，中间是绿树成荫的草坪和白色的房子。凯蒂那个恶棍你能想到班吉和父亲而不是我吗

paragraphs.en: What else can I think about what else have I thought about The boy turned from the street. He climbed a picket fence without looking back and crossed the lawn to a tree and laid the pole down and climbed into the fork of the tree and sat there, his back to the road and the dappled sun motionless at last upon his white shirt. Else have I thought about I cant even cry I died last year I told you I had but I didnt know then what I meant I didnt know what I was saying Some days in late August at home are like this, the air thin and eager like this, with something in it sad and nostalgic and familiar. Man the sum of his climatic experiences Father said. Man the sum of what have you. A problem in impure properties carried tediously to an unvarying nil: stalemate of dust and desire. But now I know I’m dead I tell you
paragraphs.zh: 关于那个从街上转身的男孩，我还能想到什么。他头也不回地爬上栅栏，穿过草坪，来到一棵树前，放下杆子，爬上树杈，坐在那里，背对着马路，斑驳的阳光终于一动不动地照在他的白衬衫上。另外我想过我什至不能哭泣我去年死了我告诉过你我死了但我当时不知道我的意思我不知道我在说什么八月下旬在家的日子就是这样，空气像这样稀薄而渴望，里面有一些悲伤、怀旧和熟悉的东西。父亲说，人类是他的气候经历的总和。男人是你所拥有的一切的总和。不纯属性的问题被乏味地带到一成不变的零：尘埃和欲望的僵局。但现在我知道我已经死了我告诉你

paragraphs.en: Then why must you listen we can go away you and Benjy and me where nobody knows us where The buggy was drawn by a white horse, his feet clopping in the thin dust; spidery wheels chattering thin and dry, moving uphill beneath a rippling shawl of leaves. Elm. No: ellum. Ellum.
paragraphs.zh: 那么你为什么一定要听我们可以离开你和班吉和我，没有人知道我们在哪里马车是由一匹白马牵引的，他的脚踩在薄薄的灰尘中；蜘蛛般的轮子细细而干燥地嘎嘎作响，在树叶的涟漪下向山上移动。榆树。不：埃勒姆。埃勒姆。

paragraphs.en: On what on your school money the money they sold the pasture for so you could go to Harvard dont you see you’ve got to finish now if you dont finish he’ll have nothing
paragraphs.zh: 靠你的学费，他们卖掉牧场的钱，这样你就可以去哈佛了，你不知道吗，你现在必须完成学业，如果你不完成，他将一无所有

paragraphs.en: Sold the pasture His white shirt was motionless in the fork, in the flickering shade. The wheels were spidery. Beneath the sag of the buggy the hooves neatly rapid like the motions of a lady doing embroidery, diminishing without progress like a figure on a treadmill being drawn rapidly offstage. The street turned again. I could see the white cupola, the round stupid assertion of the clock. Sold the pasture
paragraphs.zh: 卖掉了牧场他的白衬衫在叉子上一动不动，在闪烁的阴影中。车轮像蜘蛛网一样。马车下垂的马蹄声整齐而快速，就像一位刺绣女士的动作，然后毫无进展地逐渐减弱，就像跑步机上的人物被迅速拉出舞台。街道再次转弯。我可以看到白色的圆顶，圆形愚蠢的时钟断言。卖了牧场

paragraphs.en: Father will be dead in a year they say if he doesnt stop drinking and he wont stop he cant stop since I since last summer and then they’ll send Benjy to Jackson I cant cry I cant even cry one minute she was standing in the door the next minute he was pulling at her dress and bellowing his voice hammered back and forth between the walls in waves and she shrinking against the wall getting smaller and smaller with her white face her eyes like thumbs dug into it until he pushed her out of the room his voice hammering back and forth as though its own momentum would not let it stop as though there were no place for it in silence bellowing
paragraphs.zh: 父亲一年后就会死，他们说如果他不停止喝酒，他不会停止，从去年夏天开始，他就不能停止，然后他们会把班吉送到杰克逊，我不能哭，我什至不能哭，一分钟她站在门口，下一分钟他拉扯她的衣服，咆哮他的声音在墙壁之间来回敲打，她靠在墙上越来越小，她苍白的脸她的眼睛像拇指一样深陷直到他把她推出房间他的声音来来回回地敲击着，仿佛它自身的动力无法让它停下来，仿佛没有地方可以安静地咆哮

paragraphs.en: When you opened the door a bell tinkled, but just once, high and clear and small in the neat obscurity above the door, as though it were gauged and tempered to make that single clear small sound so as not to wear the bell out nor to require the expenditure of too much silence in restoring it when the door opened upon the recent warm scent of baking; a little dirty child with eyes like a toy bear’s and two patent-leather pig-tails.
paragraphs.zh: 当你打开门时，铃铛叮当响了一次，但只有一次，在门上方整洁的朦胧中，它又高又清晰，很小，仿佛它经过测量和调和，发出那单一的清晰的小声音，以免磨损铃铛，也不需要花太多的沉默来恢复它，当门打开时，最近温暖的烘烤气味;一个肮脏的小孩子，眼睛像玩具熊一样，扎着两条漆皮辫子。

paragraphs.en: “Hello, sister.” Her face was like a cup of milk dashed with coffee in the sweet warm emptiness. “Anybody here?”
paragraphs.zh: “姐姐你好。”她的脸就像一杯牛奶，在甜蜜温暖的空虚中撒上咖啡。“有人吗？”

paragraphs.en: But she merely watched me until a door opened and the lady came. Above the counter where the ranks of crisp shapes behind the glass her neat grey face her hair tight and sparse from her neat grey skull, spectacles in neat grey rims riding approaching like something on a wire, like a cash box in a store. She looked like a librarian. Something among dusty shelves of ordered certitudes long divorced from reality, desiccating peacefully, as if a breath of that air which sees injustice done
paragraphs.zh: 但她只是看着我，直到门打开，那位女士进来了。柜台上方，玻璃后面一排清晰的形状，她整洁的灰色脸庞，头发紧绷，稀疏，整洁的灰色头骨，戴着整齐的灰色边框的眼镜像电线上的东西一样靠近，就像商店里的钱箱。她看起来像个图书管理员。布满灰尘的架子上摆放着早已脱离现实的有序确信，静静地干燥，仿佛呼吸着看到不公正的空气

paragraphs.en: “Two of these, please, ma’am.”
paragraphs.zh: “女士，请来两份。”

paragraphs.en: From under the counter she produced a square cut from a newspaper and laid it on the counter and lifted the two buns out. The little girl watched them with still and unwinking eyes like two currants floating motionless in a cup of weak coffee Land of the kike home of the wop. Watching the bread, the neat grey hands, a broad gold band on the left forefinger, knuckled there by a blue knuckle.
paragraphs.zh: 她从柜台下面拿出一张报纸剪下的正方形放在柜台上，然后把两个小面包拿出来。小女孩一动不动地看着他们，眼睛一眨不眨，就像两颗葡萄干一动不动地漂浮在一杯淡咖啡里，这就是沃普族家乡的咖啡。看着面包，那双干净的灰色双手，左手食指上戴着一条宽阔的金戒指，指节上有一个蓝色的指节。

paragraphs.en: “Do you do your own baking, ma’am?”
paragraphs.zh: “女士，你自己烘焙吗？”

paragraphs.en: “Sir?” she said. Like that. Sir? Like on the stage. Sir? “Five cents. Was there anything else?”
paragraphs.zh: “先生？”她说。就这样。先生？就像在舞台上一样。先生？“五美分。还有别的吗？”

paragraphs.en: “No, ma’am. Not for me. This lady wants something.” She was not tall enough to see over the case, so she went to the end of the counter and looked at the little girl.
paragraphs.zh: “不，女士。不适合我。这位女士想要一些东西。”她个子不够高，看不清箱子，所以她走到柜台尽头，看着小女孩。

paragraphs.en: “Did you bring her in here?”
paragraphs.zh: “你带她来这里的？”

paragraphs.en: “No, ma’am. She was here when I came.”
paragraphs.zh: “不，女士。我来的时候她就在这里。”

paragraphs.en: “You little wretch,” she said. She came out around the counter, but she didnt touch the little girl. “Have you got anything in your pockets?”
paragraphs.zh: “你这个小坏蛋，”她说。她绕过柜台走了出来，但没有碰那个小女孩。“你口袋里有东西吗？”

paragraphs.en: “She hasnt got any pockets,” I said. “She wasnt doing anything. She was just standing here, waiting for you.”
paragraphs.zh: “她没有口袋，”我说。“她什么也没做，只是站在这里等你。”

paragraphs.en: “Why didnt the bell ring, then?” She glared at me. She just needed a bunch of switches, a blackboard behind her 2 X 2 e 5. “She’ll hide it under her dress and a body’d never know it. You, child. How’d you get in here?”
paragraphs.zh: “那为什么门铃没有响呢？”她瞪着我。她只需要一堆开关，2 X 2 e 5 后面的一块黑板。“她会把它藏在衣服下面，而别人永远不会知道。你，孩子。你怎么进来的？”

paragraphs.en: The little girl said nothing. She looked at the woman, then she gave me a flying black glance and looked at the woman again, “Them foreigners,” the woman said. “How’d she get in without the bell ringing?”
paragraphs.zh: 小女孩什么也没说。她看了看那个女人，然后用黑色的眼神扫了我一眼，又看了看那个女人，“他们是外国人，”那个女人说。“门铃没有响，她是怎么进来的？”

paragraphs.en: “She came in when I opened the door,” I said. “It rang once for both of us. She couldnt reach anything from here, anyway. Besides, I dont think she would. Would you, sister?” The little girl looked at me, secretive, contemplative. “What do you want? bread?”
paragraphs.zh: “我一开门她就进来了。”我说。“我们俩都响过一次。无论如何，她从这里拿不到任何东西。此外，我认为她不会。你会吗，姐姐？”小女孩看着我，神情神秘，若有所思。“你想要什么？面包？”

paragraphs.en: She extended her fist. It uncurled upon a nickel, moist and dirty, moist dirt ridged into her flesh. The coin was damp and warm. I could smell it, faintly metallic.
paragraphs.zh: 她伸出了拳头。它展开在一块镍币上，潮湿而肮脏，潮湿的污垢深入她的肉里。硬币又湿又热。我闻到了一股淡淡的金属味。

paragraphs.en: “Have you got a five cent loaf, please, ma’am?”
paragraphs.zh: “女士，请问您有五美分的面包吗？”

paragraphs.en: From beneath the counter she produced a square cut from a newspaper sheet and laid it on the counter and wrapped a loaf into it. I laid the coin and another one on the counter. “And another one of those buns, please, ma’am.”
paragraphs.zh: 她从柜台下面拿出一张报纸，剪下一个正方形，放在柜台上，然后包了一条面包。我把硬币和另一枚放在柜台上。“女士，请再来一个面包。”

paragraphs.en: She took another bun from the case. “Give me that parcel,” she said. I gave it to her and she unwrapped it and put the third bun in and wrapped it and took up the coins and found two coppers in her apron and gave them to me. I handed them to the little girl. Her fingers closed about them, damp and hot, like worms.
paragraphs.zh: 她从箱子里又拿了一个小圆面包。“把那个包裹给我，”她说。我把它给了她，她打开它，把第三个面包放进去，包起来，拿起硬币，在她的围裙里发现了两个铜板，然后把它们给了我。我把它们递给了小女孩。她的手指紧紧握住它们，又湿又热，就像蠕虫一样。

paragraphs.en: “You going to give her that bun?” the woman said.
paragraphs.zh: “你要把那个面包给她吗？”女人说道。

paragraphs.en: “Yessum,” I said. “I expect your cooking smells as good to her as it does to me.”
paragraphs.zh: “是的，”我说。“我希望你做的饭菜对她来说和我一样好闻。”

paragraphs.en: I took up the two packages and gave the bread to the little girl, the woman all iron-grey behind the counter, watching us with cold certitude. “You wait a minute,” she said. She went to the rear. The door opened again and closed. The little girl watched me, holding the bread against her dirty dress.
paragraphs.zh: 我拿起两个包裹，把面包递给小女孩，柜台后面的那个女人全身都是铁灰色的，冷漠而笃定地看着我们。“你等一下，”她说。她走到后面。门再次打开又关上。小女孩看着我，把面包放在她脏衣服上。

paragraphs.en: “What’s your name?” I said. She quit looking at me, but she was still motionless. She didnt even seem to breathe. The woman returned. She had a funny looking thing in her hand. She carried it sort of like it might have been a dead pet rat.
paragraphs.zh: “你叫什么名字？”我说。她不再看我，但仍然一动不动。她看起来甚至没有呼吸。女人回来了。她手里拿着一个看起来很滑稽的东西。她拿着它，就像拿着一只死去的宠物老鼠一样。

paragraphs.en: “Here,” she said. The child looked at her. “Take it,” the woman said, jabbing it at the little girl. “It just looks peculiar. I calculate you wont know the difference when you eat it. Here. I cant stand here all day.” The child took it, still watching her. The woman rubbed her hands on her apron. “I got to have that bell fixed,” she said. She went to the door and jerked it open. The little bell tinkled once, faint and clear and invisible. We moved toward the door and the woman’s peering back.
paragraphs.zh: “在这里，”她说。孩子看着她。“拿走它，”女人说着，把它戳向小女孩。“它看起来很奇怪。我估计你吃的时候不会知道有什么不同。这里。我不能整天站在这里。”孩子接过它，仍然看着她。女人把手放在围裙上搓着。“我必须把那个铃修好，”她说。她走到门口，猛地把门打开。小铃铛叮叮当当地响了一声，微弱而清晰，看不见。我们朝门口走去，那个女人回头望着我们。

paragraphs.en: “Thank you for the cake,” I said.
paragraphs.zh: “谢谢你的蛋糕，”我说。

paragraphs.en: “Them foreigners,” she said, staring up into the obscurity where the bell tinkled. “Take my advice and stay clear of them, young man.”
paragraphs.zh: “他们是外国人，”她说，抬头凝视着钟声叮当作响的黑暗。“听我的建议，远离他们，年轻人。”

paragraphs.en: “Yessum,” I said. “Come on, sister.” We went out. “Thank you, ma’am.”
paragraphs.zh: “是的，”我说。“来吧，姐姐。”我们出去了。“谢谢您，女士。”

paragraphs.en: She swung the door to, then jerked it open again, making the bell give forth its single small note. “Foreigners,” she said, peering up at the bell.
paragraphs.zh: 她把门打开，然后又猛地打开，门铃发出了小小的声音。“外国人，”她抬头看着门铃说道。

paragraphs.en: We went on. “Well,” I said, “How about some ice cream?” She was eating the gnarled cake. “Do you like ice cream?” She gave me a black still look, chewing. “Come on.”
paragraphs.zh: 我们继续前行。“好吧，”我说，“来点冰淇淋怎么样？”她正在吃那块粗糙的蛋糕。“你喜欢吃冰淇淋吗？”她一动不动地用黑色的眼神看着我，咀嚼着。“快点。”

paragraphs.en: We came to the drugstore and had some ice cream. She wouldn’t put the loaf down. “Why not put it down so you can eat better?” I said, offering to take it. But she held to it, chewing the ice cream like it was taffy. The bitten cake lay on the table. She ate the ice cream steadily, then she fell to on the cake again, looking about at the showcases. I finished mine and we went out.
paragraphs.zh: 我们来到药店买了一些冰淇淋。她不肯放下面包。“为什么不把它放下，这样你就能吃得更好呢？”我说着，主动提出要拿走。但她坚持了下来，像嚼太妃糖一样咀嚼着冰淇淋。被咬过的蛋糕放在桌子上。她稳稳地吃完冰淇淋，然后又倒在蛋糕上，环顾四周的陈列柜。我完成了我的任务，然后我们就出去了。

paragraphs.en: “Which way do you live?” I said.
paragraphs.zh: “你住哪边？”我说。

paragraphs.en: A buggy, the one with the white horse it was. Only Doc Peabody is fat. Three hundred pounds. You ride with him on the uphill side, holding on. Children. Walking easier than holding uphill. Seen the doctor yet have you seen Caddy
paragraphs.zh: 一辆马车，就是那辆白马车。只有皮博迪博士是胖子。三百磅。你和他一起骑上坡，坚持住。孩子们。步行比扶着上坡更容易。看过医生了吗，你见过凯蒂吗

paragraphs.en: I dont have to I cant ask now afterward it will be all right it wont matter
paragraphs.zh: 我不需要我现在不能问以后就没事了没关系

paragraphs.en: Because women so delicate so mysterious Father said. Delicate equilibrium of periodical filth between two moons balanced. Moons he said full and yellow as harvest moons her hips thighs. Outside outside of them always but. Yellow. Feet soles with walking like. Then know that some man that all those mysterious and imperious concealed. With all that inside of them shapes an outward suavity waiting for a touch to. Liquid putrefaction like drowned things floating like pale rubber flabbily filled getting the odour of honeysuckle all mixed up.
paragraphs.zh: 父亲说，因为女人那么精致所以神秘。两个卫星之间周期性污物的微妙平衡。他说月亮又圆又黄，就像丰收的月亮落在她的臀部和大腿上一样。在他们之外总是但是。黄色的。脚底跟走路一样。后来才知道，有一个人，把所有那些神秘和专横都隐藏起来了。他们的内在塑造了一种外在的温柔，等待着触摸。腐烂的液体像被淹死的东西一样漂浮着，像苍白的橡胶一样松软地充满了金银花的气味。

paragraphs.en: “You’d better take your bread on home, hadnt you?”
paragraphs.zh: “你最好把面包带回家，不是吗？”

paragraphs.en: She looked at me. She chewed quietly and steadily; at regular intervals a small distension passed smoothly down her throat. I opened my package and gave her one of the buns. “Goodbye,” I said.
paragraphs.zh: 她看着我。她安静而稳定地咀嚼着。每隔一段时间，就会有一阵轻微的胀痛顺利地流过她的喉咙。我打开包裹，给了她一个面包。“再见，”我说。

paragraphs.en: I went on. Then I looked back. She was behind me. “Do you live down this way?” She said nothing. She walked beside me, under my elbow sort of, eating. We went on. It was quiet, hardly anyone about getting the odour of honeysuckle all mixed She would have told me not to let me sit there on the steps hearing her door twilight slamming hearing Benjy still crying Supper she would have to come down then getting honeysuckle all mixed up in it We reached the corner.
paragraphs.zh: 我继续说下去。然后我回头看了看。她在我身后。“你住这边吗？”她什么也没说。她走在我旁边，在我的胳膊肘下吃东西。我们继续前行。很安静，几乎没有人担心金银花的气味混合在一起。她会告诉我不要让我坐在台阶上，听到她的门关上的声音，听到班吉还在哭。晚饭，她必须下来，然后把金银花的气味混合在里面。我们到达了角落。

paragraphs.en: “Well, I’ve got to go down this way,” I said, “Goodbye.” She stopped too. She swallowed the last of the cake, then she began on the bun, watching me across it. “Goodbye,” I said. I turned into the street and went on, but I went to the next corner before I stopped.
paragraphs.zh: “好吧，我得走这条路了，”我说，“再见。”她也停了下来。她吞下了最后一块蛋糕，然后开始吃面包，看着我越过它。“再见，”我说。我拐进街道继续前行，但走到下一个街角才停下来。

paragraphs.en: “Which way do you live?” I said. “This way?” I pointed down the street. She just looked at me. “Do you live over that way? I bet you live close to the station, where the trains are. Dont you?” She just looked at me, serene and secret and chewing. The street was empty both ways, with quiet lawns and houses neat among the trees, but no one at all except back there. We turned and went back. Two men sat in chairs in front of a store.
paragraphs.zh: “你住哪边？”我说。“这边走？”我指着街道。她只是看着我。“你住在那边吗？我打赌你住的地方离火车站很近，那里有火车。不是吗？”她只是看着我，平静而神秘，咀嚼着。街道两边空无一人，有安静的草坪和整齐的房屋掩映在树林中，但除了后面什么人也没有。我们转身回去了。两个男人坐在一家商店前的椅子上。

paragraphs.en: “Do you all know this little girl? She sort of took up with me and I cant find where she lives.”
paragraphs.zh: “你们都认识这个小女孩吗？她有点喜欢我了，但我找不到她住在哪里。”

paragraphs.en: They quit looking at me and looked at her.
paragraphs.zh: 他们不再看我，而是看着她。

paragraphs.en: “Must be one of them new Italian families,” one said. He wore a rusty frock coat. “I’ve seen her before. What’s your name, little girl?” She looked at them blackly for awhile, her jaws moving steadily. She swallowed without ceasing to chew.
paragraphs.zh: “一定是新的意大利家庭之一，”其中一位说道。他穿着一件生锈的礼服大衣。“我以前见过她。小女孩，你叫什么名字？”她阴沉地看着他们一会儿，下巴不停地动着。她吞咽下去，没有停止咀嚼。

paragraphs.en: “Maybe she cant speak English,” the other said.
paragraphs.zh: “也许她不会说英语，”另一个说。

paragraphs.en: “They sent her after bread,” I said. “She must be able to speak something.”
paragraphs.zh: “他们派她去找面包，”我说。“她一定能说点什么。”

paragraphs.en: “What’s your pa’s name?” the first said. “Pete? Joe? name John huh?” She took another bite from the bun.
paragraphs.zh: “你爸爸叫什么名字？”第一个说。“皮特？乔？叫约翰吧？”她又咬了一口面包。

paragraphs.en: “What must I do with her?” I said. “She just follows me. I’ve got to get back to Boston.”
paragraphs.zh: “我该对她做什么？”我说。“她只是跟着我。我得回波士顿了。”

paragraphs.en: “You from the college?”
paragraphs.zh: “你是学院的？”

paragraphs.en: “Yes, sir. And I’ve got to get on back.”
paragraphs.zh: “是的，先生。我得回去了。”

paragraphs.en: “You might go up the street and turn her over to Anse. He’ll be up at the livery stable. The marshall.”
paragraphs.zh: “你可以到街上把她交给安斯。他会在马歇尔那里。警察。”

paragraphs.en: “I reckon that’s what I’ll have to do,” I said. “I’ve got to do something with her. Much obliged. Come on, sister.”
paragraphs.zh: “我想这就是我必须做的，”我说。“我得帮她做点什么。非常感谢。来吧，姐姐。”

paragraphs.en: We went up the street, on the shady side, where the shadow of the broken façade blotted slowly across the road. We came to the livery stable. The marshall wasnt there. A man sitting in a chair tilted in the broad low door, where a dark cool breeze smelling of ammonia blew among the ranked stalls, said to look at the postoffice. He didn’t know her either.
paragraphs.zh: 我们沿着街道走去，在阴凉的一侧，破碎的外墙的影子慢慢地穿过马路。我们来到了马厩。元帅不在场。一个男人斜坐在宽阔低矮的门前的椅子上，一股阴冷的微风吹过排列整齐的摊位，散发着氨味，据说是在看邮局。他也不认识她。

paragraphs.en: “Them furriners. I cant tell one from another. You might take her across the tracks where they live, and maybe somebody’ll claim her.”
paragraphs.zh: “他们是毛皮商。我分不清其中一个。你可以带她穿过他们住的铁轨，也许有人会认领她。”

paragraphs.en: We went to the postoffice. It was back down the street. The man in the frock coat was opening a newspaper.
paragraphs.zh: 我们去了邮局。又回到了街上。穿礼服的男人正在打开一份报纸。

paragraphs.en: “Anse just drove out of town,” he said. “I guess you’d better go down past the station and walk past them houses by the river. Somebody there’ll know her.”
paragraphs.zh: “安斯刚刚开车出城，”他说。“我想你最好经过车站，走过河边的房子。那里会有人认识她的。”

paragraphs.en: “I guess I’ll have to,” I said. “Come on, sister.” She pushed the last piece of the bun into her mouth and swallowed it. “Want another?” I said. She looked at me, chewing, her eyes black and unwinking and friendly. I took the other two buns out and gave her one and bit into the other. I asked a man where the station was and he showed me. “Come on, sister.”
paragraphs.zh: “我想我必须这样做，”我说。“来吧，姐姐。”她把最后一块包子塞进嘴里，咽了下去。“还想要另一个吗？”我说。她看着我，咀嚼着，她的眼睛是黑色的，一眨不眨，友善。我把另外两个馒头拿出来，给了她一个，又咬了另一个。我问一个人车站在哪里，他给我看了。“来吧，姐姐。”

paragraphs.en: We reached the station and crossed the tracks, where the river was. A bridge crossed it, and a street of jumbled frame houses followed the river, backed onto it. A shabby street, but with an air heterogeneous and vivid too. In the center of an untrimmed plot enclosed by a fence of gaping and broken pickets stood an ancient lopsided surrey and a weathered house from an upper window of which hung a garment of vivid pink.
paragraphs.zh: 我们到达车站，穿过铁轨，河就在那里。一座桥横跨河面，一条由杂乱的木屋组成的街道顺着河流而行，背靠河面。一条破旧的街道，但空气却异样而生动。在一块未经修剪的土地中央，矗立着一座古老的倾斜的萨里和一座饱经风霜的房子，房子的上层窗户挂着一件鲜艳的粉红色衣服。

paragraphs.en: “Does that look like your house?” I said. She looked at me over the bun. “This one?” I said, pointing. She just chewed, but it seemed to me that I discerned something affirmative, acquiescent even if it wasn’t eager, in her air. “This one?” I said. “Come on, then.” I entered the broken gate. I looked back at her. “Here?” I said. “This look like your house?”
paragraphs.zh: “那看起来像你家吗？”我说。她越过发髻看着我。“这个？”我指着说。她只是咀嚼着，但在我看来，我在她的神态中察觉到了某种肯定的、默许的东西，即使它并不急切。“这个？”我说。“那就来吧。”我进入了破损的大门。我回头看着她。“这里？”我说。“这看起来像你家吗？”

paragraphs.en: She nodded her head rapidly, looking at me, gnawing into the damp halfmoon of the bread. We went on. A walk of broken random flags, speared by fresh coarse blades of grass, led to the broken stoop. There was no movement about the house at all, and the pink garment hanging in no wind from the upper window. There was a bell pull with a porcelain knob, attached to about six feet of wire when I stopped pulling and knocked. The little girl had the crust edgeways in her chewing mouth.
paragraphs.zh: 她迅速地点点头，看着我，啃着潮湿的半月形面包。我们继续前行。一条断断续续的小路，被新鲜的粗糙草叶刺穿，通向破碎的门廊。房子里一点动静都没有，粉红色的衣服无风地从楼上的窗户垂下来。当我停止拉动并敲击时，有一个带有瓷旋钮的铃拉，连接到大约六英尺长的电线上。小女孩嘴里嚼着面包皮。

paragraphs.en: A woman opened the door. She looked at me, then she spoke rapidly to the little girl in Italian, with a rising inflexion, then a pause, interrogatory. She spoke to her again, the little girl looking at her across the end of the crust, pushing it into her mouth with a dirty hand.
paragraphs.zh: 一个女人打开了门。她看着我，然后用意大利语快速地对小女孩说话，语调逐渐升高，然后停顿了一下，带着询问的意思。她又对她说话了，小女孩隔着面包皮的一端看着她，用脏手把它塞进嘴里。

paragraphs.en: “She says she lives here,” I said. “I met her down town. Is this your bread?”
paragraphs.zh: “她说她住在这里，”我说。“我在城里遇见了她。这是你的面包吗？”

paragraphs.en: “No spika,” the woman said. She spoke to the little girl again. The little girl just looked at her.
paragraphs.zh: “没有斯皮卡，”女人说。她又对小女孩说话了。小女孩只是看着她。

paragraphs.en: “No live here?” I said. I pointed to the girl, then at her, then at the door. The woman shook her head. She spoke rapidly. She came to the edge of the porch and pointed down the road, speaking.
paragraphs.zh: “不住在这里吗？”我说。我指着那个女孩，然后指着她，然后指着门口。女人摇摇头。她语速很快。她来到门廊边，指着路边说话。

paragraphs.en: I nodded violently too. “You come show?” I said. I took her arm, waving my other hand toward the road. She spoke swiftly, pointing. “You come show,” I said, trying to lead her down the steps.
paragraphs.zh: 我也用力点头。“你来表演吗？”我说。我握住她的手臂，另一只手朝路挥动。她指着方向，语速很快。“你来吧，”我说，试图带她走下台阶。

paragraphs.en: “Si, si,” she said, holding back, showing me whatever it was. I nodded again.
paragraphs.zh: “Si，si，”她忍住说，给我看那是什么。我又点了点头。

paragraphs.en: “Thanks. Thanks. Thanks.” I went down the steps and walked toward the gate, not running, but pretty fast. I reached the gate and stopped and looked at her for a while. The crust was gone now, and she looked at me with her black, friendly stare. The woman stood on the stoop, watching us.
paragraphs.zh: “谢谢。谢谢。谢谢。”我走下台阶，朝大门走去，没有跑，但速度很快。我走到门口，停下来看了她一会儿。现在硬皮已经消失了，她用黑色、友好的目光看着我。那女人站在门廊上，看着我们。

paragraphs.en: “Come on, then,” I said. “We’ll have to find the right one sooner or later.”
paragraphs.zh: “那么，来吧，”我说。“我们迟早要找到合适的人。”

paragraphs.en: She moved along just under my elbow. We went on. The houses all seemed empty. Not a soul in sight. A sort of breathlessness that empty houses have. Yet they couldnt all be empty. All the different rooms, if you could just slice the walls away all of a sudden Madam, your daughter, if you please. No. Madam, for God’s sake, your daughter. She moved along just under my elbow, her shiny tight pigtails, and then the last house played out and the road curved out of sight beyond a wall, following the river. The woman was emerging from the broken gate, with a shawl over her head and clutched under her chin. The road curved on, empty. I found a coin and gave it to the little girl. A quarter. “Goodbye, sister,” I said. Then I ran.
paragraphs.zh: 她在我的肘下移动。我们继续前行。所有的房子看起来都是空的。看不见一个灵魂。一种空荡荡的房子里有的喘不过气来的感觉。但它们不可能都是空的。所有不同的房间，如果你能突然把墙壁切掉的话，女士，你的女儿，如果你愿意的话。不，女士，看在上帝的份上，你的女儿。她在我的胳膊肘下向前走着，辫子闪闪发亮，最后一座房子消失了，道路沿着河流蜿蜒在墙外，看不见了。那个女人正从破损的大门中走出来，头上盖着一条围巾，下巴夹在下面。道路蜿蜒前行，空无一人。我找到了一枚硬币，交给了小女孩。四分之一。“再见，姐姐，”我说。然后我就跑了。

paragraphs.en: I ran fast, not looking back. Just before the road curved away I looked back. She stood in the road, a small figure clasping the loaf of bread to her filthy little dress, her eyes still and black and unwinking. I ran on.
paragraphs.zh: 我跑得很快，没有回头。就在道路拐弯之前，我回头看了一眼。她站在路上，身材娇小，把面包紧紧地抱在肮脏的小裙子上，眼睛一动不动，黑色的，一眨不眨。我继续跑。

paragraphs.en: A lane turned from the road. I entered it and after a while I slowed to a fast walk. The lane went between back premises—unpainted houses with more of those gay and startling coloured garments on lines, a barn broken-backed, decaying quietly among rank orchard trees, unpruned and weed-choked, pink and white and murmurous with sunlight and with bees. I looked back. The entrance to the lane was empty. I slowed still more, my shadow pacing me, dragging its head through the weeds that hid the fence.
paragraphs.zh: 一条小巷从马路拐过来。我走进去，过了一会儿，我放慢了脚步，加快了脚步。这条小巷穿过后面的房屋——未粉刷的房屋，上面挂着更多色彩鲜艳、颜色鲜艳的衣服，还有一座破烂的谷仓，在茂盛的果园树丛中静静地腐烂，没有修剪，杂草丛生，粉红色和白色，在阳光和蜜蜂的低语中。我回头看了一眼。小巷的入口空无一人。我放慢了速度，我的影子在我身边踱步，拖着头穿过隐藏栅栏的杂草。

paragraphs.en: The lane went back to a barred gate, became defunctive in grass, a mere path scarred quietly into new grass. I climbed the gate into a woodlot and crossed it and came to another wall and followed that one, my shadow behind me now. There were vines and creepers where at home would be honeysuckle. Coming and coming especially in the dusk when it rained, getting honeysuckle all mixed up in it as though it were not enough without that, not unbearable enough. What did you let him for kiss kiss
paragraphs.zh: 这条小路又回到一扇上了铁栅栏的大门，在草丛中变得毫无生气，一条小路悄悄地长成了新的草丛。我爬上大门，进入一片林地，穿过它，来到另一堵墙边，沿着那堵墙走，我的影子现在在我身后。家里种的是金银花，但那里却长满了藤蔓和爬山虎。来来往往，尤其是黄昏下雨的时候，金银花都混在里面，好像没有它还不够，还不够难以忍受。你让他吻什么

paragraphs.en: I didn’t let him I made him watching me getting mad What do you think of that? Red print of my hand coming up through her face like turning a light on under your hand her eyes going bright
paragraphs.zh: 我没有让他看到我生气，你觉得怎么样？我手上的红色印记从她脸上浮现出来，就像在你手下打开一盏灯，她的眼睛变得明亮

paragraphs.en: It’s not for kissing I slapped you. Girl’s elbows at fifteen Father said you swallow like you had a fishbone in your throat what’s the matter with you and Caddy across the table not to look at me. It’s for letting it be some darn town squirt I slapped you you will will you now I guess you say calf rope. My red hand coming up out of her face. What do you think of that scouring her head into the. Grass sticks crisscrossed into the flesh tingling scouring her head. Say calf rope say it
paragraphs.zh: 我不是为了接吻才打你的。女孩十五岁的肘部父亲说你吞口水就像喉咙里有鱼刺一样你和凯蒂在桌子对面不看我是怎么回事。这是为了让它成为一些该死的城镇喷子，我打了你一巴掌，你会的，现在我猜你说的是小牛绳。我的红手从她脸上伸出来。你对她的头脑里的这种冲劲有什么看法？草枝纵横交错地扎进肉里，刺痛着她的头。说小牛绳说吧

paragraphs.en: I didnt kiss a dirty girl like Natalie anyway The wall went into shadow, and then my shadow, I had tricked it again. I had forgot about the river curving along the road. I climbed the wall. And then she watched me jump down, holding the loaf against her dress.
paragraphs.zh: 无论如何，我没有亲吻像娜塔莉这样肮脏的女孩。墙壁进入了阴影，然后我的影子，我又欺骗了它。我忘记了河水沿着路蜿蜒而过。我爬上了墙。然后她看着我跳下来，把面包靠在她的衣服上。

paragraphs.en: I stood in the weeds and we looked at one another for a while.
paragraphs.zh: 我站在杂草丛中，我们互相看了一会儿。

paragraphs.en: “Why didnt you tell me you lived out this way, sister?” The loaf was wearing slowly out of the paper; already it needed a new one. “Well, come on then and show me the house.” not a dirty girl like Natalie. It was raining we could hear it on the roof, sighing through the high sweet emptiness of the barn.
paragraphs.zh: “姐姐，你为什么不告诉我你是这样生活的？”面包慢慢地从纸上磨损了；它已经需要一个新的了。“好吧，那就带我看看房子吧。”不是像娜塔莉那样肮脏的女孩。正在下雨，我们可以听到屋顶上的雨声，透过谷仓高高甜美的空旷感叹息。

paragraphs.en: There? touching her
paragraphs.zh: 在那里？抚摸她

paragraphs.en: Not there
paragraphs.zh: 不在那里

paragraphs.en: There? not raining hard but we couldnt hear anything but the roof and as if it was my blood or her blood
paragraphs.zh: 在那里？雨不大，但我们除了屋顶之外什么也听不到，就好像那是我的血或她的血

paragraphs.en: She pushed me down the ladder and ran off and left me Caddy did
paragraphs.zh: 她把我推下梯子然后跑掉了，留下了我，凯蒂就是这么做的

paragraphs.en: Was it there it hurt you when Caddy did ran off was it there
paragraphs.zh: 当凯蒂逃跑时，它伤害了你吗？

paragraphs.en: Oh She walked just under my elbow, the top of her patent leather head, the loaf fraying out of the newspaper.
paragraphs.zh: 哦，她走在我的肘下，她的漆皮头顶上，面包从报纸上磨损了。

paragraphs.en: “If you dont get home pretty soon you’re going to wear that loaf out. And then what’ll your mamma say?” I bet I can lift you up
paragraphs.zh: “如果你不尽快回家，那条面包就会被磨坏。然后你妈妈会说什么？”我打赌我可以举起你

paragraphs.en: You cant I’m too heavy
paragraphs.zh: 你不能我太重了

paragraphs.en: Did Caddy go away did she go to the house you cant see the barn from our house did you ever try to see the barn from
paragraphs.zh: 凯蒂走了吗？她去了那所房子吗？从我们家看不到谷仓，你有没有尝试过从我们家看到谷仓？

paragraphs.en: It was her fault she pushed me she ran away
paragraphs.zh: 都是她的错她推了我她跑了

paragraphs.en: I can lift you up see how I can
paragraphs.zh: 我可以举起你看看我能怎样

paragraphs.en: Oh her blood or my blood Oh We went on in the thin dust, our feet silent as rubber in the thin dust where pencils of sun slanted in the trees. And I could feel water again running swift and peaceful in the secret shade.
paragraphs.zh: 哦，她的血还是我的血哦，我们在薄薄的尘土中前行，我们的双脚在薄薄的尘土中像橡胶一样安静，阳光斜照在树林里。我能再次感觉到水在秘密的树荫下快速而平静地流淌。

paragraphs.en: “You live a long way, dont you. You’re mighty smart to go this far to town by yourself.” It’s like dancing sitting down did you ever dance sitting down? We could hear the rain, a rat in the crib, the empty barn vacant with horses. How do you hold to dance do you hold like this
paragraphs.zh: “你住的路很远，不是吗？你一个人跑这么远进城，真是太聪明了。”就像坐着跳舞你曾经坐着跳舞吗？我们可以听到雨声、婴儿床里的老鼠声、空荡荡的谷仓里空荡荡的马匹的声音。你如何保持跳舞你这样保持吗

paragraphs.zh: 我曾经这样抱着你以为我不够坚强是不是

paragraphs.zh: 哦哦哦哦

paragraphs.zh: 我坚持这样使用我的意思是你听到我说的话了吗？
