paragraphs.zh: 哦哦哦哦哦

paragraphs.en: The road went on, still and empty, the sun slanting more and more. Her stiff little pigtails were bound at the tips with bits of crimson cloth. A corner of the wrapping flapped a little as she walked, the nose of the loaf naked. I stopped.
paragraphs.zh: 路继续前行，寂静而空旷，阳光越来越斜。她那僵硬的小辫子末端用深红色的布片绑着。她走路时，包装纸的一角轻轻拍动，面包的鼻子裸露在外。我停了下来。

paragraphs.en: “Look here. Do you live down this road? We havent passed a house in a mile, almost.”
paragraphs.zh: “看这里。你住在这条路上吗？我们几乎一英里内都没有经过一栋房子。”

paragraphs.en: She looked at me, black and secret and friendly.
paragraphs.zh: 她看着我，肤色黝黑，神秘而友善。

paragraphs.en: “Where do you live, sister? Dont you live back there in town?”
paragraphs.zh: “姐姐，你住在哪里？你不住在城里吗？”

paragraphs.en: There was a bird somewhere in the woods, beyond the broken and infrequent slanting of sunlight.
paragraphs.zh: 在树林里的某个地方，在破碎的、罕见的斜射阳光之外，有一只鸟。

paragraphs.en: “Your papa’s going to be worried about you. Dont you reckon you’ll get a whipping for not coming straight home with that bread?”
paragraphs.zh: “你爸爸会担心你的。你不觉得你会因为不带面包直接回家而受到鞭打吗？”

paragraphs.en: The bird whistled again, invisible, a sound meaningless and profound, inflexionless, ceasing as though cut off with the blow of a knife, and again, and that sense of water swift and peaceful above secret places, felt, not seen not heard.
paragraphs.zh: 那只鸟又吹了一声口哨，看不见，毫无意义，深沉，没有屈折，仿佛被刀子一击切断了，然后又吹了一声，那种水流在秘密地方上空湍急而平静的感觉，感觉起来，看不见，听不见。

paragraphs.en: “Oh, hell, sister.” About half the paper hung limp. “That’s not doing any good now.” I tore it off and dropped it beside the road. “Come on. We’ll have to go back to town. We’ll go back along the river.”
paragraphs.zh: “哦，见鬼，姐姐。”大约一半的纸松软地挂着。“现在这样做没有任何好处。”我把它撕下来扔在路边。“走吧。我们得回城里了。我们沿着河回去。”

paragraphs.en: We left the road. Among the moss little pale flowers grew, and the sense of water mute and unseen. I hold to use like this I mean I use to hold She stood in the door looking at us her hands on her hips
paragraphs.zh: 我们离开了路。苔藓中长出了一些淡色的小花，水的感觉是静悄悄的、看不见的。我握住这样使用我的意思是我曾经握住她站在门口看着我们她双手放在臀部

paragraphs.en: You pushed me it was your fault it hurt me too
paragraphs.zh: 你推了我，是你的错，也伤害了我

paragraphs.en: We were dancing sitting down I bet Caddy cant dance sitting down
paragraphs.zh: 我们坐着跳舞我打赌凯蒂不能坐着跳舞

paragraphs.en: Stop that stop that
paragraphs.zh: 停止那个停止那个

paragraphs.en: I was just brushing the trash off the back of your dress
paragraphs.zh: 我只是把你衣服后面的垃圾掸掉

paragraphs.en: You keep your nasty old hands off of me it was your fault you pushed me down I’m mad at you
paragraphs.zh: 你别再碰我了，是你的错，你把我推倒了，我生你的气

paragraphs.en: I dont care she looked at us stay mad she went away We began to hear the shouts, the splashings; I saw a brown body gleam for an instant.
paragraphs.zh: 我不在乎她看着我们保持生气她走了我们开始听到喊叫声，溅水声；我看到棕色的身体瞬间闪闪发光。

paragraphs.en: Stay mad. My shirt was getting wet and my hair. Across the roof hearing the roof loud now I could see Natalie going through the garden among the rain. Get wet I hope you catch pneumonia go on home Cowface. I jumped hard as I could into the hogwallow the mud yellowed up to my waist stinking I kept on plunging until I fell down and rolled over in it “Hear them in swimming, sister? I wouldn’t mind doing that myself.” If I had time. When I have time. I could hear my watch. mud was warmer than the rain it smelled awful. She had her back turned I went around in front of her. You know what I was doing? She turned her back I went around in front of her the rain creeping into the mud flatting her bodice through her dress it smelled horrible. I was hugging her that’s what I was doing. She turned her back I went around in front of her. I was hugging her I tell you.
paragraphs.zh: 保持生气。我的衬衫和头发都湿了。穿过屋顶，听到屋顶的声音，现在我可以看到娜塔莉在雨中穿过花园。淋湿了，我希望你得了肺炎，回家去吧。我用尽全身力气跳进了泥坑，泥浆已经泛黄到了我的腰部，散发着恶臭。我一直往下跳，直到摔倒并在泥坑里打滚。“听到他们游泳了吗，姐姐？我不介意自己这么做。”如果我有时间的话。当我有时间的时候。我能听到我的手表的声音。泥土比雨还热，闻起来很臭。她转过身去，我绕到她前面。你知道我在做什么吗？她转过身来，我在她面前转过身去，雨水渗入泥浆，透过她的裙子，压平了她的紧身胸衣，闻起来很可怕。我拥抱她，这就是我正在做的事情。她转过身去，我绕到她面前。我告诉你，我正在拥抱她。

paragraphs.en: I dont give a damn what you were doing
paragraphs.zh: 我根本不在乎你在做什么

paragraphs.en: You dont you dont I’ll make you I’ll make you give a damn. She hit my hands away I smeared mud on her with the other hand I couldn’t feel the wet smacking of her hand I wiped mud from my legs smeared it on her wet hard turning body hearing her fingers going into my face but I couldn’t feel it even when the rain began to taste sweet on my lips
paragraphs.zh: 你不，你不，我会让你，我会让你该死的。她把我的手打开，我用另一只手在她身上抹上泥土，我感觉不到她手上湿漉漉的拍打声，我擦掉腿上的泥土，把它抹在她湿漉漉、坚硬转动的身体上，听到她的手指伸进我的脸，但即使雨开始在我的嘴唇上尝起来甜甜的，我也感觉不到。

paragraphs.en: They saw us from the water first, heads and shoulders. They yelled and one rose squatting and sprang among them. They looked like beavers, the water lipping about their chins, yelling.
paragraphs.zh: 他们首先从水中看到了我们的头和肩膀。他们大喊大叫，一朵玫瑰蹲下来，跳到他们中间。他们看起来像海狸，水流过他们的下巴，大喊大叫。

paragraphs.en: “Take that girl away! What did you want to bring a girl here for? Go on away!”
paragraphs.zh: “把那个女孩带走！你带一个女孩来这里做什么？走开！”

paragraphs.en: “She wont hurt you. We just want to watch you for a while.”
paragraphs.zh: “她不会伤害你。我们只是想看你一会儿。”

paragraphs.en: They squatted in the water. Their heads drew into a clump, watching us, then they broke and rushed toward us, hurling water with their hands. We moved quick.
paragraphs.zh: 他们蹲在水里。他们的头聚成一团，看着我们，然后突然冲向我们，用手泼水。我们行动得很快。

paragraphs.en: “Look out, boys; she wont hurt you.”
paragraphs.zh: “小心点，孩子们，她不会伤害你们的。”

paragraphs.en: “Go on away, Harvard!” It was the second boy, the one that thought the horse and wagon back there at the bridge. “Splash them, fellows!”
paragraphs.zh: “走吧，哈佛！”这是第二个男孩，那个想到桥上那匹马和马车的人。“泼他们吧，伙计们！”

paragraphs.en: “Let’s get out and throw them in,” another said. “I aint afraid of any girl.”
paragraphs.zh: “我们出去把它们扔进去吧，”另一个人说。“我不怕任何女孩。”

paragraphs.en: “Splash them! Splash them!” They rushed toward us, hurling water. We moved back. “Go on away!” they yelled. “Go on away!”
paragraphs.zh: “泼他们！泼他们！”他们向我们冲来，泼水。我们搬回来了。“走吧！”他们喊道。“走吧！”

paragraphs.en: We went away. They huddled just under the bank, their slick heads in a row against the bright water. We went on. “That’s not for us, is it.” The sun slanted through to the moss here and there, leveller. “Poor kid, you’re just a girl.” Little flowers grew among the moss, littler than I had ever seen. “You’re just a girl. Poor kid.” There was a path, curving along beside the water. Then the water was still again, dark and still and swift. “Nothing but a girl. Poor sister.” We lay in the wet grass panting the rain like cold shot on my back. Do you care now do you do you
paragraphs.zh: 我们就走了。他们挤在岸边，光滑的脑袋在明亮的水面上排成一排。我们继续前行。“那不适合我们，是吗？”阳光斜射到各处的苔藓上，平整了。“可怜的孩子，你只是个女孩。”苔藓中长出了小花，比我见过的还要小。“你只是个女孩。可怜的孩子。”水边有一条蜿蜒的小路。然后水又平静了，漆黑、平静、湍急。“除了一个女孩什么都不是。可怜的妹妹。”我们躺在湿漉漉的草地上，雨水像冰冷的子弹打在我的背上，气喘吁吁。你现在在乎吗你在乎吗

paragraphs.en: My Lord we sure are in a mess get up. Where the rain touched my forehead it began to smart my hand came red away streaking off pink in the rain. Does it hurt
paragraphs.zh: 我的主啊，我们确实一团糟，起床了。雨水接触到我的额头的地方开始刺痛我的手，在雨中留下了红色的痕迹。痛吗

paragraphs.en: Of course it does what do you reckon
paragraphs.zh: 当然，你认为它会做什么

paragraphs.en: I tried to scratch your eyes out my Lord we sure do stink we better try to wash it off in the branch “There’s town again, sister. You’ll have to go home now. I’ve got to get back to school. Look how late it’s getting. You’ll go home now, wont you?” But she just looked at me with her black, secret, friendly gaze, the half-naked loaf clutched to her breast. “It’s wet. I thought we jumped back in time.” I took my handkerchief and tried to wipe the loaf, but the crust began to come off, so I stopped. “We’ll just have to let it dry itself. Hold it like this.” She held it like that. It looked kind of like rats had been eating it now. and the water building and building up the squatting back the sloughed mud stinking surfaceward pocking the pattering surface like grease on a hot stove. I told you I’d make you
paragraphs.zh: 我试图把你的眼睛挖出来，上帝啊，我们确实很臭，我们最好试着在树枝上把它洗掉。“又进城了，姐妹。你现在必须回家了。我得回学校了。看看已经这么晚了。你现在就回家吧，不是吗？”但她只是用黑色、秘密、友好的目光看着我，半裸的面包紧紧地抱在胸前。“湿了。我以为我们回到了过去。”我拿起手帕，试图擦拭面包，但面包皮开始脱落，所以我停了下来。“我们只需让它自然风干即可。像这样握住它。”她就这样握着。看起来有点像老鼠现在正在吃它。水积聚着，积聚着，脱落的泥土散发着恶臭，在啪嗒啪嗒的表面上留下痕迹，就像热炉子上的油脂一样。我告诉过你我会让你

paragraphs.en: I dont give a goddam what you do
paragraphs.zh: 我才不在乎你做什么

paragraphs.en: Then we heard the running and we stopped and looked back and saw him coming up the path running, the level shadows flicking upon his legs.
paragraphs.zh: 然后我们听到了奔跑的声音，我们停下来，回头一看，看到他沿着小路奔跑着，平坦的阴影在他的腿上闪烁。

paragraphs.en: “He’s in a hurry. We’d—” then I saw another man, an oldish man running heavily, clutching a stick, and a boy naked from the waist up, clutching his pants as he ran.
paragraphs.zh: “他很着急。我们会——”然后我看到另一个男人，一个老人，抓着一根棍子，沉重地跑着，还有一个男孩，腰部以上赤裸着，边跑边抓着裤子。

paragraphs.en: “There’s Julio,” the little girl said, and then I saw his Italian face and his eyes as he sprang upon me. We went down. His hands were jabbing at my face and he was saying something and trying to bite me, I reckon, and then they hauled him off and held him heaving and thrashing and yelling and they held his arms and he tried to kick me until they dragged him back. The little girl was howling, holding the loaf in both arms. The half-naked boy was darting and jumping up and down, clutching his trousers and someone pulled me up in time to see another stark naked figure come around the tranquil bend in the path running and change direction in midstride and leap into the woods, a couple of garments rigid as boards behind it. Julio still struggled. The man who had pulled me up said, “Whoa, now. We got you.” He wore a vest but no coat. Upon it was a metal shield. In his other hand he clutched a knotted, polished stick.
paragraphs.zh: “那是胡里奥，”小女孩说，然后我看到了他的意大利面孔和他跳到我身上时的眼睛。我们下去了。他的双手戳着我的脸，他在说着什么，想咬我，我想，然后他们把他拉开，让他不断地挣扎、殴打和大喊大叫，他们抓住他的手臂，他试图踢我，直到他们把他拖回来。小女孩双手抱着面包，嚎叫着。那个半裸的男孩紧紧抓着裤子，上下跳跃，有人及时把我拉了起来，我看到另一个赤身裸体的人影绕过小路安静的拐弯处跑来，中途改变方向，跳进树林里，身后有几件像木板一样僵硬的衣服。胡里奥仍在挣扎。把我拉上来的那个人说：“哇，现在。我们抓住你了。”他穿着一件背心，但没有穿外套。其上有一个金属盾牌。他的另一只手握着一根打结的、擦得锃亮的棍子。

paragraphs.en: “You’re Anse, aren’t you?” I said. “I was looking for you. What’s the matter?”
paragraphs.zh: “你是安斯，不是吗？”我说。“我正在找你，有什么事吗？”

paragraphs.en: “I warn you that anything you say will be used against you,” he said. “You’re under arrest.”
paragraphs.zh: “我警告你，你所说的任何话都会被用来对付你，”他说。“你被捕了。”

paragraphs.en: “I killa heem,” Julio said. He struggled. Two men held him. The little girl howled steadily, holding the bread. “You steala my seester,” Julio said. “Let go, meesters.”
paragraphs.zh: “我杀了哼，”胡里奥说。他挣扎着。两个男人拉住了他。小女孩拿着面包，不停地嚎叫。“你偷了我的先知，”胡里奥说。“放开吧，米斯特们。”

paragraphs.en: “Steal his sister?” I said. “Why, I’ve been—”
paragraphs.zh: “抢他妹妹？”我说。“为什么，我一直——”

paragraphs.en: “Shet up,” Anse said. “You can tell that to Squire.”
paragraphs.zh: “闭嘴，”安斯说。“你可以把这件事告诉乡绅。”

paragraphs.en: “Steal his sister?” I said. Julio broke from the men and sprang at me again, but the marshall met him and they struggled until the other two pinioned his arms again. Anse released him, panting.
paragraphs.zh: “抢他妹妹？”我说。胡里奥挣脱了人群，再次向我扑来，但元帅遇到了他，他们挣扎着，直到另外两个人再次抓住了他的手臂。安斯气喘吁吁地松开了他。

paragraphs.en: “You durn furriner,” he said, “I’ve a good mind to take you up too, for assault and battery.” He turned to me again. “Will you come peaceable, or do I handcuff you?”
paragraphs.zh: “你这个该死的家伙，”他说，“我也很乐意以攻击和殴打的罪名逮捕你。”他再次转向我。“你愿意和平地来，还是我给你戴上手铐？”

paragraphs.en: “I’ll come peaceable,” I said. “Anything, just so I can find someone—do something with—Stole his sister,” I said. “Stole his—”
paragraphs.zh: “我会平静地来，”我说。“什么都可以，只要我能找到一个人——做点什么——偷走他的妹妹，”我说。“偷了他的——”

paragraphs.en: “I’ve warned you,” Anse said, “He aims to charge you with meditated criminal assault. Here, you, make that gal shut up that noise.”
paragraphs.zh: “我已经警告过你了，”安斯说，“他的目的是指控你蓄意犯罪袭击。来吧，你，让那个女孩闭嘴。”

paragraphs.en: “Oh,” I said. Then I began to laugh. Two more boys with plastered heads and round eyes came out of the bushes, buttoning shirts that had already dampened onto their shoulders and arms, and I tried to stop the laughter, but I couldnt.
paragraphs.zh: “哦，”我说。然后我开始笑。又有两个头戴石膏、眼睛圆睁的男孩从灌木丛中走了出来，把已经湿透的衬衫扣在肩膀和手臂上，我试图阻止笑声，但我做不到。

paragraphs.en: “Watch him, Anse, he’s crazy, I believe.”
paragraphs.zh: “看着他，安斯，我相信他疯了。”

paragraphs.en: “I’ll h-have to qu-quit,” I said, “It’ll stop in a mu-minute. The other time it said ah ah ah,” I said, laughing. “Let me sit down a while.” I sat down, they watching me, and the little girl with her streaked face and the gnawed looking loaf, and the water swift and peaceful below the path. After a while the laughter ran out. But my throat wouldnt quit trying to laugh, like retching after your stomach is empty.
paragraphs.zh: “我必须退出，”我说，“它会在一分钟内停止。另一次它说啊啊啊，”我笑着说。“让我坐一会儿。”我坐下来，他们看着我，还有脸上有条纹的小女孩，看着被啃过的面包，还有小路下面湍急而平静的水流。过了一会儿，笑声消失了。但我的喉咙却不停地想笑，就像胃空了之后干呕一样。

paragraphs.en: “Whoa, now,” Anse said. “Get a grip on yourself.”
paragraphs.zh: “哇哦，现在，”安斯说。“控制住自己。”

paragraphs.en: “Yes,” I said, tightening my throat. There was another yellow butterfly, like one of the sunflecks had come loose. After a while I didnt have to hold my throat so tight. I got up. “I’m ready. Which way?”
paragraphs.zh: “是的，”我说，收紧了喉咙。还有另一只黄色的蝴蝶，就像其中一个太阳斑已经脱落了。过了一会儿，我就不用那么紧地捂住喉咙了。我起身。“我准备好了。走哪条路？”

paragraphs.en: We followed the path, the two others watching Julio and the little girl and the boys somewhere in the rear. The path went along the river to the bridge. We crossed it and the tracks, people coming to the doors to look at us and more boys materializing from somewhere until when we turned into the main street we had quite a procession. Before the drugstore stood an auto, a big one, but I didn’t recognise them until Mrs Bland said,
paragraphs.zh: 我们沿着小路走，另外两个人看着胡里奥、小女孩和男孩们在后面的某个地方。这条路沿着河一直延伸到桥上。我们穿过它和铁轨，人们来到门口看着我们，更多的男孩从某个地方出现，直到我们拐进主街时，我们已经排起了长队。药店前停着一辆汽车，一辆大汽车，但我没认出它们，直到布兰德太太说：

paragraphs.en: “Why, Quentin! Quentin Compson!” Then I saw Gerald, and Spoade in the back seat, sitting on the back of his neck. And Shreve. I didnt know the two girls.
paragraphs.zh: “为什么，昆丁！昆丁康普生！”然后我看到杰拉尔德和斯波德坐在后座上，坐在他的脖子后面。还有施里夫。我不认识这两个女孩。

paragraphs.en: “Quentin Compson!” Mrs Bland said.
paragraphs.zh: “昆丁康普生！”布兰德夫人说道。

paragraphs.en: “Good afternoon,” I said, raising my hat. “I’m under arrest. I’m sorry I didnt get your note. Did Shreve tell you?”
paragraphs.zh: “下午好，”我举起帽子说。“我被捕了。很抱歉我没有收到你的字条。施里夫告诉你了吗？”

paragraphs.en: “Under arrest?” Shreve said. “Excuse me,” he said. He heaved himself up and climbed over their feet and got out. He had on a pair of my flannel pants, like a glove. I didnt remember forgetting them. I didnt remember how many chins Mrs Bland had, either. The prettiest girl was with Gerald in front, too. They watched me through veils, with a kind of delicate horror. “Who’s under arrest?” Shreve said. “What’s this, mister?”
paragraphs.zh: “被捕了？”施里夫说道。“对不起，”他说。他站起来，爬到他们的脚上，下了车。他穿着我的法兰绒裤，就像手套一样。我不记得忘记了它们。我也不记得布兰德太太有多少下巴。最漂亮的女孩也和杰拉尔德在前面。他们透过面纱看着我，带着一种微妙的恐惧。“谁被捕了？”施里夫说道。“这是什么，先生？”

paragraphs.en: “Gerald,” Mrs Bland said, “Send these people away. You get in this car, Quentin.”
paragraphs.zh: “杰拉德，”布兰德夫人说，“把这些人送走。昆丁，你上这辆车。”

paragraphs.en: Gerald got out. Spoade hadnt moved.
paragraphs.zh: 杰拉尔德下了车。斯波德没有动。

paragraphs.en: “What’s he done, Cap?” he said. “Robbed a hen house?”
paragraphs.zh: “他做了什么，队长？”他说。“抢了鸡舍？”

paragraphs.en: “I warn you,” Anse said. “Do you know the prisoner?”
paragraphs.zh: “我警告你，”安斯说。“你认识那个囚犯吗？”

paragraphs.en: “Know him,” Shreve said. “Look here—”
paragraphs.zh: “认识他，”施里夫说。“看这里——”

paragraphs.en: “Then you can come along to the squire’s. You’re obstructing justice. Come along.” He shook my arm.
paragraphs.zh: “那你就可以去乡绅家了。你这是妨碍司法公正。走吧。”他摇动我的手臂。

paragraphs.en: “Well, good afternoon,” I said. “I’m glad to have seen you all. Sorry I couldnt be with you.”
paragraphs.zh: “嗯，下午好，”我说。“我很高兴见到你们大家。很抱歉我不能和你们在一起。”

paragraphs.en: “You, Gerald,” Mrs Bland said.
paragraphs.zh: “你，杰拉尔德，”布兰德夫人说。

paragraphs.en: “Look here, constable,” Gerald said.
paragraphs.zh: “看这里，警官，”杰拉尔德说。

paragraphs.en: “I warn you you’re interfering with an officer of the law,” Anse said. “If you’ve anything to say, you can come to the squire’s and make cognizance of the prisoner.” We went on. Quite a procession now, Anse and I leading. I could hear them telling them what it was, and Spoade asking questions, and then Julio said something violently in Italian and I looked back and saw the little girl standing at the curb, looking at me with her friendly, inscrutable regard.
paragraphs.zh: “我警告你，你正在干扰执法人员，”安斯说。“有什么话可以到乡绅那里去认罪。”我们继续前行。现在队伍已经相当庞大了，我和安斯在前面带路。我能听到他们告诉他们那是什么，斯波德在问问题，然后胡里奥用意大利语粗暴地说了些什么，我回头看到那个小女孩站在路边，用她友好的、难以理解的目光看着我。

paragraphs.en: “Git on home,” Julio shouted at her, “I beat hell outa you.”
paragraphs.zh: “回家吧，”胡里奥对她喊道，“我打败了你。”

paragraphs.en: We went down the street and turned into a bit of lawn in which, set back from the street, stood a one storey building of brick trimmed with white. We went up the rock path to the door, where Anse halted everyone except us and made them remain outside. We entered a bare room smelling of stale tobacco. There was a sheet iron stove in the center of a wooden frame filled with sand, and a faded map on the wall and the dingy plat of a township. Behind a scarred littered table a man with a fierce roach of iron grey hair peered at us over steel spectacles.
paragraphs.zh: 我们沿着街道走，拐进一小片草坪，草坪上矗立着一栋镶着白色砖墙的单层建筑。我们沿着岩石小路走到门口，安斯拦住了除了我们之外的所有人，让他们留在外面。我们走进一间空荡荡的房间，里面弥漫着陈旧的烟草味。装满沙子的木架中央有一个铁皮炉子，墙上挂着一张褪色的地图和肮脏的城镇平面图。在一张伤痕累累、乱七八糟的桌子后面，一个有着一头凶猛的铁灰色头发的男人透过钢制眼镜凝视着我们。

paragraphs.en: “Got him, did ye, Anse?” he said.
paragraphs.zh: “找到他了，是吗，安斯？”他说。

paragraphs.en: “Got him, Squire.”
paragraphs.zh: “抓住他了，乡绅。”

paragraphs.en: He opened a huge dusty book and drew it to him and dipped a foul pen into an inkwell filled with what looked like coal dust.
paragraphs.zh: 他打开一本满是灰尘的大书，把它拉到自己面前，然后将一支肮脏的钢笔浸入充满了看起来像煤尘的墨水池中。

paragraphs.en: “Look here, mister,” Shreve said.
paragraphs.zh: “看这里，先生，”施里夫说。

paragraphs.en: “The prisoner’s name,” the squire said. I told him. He wrote it slowly into the book, the pen scratching with excruciating deliberation.
paragraphs.zh: “囚犯的名字。”乡绅说道。我告诉他。他慢慢地把它写进了书里，笔在痛苦的思索中划过。

paragraphs.en: “Look here, mister,” Shreve said, “We know this fellow. We—”
paragraphs.zh: “看这里，先生，”施里夫说，“我们认识这个人。我们——”

paragraphs.en: “Order in the court,” Anse said.
paragraphs.zh: “法庭命令，”安斯说。

paragraphs.en: “Shut up, bud,” Spoade said. “Let him do it his way. He’s going to anyhow.”
paragraphs.zh: “闭嘴，伙计，”斯波德说。“让他按照他的方式去做吧。无论如何他都会这么做。”

paragraphs.en: “Age,” the squire said. I told him. He wrote that, his mouth moving as he wrote. “Occupation.” I told him. “Harvard student, hey?” he said. He looked up at me, bowing his neck a little to see over the spectacles. His eyes were clear and cold, like a goat’s. “What are you up to, coming out here kidnapping children?”
paragraphs.zh: “年龄，”乡绅说。我告诉他。他写着这句话，边写边动着嘴。“职业。”我告诉他。“哈佛的学生，嘿？”他说。他抬头看着我，稍微低下脖子，透过眼镜看清情况。他的眼睛清澈而冰冷，就像山羊的眼睛一样。“你来这里绑架孩子到底想做什么？”

paragraphs.en: “They’re crazy, Squire,” Shreve said. “Whoever says this boy’s kidnapping—”
paragraphs.zh: “他们疯了，乡绅，”施里夫说。“无论谁说这个男孩被绑架了——”

paragraphs.en: Julio moved violently. “Crazy?” he said. “Dont I catcha heem, eh? Dont I see weetha my own eyes—”
paragraphs.zh: 胡里奥剧烈地动了一下。“疯狂的？”他说。“我没听懂吗？嗯？我没看到我自己的眼睛——”

paragraphs.en: “You’re a liar,” Shreve said. “You never—”
paragraphs.zh: “你是个骗子，”施里夫说。“你从来没有——”

paragraphs.en: “Order, order,” Anse said, raising his voice.
paragraphs.zh: “命令，命令。”安斯提高了声音说道。

paragraphs.en: “You fellers shet up,” the squire said. “If they dont stay quiet, turn ’em out, Anse.” They got quiet. The squire looked at Shreve, then at Spoade, then at Gerald. “You know this young man?” he said to Spoade.
paragraphs.zh: “你们这些家伙给我闭嘴，”乡绅说。“如果他们不保持安静，就把他们赶出去，安斯。”他们安静了。乡绅看了看施里夫，又看了看斯波德，又看了看杰拉尔德。“你认识这个年轻人？”他对斯波德说道。

paragraphs.en: “Yes, your honour,” Spoade said. “He’s just a country boy in school up there. He dont mean any harm. I think the marshall’ll find it’s a mistake. His father’s a congregational minister.”
paragraphs.zh: “是的，法官大人，”斯波德说。“他只是那里学校里的一个乡下男孩。他没有任何恶意。我想法警会发现这是一个错误。他的父亲是一名公理会牧师。”

paragraphs.en: “H’m,” the squire said. “What was you doing, exactly?” I told him, he watching me with his cold, pale eyes. “How about it, Anse?”
paragraphs.zh: “嗯，”乡绅说。“你到底在做什么？”我告诉他，他用冰冷、苍白的眼睛看着我。“怎么样，安斯？”

paragraphs.en: “Might have been,” Anse said. “Them durn furriners.”
paragraphs.zh: “可能是，”安斯说。“他们讨厌毛皮商。”

paragraphs.en: “I American,” Julio said. “I gotta da pape’.”
paragraphs.zh: “我是美国人，”胡里奥说。“我得做爸爸。”

paragraphs.en: “Where’s the gal?”
paragraphs.zh: “那姑娘在哪儿？”

paragraphs.en: “He sent her home,” Anse said.
paragraphs.zh: “他送她回家，”安斯说。

paragraphs.en: “Was she scared or anything?”
paragraphs.zh: “她是害怕了还是怎么了？”

paragraphs.en: “Not till Julio there jumped on the prisoner. They were just walking along the river path, towards town. Some boys swimming told us which way they went.”
paragraphs.zh: “直到胡里奥跳到了囚犯身上。他们当时正沿着河边小路向城镇走去。一些游泳的男孩告诉我们他们去了哪条路。”

paragraphs.en: “It’s a mistake, Squire,” Spoade said. “Children and dogs are always taking up with him like that. He cant help it.”
paragraphs.zh: “这是一个错误，乡绅，”斯波德说。“孩子们和狗总是这样对待他。他无能为力。”

paragraphs.en: “H’m,” the squire said. He looked out of the window for a while. We watched him. I could hear Julio scratching himself. The squire looked back.
paragraphs.zh: “嗯，”乡绅说。他向窗外看了一会儿。我们看着他。我能听到胡里奥抓自己的声音。乡绅回头看了一眼。

paragraphs.en: “Air you satisfied the gal aint took any hurt, you, there?”
paragraphs.zh: “你确信女孩没有受伤，你在吗？”

paragraphs.en: “No hurt now,” Julio said sullenly.
paragraphs.zh: “现在没受伤了，”胡里奥闷闷不乐地说。

paragraphs.en: “You quit work to hunt for her?”
paragraphs.zh: “你辞去工作去寻找她？”

paragraphs.en: “Sure I quit. I run. I run like hell. Looka here, looka there, then man tella me he seen him giva her she eat. She go weetha.”
paragraphs.zh: “当然，我放弃了。我跑。我拼命跑。看这里，看那里，然后有人告诉我他看到他给她吃东西。她走了。”

paragraphs.en: “H’m,” the squire said. “Well, son, I calculate you owe Julio something for taking him away from his work.”
paragraphs.zh: “嗯，”乡绅说。“好吧，儿子，我想你欠胡里奥一些东西，因为你让他离开了工作。”

paragraphs.en: “Yes, sir,” I said. “How much?”
paragraphs.zh: “是的，先生，”我说。“多少？”

paragraphs.en: “Dollar, I calculate.”
paragraphs.zh: “美元，我算一下。”

paragraphs.en: I gave Julio a dollar.
paragraphs.zh: 我给了胡里奥一美元。

paragraphs.en: “Well,” Spoade said, “If that’s all—I reckon he’s discharged, your honour?”
paragraphs.zh: “好吧，”斯波德说，“如果仅此而已——我想他已经出院了，法官大人？”

paragraphs.en: The squire didn’t look at him. “How far’d you run him, Anse?”
paragraphs.zh: 乡绅没有看他。“安斯，你把他追赶到什么程度了？”

paragraphs.en: “Two miles, at least. It was about two hours before we caught him.”
paragraphs.zh: “至少两英里。我们大约两个小时后才抓住他。”

paragraphs.en: “H’m,” the squire said. He mused a while. We watched him, his stiff crest, the spectacles riding low on his nose. The yellow shape of the window grew slowly across the floor, reached the wall, climbing. Dust motes whirled and slanted. “Six dollars.”
paragraphs.zh: “嗯，”乡绅说。他沉思了一会儿。我们看着他，他的头顶僵硬，眼镜低垂在鼻子上。窗户的黄色形状在地板上慢慢生长，一直爬到墙上。尘埃旋转倾斜。“六块钱。”

paragraphs.en: “Six dollars?” Shreve said. “What’s that for?”
paragraphs.zh: “六块钱？”施里夫说道。“那是干什么用的？”

paragraphs.en: “Six dollars,” the squire said. He looked at Shreve a moment, then at me again.
paragraphs.zh: “六美元，”乡绅说。他看了施里夫一会儿，然后又看了我一眼。

paragraphs.en: “Look here,” Shreve said.
paragraphs.zh: “看这里，”施里夫说。

paragraphs.en: “Shut up,” Spoade said. “Give it to him, bud, and let’s get out of here. The ladies are waiting for us. You got six dollars?”
paragraphs.zh: “闭嘴，”斯波德说。“把它给他，伙计，我们离开这里吧。女士们正在等我们。你有六块钱吗？”

paragraphs.en: “Yes,” I said. I gave him six dollars.
paragraphs.zh: “是的，”我说。我给了他六块钱。

paragraphs.en: “Case dismissed,” he said.
paragraphs.zh: “案件被驳回，”他说。

paragraphs.en: “You get a receipt,” Shreve said. “You get a signed receipt for that money.”
paragraphs.zh: “你会收到一张收据，”施里夫说。“你会得到一张签字的收据。”

paragraphs.en: The squire looked at Shreve mildly. “Case dismissed,” he said without raising his voice.
paragraphs.zh: 乡绅温和地看着施里夫。“案件被驳回，”他没有提高声音说道。

paragraphs.en: “I’ll be damned—” Shreve said.
paragraphs.zh: “我该死——”施里夫说。

paragraphs.en: “Come on here,” Spoade said, taking his arm. “Good afternoon, Judge. Much obliged.” As we passed out the door Julio’s voice rose again, violent, then ceased. Spoade was looking at me, his brown eyes quizzical, a little cold. “Well, bud, I reckon you’ll do your girl chasing in Boston after this.”
paragraphs.zh: “过来，”斯波德拉着他的胳膊说道。“下午好，法官。非常感谢。”当我们走出门时，胡里奥的声音再次响起，充满暴力，然后就停止了。斯波德看着我，他棕色的眼睛充满好奇，有点冷漠。“好吧，伙计，我想你会在这之后去波士顿追你的女孩。”

paragraphs.en: “You damned fool,” Shreve said, “What the hell do you mean anyway, straggling off here, fooling with these damn wops?”
paragraphs.zh: “你这个该死的傻瓜，”施里夫说，“你居然跑到这里来，跟这些该死的狗娘养的，到底是什么意思？”

paragraphs.en: “Come on,” Spoade said, “They must be getting impatient.”
paragraphs.zh: “得了吧，”斯波德说，“他们肯定不耐烦了。”

paragraphs.en: Mrs Bland was talking to them. They were Miss Holmes and Miss Daingerfield and they quit listening to her and looked at me again with that delicate and curious horror, their veils turned back upon their little white noses and their eyes fleeing and mysterious beneath the veils.
paragraphs.zh: 布兰德夫人正在跟他们说话。她们是福尔摩斯小姐和丹格菲尔德小姐，她们不再听她说话，再次用那种微妙而好奇的恐惧看着我，她们的面纱转回到她们白色的小鼻子上，她们的眼睛在面纱下四处逃窜，神秘莫测。

paragraphs.en: “Quentin Compson,” Mrs Bland said, “What would your mother say? A young man naturally gets into scrapes, but to be arrested on foot by a country policeman. What did they think he’d done, Gerald?”
paragraphs.zh: “昆丁·康普生，”布兰德太太说，“你妈妈会怎么说？一个年轻人自然会陷入困境，但却被一个乡村警察步行逮捕。他们认为他做了什么，杰拉尔德？”

paragraphs.en: “Nothing,” Gerald said.
paragraphs.zh: “没什么，”杰拉尔德说。

paragraphs.en: “Nonsense. What was it, you, Spoade?”
paragraphs.zh: “胡说八道。你，斯波德，那是什么？”

paragraphs.en: “He was trying to kidnap that little dirty girl, but they caught him in time,” Spoade said.
paragraphs.zh: “他试图绑架那个肮脏的小女孩，但他们及时抓住了他，”斯波德说。

paragraphs.en: “Nonsense,” Mrs Bland said, but her voice sort of died away and she stared at me for a moment, and the girls drew their breaths in with a soft concerted sound. “Fiddlesticks,” Mrs Bland said briskly, “If that isn’t just like these ignorant lowclass Yankees. Get in, Quentin.”
paragraphs.zh: “胡说八道，”布兰德太太说，但她的声音渐渐消失了，她盯着我看了一会儿，女孩们用轻柔的、一致的声音吸了一口气。“费德提克，”布兰德夫人轻快地说，“如果这不像这些无知的下层北方佬。上车吧，昆丁。”

paragraphs.en: Shreve and I sat on two small collapsible seats. Gerald cranked the car and got in and we started.
paragraphs.zh: 施里夫和我坐在两个可折叠的小座椅上。杰拉尔德发动汽车，上了车，我们开始了。

paragraphs.en: “Now, Quentin, you tell me what all this foolishness is about,” Mrs Bland said. I told them, Shreve hunched and furious on his little seat and Spoade sitting again on the back of his neck beside Miss Daingerfield.
paragraphs.zh: “现在，昆丁，你告诉我这些愚蠢的事情是怎么回事，”布兰德夫人说。我告诉他们，施里夫在他的小座位上弓着背，怒气冲冲，斯波德又坐在丹格菲尔德小姐旁边的脖子后面。

paragraphs.en: “And the joke is, all the time Quentin had us all fooled,” Spoade said. “All the time we thought he was the model youth that anybody could trust a daughter with, until the police showed him up at his nefarious work.”
paragraphs.zh: “笑话是，昆丁一直在愚弄我们，”斯波德说。“我们一直认为他是任何人都可以信任女儿的模范青年，直到警察发现他从事邪恶工作。”

paragraphs.en: “Hush up, Spoade,” Mrs Bland said. We drove down the street and crossed the bridge and passed the house where the pink garment hung in the window. “That’s what you get for not reading my note. Why didnt you come and get it? Mr MacKenzie says he told you it was there.”
paragraphs.zh: “安静点，斯波德，”布兰德太太说。我们沿着街道行驶，过了桥，经过了窗户上挂着粉红色衣服的房子。“这就是你没有读我的便条所得到的结果。你为什么不来拿它？麦肯齐先生说他告诉过你它就在那里。”

paragraphs.en: “Yessum. I intended to, but I never went back to the room.”
paragraphs.zh: “是的，我本来打算去的，但我再也没有回过房间。”

paragraphs.en: “You’d have let us sit there waiting I dont know how long, if it hadnt been for Mr MacKenzie. When he said you hadnt come back, that left an extra place, so we asked him to come. We’re very glad to have you anyway, Mr MacKenzie.” Shreve said nothing. His arms were folded and he glared straight ahead past Gerald’s cap. It was a cap for motoring in England. Mrs Bland said so. We passed that house, and three others, and another yard where the little girl stood by the gate. She didnt have the bread now, and her face looked like it had been streaked with coaldust. I waved my hand, but she made no reply, only her head turned slowly as the car passed, following us with her unwinking gaze. Then we ran beside the wall, our shadows running along the wall, and after a while we passed a piece of torn newspaper lying beside the road and I began to laugh again. I could feel it in my throat and I looked off into the trees where the afternoon slanted, thinking of afternoon and of the bird and the boys in swimming. But still I couldnt stop it and then I knew that if I tried too hard to stop it I’d be crying and I thought about how I’d thought about I could not be a virgin, with so many of them walking along in the shadows and whispering with their soft girlvoices lingering in the shadowy places and the words coming out and perfume and eyes you could feel not see, but if it was that simple to do it wouldnt be anything and if it wasnt anything, what was I and then Mrs Bland said, “Quentin? Is he sick, Mr MacKenzie?” and then Shreve’s fat hand touched my knee and Spoade began talking and I quit trying to stop it.
paragraphs.zh: “如果不是麦肯齐先生，你会让我们坐在那里等我不知道多久。当他说你还没有回来时，就留下了一个额外的位置，所以我们请他来。无论如何，我们很高兴有你，麦肯齐先生。”施里夫什么也没说。他双臂交叉，目光越过杰拉尔德的帽子直视前方。这是英国汽车的上限。布兰德夫人如此说道。我们经过那所房子，还有另外三所房子，还有小女孩站在门口的另一个院子。她现在没有面包了，她的脸看起来就像沾满了煤尘。我挥了挥手，她却没有回答，只是随着车子的驶过，她的头缓缓转过，一眨不眨地跟随着我们。然后我们沿着墙边跑，我们的影子沿着墙跑，过了一会儿，我们经过路边一张撕破的报纸，我又开始笑了。我能感觉到它在我的喉咙里，我望向下午倾斜的树林，想着下午、那只鸟和游泳的男孩们。但我还是无法阻止它，然后我知道，如果我太努力地阻止它，我会哭，我想到我是如何想到我不可能是处女的，这么多人在阴影中行走，用她们柔和的女声低声窃窃私语，她们的声音在阴暗的地方徘徊，而出来的话语、香水和眼睛你感觉不到，但如果做起来那么简单，那就什么都不是了，如果不是什么，我和布兰德夫人又算什么呢？问道：“昆丁？麦肯齐先生，他病了吗？”然后施里夫肥胖的手碰到了我的膝盖，斯波德开始说话，我不再试图阻止它。

paragraphs.en: “If that hamper is in his way, Mr MacKenzie, move it over on your side. I brought a hamper of wine because I think young gentlemen should drink wine, although my father, Gerald’s grandfather” ever do that Have you ever done that In the grey darkness a little light her hands locked about
paragraphs.zh: “如果那个篮子挡住了他的路，麦肯齐先生，就把它移到你这边。我带了一篮子酒，因为我认为年轻的绅士应该喝酒，尽管我的父亲，杰拉尔德的祖父”曾经这样做过吗？你曾经这样做过吗？在灰色的黑暗中，一点点光芒，她的双手锁住了

paragraphs.en: “They do, when they can get it,” Spoade said. “Hey, Shreve?” her knees her face looking at the sky the smell of honeysuckle upon her face and throat
paragraphs.zh: “只要他们能得到它，他们就会这么做，”斯波德说。“喂，施里夫？”她的膝盖她的脸看着天空她的脸和喉咙上有金银花的味道

paragraphs.en: “Beer, too,” Shreve said. His hand touched my knee again. I moved my knee again. like a thin wash of lilac coloured paint talking about him bringing
paragraphs.zh: “还有啤酒，”施里夫说。他的手再次触碰了我的膝盖。我又动了动膝盖。就像淡淡的淡紫色油漆在谈论着他带来的

paragraphs.en: “You’re not a gentleman,” Spoade said. him between us until the shape of her blurred not with dark

paragraphs.en: It kept on running for a long time, but my face felt cold and sort of dead, and my eye, and the cut place on my finger was smarting again. I could hear Shreve working the pump, then he came back with the basin and a round blob of twilight wobbling in it, with a yellow edge like a fading balloon, then my reflection. I tried to see my face in it.
paragraphs.zh: 它持续了很长一段时间，但我的脸感觉冰冷，有点死气沉沉，我的眼睛和手指上的伤口又开始刺痛。我能听到施里夫开水泵的声音，然后他带着盆回来了，一团暮色在盆里摇晃，黄色的边缘就像一个褪色的气球，然后是我的倒影。我试图在其中看到我的脸。

paragraphs.en: “Has it stopped?” Shreve said. “Give me the rag.” He tried to take it from my hand.
paragraphs.zh: “停了吗？”施里夫说道。“把抹布给我。”他试图从我手中夺走它。

paragraphs.en: “Look out,” I said, “I can do it. Yes, it’s about stopped now.” I dipped the rag again, breaking the balloon. The rag stained the water. “I wish I had a clean one.”
paragraphs.zh: “小心点，”我说，“我能做到。是的，现在就要停止了。”我又把抹布浸了一下，把气球弄破了。抹布弄脏了水。“我希望我有一个干净的。”

paragraphs.en: “You need a piece of beefsteak for that eye,” Shreve said. “Damn if you wont have a shiner tomorrow. The son of a bitch,” he said.
paragraphs.zh: “你需要一块牛排来做那只眼睛，”施里夫说。“如果你明天没有闪亮的东西，那该死的。狗娘养的，”他说。

paragraphs.en: “Did I hurt him any?” I wrung out the handkerchief and tried to clean the blood off of my vest.
paragraphs.zh: “我有伤害他吗？”我拧干手帕，试图擦掉背心上的血迹。

paragraphs.en: “You cant get that off,” Shreve said. “You’ll have to send it to the cleaner’s. Come on, hold it on your eye, why dont you.”
paragraphs.zh: “你脱不下来，”施里夫说。“你必须把它送到清洁工那里。来吧，把它放在你的眼睛上，为什么不呢。”

paragraphs.en: “I can get some of it off,” I said. But I wasn’t doing much good. “What sort of shape is my collar in?”
paragraphs.zh: “我可以摘掉一些，”我说。但我并没有做得很好。“我的领子是什么形状的？”

paragraphs.en: “I dont know,” Shreve said. “Hold it against your eye. Here.”
paragraphs.zh: “我不知道，”施里夫说。“把它放在你的眼睛上。这里。”

paragraphs.en: “Look out,” I said. “I can do it. Did I hurt him any?”
paragraphs.zh: “小心，”我说。“我能做到。我伤到他了吗？”

paragraphs.en: “You may have hit him. I may have looked away just then or blinked or something. He boxed the hell out of you. He boxed you all over the place. What did you want to fight him with your fists for? You goddamn fool. How do you feel?”
paragraphs.zh: “你可能打了他。我当时可能把目光移开了，或者眨了眨眼或者其他什么。他把你打得屁滚尿流。他把你打得到处都是。你为什么要用拳头和他打？你这个该死的傻瓜。你感觉怎么样？”

paragraphs.en: “I feel fine,” I said. “I wonder if I can get something to clean my vest.”
paragraphs.zh: “我感觉很好，”我说。“我想知道是否能找到一些东西来清洁我的背心。”

paragraphs.en: “Oh, forget your damn clothes. Does your eye hurt?”
paragraphs.zh: “哦，忘记你那该死的衣服了。你的眼睛疼吗？”

paragraphs.en: “I feel fine,” I said. Everything was sort of violet and still, the sky green paling into gold beyond the gable of the house and a plume of smoke rising from the chimney without any wind. I heard the pump again. A man was filling a pail, watching us across his pumping shoulder. A woman crossed the door, but she didnt look out. I could hear a cow lowing somewhere.
paragraphs.zh: “我感觉很好，”我说。一切都是紫罗兰色，寂静无声，房子山墙外的天空从绿色变成金色，烟囱里升起一缕炊烟，没有一丝风。我又听到了水泵的声音。一个男人正在给桶装水，用他那抽动的肩膀看着我们。一个女人穿过门，但她没有向外看。我能听到某处有一头牛在哞哞叫。

paragraphs.en: “Come on,” Shreve said, “Let your clothes alone and put that rag on your eye. I’ll send your suit out first thing tomorrow.”
paragraphs.zh: “来吧，”施里夫说，“别管你的衣服，用那块布蒙住你的眼睛。明天我会第一时间把你的衣服送出去。”

paragraphs.en: “All right. I’m sorry I didn’t bleed on him a little, at least.”
paragraphs.zh: “好吧。我很抱歉，至少我没有让他流一点血。”

paragraphs.en: “Son of a bitch,” Shreve said. Spoade came out of the house, talking to the woman I reckon, and crossed the yard. He looked at me with his cold, quizzical eyes.
paragraphs.zh: “狗娘养的，”施里夫说。斯波德从房子里出来，我猜是在和那个女人说话，然后穿过院子。他用冰冷、疑惑的眼神看着我。

paragraphs.en: “Well, bud,” he said, looking at me, “I’ll be damned if you dont go to a lot of trouble to have your fun. Kidnapping, then fighting. What do you do on your holidays? burn houses?”
paragraphs.zh: “好吧，伙计，”他看着我说，“如果你不费尽心思去享受乐趣，我就该死了。绑架，然后打架。你假期做什么？烧房子？”

paragraphs.en: “I’m all right,” I said. “What did Mrs Bland say?”
paragraphs.zh: “我没事，”我说。“布兰德夫人说什么？”

paragraphs.en: “She’s giving Gerald hell for bloodying you up. She’ll give you hell for letting him, when she sees you. She dont object to the fighting, it’s the blood that annoys her. I think you lost caste with her a little by not holding your blood better. How do you feel?”
paragraphs.zh: “她会因为杰拉德让你流血而让你下地狱。当她看到你的时候，她会因为让他放了你而让你下地狱。她并不反对战斗，而是血让她恼火。我认为你因为没有更好地保留你的血而失去了与她的种姓。你感觉如何？”

paragraphs.en: “Sure,” Shreve said, “If you cant be a Bland, the next best thing is to commit adultery with one or get drunk and fight him, as the case may be.”
paragraphs.zh: “当然，”施里夫说，“如果你不能成为布兰德人，那么下一个最好的办法就是与一个布兰德人通奸，或者喝醉酒并与他打架，视情况而定。”

paragraphs.en: “Quite right,” Spoade said. “But I didnt know Quentin was drunk.”
paragraphs.zh: “完全正确，”斯波德说。“但我不知道昆丁喝醉了。”

paragraphs.en: “He wasnt,” Shreve said. “Do you have to be drunk to want to hit that son of a bitch?”
paragraphs.zh: “他不是，”施里夫说。“你一定是喝醉了才想打那个王八蛋吗？”

paragraphs.en: “Well, I think I’d have to be pretty drunk to try it, after seeing how Quentin came out. Where’d he learn to box?”
paragraphs.zh: “嗯，我想我得喝醉了才能尝试一下，看到昆丁是怎么出来的。他在哪里学拳击的？”

paragraphs.en: “He’s been going to Mike’s every day, over in town,” I said.
paragraphs.zh: “他每天都去城里的迈克家，”我说。

paragraphs.en: “He has?” Spoade said. “Did you know that when you hit him?”
paragraphs.zh: “他有吗？”斯波德说道。“你打他的时候知道吗？”

paragraphs.en: “I dont know,” I said. “I guess so. Yes.”
paragraphs.zh: “我不知道，”我说。“我想是的。是的。”

paragraphs.en: “Wet it again,” Shreve said. “Want some fresh water?”
paragraphs.zh: “再把它弄湿，”施里夫说。“想要一些淡水吗？”

paragraphs.en: “This is all right,” I said. I dipped the cloth again and held it to my eye. “Wish I had something to clean my vest.” Spoade was still watching me.
paragraphs.zh: “没关系，”我说。我再次浸湿布并将其放在眼睛上。“希望我有东西可以清洁我的背心。”斯波德仍在注视着我。

paragraphs.en: “Say,” he said, “What did you hit him for? What was it he said?”
paragraphs.zh: “说吧，”他说，“你为什么打他？他说什么？”

paragraphs.en: “I dont know. I dont know why I did.”
paragraphs.zh: “我不知道。我不知道我为什么这么做。”

paragraphs.en: “The first I knew was when you jumped up all of a sudden and said, ‘Did you ever have a sister? Did you?’ and when he said No, you hit him. I noticed you kept on looking at him, but you didnt seem to be paying any attention to what anybody was saying until you jumped up and asked him if he had any sisters.”
paragraphs.zh: “我知道的第一件事是，你突然跳起来问，‘你有妹妹吗？有吗？’当他说没有时，你就打了他。我注意到你一直看着他，但你似乎并没有注意到别人在说什么，直到你跳起来问他是否有姐妹。”

paragraphs.en: “Ah, he was blowing off as usual,” Shreve said, “about his women. You know: like he does, before girls, so they dont know exactly what he’s saying. All his damn innuendo and lying and a lot of stuff that dont make sense even. Telling us about some wench that he made a date with to meet at a dance hall in Atlantic City and stood her up and went to the hotel and went to bed and how he lay there being sorry for her waiting on the pier for him, without him there to give her what she wanted. Talking about the body’s beauty and the sorry ends thereof and how tough women have it, without anything else they can do except lie on their backs. Leda lurking in the bushes, whimpering and moaning for the swan, see. The son of a bitch. I’d hit him myself. Only I’d grabbed up her damn hamper of wine and done it if it had been me.”
paragraphs.zh: “啊，他像往常一样吹嘘他的女人。你知道：就像他在女孩面前所做的那样，所以她们不知道他到底在说什么。他所有该死的暗示和谎言以及许多甚至没有意义的东西。告诉我们他在大西洋城的一个舞厅里与一个女孩约会，然后让她站起来，去了旅馆，上床睡觉，以及他如何躺在那里为她在码头等待而感到抱歉。他，没有他在场，无法给她她想要的东西，以及女人所经历的一切，除了仰卧在灌木丛中，为天鹅哭泣和呻吟之外，她们别无选择，只有我自己抓起她那该死的酒篮才这么做。”

paragraphs.en: “Oh,” Spoade said, “the champion of dames. Bud, you excite not only admiration, but horror.” He looked at me, cold and quizzical. “Good God,” he said.
paragraphs.zh: “哦，”斯波德说，“女士们的冠军。巴德，你不仅让人钦佩，还让人恐惧。”他看着我，眼神冰冷而疑惑。“上帝啊，”他说。

paragraphs.en: “I’m sorry I hit him,” I said. “Do I look too bad to go back and get it over with?”
paragraphs.zh: “我很抱歉我打了他，”我说。“我看起来太糟糕了，无法回去解决这件事吗？”

paragraphs.en: “Apologies, hell,” Shreve said, “Let them go to hell. We’re going to town.”
paragraphs.zh: “抱歉，见鬼，”施里夫说，“让他们见鬼去吧。我们要去城里。”

paragraphs.en: “He ought to go back so they’ll know he fights like a gentleman,” Spoade said. “Gets licked like one, I mean.”
paragraphs.zh: “他应该回去，这样他们就会知道他像一位绅士一样战斗，”斯波德说。“我是说，像人一样被舔。”

paragraphs.en: “Like this?” Shreve said, “With his clothes all over blood?”
paragraphs.zh: “像这样？”施里夫说：“衣服上都是血？”

paragraphs.en: “Why, all right,” Spoade said, “You know best.”
paragraphs.zh: “好吧，”斯波德说，“你最清楚。”

paragraphs.en: “He cant go around in his undershirt,” Shreve said, “He’s not a senior yet. Come on, let’s go to town.”
paragraphs.zh: “他不能穿着背心到处走，”施里夫说，“他还不是高年级学生。走吧，我们进城去。”

paragraphs.en: “You neednt come,” I said. “You go on back to the picnic.”
paragraphs.zh: “你不必来，”我说。“你回去野餐吧。”

paragraphs.en: “Hell with them,” Shreve said. “Come on here.”
paragraphs.zh: “让他们见鬼去吧，”施里夫说。“到这里来吧。”

paragraphs.en: “What’ll I tell them?” Spoade said. “Tell them you and Quentin had a fight too?”
paragraphs.zh: “我要告诉他们什么？”斯波德说道。“告诉他们你和昆丁也吵架了？”

paragraphs.en: “Tell them nothing,” Shreve said. “Tell her her option expired at sunset. Come on, Quentin. I’ll ask that woman where the nearest interurban—”
paragraphs.zh: “什么也不告诉他们，”施里夫说。“告诉她，她的选择权在日落时就到期了。来吧，昆丁。我去问那个女人，最近的城际公路在哪里——”

paragraphs.en: “No,” I said, “I’m not going back to town.”
paragraphs.zh: “不，”我说，“我不会回城里。”

paragraphs.en: Shreve stopped, looking at me. Turning, his glasses looked like small yellow moons.
paragraphs.zh: 施里夫停了下来，看着我。转过身来，他的眼镜看起来像黄色的小月亮。

paragraphs.en: “What are you going to do?”
paragraphs.zh: “你要做什么？”

paragraphs.en: “I’m not going back to town yet. You go on back to the picnic. Tell them I wouldnt come back because my clothes were spoiled.”
paragraphs.zh: “我还不回城里。你回去去野餐吧。告诉他们我不会回来了，因为我的衣服坏了。”

paragraphs.en: “Look here,” he said, “What are you up to?”
paragraphs.zh: “看这里，”他说，“你在做什么？”

paragraphs.en: “Nothing. I’m all right. You and Spoade go on back. I’ll see you tomorrow.” I went on across the yard, toward the road.
paragraphs.zh: “没什么。我没事。你和斯波德回去吧。明天见。”我继续穿过院子，朝马路走去。

paragraphs.en: “Do you know where the station is?” Shreve said.
paragraphs.zh: “你知道车站在哪里吗？”施里夫说道。

paragraphs.en: “I’ll find it. I’ll see you all tomorrow. Tell Mrs Bland I’m sorry I spoiled her party.” They stood watching me. I went around the house. A rock path went down to the road. Roses grew on both sides of the path. I went through the gate, onto the road. It dropped downhill, toward the woods, and I could make out the auto beside the road. I went up the hill. The light increased as I mounted, and before I reached the top I heard a car. It sounded far away across the twilight and I stopped and listened to it. I couldnt make out the auto any longer, but Shreve was standing in the road before the house, looking up the hill. Behind him the yellow light lay like a wash of paint on the roof of the house. I lifted my hand and went on over the hill, listening to the car. Then the house was gone and I stopped in the green and yellow light and heard the car growing louder and louder, until just as it began to die away it ceased all together. I waited until I heard it start again. Then I went on.
paragraphs.zh: “我会找到的。明天见。告诉布兰德夫人，我很抱歉破坏了她的聚会。”他们站着看着我。我绕着房子转了一圈。一条岩石小路通向大路。小路两旁都开满了玫瑰。我穿过大门，走上马路。车子下坡，向树林驶去，我能辨认出路边的汽车。我上了山。当我登上山顶时，光线越来越亮，在我到达山顶之前，我听到了汽车的声音。暮色中传来很远的声音，我停下来听。我已经看不清那辆车了，但施里夫正站在屋前的路上，朝山上望去。在他身后，黄色的光芒就像屋顶上的一抹油漆。我举起手，继续翻过山坡，听着汽车的声音。然后房子消失了，我在绿色和黄色的灯光下停下来，听到汽车的声音越来越大，直到它开始消失时，它完全停止了。我一直等到听到它再次开始的声音。然后我继续说。

paragraphs.en: As I descended the light dwindled slowly, yet at the same time without altering its quality, as if I and not light were changing, decreasing, though even when the road ran into trees you could have read a newspaper. Pretty soon I came to a lane. I turned into it. It was closer and darker than the road, but when it came out at the trolley stop—another wooden marquee—the light was still unchanged. After the lane it seemed brighter, as though I had walked through night in the lane and come out into morning again. Pretty soon the car came. I got on it, they turning to look at my eye, and found a seat on the left side.
paragraphs.zh: 当我下降时，光线慢慢地减弱，但同时却没有改变它的质量，就好像我而不是光线在变化、减弱，尽管即使当道路碰到树木时，你也可以阅读报纸。很快我就来到了一条小巷。我变成了它。它比马路更近、更暗，但当它出现在电车车站——另一个木制大帐篷时——光线仍然没有改变。过了巷子，天色似乎明亮了一些，仿佛我在巷子里走过了黑夜，出来又到了早晨。很快车就来了。我上了车，他们转头看着我的眼睛，然后在左边找到了一个座位。

paragraphs.en: The lights were on in the car, so while we ran between trees I couldnt see anything except my own face and a woman across the aisle with a hat sitting right on top of her head, with a broken feather in it, but when we ran out of the trees I could see the twilight again, that quality of light as if time really had stopped for a while, with the sun hanging just under the horizon, and then we passed the marquee where the old man had been eating out of the sack, and the road going on under the twilight, into twilight and the sense of water peaceful and swift beyond. Then the car went on, the draught building steadily up in the open door until it was drawing steadily through the car with the odour of summer and darkness except honeysuckle. Honeysuckle was the saddest odour of all, I think. I remember lots of them. Wistaria was one. On the rainy days when Mother wasnt feeling quite bad enough to stay away from the windows we used to play under it. When Mother stayed in bed Dilsey would put old clothes on us and let us go out in the rain because she said rain never hurt young folks. But if Mother was up we always began by playing on the porch until she said we were making too much noise, then we went out and played under the wistaria frame.
paragraphs.zh: 车里的灯亮着，所以当我们在树林间奔跑时，除了我自己的脸和过道对面的一个女人，她什么也看不见，她戴着一顶帽子，帽子里插着一根折断的羽毛，但当我们跑出树林时，我又看到了暮色，那种光的质量就好像时间真的停止了一会儿，太阳挂在地平线下，然后我们经过了大帐篷，老人一直在麻袋里吃东西，路还在继续。在暮色下，进入暮色和远处水的平静和迅速的感觉。然后车子继续前行，敞开的车门里的气流逐渐上升，直到它带着夏天和黑暗的气味（除了金银花以外）稳定地穿过车子。我认为金银花是所有气味中最悲伤的。我记得很多。紫藤就是其中之一。下雨天，当母亲感觉不太难受，不能离开窗户时，我们就在窗户下玩耍。当母亲躺在床上时，迪尔西会给我们穿上旧衣服，让我们在雨中出去，因为她说雨不会伤害年轻人。但如果母亲起来了，我们总是先在门廊上玩耍，直到她说我们发出太大的声音，然后我们就出去在紫藤架下玩耍。

paragraphs.en: This was where I saw the river for the last time this morning, about here. I could feel water beyond the twilight, smell. When it bloomed in the spring and it rained the smell was everywhere you didnt notice it so much at other times but when it rained the smell began to come into the house at twilight either it would rain more at twilight or there was something in the light itself but it always smelled strongest then until I would lie in bed thinking when will it stop when will it stop. The draft in the door smelled of water, a damp steady breath. Sometimes I could put myself to sleep saying that over and over until after the honeysuckle got all mixed up in it the whole thing came to symbolise night and unrest I seemed to be lying neither asleep nor awake looking down a long corridor of grey halflight where all stable things had become shadowy paradoxical all I had done shadows all I had felt suffered taking visible form antic and perverse mocking without relevance inherent themselves with the denial of the significance they should have affirmed thinking I was I was not who was not was not who.
paragraphs.zh: 这是我今天早上最后一次看到这条河的地方，就在这儿。我能感觉到暮色之外有水的味道。春天开花的时候，下雨的时候，到处都是这种气味，在其他时候你不会注意到那么多，但是当下雨的时候，这种气味开始在黄昏时进入房子，要么黄昏时雨会更多，要么光线本身有什么东西，但它总是闻起来最强烈，直到我躺在床上思考它什么时候会停止什么时候会停止。门里的风有一股水味，一股潮湿而稳定的气息。有时我可以让自己入睡，一遍又一遍地说，直到金银花完全混合在其中之后，整个事情开始象征着黑夜和不安，我似乎躺在床上，既不睡也不醒，俯视着一条灰色半光的长廊，那里所有稳定的东西都变得阴暗自相矛盾，我所做的一切都是阴影，我所感受到的一切都以可见的形式滑稽和反常的嘲笑，与否认他们本应肯定的意义有关，认为我不是我不是谁不是谁。

paragraphs.en: I could smell the curves of the river beyond the dusk and I saw the last light supine and tranquil upon tideflats like pieces of broken mirror, then beyond them lights began in the pale clear air, trembling a little like butterflies hovering a long way off. Benjamin the child of. How he used to sit before that mirror. Refuge unfailing in which conflict tempered silenced reconciled. Benjamin the child of mine old age held hostage into Egypt. O Benjamin. Dilsey said it was because Mother was too proud for him. They come into white people’s lives like that in sudden sharp black trickles that isolate white facts for an instant in unarguable truth like under a microscope; the rest of the time just voices that laugh when you see nothing to laugh at, tears when no reason for tears. They will bet on the odd or even number of mourners at a funeral. A brothel full of them in Memphis went into a religious trance ran naked into the street. It took three policemen to subdue one of them. Yes Jesus O good man Jesus O that good man.
paragraphs.zh: 我能闻到暮色之外河流的曲线，我看到最后一道光仰卧在潮滩上，平静地像一块破碎的镜子，然后在他们身后，苍白清澈的空气中开始出现灯光，有点像蝴蝶在很远的地方盘旋一样颤抖。本杰明的孩子。他以前是如何坐在镜子前的。冲突缓和、和解的避难所始终如一。本杰明我晚年的孩子被扣为埃及人质。欧本杰明. 迪尔西说那是因为母亲太为他骄傲了。它们像突然尖锐的黑色细流一样进入白人的生活，像在显微镜下一样，将白人的事实暂时隔离在无可争议的真理中；其余的时间只是当你看到没什么可笑的时候笑，当你无缘无故流泪时流泪。他们会押注葬礼上哀悼者的人数是单数或双数。孟菲斯的一家妓院挤满了她们，她们陷入了宗教恍惚状态，赤身裸体跑到街上。三名警察才制服其中一名。是的，耶稣啊，好人啊，耶稣啊，好人。

paragraphs.en: The car stopped. I got out, with them looking at my eye. When the trolley came it was full. I stopped on the back platform.
paragraphs.zh: 车停了。我下了车，他们看着我的眼睛。手推车来的时候已经满了。我停在后面的月台上。

paragraphs.en: “Seats up front,” the conductor said. I looked into the car. There were no seats on the left side.
paragraphs.zh: “前面的座位，”售票员说。我往车里看了看。左边没有座位。

paragraphs.en: “I’m not going far,” I said. “I’ll just stand here.”
paragraphs.zh: “我不会走太远，”我说。“我就站在这里。”

paragraphs.en: We crossed the river. The bridge, that is, arching slow and high into space, between silence and nothingness where lights—yellow and red and green—trembled in the clear air, repeating themselves.
paragraphs.zh: 我们过了河。这座桥缓慢而高高地拱入太空，在寂静与虚无之间，黄色、红色和绿色的灯光在清澈的空气中颤抖，不断重复。

paragraphs.en: “Better go up front and get a seat,” the conductor said.
paragraphs.zh: “最好去前面找个座位，”售票员说。

paragraphs.en: “I get off pretty soon,” I said. “A couple of blocks.”
paragraphs.zh: “我很快就下车了，”我说。“几个街区。”

paragraphs.en: I got off before we reached the postoffice. They’d all be sitting around somewhere by now though, and then I was hearing my watch and I began to listen for the chimes and I touched Shreve’s letter through my coat, the bitten shadows of the elms flowing upon my hand. And then as I turned into the quad the chimes did begin and I went on while the notes came up like ripples on a pool and passed me and went on, saying Quarter to what? All right. Quarter to what.
paragraphs.zh: 在我们到达邮局之前我就下车了。不过，现在他们都坐在某个地方了，然后我听到了手表的声音，开始听铃声，我隔着外套触摸施里夫的信，榆树被咬过的影子在我的手上流动。然后，当我进入四重奏时，铃声确实开始了，我继续说，而音符就像池子上的涟漪一样升起，经过我，继续说，四分之一到什么？好的。四分之一到什么。

paragraphs.en: Our windows were dark. The entrance was empty. I walked close to the left wall when I entered, but it was empty: just the stairs curving up into shadows echoes of feet in the sad generations like light dust upon the shadows, my feet waking them like dust, lightly to settle again.
paragraphs.zh: 我们的窗户很暗。入口处空无一人。当我走进去时，我靠近左墙走去，但里面空无一人：只有弯曲的楼梯变成阴影，悲伤的世代中脚步的回响，就像阴影上的轻尘，我的脚像灰尘一样唤醒它们，轻轻地再次落定。

paragraphs.en: I could see the letter before I turned the light on, propped against a book on the table so I would see it. Calling him my husband. And then Spoade said they were going somewhere, would not be back until late, and Mrs Bland would need another cavalier. But I would have seen him and he cannot get another car for an hour because after six oclock. I took out my watch and listened to it clicking away, not knowing it couldnt even lie. Then I laid it face up on the table and took Mrs Bland’s letter and tore it across and dropped the pieces into the waste basket and took off my coat, vest, collar, tie and shirt. The tie was spoiled too, but then niggers. Maybe a pattern of blood he could call that the one Christ was wearing. I found the gasoline in Shreve’s room and spread the vest on the table, where it would be flat, and opened the gasoline.
paragraphs.zh: 在我打开灯之前我就可以看到这封信，它靠在桌子上的一本书上，这样我就可以看到它。称他为我的丈夫。然后斯波德说他们要去某个地方，很晚才会回来，布兰德夫人需要另一个骑士。但我本来会见到他，但他在一个小时内无法找到另一辆车，因为六点以后了。我拿出手表，听着它走动的声音，却不知道它根本不会撒谎。然后我把它面朝上放在桌子上，拿起布兰德太太的信，把它撕下来，把碎片扔进废纸篓里，然后脱掉我的外套、背心、领子、领带和衬衫。领带也被弄坏了，但还是黑鬼。也许他可以称之为基督所穿着的一种血迹。我在施里夫的房间里找到了汽油，把背心平铺在桌子上，打开汽油。

paragraphs.en: the first car in town a girl Girl that’s what Jason couldn’t bear smell of gasoline making him sick then got madder than ever because a girl Girl had no sister but Benjamin Benjamin the child of my sorrowful if I’d just had a mother so I could say Mother Mother It took a lot of gasoline, and then I couldnt tell if it was still the stain or just the gasoline. It had started the cut to smarting again so when I went to wash I hung the vest on a chair and lowered the light cord so that the bulb would be drying the splotch. I washed my face and hands, but even then I could smell it within the soap stinging, constricting the nostrils a little. Then I opened the bag and took the shirt and collar and tie out and put the bloody ones in and closed the bag, and dressed. While I was brushing my hair the half hour went. But there was until the three quarters anyway, except suppose seeing on the rushing darkness only his own face no broken feather unless two of them but not two like that going to Boston the same night then my face his face for an instant across the crashing when out of darkness two lighted windows in rigid fleeing crash gone his face and mine just I see saw did I see not goodbye the marquee empty of eating the road empty in darkness in silence the bridge arching into silence darkness sleep the water peaceful and swift not goodbye
paragraphs.zh: 城里第一辆车是个女孩，杰生无法忍受汽油味，让他恶心，然后变得比以前更疯狂，因为女孩没有妹妹，但本杰明本杰明是我的孩子，如果我只有一个母亲，我会感到悲伤，所以我可以说妈妈妈妈，花了很多汽油，然后我不知道这仍然是污渍还是只是汽油。它又开始刺痛了，所以当我去洗的时候，我把背心挂在椅子上，放下灯线，这样灯泡就能把斑点擦干。我洗了脸和手，但即便如此，我还是能闻到肥皂刺痛的味道，鼻孔有点收缩。然后我打开袋子，拿出衬衫、领子和领带，把血淋淋的放进去，关上袋子，穿好衣服。当我梳头的时候，半个小时就过去了。但无论如何，直到三刻钟为止，除了假设在汹涌的黑暗中看到只有他自己的脸没有折断的羽毛，除非他们中的两个，但不是两个像那样的人当晚去波士顿然后我的脸他的脸瞬间划过崩溃的时候，从黑暗中两扇亮着灯的窗户在僵硬的逃逸中崩溃消失了他的脸和我的只是我看到看到我没有看到再见空空的大帐篷在沉默中空空的黑暗中桥梁拱入沉默黑暗睡眠水平静而迅速不是再见

paragraphs.en: I turned out the light and went into my bedroom, out of the gasoline but I could still smell it. I stood at the window the curtains moved slow out of the darkness touching my face like someone breathing asleep, breathing slow into the darkness again, leaving the touch. After they had gone up stairs Mother lay back in her chair, the camphor handkerchief to her mouth. Father hadn’t moved he still sat beside her holding her hand the bellowing hammering away like no place for it in silence When I was little there was a picture in one of our books, a dark place into which a single weak ray of light came slanting upon two faces lifted out of the shadow. You know what I’d do if I were King? she never was a queen or a fairy she was always a king or a giant or a general I’d break that place open and drag them out and I’d whip them good It was torn out, jagged out. I was glad. I’d have to turn back to it until the dungeon was Mother herself she and Father upward into weak light holding hands and us lost somewhere below even them without even a ray of light. Then the honeysuckle got into it. As soon as I turned off the light and tried to go to sleep it would begin to come into the room in waves building and building up until I would have to pant to get any air at all out of it until I would have to get up and feel my way like when I was a little boy hands can see touching in the mind shaping unseen door Door now nothing hands can see My nose could see gasoline, the vest on the table, the door. The corridor was still empty of all the feet in sad generations seeking water. yet the eyes unseeing clenched like teeth not disbelieving doubting even the absence of pain shin ankle knee the long invisible flowing of the stair-railing where a misstep in the darkness filled with sleeping Mother Father Caddy Jason Maury door I am not afraid only Mother Father Caddy Jason Maury getting so far ahead sleeping I will sleep fast when I door Door door It was empty too, the pipes, the porcelain, the stained quiet walls, the throne of contemplation. I had forgotten the glass, but I could hands can see cooling fingers invisible swan-throat where less than Moses rod the glass touch tentative not to drumming lean cool throat drumming cooling the metal the glass full overfull cooling the glass the fingers flushing sleep leaving the taste of dampened sleep in the long silence of the throat I returned up the corridor, waking the lost feet in whispering battalions in the silence, into the gasoline, the watch telling its furious lie on the dark table. Then the curtains breathing out of the dark upon my face, leaving the breathing upon my face. A quarter hour yet. And then I’ll not be. The peacefullest words. Peacefullest words. Non fui. Sum. Fui. Nom sum. Somewhere I heard bells once. Mississippi or Massachusetts. I was. I am not. Massachusetts or Mississippi. Shreve has a bottle in his trunk. Aren’t you even going to open it Mr and Mrs Jason Richmond Compson announce the Three times. Days. Aren’t you even going to open it marriage of their daughter Candace that liquor teaches you to confuse the means with the end. I am. Drink. I was not. Let us sell Benjy’s pasture so that Quentin may go to Harvard and I may knock my bones together and together. I will be dead in. Was it one year Caddy said. Shreve has a bottle in his trunk. Sir I will not need Shreve’s I have sold Benjy’s pasture and I can be dead in Harvard Caddy said in the caverns and the grottoes of the sea tumbling peacefully to the wavering tides because Harvard is such a fine sound forty acres is no high price for a fine sound. A find dead sound we will swap Benjy’s pasture for a fine dead sound. It will last him a long time because he cannot hear it unless he can smell it as soon as she came in the door he began to cry I thought all the time it was just one of those town squirts that Father was always teasing her about until. I didnt notice him any more than any other stranger drummer or what thought they were army shirts until all of a sudden I knew he wasn’t thinking of me at all as a potential source of harm, but was thinking of her when he looked at me was looking at me through her like through a piece of coloured glass why must you meddle with me dont you know it wont do any good I thought you’d have left that for Mother and Jason
paragraphs.zh: 我关掉灯，走进卧室，汽油味消失了，但我仍然能闻到它的味道。我站在窗前，窗帘慢慢地从黑暗中移出，触碰着我的脸，就像一个熟睡的人，再次缓慢地呼吸到黑暗中，留下了触感。他们上楼后，母亲靠在椅子上，把樟脑帕放在嘴边。父亲没有动，仍然坐在她身边，握着她的手，轰鸣声敲打着，仿佛寂静无处可容。当我还小的时候，我们的一本书中有一幅图画，一个黑暗的地方，一束微弱的光线斜射在两张从阴影中抬起的脸上。你知道如果我是国王我会做什么吗？她从来不是女王或仙女，她永远是国王、巨人或将军，我会把那个地方打开，把他们拖出来，我会把他们鞭打好，它被撕掉了，锯齿状的。我很高兴。我必须回头看，直到地牢变成母亲本人，她和父亲手牵手向上进入微弱的光线，而我们迷失在下面的某个地方，甚至连他们都没有一丝光亮。然后金银花就进去了。当我关掉灯并试图去睡觉时，它就会开始以波浪的形式进入房间，越来越大，直到我不得不气喘吁吁地从里面吸出任何空气，直到我不得不站起来摸索，就像我还是个小男孩时一样，手可以看到心灵中的触摸，塑造看不见的门，现在手什么都看不到了，我的鼻子可以看到汽油，桌子上的背心，门。走廊里仍然空无一人，悲伤的一代代人都在寻找水源。然而眼睛却看不见，像牙齿一样咬紧，不相信，怀疑，甚至没有疼痛，小腿脚踝膝盖，长长的隐形流动的楼梯栏杆，在黑暗中的一个失误，充满了熟睡的父亲凯蒂杰生莫里门，我不害怕，只有母亲父亲凯蒂杰生莫里睡得这么远，当我开门时，我会睡得很快，门门也空了，管道，瓷器，肮脏的安静的墙壁，沉思的宝座。我忘记了玻璃，但我能看到双手能看到冷却的手指看不见的天鹅喉咙，不到摩西杆触碰玻璃试探性地不敲击，精益凉爽的喉咙敲击冷却金属，玻璃满溢出，冷却玻璃，手指冲洗睡眠，在喉咙的长期沉默中留下潮湿的睡眠味道。然后窗帘从黑暗中呼出气息，落在我脸上，把呼吸留在我脸上。还有一刻钟。然后我就不会了。最平静的话语。最平静的话语。非福伊。和。富伊。名义总和。我曾经在某个地方听到过钟声。密西西比州或马萨诸塞州。我是。我不是。马萨诸塞州或密西西比州。施里夫的行李箱里有一瓶。你不打算打开它吗？杰生里士满康普生先生和夫人宣布了三遍。天。难道你不打算打开他们女儿坎迪斯的婚姻吗？酒精教会你混淆手段与结果。我是。喝。我不是。让我们卖掉班吉的牧场吧，这样昆丁就可以去哈佛了，我也可以把我的骨头敲在一起，敲在一起。我会死的。凯蒂说是一年吗？施里夫的行李箱里有一瓶。先生，我不需要施里夫的，我已经卖掉了班吉的牧场，我可以死在哈佛了。凯蒂说，在大海的洞穴和石窟里，平静地随着波动的潮汐翻滚，因为哈佛是如此美好的声音，四十英亩对于一个美好的声音来说，价格并不高。找到死声音我们将把班吉的牧场换成精美的死声音。这会持续他很长一段时间，因为他听不到，除非他能闻到。她一进门，他就开始哭。我一直以为这只是父亲总是取笑她的镇上的水鬼之一。我没有比任何其他陌生人鼓手更注意到他，也没有想到他们是军衬衫，直到突然间我知道他根本没有把我视为潜在的伤害源，而是在想她，当他看着我时，他就像透过一块有色玻璃一样透过她看着我，为什么你一定要干涉我，你不知道这不会有任何好处，我以为你会把它留给母亲和杰生

paragraphs.en: did Mother set Jason to spy on you I wouldnt have.
paragraphs.zh: 是妈妈让杰生监视你的吗？我不会的。

paragraphs.en: Women only use other people’s codes of honour it’s because she loves Caddy staying downstairs even when she was sick so Father couldnt kid Uncle Maury before Jason Father said Uncle Maury was too poor a classicist to risk the blind immortal boy in person he should have chosen Jason because Jason would have made only the same kind of blunder Uncle Maury himself would have made not one to get him a black eye the Patterson boy was smaller than Jason too they sold the kites for a nickel apiece until the trouble over finances Jason got a new partner still smaller one small enough anyway because T. P. said Jason still treasurer but Father said why should Uncle Maury work if he father could support five or six niggers that did nothing at all but sit with their feet in the oven he certainly could board and lodge Uncle Maury now and then and lend him a little money who kept his Father’s belief in the celestial derivation of his own species at such a fine heat then Mother would cry and say that Father believed his people were better than hers that he was ridiculing Uncle Maury to teach us the same thing she couldnt see that Father was teaching us that all men are just accumulations dolls stuffed with sawdust swept up from the trash heaps where all previous dolls had been thrown away the sawdust flowing from what wound in what side that not for me died not. It used to be I thought of death as a man something like Grandfather a friend of his a kind of private and particular friend like we used to think of Grandfather’s desk not to touch it not even to talk loud in the room where it was I always thought of them as being together somewhere all the time waiting for old Colonel Sartoris to come down and sit with them waiting on a high place beyond cedar trees Colonel Sartoris was on a still higher place looking out across at something and they were waiting for him to get done looking at it and come down Grandfather wore his uniform and we could hear the murmur of their voices from beyond the cedars they were always talking and Grandfather was always right
paragraphs.zh: 女人只用别人的荣誉准则，因为她喜欢凯蒂在楼下，即使她生病了，所以父亲不能在杰生之前欺骗莫里舅舅。父亲说，莫里舅舅太可怜了，他是一位古典主义者，不能亲自冒着盲目的不朽男孩的风险，他应该选择杰生，因为杰生只会犯同样的错误，莫里舅舅自己也会犯同样的错误，不会让他打青，帕特森男孩也比杰生小，他们杰生把风筝卖了一个五分钱，直到财务问题杰生找到了一个新的合伙人，还是更小的一个足够小，因为蒂·皮说杰生仍然是财务主管，但父亲说莫里舅舅为什么要工作，如果他父亲能养活五六个黑鬼，他们什么都不做，只是坐在烤箱里，他当然可以时不时地寄宿莫里舅舅，借给他一点钱，让他的父亲在这样的情况下保持对他自己物种的天体起源的信念。妈妈会哭着说，父亲相信他的人民比她的人民更好，他在嘲笑莫里舅舅教我们同样的事情，她看不到父亲在教我们，所有的男人都只是从垃圾堆里扫出来的木屑塞满的娃娃，以前的娃娃都被扔掉了，木屑从哪一边的伤口流出来，不为我而死。我曾经把死亡视为一个人，就像祖父一样，是他的朋友，是一种私人的、特殊的朋友，就像我们过去常常想到祖父的桌子一样，不能碰它，甚至不能在房间里大声说话。看完了，下来了，祖父穿着制服，我们可以听到雪松后面传来他们的低语声，他们总是在说话，祖父总是对的

paragraphs.zh: 三季度开始了。第一个音符响起，分寸而平静，平静而专横，为下一个音符清空了从容的沉默，那就是，如果人们只能永远改变彼此，那么就像火焰一样融合在一起，瞬间旋转，然后沿着凉爽的永恒黑暗被彻底吹散，而不是躺在那里试图不去想秋千，直到所有的雪松都散发出班吉如此讨厌的生动的死香水味。仅仅通过想象那团，在我看来，我就可以听到低语声，秘密的浪潮，闻到狂野不秘密的肉体下热血的跳动，注视着红色的眼睑，不受束缚的猪成双成对地冲入大海，我们必须保持清醒，看到邪恶发生一段时间，这并不总是如此，对于一个有勇气的人来说，甚至不需要那么长的时间，你认为这种勇气吗？是的，先生，你不，他每个人都是他自己的美德，无论你是否认为勇敢，都比行为本身比任何行为更重要，否则你就不可能是认真的，我你不相信我是认真的，我认为你太认真了，不会给我任何惊慌的理由，否则你不会感到被迫告诉我你犯了乱伦，否则我没有说谎，我没有说谎，他你想把人类自然的愚蠢升华为恐怖，然后用事实驱除它，我是把她从喧闹的世界中孤立出来，这样它就必须逃离我们的需要，然后它的声音就好像它从未存在过一样，他做了你试图让她这样做，我我害怕我担心她可能会这样做，然后它不会有任何好处，但如果我能告诉你我们做到了，那么其他人就不会如此，然后世界就会咆哮消失，他和现在这个另一个你现在也没有说谎，但你仍然对你自己的那部分的东西视而不见。一般真理自然事件的顺序及其原因，笼罩着每个人的额头，即使是本吉斯，你不是在思考有限性，你正在考虑一种神化，在这种神化中，暂时的精神状态将在肉体之上变得对称，并意识到两者本身和肉体，它不会完全抛弃你，甚至不会死，我是暂时的，你无法忍受认为有一天它不会再像现在这样伤害你，你似乎只把它当作一种经历，可以在一夜之间变白你的头发，可以说，在不改变你的外表的情况下，你不会这样做，在这种情况下，这将是一场赌博，奇怪的是，一个偶然怀孕的人，他的每一次呼吸都是一个新的骰子，已经装在他身上，他不会面对这样的情况。他事先就知道他必须面对的最后一个主要问题，而无需采取各种权宜之计，从暴力到小诡计，这些权宜之计不会欺骗一个孩子，直到有一天，他在非常厌恶的情况下，盲目地翻牌，冒着一切风险。没有人会在绝望、悔恨或丧亲之痛的第一怒之下这样做，只有当他意识到即使是绝望、悔恨或丧亲之痛对黑暗骰子来说也不是特别重要时，我是暂时的，他是这样的。很难相信爱情或悲伤是一种未经设计而购买的债券，它会随心所欲地成熟，在没有任何警告的情况下被召回，被当时诸神碰巧漂浮的任何问题所取代，不，你不会这样做，除非你开始相信，即使她也不完全值得绝望，我我永远不会这样做，没有人知道我知道什么，他我认为你最好立即去剑桥，你可能会去缅因州一个月，如果你小心的话，你可以负担得起，这可能是一个很好的选择。观看便士的事情比耶稣治愈了更多的伤疤，我想我意识到了你所相信的，下周或下个月我会在那里实现，然后他你会记得，自从你出生以来，去哈佛一直是你母亲的梦想，没有哪个康普生曾经让一位女士失望过，我暂时对我们所有人来说都会更好，他每个人都是自己美德的仲裁者，但不要让任何人为另一个人的福祉开处方，我暂时，他是最悲伤的人总而言之，世界上没有其他事情，它不是绝望，直到时间，甚至不是时间，直到它出现

paragraphs.en: The last note sounded. At last it stopped vibrating and the darkness was still again. I entered the sitting room and turned on the light. I put my vest on. The gasoline was faint now, barely noticeable, and in the mirror the stain didnt show. Not like my eye did, anyway. I put on my coat. Shreve’s letter crackled through the cloth and I took it out and examined the address, and put it in my side pocket. Then I carried the watch into Shreve’s room and put it in his drawer and went to my room and got a fresh handkerchief and went to the door and put my hand on the light switch. Then I remembered I hadnt brushed my teeth, so I had to open the bag again. I found my toothbrush and got some of Shreve’s paste and went out and brushed my teeth. I squeezed the brush as dry as I could and put it back in the bag and shut it, and went to the door again. Before I snapped the light out I looked around to see if there was anything else, then I saw that I had forgotten my hat. I’d have to go by the postoffice and I’d be sure to meet some of them, and they’d think I was a Harvard Square student making like he was a senior. I had forgotten to brush it too, but Shreve had a brush, so I didnt have to open the bag any more.
paragraphs.zh: 最后一个音符响起。最后它停止了震动，黑暗又归于寂静。我走进客厅，打开灯。我穿上背心。汽油现在很淡，几乎无法察觉，镜子里也看不到污渍。无论如何，不​​像我的眼睛。我穿上外套。施里夫的信透过布噼啪作响，我把它拿出来，检查了地址，然后把它放进了我的侧袋里。然后我把手表带进施里夫的房间，放进他的抽屉里，然后走进自己的房间，拿了一块新手帕，走到门口，把手放在电灯开关上。然后我想起我还没有刷牙，所以我不得不再次打开袋子。我找到牙刷，拿了一些施里夫的牙膏，出去刷牙。我尽可能地把刷子挤干，然后把它放回袋子里，关上袋子，然后又向门口走去。在我关掉灯之前，我环顾四周看看是否还有其他东西，然后我发现我忘记带帽子了。我必须去邮局，我肯定会遇到他们中的一些人，他们会认为我是哈佛广场的学生，表现得像个大四学生。我也忘记刷了，不过施里夫有刷子，所以我不用再打开包了。

paragraphs.en: Once a bitch always a bitch, what I say. I says you’re lucky if her playing out of school is all that worries you. I says she ought to be down there in that kitchen right now, instead of up there in her room, gobbing paint on her face and waiting for six niggers that cant even stand up out of a chair unless they’ve got a pan full of bread and meat to balance them, to fix breakfast for her. And Mother says,
paragraphs.zh: 一回是婊子，一辈子都是婊子，我就是这么说的。我说，要是你担心的只是她逃学，那你可真走运。我说她这会儿就该待在下面厨房里，别躲在楼上自己房间里，往脸上抹脂粉，等着六个黑鬼给她做早饭；那帮人，要不是有一盘面包和肉坠着给他们找平衡，连从椅子上站起来都做不到。母亲就说，

paragraphs.en: “But to have the school authorities think that I have no control over her, that I cant—”
paragraphs.zh: “但是学校当局认为我无法控制她，我不能——”

paragraphs.en: “Well,” I says, “You cant, can you? You never have tried to do anything with her,” I says, “How do you expect to begin this late, when she’s seventeen years old?”
paragraphs.zh: “好吧，”我说，“你不能，对吧？你从来没有尝试过对她做任何事，”我说，“你怎么能指望这么晚才开始呢，她已经十七岁了？”

paragraphs.en: She thought about that for a while.
paragraphs.zh: 她想了一会儿。

paragraphs.en: “But to have them think that . . . I didn’t even know she had a report card. She told me last fall that they had quit using them this year. And now for Professor Junkin to call me on the telephone and tell me if she’s absent one more time, she will have to leave school. How does she do it? Where does she go? You’re down town all day; you ought to see her if she stays on the streets.”
paragraphs.zh: “但是让他们认为……我什至不知道她有成绩单。去年秋天她告诉我，他们今年不再使用成绩单。现在琼金教授打电话告诉我，如果她再缺课一次，她就必须离开学校。她是怎么做到的？她去哪里？你整天都在城里；如果她留在街上，你应该看看她。”

paragraphs.en: “Yes,” I says, “If she stayed on the streets. I dont reckon she’d be playing out of school just to do something she could do in public,” I says.
paragraphs.zh: “是的，”我说，“如果她留在街上。我认为她不会为了做一些她可以在公共场合做的事情而在学校外面玩耍。”我说。

paragraphs.en: “What do you mean?” she says.
paragraphs.zh: “你什么意思？”她说。

paragraphs.en: “I dont mean anything,” I says. “I just answered your question.” Then she begun to cry again, talking about how her own flesh and blood rose up to curse her.
paragraphs.zh: “我没什么意思，”我说。“我刚刚回答了你的问题。”然后她又开始哭泣，讲述着自己的亲骨肉如何站起来咒骂她。

paragraphs.en: “You asked me,” I says.
paragraphs.zh: “你问我了，”我说。

paragraphs.en: “I dont mean you,” she says. “You are the only one of them that isn’t a reproach to me.”
paragraphs.zh: “我不是说你，”她说。“他们之中，只有你一个没有责怪我。”

paragraphs.en: “Sure,” I says, “I never had time to be. I never had time to go to Harvard like Quentin or drink myself into the ground like Father. I had to work. But of course if you want me to follow her around and see what she does, I can quit the store and get a job where I can work at night. Then I can watch her during the day and you can use Ben for the night shift.”
paragraphs.zh: “当然，”我说，“我从来没有时间。我从来没有时间像昆丁那样去哈佛，也没有时间像父亲那样喝得酩酊大醉。我必须工作。但是当然，如果你想让我跟着她，看看她做什么，我可以离开商店，找一份可以晚上工作的工作。然后我可以白天照顾她，你可以让本上夜班。”

paragraphs.en: “I know I’m just a trouble and a burden to you,” she says, crying on the pillow.
paragraphs.zh: “我知道我对你来说只是一个麻烦和负担，”她在枕头上哭泣着说道。

paragraphs.en: “I ought to know it,” I says. “You’ve been telling me that for thirty years. Even Ben ought to know it now. Do you want me to say anything to her about it?”
paragraphs.zh: “我应该知道，”我说。“这件事你已经告诉我三十年了。现在就连本也应该知道了。你想让我对她说点什么吗？”

paragraphs.en: “Do you think it will do any good?” she says.
paragraphs.zh: “你觉得这有什么好处吗？”她说。

paragraphs.en: “Not if you come down there interfering just when I get started,” I says. “If you want me to control her, just say so and keep your hands off. Everytime I try to, you come butting in and then she gives both of us the laugh.”
paragraphs.zh: “如果你在我开始的时候过来干扰的话，就不会了，”我说。“如果你想让我控制她，就直接说出来，别把手拿开。每次我试图控制她时，你都会插嘴，然后她就会让我们俩都笑起来。”

paragraphs.en: “Remember she’s your own flesh and blood,” she says.
paragraphs.zh: “记住她是你的骨肉，”她说。

paragraphs.en: “Sure,” I says, “that’s just what I’m thinking of—flesh. And a little blood too, if I had my way. When people act like niggers, no matter who they are the only thing to do is treat them like a nigger.”
paragraphs.zh: “当然，”我说，“这正是我所想的——肉。如果我愿意的话，还有一点血。当人们表现得像黑鬼时，无论他们是谁，唯一能做的就是像对待黑鬼一样对待他们。”

paragraphs.en: “I’m afraid you’ll lose your temper with her,” she says.
paragraphs.zh: “我担心你会对她发脾气，”她说。

paragraphs.en: “Well,” I says, “You haven’t had much luck with your system. You want me to do anything about it, or not? Say one way or the other; I’ve got to get on to work.”
paragraphs.zh: “好吧，”我说，“你的系统运气不太好。你想让我做点什么吗？不管怎样，我得继续工作了。”

paragraphs.en: “I know you have to slave your life away for us,” she says. “You know if I had my way, you’d have an office of your own to go to, and hours that became a Bascomb. Because you are a Bascomb, despite your name. I know that if your father could have forseen—”
paragraphs.zh: “我知道你必须为我们付出生命，”她说。“你知道，如果我按照我的方式行事，你就会有自己的办公室，并且有成为巴斯科姆人的工作时间。因为你是巴斯科姆人，不管你的名字如何。我知道，如果你的父亲能够预见到的话——”

paragraphs.en: “Well,” I says, “I reckon he’s entitled to guess wrong now and then, like anybody else, even a Smith or a Jones.” She begun to cry again.
paragraphs.zh: “嗯，”我说，“我认为他有权利偶尔猜错，就像其他人一样，即使是史密斯或琼斯。”她又开始哭了。

paragraphs.en: “To hear you speak bitterly of your dead father,” she says.
paragraphs.zh: “听到你痛苦地谈论你死去的父亲，”她说。

paragraphs.en: “All right,” I says, “all right. Have it your way. But as I haven’t got an office, I’ll have to get on to what I have got. Do you want me to say anything to her?”
paragraphs.zh: “好吧，”我说，“好吧。随你便吧。但由于我没有办公室，所以我必须继续我所拥有的工作。你想让我对她说什么吗？”

paragraphs.en: “I’m afraid you’ll lose your temper with her,” she says.
paragraphs.zh: “我担心你会对她发脾气，”她说。

paragraphs.en: “All right,” I says, “I wont say anything, then.”
paragraphs.zh: “好吧，”我说，“那我什么也不说了。”

paragraphs.en: “But something must be done,” she says. “To have people think I permit her to stay out of school and run about the streets, or that I cant prevent her doing it. . . . Jason, Jason,” she says, “How could you. How could you leave me with these burdens.”
paragraphs.zh: “但必须采取一些措施，”她说。“让人们认为我允许她不上学，在街上乱跑，或者我无法阻止她这样做……杰生，杰生，”她说，“你怎么能。你怎么能让我背负这些负担。”

paragraphs.en: “Now, now,” I says, “You’ll make yourself sick. Why dont you either lock her up all day too, or turn her over to me and quit worrying over her?”
paragraphs.zh: “现在，现在，”我说，“你会让自己生病的。你为什么不把她也关起来一整天，或者把她交给我，不再担心她呢？”

paragraphs.en: “My own flesh and blood,” she says, crying. So I says,
paragraphs.zh: “我自己的骨肉，”她哭着说道。所以我说，

paragraphs.en: “All right. I’ll tend to her. Quit crying, now.”
paragraphs.zh: “好吧。我会照顾她的。现在别哭了。”

paragraphs.en: “Dont lose your temper,” she says. “She’s just a child, remember.”
paragraphs.zh: “别发脾气，”她说。“她只是个孩子，记住。”

paragraphs.en: “No,” I says, “I wont.” I went out, closing the door.
paragraphs.zh: “不，”我说，“我不会。”我出去了，关上门。

paragraphs.en: “Jason,” she says. I didn’t answer. I went down the hall. “Jason,” she says beyond the door. I went on down stairs. There wasn’t anybody in the diningroom, then I heard her in the kitchen. She was trying to make Dilsey let her have another cup of coffee. I went in.
paragraphs.zh: “杰生，”她说。我没有回答。我沿着大厅走去。“杰生，”她在门外说道。我继续下楼梯。餐厅里没有人，然后我听到她在厨房里。她试图让迪尔西再让她喝一杯咖啡。我进去了。

paragraphs.en: “I reckon that’s your school costume, is it?” I says. “Or maybe today’s a holiday?”
paragraphs.zh: “我想那是你的校服，是吗？”我说。“或者也许今天是假期？”

paragraphs.en: “Just a half a cup, Dilsey,” she says. “Please.”
paragraphs.zh: “只要半杯，迪尔西，”她说。“请。”

paragraphs.en: “No, suh,” Dilsey says, “I aint gwine do it. You aint got no business wid mo’n one cup, a seventeen year old gal, let lone whut Miss Cahline say. You go on and git dressed for school, so you kin ride to town wid Jason. You fixin to be late again.”
paragraphs.zh: “不，先生，”迪尔西说，“我不会这么做的。你和我一个十七岁的女孩没有关系，不管卡林小姐怎么说。你继续穿好衣服去学校，所以你可以和杰生一起骑车去城里。你又要迟到了。”

paragraphs.en: “No she’s not,” I says. “We’re going to fix that right now.” She looked at me, the cup in her hand. She brushed her hair back from her face, her kimono slipping off her shoulder. “You put that cup down and come in here a minute,” I says.
paragraphs.zh: “不，她不是，”我说。“我们现在就解决这个问题。”她手里拿着杯子，看着我。她把头发从脸上拨开，和服从肩上滑落。“你把杯子放下，到这里来一下，”我说。

paragraphs.en: “What for?” she says.
paragraphs.zh: “干什么？”她说。

paragraphs.en: “Come on,” I says. “Put that cup in the sink and come in here.”
paragraphs.zh: “来吧，”我说。“把杯子放在水槽里，然后进来。”

paragraphs.en: “What you up to now, Jason?” Dilsey says.
paragraphs.zh: “杰生，你现在在做什么？”迪尔西说道。

paragraphs.en: “You may think you can run over me like you do your grandmother and everybody else,” I says, “But you’ll find out different. I’ll give you ten seconds to put that cup down like I told you.”
paragraphs.zh: “你可能认为你可以像对待你的祖母和其他人一样从我身上碾过去，”我说，“但你会发现不同。我会给你十秒钟的时间，让你像我告诉你的那样把杯子放下。”

paragraphs.en: She quit looking at me. She looked at Dilsey. “What time is it, Dilsey?” she says. “When it’s ten seconds, you whistle. Just a half a cup. Dilsey, pl—”
paragraphs.zh: 她不再看我了。她看着迪尔西。“迪尔西，现在几点了？”她说。“十秒的时候，你吹口哨。就半杯。迪尔西，请——”

paragraphs.en: I grabbed her by the arm. She dropped the cup. It broke on the floor and she jerked back, looking at me, but I held her arm. Dilsey got up from her chair.
paragraphs.zh: 我抓住她的手臂。她把杯子掉了。它在地板上摔碎了，她猛地向后退去，看着我，但我抓住了她的手臂。迪尔西从椅子上站起来。

paragraphs.en: “You, Jason,” she says.
paragraphs.zh: “你，杰生，”她说。

paragraphs.en: “You turn me loose,” Quentin says, “I’ll slap you.”
paragraphs.zh: 昆丁说：“你放开我，我就扇你耳光。”

paragraphs.en: “You will, will you?” I says, “You will will you?” She slapped at me. I caught that hand too and held her like a wildcat. “You will, will you?” I says. “You think you will?”
paragraphs.zh: “你会的，是吗？”我说：“你愿意吗？”她打了我一巴掌。我也抓住了那只手，像一只野猫一样抱着她。“你会的，是吗？”我说。“你觉得你会吗？”

paragraphs.en: “You, Jason!” Dilsey says. I dragged her into the diningroom. Her kimono came unfastened, flapping about her, damn near naked. Dilsey came hobbling along. I turned and kicked the door shut in her face.
paragraphs.zh: “你，杰生！”迪尔西说道。我拉着她进了餐厅。她的和服解开了，在她身上飘扬，几乎赤身裸体。迪尔西一瘸一拐地走来。我转身，当着她的面把门踢上。

paragraphs.en: “You keep out of here,” I says.
paragraphs.zh: “你别来这里，”我说。

paragraphs.en: Quentin was leaning against the table, fastening her kimono. I looked at her.
paragraphs.zh: 昆丁靠在桌子上，系好和服。我看着她。

paragraphs.en: “Now,” I says, “I want to know what you mean, playing out of school and telling your grandmother lies and forging her name on your report and worrying her sick. What do you mean by it?”
paragraphs.zh: “现在，”我说，“我想知道你在学校外玩耍、对你祖母撒谎、在你的报告上伪造她的名字并担心她生病是什么意思。你这是什么意思？”

paragraphs.en: She didn’t say anything. She was fastening her kimono up under her chin, pulling it tight around her, looking at me. She hadn’t got around to painting herself yet and her face looked like she had polished it with a gun rag. I went and grabbed her wrist. “What do you mean?” I says.
paragraphs.zh: 她什么也没说。她把和服系在下巴下面，紧紧地裹住自己，看着我。她还没来得及给自己画画，她的脸看起来就像是用抹布擦过的一样。我走过去抓住她的手腕。“你是什么意思？”我说。

paragraphs.en: “None of your damn business,” she says. “You turn me loose.”
paragraphs.zh: “不关你的事，”她说。“你放开我。”

paragraphs.en: Dilsey came in the door. “You, Jason,” she says.
paragraphs.zh: 迪尔西进门了。“你，杰生，”她说。

paragraphs.en: “You get out of here, like I told you,” I says, not even looking back. “I want to know where you go when you play out of school,” I says. “You keep off the streets, or I’d see you. Who do you play out with? Are you hiding out in the woods with one of those damn slick-headed jellybeans? Is that where you go?”
paragraphs.zh: “你离开这里，就像我告诉你的那样，”我说，甚至没有回头。“我想知道你放学后去哪里玩，”我说。“你别上街，否则我会看到你的。你和谁一起玩？你是不是和那些该死的油头软糖一起躲在树林里？那是你去的地方吗？”

paragraphs.en: “You—you old goddamn!” she says. She fought, but I held her. “You damn old goddamn!” she says.
paragraphs.zh: “你——你这个老混蛋！”她说。她反抗，但我抱住了她。“你这个该死的老家伙！”她说。

paragraphs.en: “I’ll show you,” I says. “You may can scare an old woman off, but I’ll show you who’s got hold of you now.” I held her with one hand, then she quit fighting and watched me, her eyes getting wide and black.
paragraphs.zh: “我会告诉你，”我说。“你可能会吓跑一个老太婆，但我会让你看看现在是谁抓住了你。”我用一只手握住她，然后她停止战斗并看着我，她的眼睛睁得大大的，黑色的。

paragraphs.en: “What are you going to do?” she says.
paragraphs.zh: “你要做什么？”她说。

paragraphs.en: “You wait until I get this belt out and I’ll show you,” I says, pulling my belt out. Then Dilsey grabbed my arm.
paragraphs.zh: “你等我把这条腰带拿出来给你看，”我一边说，一边把腰带拉出来。然后迪尔西抓住了我的手臂。

paragraphs.en: “Jason,” she says, “You, Jason! Aint you shamed of yourself.”
paragraphs.zh: “杰生，”她说，“你，杰生！你不是为自己感到羞耻吗？”

paragraphs.en: “Dilsey,” Quentin says, “Dilsey.”
paragraphs.zh: “迪尔西，”昆丁说，“迪尔西。”

paragraphs.en: “I aint gwine let him,” Dilsey says, “Dont you worry, honey.” She held to my arm. Then the belt came out and I jerked loose and flung her away. She stumbled into the table. She was so old she couldn’t do any more than move hardly. But that’s all right: we need somebody in the kitchen to eat up the grub the young ones cant tote off. She came hobbling between us, trying to hold me again. “Hit me, den,” she says, “ef nothin else but hittin somebody wont do you. Hit me,” she says.
paragraphs.zh: “我不会让他这么做，”迪尔西说，“别担心，亲爱的。”她握住我的手臂。然后皮带掉了出来，我猛地松开，把她扔开了。她跌跌撞撞地撞到了桌子上。她太老了，除了几乎无法动弹之外，什么也做不了。但这没关系：我们需要有人在厨房里吃掉小孩子无法带走的食物。她一瘸一拐地来到我们中间，试图再次抱住我。“打我，书房，”她说，“除非打别人，否则不会对你造成伤害。打我，”她说。

paragraphs.en: “You think I wont?” I says.
paragraphs.zh: “你认为我不会？”我说。

paragraphs.en: “I dont put no devilment beyond you,” she says. Then I heard Mother on the stairs. I might have known she wasn’t going to keep out of it. I let go. She stumbled back against the wall, holding her kimono shut.
paragraphs.zh: “我不会对你施加任何恶意，”她说。然后我听到妈妈在楼梯上。我可能知道她不会袖手旁观。我放手了。她跌跌撞撞地靠在墙上，紧紧抓住和服。

paragraphs.en: “All right,” I says, “We’ll just put this off a while. But dont think you can run it over me. I’m not an old woman, nor an old half dead nigger, either. You damn little slut,” I says.
paragraphs.zh: “好吧，”我说，“我们就把这件事推迟一段时间。但是别以为你能把它压在我身上。我不是一个老太婆，也不是一个半死不活的老黑鬼。你这个该死的小荡妇，”我说。

paragraphs.en: “Dilsey,” she says, “Dilsey, I want my mother.”
paragraphs.zh: “迪尔西，”她说，“迪尔西，我想要我的妈妈。”

paragraphs.en: Dilsey went to her. “Now, now,” she says, “He aint gwine so much as lay his hand on you while Ise here.” Mother came on down the stairs.
paragraphs.zh: 迪尔西走到她身边。“现在，现在，”她说，“一诚在这里的时候，他根本就没有把手放在你身上。”妈妈从楼梯上下来了。

paragraphs.en: “Jason,” she says, “Dilsey.”
paragraphs.zh: “杰生，”她说，“迪尔西。”

paragraphs.en: “Now, now,” Dilsey says, “I aint gwine let him tech you.” She put her hand on Quentin. She knocked it down.
paragraphs.zh: “现在，现在，”迪尔西说，“我不会让他科技你。”她把手放在昆丁身上。她把它打倒了。

paragraphs.en: “You damn old nigger,” she says. She ran toward the door.
paragraphs.zh: “你这个该死的老黑鬼，”她说。她跑向门口。

paragraphs.en: “Dilsey,” Mother says on the stairs. Quentin ran up the stairs, passing her. “Quentin,” Mother says, “You, Quentin.” Quentin ran on. I could hear her when she reached the top, then in the hall. Then the door slammed.
paragraphs.zh: “迪尔西，”母亲在楼梯上说道。昆丁跑上楼梯，从她身边经过。“昆丁，”妈妈说，“你，昆丁。”昆丁继续跑。当她到达顶部，然后到达大厅时，我能听到她的声音。然后门关上了。

paragraphs.en: Mother had stopped. Then she came on. “Dilsey,” she says.
paragraphs.zh: 母亲停了下来。然后她就上来了。“迪尔西，”她说。

paragraphs.en: “All right,” Dilsey says, “Ise comin. You go on and git dat car and wait now,” she says, “so you kin cahy her to school.”
paragraphs.zh: “好吧，”迪尔西说，“我来了。你继续开那辆车，现在就等着，”她说，“这样你就可以送她去学校了。”

paragraphs.en: “Dont you worry,” I says. “I’ll take her to school and I’m going to see that she stays there. I’ve started this thing, and I’m going through with it.”
paragraphs.zh: “别担心，”我说。“我会带她去学校，我会确保她留在那儿。我已经开始了这件事，并且正在完成它。”

paragraphs.en: “Jason,” Mother says on the stairs.
paragraphs.zh: “杰生，”妈妈在楼梯上说道。

paragraphs.en: “Go on, now,” Dilsey says, going toward the door. “You want to git her started too? Ise comin, Miss Cahline.”
paragraphs.zh: “现在继续，”迪尔西一边说一边朝门口走去。“你也想让她开始吗？我来了，卡琳小姐。”

paragraphs.en: I went on out. I could hear them on the steps. “You go on back to bed now,” Dilsey was saying, “Dont you know you aint feeling well enough to git up yet? Go on back, now. I’m gwine to see she gits to school in time.”
paragraphs.zh: 我继续往外走。我可以听到他们在台阶上的声音。“你现在回床上去吧，”迪尔西说，“你不知道你还没有起床吗？现在就回去吧。我一定要看到她及时赶到学校。”

paragraphs.en: I went on out the back to back the car out, then I had to go all the way round to the front before I found them.
paragraphs.zh: 我从后面把车倒出来，然后我不得不绕到前面才找到他们。

paragraphs.en: “I thought I told you to put that tire on the back of the car,” I says.
paragraphs.zh: “我想我告诉过你把那个轮胎放在车后部，”我说。

paragraphs.en: “I aint had time,” Luster says. “Aint nobody to watch him till mammy git done in de kitchen.”
paragraphs.zh: “我没有时间，”勒斯特说。“在妈妈把厨房做完之前，没有人看管他。”

paragraphs.en: “Yes,” I says, “I feed a whole damn kitchen full of niggers to follow around after him, but if I want an automobile tire changed, I have to do it myself.”
