paragraphs.zh: “是的，”我说，“我喂饱了整个该死的厨房，里面全是黑鬼跟着他，但如果我想换汽车轮胎，我就得自己动手。”

paragraphs.en: “I aint had nobody to leave him wid,” he says. Then he begun moaning and slobbering.
paragraphs.zh: “我没有人可以把他丢下，”他说。然后他开始呻吟并流口水。

paragraphs.en: “Take him on round to the back,” I says. “What the hell makes you want to keep him around here where people can see him?” I made them go on, before he got started bellowing good. It’s bad enough on Sundays, with that damn field full of people that haven’t got a side show and six niggers to feed, knocking a damn oversize mothball around. He’s going to keep on running up and down that fence and bellowing every time they come in sight until first thing I know they’re going to begin charging me golf dues, then Mother and Dilsey’ll have to get a couple of china door knobs and a walking stick and work it out, unless I play at night with a lantern. Then they’d send us all to Jackson, maybe. God knows, they’d hold Old Home week when that happened.
paragraphs.zh: “把他带到后面去，”我说。“到底是什么让你想把他留在这里，让人们都能看到他？”在他开始大喊大叫之前，我让他们继续说下去。周日的情况就已经够糟糕了，那该死的场地里挤满了没有余兴表演的人，还有六个黑人要喂饱，把一个该死的超大樟脑丸撞得满地都是。他会继续在栅栏上跑来跑去，每次看到他们就吼叫，直到我知道他们要开始向我收取高尔夫球费，然后妈妈和迪尔西就得拿几个瓷器门把手和一根手杖来解决这个问题，除非我晚上打灯笼。然后他们可能会把我们都送到杰克逊。天知道，当这种情况发生时，他们会举办“老家周”。

paragraphs.en: I went on back to the garage. There was the tire, leaning against the wall, but be damned if I was going to put it on. I backed out and turned around. She was standing by the drive. I says,
paragraphs.zh: 我又回到车库。轮胎就在那里，靠在墙上，但该死的，如果我要把它穿上的话。我退了出去，转身。她站在车道旁。我说，

paragraphs.en: “I know you haven’t got any books: I just want to ask you what you did with them, if it’s any of my business. Of course I haven’t got any right to ask,” I says, “I’m just the one that paid $11.65 for them last September.”
paragraphs.zh: “我知道你没有任何书：我只是想问你你对它们做了什么，这是否关乎我的事。当然我没有权利问，”我说，“我只是去年 9 月花了 11.65 美元买下这些书的人。”

paragraphs.en: “Mother buys my books,” she says. “There’s not a cent of your money on me. I’d starve first.”
paragraphs.zh: “妈妈给我买书，”她说。“你的钱一分钱也没有在我身上。我会先饿死的。”

paragraphs.en: “Yes?” I says. “You tell your grandmother that and see what she says. You dont look all the way naked,” I says, “even if that stuff on your face does hide more of you than anything else you’ve got on.”
paragraphs.zh: “是吗？”我说。“你告诉你的祖母，看看她怎么说。你看起来并不完全赤身裸体，”我说，“即使你脸上的东西确实比你身上的其他东西更能隐藏你。”

paragraphs.en: “Do you think your money or hers either paid for a cent of this?” she says.
paragraphs.zh: “你认为你的钱还是她的钱能支付其中一分钱吗？”她说。

paragraphs.en: “Ask your grandmother,” I says. “Ask her what became of those checks. You saw her burn one of them, as I remember.” She wasn’t even listening, with her face all gummed up with paint and her eyes hard as a fice dog’s.
paragraphs.zh: “问问你祖母，”我说。“问问她那些支票怎么样了。我记得你看到她烧掉了其中一张。”她根本没在听，脸上涂满了油漆，眼神冷酷得像只公务犬。

paragraphs.en: “Do you know what I’d do if I thought your money or hers either bought one cent of this?” she says, putting her hand on her dress.
paragraphs.zh: “你知道如果我认为你或她的钱能买一分钱的话我会怎么做？”她一边说，一边把手放在裙子上。

paragraphs.en: “What would you do?” I says, “Wear a barrel?”
paragraphs.zh: “你会怎么做？”我说：“带个桶？”

paragraphs.en: “I’d tear it right off and throw it into the street,” she says. “Dont you believe me?”
paragraphs.zh: “我会把它撕下来扔到街上，”她说。“你不相信我吗？”

paragraphs.en: “Sure you would,” I says. “You do it every time.”
paragraphs.zh: “当然你会的，”我说。“你每次都这么做。”

paragraphs.en: “See if I wouldn’t,” She says. She grabbed the neck of her dress in both hands and made like she would tear it.
paragraphs.zh: “看看我是否不会，”她说。她双手抓住衣领，做出要把它撕碎的样子。

paragraphs.en: “You tear that dress,” I says, “And I’ll give you a whipping right here that you’ll remember all your life.”
paragraphs.zh: “你撕破了那件衣服，”我说，“我会在这里鞭打你，让你终生难忘。”

paragraphs.en: “See if I dont,” she says. Then I saw that she really was trying to tear it, to tear it right off of her. By the time I got the car stopped and grabbed her hands there was about a dozen people looking. It made me so mad for a minute it kind of blinded me.
paragraphs.zh: “看看我是否不这样做，”她说。然后我看到她真的想把它撕下来，想把它从她身上撕下来。当我把车停下并抓住她的手时，大约有十几个人在看着。它让我生气了一分钟，让我失明了。

paragraphs.en: “You do a thing like that again and I’ll make you sorry you ever drew breath,” I says.
paragraphs.zh: “你再做这样的事，我会让你后悔的。”我说。

paragraphs.en: “I’m sorry now,” she says. She quit, then her eyes turned kind of funny and I says to myself if you cry here in this car, on the street, I’ll whip you. I’ll wear you out. Lucky for her she didn’t, so I turned her wrists loose and drove on. Luckily we were near an alley, where I could turn into the back street and dodge the square. They were already putting the tent up in Beard’s lot. Earl had already given me the two passes for our show windows. She sat there with her face turned away, chewing her lip. “I’m sorry now,” she says. “I dont see why I was ever born.”
paragraphs.zh: “我现在很抱歉，”她说。她退出了，然后她的眼睛变得有点滑稽，我对自己说，如果你在这辆车里，在街上哭，我会鞭打你。我会让你筋疲力尽。幸运的是，她没有这么做，所以我松开她的手腕，继续开车。幸运的是，我们靠近一条小巷，我可以在那里拐进后街，避开广场。他们已经在比尔德的地盘上搭起了帐篷。厄尔已经给了我两张橱窗通行证。她坐在那里，背过脸，咬着嘴唇。“我现在很抱歉，”她说。“我不明白我为何出生。”

paragraphs.en: “And I know of at least one other person that dont understand all he knows about that,” I says. I stopped in front of the school house. The bell had rung, and the last of them were just going in. “You’re on time for once, anyway,” I says. “Are you going in there and stay there, or am I coming with you and make you?” She got out and banged the door. “Remember what I say,” I says, “I mean it. Let me hear one more time that you were slipping up and down back alleys with one of those damn squirts.”
paragraphs.zh: “据我所知，至少还有一个人并不了解他所知道的一切，”我说。我在校舍前停了下来。铃声响了，最后一个人正要进去。“无论如何，你还是准时了一次，”我说。“你是要进去并留在那里，还是我和你一起去并创造你？”她下了车，敲响了门。“记住我说的话，”我说，“我是认真的。让我再听一次，你带着那些该死的潮吹在后巷里滑来滑去。”

paragraphs.en: She turned back at that. “I dont slip around,” she says. “I dare anybody to know everything I do.”
paragraphs.zh: 说到这里她回头了。“我不会溜走，”她说。“我敢于让任何人知道我所做的一切。”

paragraphs.en: “And they all know it, too,” I says. “Everybody in this town knows what you are. But I wont have it anymore, you hear? I dont care what you do, myself,” I says, “But I’ve got a position in this town, and I’m not going to have any member of my family going on like a nigger wench. You hear me?”
paragraphs.zh: “他们也都知道这一点，”我说。“这个镇上的每个人都知道你是谁。但我不会再拥有它了，你听到了吗？我自己不在乎你做什么，”我说，“但我在这个镇上有一个职位，我不会让我的家人像一个黑鬼姑娘一样。你听到了吗？”

paragraphs.en: “I dont care,” she says, “I’m bad and I’m going to hell, and I dont care. I’d rather be in hell than anywhere where you are.”
paragraphs.zh: “我不在乎，”她说，“我很坏，我会下地狱，但我不在乎。我宁愿在地狱也不愿在你所在的任何地方。”

paragraphs.en: “If I hear one more time that you haven’t been to school, you’ll wish you were in hell,” I says. She turned and ran on across the yard. “One more time, remember,” I says. She didn’t look back.
paragraphs.zh: “如果我再听到你没有上过学，你会希望自己是在地狱里，”我说。她转身跑过院子。“再一次，记住，”我说。她没有回头。

paragraphs.en: I went to the postoffice and got the mail and drove on to the store and parked. Earl looked at me when I came in. I gave him a chance to say something about my being late, but he just said,
paragraphs.zh: 我去邮局取了邮件，然后开车去商店停车。当我进来时，厄尔看着我。我给了他机会说一些关于我迟到的事情，但他只是说：

paragraphs.en: “Those cultivators have come. You’d better help Uncle Job put them up.”
paragraphs.zh: “那些修炼者都来了，你还是帮乔布伯伯把他们放起来吧。”

paragraphs.en: I went on to the back, where old Job was uncrating them, at the rate of about three bolts to the hour.
paragraphs.zh: 我继续走到后面，老约伯正以大约每小时三个螺栓的速度打开它们的包装。

paragraphs.en: “You ought to be working for me,” I says. “Every other no-count nigger in town eats in my kitchen.”
paragraphs.zh: “你应该为我工作，”我说。“镇上所有其他不计其数的黑鬼都在我的厨房里吃饭。”

paragraphs.en: “I works to suit de man whut pays me Sat’dy night,” he says. “When I does dat, it dont leave me a whole lot of time to please other folks.” He screwed up a nut. “Aint nobody works much in dis country cep de boll-weevil, noways,” he says.
paragraphs.zh: “我工作是为了适应周六晚上给我报酬的人，”他说。“当我这么做的时候，我并没有太多时间去取悦别人。”他拧坏了一个螺母。“在这个有棉象鼻虫的国家里，没有人会做很多工作，”他说。

paragraphs.en: “You’d better be glad you’re not a boll-weevil waiting on those cultivators,” I says. “You’d work yourself to death before they’d be ready to prevent you.”
paragraphs.zh: “你最好庆幸自己不是等待那些耕种者的棉铃象甲虫，”我说。“在他们准备好阻止你之前，你会努力工作到死。”

paragraphs.en: “Dat’s de troof,” he says, “Boll-weevil got tough time. Work ev’y day in de week out in de hot sun, rain er shine. Aint got no front porch to set on en watch de wattermilyuns growin and Sat’dy dont mean nothin a-tall to him.”
paragraphs.zh: “就是这样，”他说，“棉铃象鼻虫的日子不好过。一周中的每一天都要在烈日下工作，风雨无阻。没有前廊可以观察瓦特米林的生长，周六对他来说没什么意义。”

paragraphs.en: “Saturday wouldn’t mean nothing to you, either,” I says, “if it depended on me to pay you wages. Get those things out of the crates now and drag them inside.”
paragraphs.zh: “星期六对你来说也没什么意义，”我说，“如果我要给你发工资的话。现在把那些东西从板条箱里拿出来，拖进去。”

paragraphs.en: I opened her letter first and took the check out. Just like a woman. Six days late. Yet they try to make men believe that they’re capable of conducting a business. How long would a man that thought the first of the month came on the sixth last in business. And like as not, when they sent the bank statement out, she would want to know why I never deposited my salary until the sixth. Things like that never occur to a woman.
paragraphs.zh: 我先拆开她的信，然后取出支票。就像一个女人一样。晚了六天。然而，他们试图让人们相信他们有能力开展业务。一个认为本月第一天在生意上倒数第六个的人会持续多久？就像没有一样，当他们寄出银行对账单时，她会想知道为什么我直到第六天才存入工资。女人从来不会发生这样的事。

paragraphs.en: “I had no answer to my letter about Quentin’s easter dress. Did it arrive all right? I’ve had no answer to the last two letters I wrote her, though the check in the second one was cashed with the other check. Is she sick? Let me know at once or I’ll come there and see for myself. You promised you would let me know when she needed things. I will expect to hear from you before the 10th. No you’d better wire me at once. You are opening my letters to her. I know that as well as if I were looking at you. You’d better wire me at once about her to this address.”
paragraphs.zh: “关于昆丁复活节礼服的信，我没有得到答复。它还好吗？我写给她的最后两封信都没有答复，尽管第二封支票是和另一封支票一起兑现的。她生病了吗？立即告诉我，否则我会亲自去看看。你答应过当她需要东西时你会告诉我。我希望在十号之前收到你的消息。不，你最好立即给我发电报。你正在打开我的信我知道，就像我在看着你一样，你最好立即给我发电报到这个地址。”

paragraphs.en: About that time Earl started yelling at Job, so I put them away and went over to try to put some life into him. What this country needs is white labour. Let these damn trifling niggers starve for a couple of years, then they’d see what a soft thing they have.
paragraphs.zh: 大约在那个时候，厄尔开始对乔布大喊大叫，所以我把它们收起来，走过去试图给他注入一些活力。这个国家需要的是白人劳动力。让这些该死的小黑鬼挨饿几年，然后他们就会看到自己有多么柔软的东西。

paragraphs.en: Along toward ten oclock I went up front. There was a drummer there. It was a couple of minutes to ten, and I invited him up the street to get a coca-cola. We got to talking about crops.
paragraphs.zh: 快到十点时，我走到前面。那里有一个鼓手。差几分钟就到十点了，我邀请他到街上去买杯可口可乐。我们开始谈论农作物。

paragraphs.en: “There’s nothing to it,” I says, “Cotton is a speculator’s crop. They fill the farmer full of hot air and get him to raise a big crop for them to whipsaw on the market, to trim the suckers with. Do you think the farmer gets anything out of it except a red neck and a hump in his back? You think the man that sweats to put it into the ground gets a red cent more than a bare living,” I says. “Let him make a big crop and it wont be worth picking; let him make a small crop and he wont have enough to gin. And what for? so a bunch of damn eastern jews, I’m not talking about men of the jewish religion,” I says, “I’ve known some jews that were fine citizens. You might be one yourself,” I says.
paragraphs.zh: “这没什么，”我说，“棉花是投机者的作物。他们让农民充满热气，让他种植大量作物，以便他们在市场上进行洗盘，修剪吸盘。你认为农民除了红脖子和背上的驼峰之外，还能得到什么吗？你认为那些流汗把棉花埋进地里的人比赤裸裸的生活多赚一分钱，”我说。“让他收成大，就不值得采摘；让他收成小，他就没有足够的杜松子酒了。那又是为了什么呢？一群该死的东方犹太人，我不是在谈论犹太教的人，”我说，“我认识一些犹太人，他们都是好公民。你自己也可能是其中之一，”我说。

paragraphs.en: “No,” he says, “I’m an American.”
paragraphs.zh: “不，”他说，“我是美国人。”

paragraphs.en: “No offense,” I says. “I give every man his due, regardless of religion or anything else. I have nothing against jews as an individual,” I says. “It’s just the race. You’ll admit that they produce nothing. They follow the pioneers into a new country and sell them clothes.”
paragraphs.zh: “无意冒犯，”我说。“我给予每个人应有的权利，无论宗教信仰或其他什么。我对犹太人作为个人没有任何反对意见，”我说。“这只是比赛。你会承认他们什么也没生产。他们跟随先驱者进入一个新的国家，并向他们出售衣服。”

paragraphs.en: “You’re thinking of Armenians,” he says, “aren’t you. A pioneer wouldn’t have any use for new clothes.”
paragraphs.zh: “你想到的是亚美尼亚人，”他说，“不是吗？拓荒者不会穿新衣服。”

paragraphs.en: “No offense,” I says. “I dont hold a man’s religion against him.”
paragraphs.zh: “无意冒犯，”我说。“我不会因为一个人的宗教信仰而反对他。”

paragraphs.en: “Sure,” he says, “I’m an American. My folks have some French blood, why I have a nose like this. I’m an American, all right.”
paragraphs.zh: “当然，”他说，“我是美国人。我的家人有一些法国血统，为什么我有这样的鼻子。我是美国人，好吧。”

paragraphs.en: “So am I,” I says. “Not many of us left. What I’m talking about is the fellows that sit up there in New York and trim the sucker gamblers.”
paragraphs.zh: “我也是，”我说。“我们中没有多少人离开。我说的是那些坐在纽约那里打击傻瓜赌徒的人。”

paragraphs.en: “That’s right,” he says. “Nothing to gambling, for a poor man. There ought to be a law against it.”
paragraphs.zh: “没错，”他说。“对于一个穷人来说，赌博没什么意义。应该有一条法律禁止赌博。”

paragraphs.en: “Dont you think I’m right?” I says.
paragraphs.zh: “你不觉得我说得对吗？”我说。

paragraphs.en: “Yes,” he says, “I guess you’re right. The farmer catches it coming and going.”
paragraphs.zh: “是的，”他说，“我想你是对的。农民会抓住它来来去去。”

paragraphs.en: “I know I’m right,” I says. “It’s a sucker game, unless a man gets inside information from somebody that knows what’s going on. I happen to be associated with some people who’re right there on the ground. They have one of the biggest manipulators in New York for an adviser. Way I do it,” I says, “I never risk much at a time. It’s the fellow that thinks he knows it all and is trying to make a killing with three dollars that they’re laying for. That’s why they are in the business.”
paragraphs.zh: “我知道我是对的，”我说。“这是一场愚蠢的游戏，除非一个人从知道发生了什么事的人那里得到内幕信息。我碰巧和一些就在现场的人有联系。他们有纽约最大的操纵者之一作为顾问。我就是这样做的，”我说，“我从来不会一次冒太大的风险。那些人认为他知道一切，并试图用他们所投入的三美元大赚一笔。这就是为什么他们在生意。”

paragraphs.en: Then it struck ten. I went up to the telegraph office. It opened up a little, just like they said. I went into the corner and took out the telegram again, just to be sure. While I was looking at it a report came in. It was up two points. They were all buying. I could tell that from what they were saying. Getting aboard. Like they didn’t know it could go but one way. Like there was a law or something against doing anything but buying. Well, I reckon those eastern jews have got to live too. But I’ll be damned if it hasn’t come to a pretty pass when any damn foreigner that cant make a living in the country where God put him, can come to this one and take money right out of an American’s pockets. It was up two points more. Four points. But hell, they were right there and knew what was going on. And if I wasn’t going to take the advice, what was I paying them ten dollars a month for. I went out, then I remembered and came back and sent the wire. “All well. Q writing today.”
paragraphs.zh: 然后就敲响了十点。我去了电报局。就像他们说的那样，它打开了一点。我走到角落里，再次拿出电报，只是为了确定一下。当我看的时候，一份报告进来了。它上涨了两点。他们都在买。从他们所说的我可以看出这一点。上船。就像他们不知道事情只能以一种方式进行一样。就像有法律或其他东西禁止除了购买之外做任何事情。嗯，我认为那些东方犹太人也必须生存。但如果事情没有进展顺利的话，我就该死了，任何一个在上帝安置他的国家都无法谋生的该死的外国人，可以来到这个国家，直接从美国人的口袋里拿钱。又上涨了两点。四点。但见鬼，他们就在那里并且知道发生了什么。如果我不接受他们的建议，我每个月付给他们十美元做什么呢？我出去了，然后我想起来了，然后回来发了电报。“一切顺利。今天写Q。”

paragraphs.en: “Q?” the operator says.
paragraphs.zh: “问？”接线员说。

paragraphs.en: “Yes,” I says, “Q. Cant you spell Q?”
paragraphs.zh: “是的，”我说，“Q。你不会拼写 Q 吗？”

paragraphs.en: “I just asked to be sure,” he says.
paragraphs.zh: “我只是想确定一下，”他说。

paragraphs.en: “You send it like I wrote it and I’ll guarantee you to be sure,” I says. “Send it collect.”
paragraphs.zh: “你按照我写的方式发送，我保证你确定，”我说。“寄过来吧。”

paragraphs.en: “What you sending, Jason?” Doc Wright says, looking over my shoulder. “Is that a code message to buy?”
paragraphs.zh: “杰生，你送什么？”赖特医生越过我的肩膀说道。“这是要买的暗号吗？”

paragraphs.en: “That’s all right about that,” I says. “You boys use your own judgment. You know more about it than those New York folks do.”
paragraphs.zh: “没关系，”我说。“你们这些孩子有自己的判断力。你们比那些纽约人更了解这一点。”

paragraphs.en: “Well, I ought to,” Doc says, “I’d a saved money this year raising it at two cents a pound.”
paragraphs.zh: “嗯，我应该这样做，”多克说，“今年我把价格提高到每磅两美分，这样我就省了钱。”

paragraphs.en: Another report came in. It was down a point.
paragraphs.zh: 另一份报告传来。下降了一个百分点。

paragraphs.en: “Jason’s selling,” Hopkins says. “Look at his face.”
paragraphs.zh: “杰生正在出售，”霍普金斯说。“看看他的脸。”

paragraphs.en: “That’s all right about what I’m doing,” I says. “You boys follow your own judgment. Those rich New York jews have got to live like everybody else,” I says.
paragraphs.zh: “我正在做的事情没什么问题，”我说。“你们小伙子遵循你们自己的判断。那些富有的纽约犹太人必须像其他人一样生活，”我说。

paragraphs.en: I went on back to the store. Earl was busy up front. I went on back to the desk and read Lorraine’s letter. “Dear daddy wish you were here. No good parties when daddys out of town I miss my sweet daddy.” I reckon she does. Last time I gave her forty dollars. Gave it to her. I never promise a woman anything nor let her know what I’m going to give her. That’s the only way to manage them. Always keep them guessing. If you cant think of any other way to surprise them, give them a bust in the jaw.
paragraphs.zh: 我又回到了商店。厄尔在前面很忙。我回到办公桌前，读了洛兰的信。“亲爱的爸爸希望你在这里。爸爸出城时没有什么好的聚会，我想念我可爱的爸爸。”我想她是的。上次我给了她四十块钱。给了她。我从不向女人承诺任何事情，也不让她知道我要给她什么。这是管理它们的唯一方法。总是让他们猜测。如果你想不出任何其他方法可以让他们大吃一惊，那就狠狠地打他们的下巴吧。

paragraphs.en: I tore it up and burned it over the spittoon. I make it a rule never to keep a scrap of paper bearing a woman’s hand, and I never write them at all. Lorraine is always after me to write to her but I says anything I forgot to tell you will save till I get to Memphis again but I says I dont mind you writing me now and then in a plain envelope, but if you ever try to call me up on the telephone, Memphis wont hold you I says. I says when I’m up there I’m one of the boys, but I’m not going to have any woman calling me on the telephone. Here I says, giving her the forty dollars. If you ever get drunk and take a notion to call me on the phone, just remember this and count ten before you do it.
paragraphs.zh: 我把它撕碎并在痰盂上烧了。我立下一条规矩，决不留一张有女人手迹的纸片，而且我根本不写。洛兰总是追着我给她写信，但我说我忘记告诉你的任何事情都会保存到我再次到达孟菲斯，但我说我不介意你时不时地用普通信封给我写信，但如果你试图打电话给我，我说孟菲斯不会留住你。我说当我在那里时我是男孩之一，但我不会让任何女人打电话给我。我说到这里，给了她四十美元。如果你喝醉了并想给我打电话，请记住这一点，然后数到十再做。

paragraphs.en: “When’ll that be?” she says.
paragraphs.zh: “那会是什么时候？”她说。

paragraphs.en: “What?” I says.
paragraphs.zh: “什么？”我说。

paragraphs.en: “When you’re coming back,” she says.
paragraphs.zh: “当你回来的时候，”她说。

paragraphs.en: “I’ll let you know,” I says. Then she tried to buy a beer, but I wouldn’t let her. “Keep your money,” I says. “Buy yourself a dress with it.” I gave the maid a five, too. After all, like I say money has no value; it’s just the way you spend it. It dont belong to anybody, so why try to hoard it. It just belongs to the man that can get it and keep it. There’s a man right here in Jefferson made a lot of money selling rotten goods to niggers, lived in a room over the store about the size of a pigpen, and did his own cooking. About four or five years ago he was taken sick. Scared the hell out of him so that when he was up again he joined the church and bought himself a Chinese missionary, five thousand dollars a year. I often think how mad he’ll be if he was to die and find out there’s not any heaven, when he thinks about that five thousand a year. Like I say, he’d better go on and die now and save money.
paragraphs.zh: “我会让你知道的，”我说。然后她想买啤酒，但我不让。“保留你的钱，”我说。“用它给自己买一件衣服。”我也给了女仆五分。毕竟，就像我说的，金钱没有价值；这只是你花钱的方式。它不属于任何人，所以为什么要试图囤积它。它只属于能够得到它并保留它的人。杰斐逊有一个人靠向黑人出售腐烂的商品赚了很多钱，他住在商店楼上一个猪圈大小的房间里，自己做饭。大约四五年前，他生了一场病。把他吓坏了，当他再次醒来时，他加入了教会，给自己买了一个中国传教士，每年五千美元。我常常想，如果他死后发现根本没有天堂，当他想到每年那五千人时，他会多么生气。就像我说的，他最好现在就去死，省点钱。

paragraphs.en: When it was burned good I was just about to shove the others into my coat when all of a sudden something told me to open Quentin’s before I went home, but about that time Earl started yelling for me up front, so I put them away and went and waited on the damn redneck while he spent fifteen minutes deciding whether he wanted a twenty cent hame string or a thirty-five cent one.
paragraphs.zh: 当它烧好时，我正要把其他人塞进我的外套里，突然有什么东西告诉我在回家之前打开昆丁的，但就在那时厄尔开始在前面对我大喊大叫，所以我把它们收起来然后去等待那个该死的乡巴佬，而他花了十五分钟决定他是想要一根二十美分的火腿绳还是一根三十五美分的火腿绳。

paragraphs.en: “You’d better take that good one,” I says. “How do you fellows ever expect to get ahead, trying to work with cheap equipment?”
paragraphs.zh: “你最好拿走那个好的，”我说。“你们这些家伙，尝试使用廉价设备，如何才能取得成功呢？”

paragraphs.en: “If this one aint any good,” he says, “why have you got it on sale?”
paragraphs.zh: “如果这个不好，”他说，“为什么还要打折呢？”

paragraphs.en: “I didn’t say it wasn’t any good,” I says, “I said it’s not as good as that other one.”
paragraphs.zh: “我没说它不好，”我说，“我只是说它不如另一个好。”

paragraphs.en: “How do you know it’s not,” he says. “You ever use airy one of them?”
paragraphs.zh: “你怎么知道不是，”他说。“你用过其中一款吗？”

paragraphs.en: “Because they dont ask thirty-five cents for it,” I says. “That’s how I know it’s not as good.”
paragraphs.zh: “因为他们不会要价三十五美分，”我说。“这就是我知道情况没那么好的原因。”

paragraphs.en: He held the twenty cent one in his hands, drawing it through his fingers. “I reckon I’ll take this hyer one,” he says. I offered to take it and wrap it, but he rolled it up and put it in his overalls. Then he took out a tobacco sack and finally got it untied and shook some coins out. He handed me a quarter. “That fifteen cents will buy me a snack of dinner,” he says.
paragraphs.zh: 他手里拿着那张二十美分的硬币，从手指间抽出来。“我想我会选择这个，”他说。我主动提出把它包起来，但他把它卷起来放进工作服里。然后他拿出一个烟袋，终于把它解开，抖出了一些硬币。他递给我 25 美分。“这十五美分可以给我买一份晚餐小吃，”他说。

paragraphs.en: “All right,” I says, “You’re the doctor. But dont come complaining to me next year when you have to buy a new outfit.”
paragraphs.zh: “好吧，”我说，“你是医生。但是明年你必须买一套新衣服时，不要来找我抱怨。”

paragraphs.en: “I aint makin next year’s crop yit,” he says. Finally I got rid of him, but every time I took that letter out something would come up. They were all in town for the show, coming in in droves to give their money to something that brought nothing to the town and wouldn’t leave anything except what those grafters in the Mayor’s office will split among themselves, and Earl chasing back and forth like a hen in a coop, saying “Yes, ma’am, Mr Compson will wait on you. Jason, show this lady a churn or a nickel’s worth of screen hooks.”
paragraphs.zh: “我不会生产明年的农作物，”他说。最后我摆脱了他，但每次我把那封信拿出来时都会出现一些东西。他们都在镇上看演出，成群结队地把钱捐给了一些对镇上没有任何好处的东西，除了市长办公室里的那些贪污者会分给他们自己之外，什么也不会留下，厄尔像鸡笼里的母鸡一样来回追赶，说：“是的，女士，康普生先生会等你的。杰生，给这位女士展示一下搅拌机或价值五分钱的屏幕挂钩。”

paragraphs.en: Well, Jason likes work. I says no I never had university advantages because at Harvard they teach you how to go for a swim at night without knowing how to swim and at Sewanee they dont even teach you what water is. I says you might send me to the state University; maybe I’ll learn how to stop my clock with a nose spray and then you can send Ben to the Navy I says or to the cavalry anyway, they use geldings in the cavalry. Then when she sent Quentin home for me to feed too I says I guess that’s right too, instead of me having to go way up north for a job they sent the job down here to me and then Mother begun to cry and I says it’s not that I have any objection to having it here; if it’s any satisfaction to you I’ll quit work and nurse it myself and let you and Dilsey keep the flour barrel full, or Ben. Rent him out to a sideshow; there must be folks somewhere that would pay a dime to see him, then she cried more and kept saying my poor afflicted baby and I says yes he’ll be quite a help to you when he gets his growth not being more than one and a half times as high as me now and she says she’d be dead soon and then we’d all be better off and so I says all right, all right, have it your way. It’s your grandchild, which is more than any other grandparents it’s got can say for certain. Only I says it’s only a question of time. If you believe she’ll do what she says and not try to see it, you fool yourself because the first time that was that Mother kept on saying thank God you are not a Compson except in name, because you are all I have left now, you and Maury, and I says well I could spare Uncle Maury myself and then they came and said they were ready to start. Mother stopped crying then. She pulled her veil down and we went down stairs. Uncle Maury was coming out of the diningroom, his handkerchief to his mouth. They kind of made a lane and we went out the door just in time to see Dilsey driving Ben and T. P. back around the corner. We went down the steps and got in. Uncle Maury kept saying Poor little sister, poor little sister, talking around his mouth and patting Mother’s hand. Talking around whatever it was.
paragraphs.zh: 嗯，杰生喜欢工作。我说不，我从来没有大学优势，因为在哈佛，他们教你如何在不知道如何游泳的情况下在晚上去游泳，而在塞瓦尼，他们甚至不教你什么是水。我说你可以送我去州立大学；也许我会学习如何用鼻喷雾剂停止我的时钟，然后你可以把本送到海军，我说或者无论如何，骑兵，他们在骑兵中使用骟马。然后当她把昆丁也送回家给我吃饭时，我说我想这也是对的，我不用去北方找工作，而是把工作送到了这里，然后妈妈开始哭了，我说我并不是反对在这里工作；我只是说我不反对。如果你满意的话，我会辞掉工作，亲自护理，让你和迪尔西把面粉桶装满，或者本。把他租出去参加杂耍表演；一定会有人愿意花一毛钱去看他，然后她哭得更厉害，一直说我可怜的受苦的孩子，我说是的，当他的成长速度不超过我现在的一倍半时，他会对你有很大帮助，她说她很快就会死，然后我们都会过得更好，所以我说好吧，好吧，随你的吧。这是你的孙子，比其他任何祖父母都可以肯定地说。只有我说这只是时间问题。如果你相信她会照她说的做，而不是试图看到它，你就欺骗了自己，因为那是母亲第一次不断地说，感谢上帝，除了名义上，你不是一个康普生，因为你是我现在只剩下的人了，你和莫里，我说好吧，我可以饶过莫里舅舅，然后他们来了，说他们已经准备好开始了。妈妈这时候就不哭了。她拉下面纱，我们下了楼梯。莫里舅舅手帕捂着嘴，从餐厅里出来。他们划出了一条车道，我们走出门，正好看到迪尔西在拐角处开车送本和蒂·皮回来。我们下了台阶，钻了进去。莫里舅舅嘴里不停地说着“可怜的小妹妹，可怜的小妹妹”，嘴里还念叨着，拍着妈妈的手。谈论任何事情。

paragraphs.en: “Have you got your band on?” she says. “Why dont they go on, before Benjamin comes out and makes a spectacle. Poor little boy. He doesn’t know. He cant even realise.”
paragraphs.zh: “你带好乐队了吗？”她说。“为什么他们不继续，在本杰明出来并大放异彩之前。可怜的小男孩。他不知道。他甚至都没有意识到。”

paragraphs.en: “There, there,” Uncle Maury says, patting her hand, talking around his mouth. “It’s better so. Let him be unaware of bereavement until he has to.”
paragraphs.zh: “好了好了，”莫里舅舅拍着她的手，嘴里念叨着。“这样更好。让他在必要的时候不要意识到丧亲之痛。”

paragraphs.en: “Other women have their children to support them in times like this,” Mother says.
paragraphs.zh: “在这样的时刻，其他妇女有自己的孩子来支持她们，”母亲说。

paragraphs.en: “You have Jason and me,” he says.
paragraphs.zh: “你有杰生和我，”他说。

paragraphs.en: “It’s so terrible to me,” she says, “Having the two of them like this, in less than two years.”
paragraphs.zh: “这对我来说太可怕了，”她说，“不到两年，他们两个就成了这样。”

paragraphs.en: “There, there,” he says. After a while he kind of sneaked his hand to his mouth and dropped them out the window. Then I knew what I had been smelling. Clove stems. I reckon he thought that the least he could do at Father’s funeral or maybe the sideboard thought it was still Father and tripped him up when he passed. Like I say, if he had to sell something to send Quentin to Harvard we’d all been a damn sight better off if he’d sold that sideboard and bought himself a one-armed strait jacket with part of the money. I reckon the reason all the Compson gave out before it got to me like Mother says, is that he drank it up. At least I never heard of him offering to sell anything to send me to Harvard.
paragraphs.zh: “那里，那里，”他说。过了一会儿，他把手伸到嘴边，把它们扔出了窗外。然后我就知道我闻到了什么味道。丁香茎。我想他认为他至少可以在父亲的葬礼上做点什么，或者也许餐具柜认为那仍然是父亲，并在他去世时绊倒了他。就像我说的，如果他必须卖掉一些东西才能送昆丁去哈佛，如果他卖掉那个餐具柜并用一部分钱给自己买了一件单臂紧身衣，我们都会过得更好。我认为康普生之所以像母亲说的那样，在到达我身边之前就已经耗尽了，是因为他把它喝光了。至少我从未听说过他愿意卖掉任何东西来送我去哈佛。

paragraphs.en: So he kept on patting her hand and saying “Poor little sister,” patting her hand with one of the black gloves that we got the bill for four days later because it was the twenty-sixth because it was the same day one month that Father went up there and got it and brought it home and wouldn’t tell anything about where she was or anything and Mother crying and saying “And you didn’t even see him? You didn’t even try to get him to make any provision for it?” and Father says “No she shall not touch his money not one cent of it” and Mother says “He can be forced to by law. He can prove nothing, unless—Jason Compson,” she says, “Were you fool enough to tell—”
paragraphs.zh: 于是他不停地拍着她的手，说“可怜的小妹妹”，用一只黑色手套拍拍她的手，四天后我们收到了账单，因为那是二十六号，因为就在一个月的同一天，父亲去那里取了它并把它带回家，不肯告诉任何关于她在哪里的事情，母亲哭着说：“你甚至没有看到他？你甚至没有试图让他为此做任何准备吗？”父亲说“不，她不能动他的钱，一分钱也不能”，母亲说“法律可以强迫他这么做。他什么也证明不了，除非——杰生康普生，”她说，“你傻到说——”

paragraphs.en: “Hush, Caroline,” Father says, then he sent me to help Dilsey get that old cradle out of the attic and I says,
paragraphs.zh: “嘘，卡罗琳，”父亲说，然后他派我去帮助迪尔西把那个旧摇篮从阁楼里拿出来，我说，

paragraphs.en: “Well, they brought my job home tonight” because all the time we kept hoping they’d get things straightened out and he’d keep her because Mother kept saying she would at least have enough regard for the family not to jeopardize my chance after she and Quentin had had theirs.
paragraphs.zh: “好吧，他们今晚把我的工作带回家了”，因为我们一直希望他们能把事情解决好，而他会保留她，因为母亲一直说，在她和昆丁有了他们的机会后，她至少会对这个家庭有足够的尊重，不会危及我的机会。

paragraphs.en: “And whar else do she belong?” Dilsey says, “Who else gwine raise her ’cep me? Aint I raised eve’y one of y’all?”
paragraphs.zh: “那她还属于什么？”迪尔西说：“还有谁抚养她长大？我不是抚养了你们所有人吗？”

paragraphs.en: “And a damn fine job you made of it,” I says. “Anyway it’ll give her something to sure enough worry over now.” So we carried the cradle down and Dilsey started to set it up in her old room. Then Mother started sure enough.
paragraphs.zh: “你把它做得非常好，”我说。“无论如何，这肯定会给她带来一些值得担心的事情。”于是我们把摇篮搬了下来，迪尔西开始把它安装在她原来的房间里。然后妈妈果然开始了。

paragraphs.en: “Hush, Miss Cahline,” Dilsey says, “You gwine wake her up.”
paragraphs.zh: “嘘，卡琳小姐，”迪尔西说，“你要把她吵醒。”

paragraphs.en: “In there?” Mother says, “To be contaminated by that atmosphere? It’ll be hard enough as it is, with the heritage she already has.”
paragraphs.zh: “在那里？”母亲说：“被那种气氛污染？以她已有的血统，已经够难的了。”

paragraphs.en: “Hush,” Father says, “Dont be silly.”
paragraphs.zh: “嘘，”父亲说，“别犯傻了。”

paragraphs.en: “Why aint she gwine sleep in here,” Dilsey says, “In the same room whar I put her ma to bed ev’y night of her life since she was big enough to sleep by herself.”
paragraphs.zh: “她为什么不睡在这里，”迪尔西说，“她每天晚上都在我哄她妈妈睡觉的同一个房间里，因为她已经足够大了，可以自己睡觉了。”

paragraphs.en: “You dont know,” Mother says, “To have my own daughter cast off by her husband. Poor little innocent baby,” she says, looking at Quentin. “You will never know the suffering you’ve caused.”
paragraphs.zh: “你不知道，”母亲说，“让我自己的女儿被她的丈夫抛弃。可怜的无辜的小宝贝，”她看着昆丁说道。“你永远不会知道你所造成的痛苦。”

paragraphs.en: “Hush, Caroline,” Father says.
paragraphs.zh: “嘘，卡罗琳，”父亲说。

paragraphs.en: “What you want to go on like that fo Jason fer?” Dilsey says.
paragraphs.zh: “你想继续这样下去吗？”迪尔西说道。

paragraphs.en: “I’ve tried to protect him,” Mother says. “I’ve always tried to protect him from it. At least I can do my best to shield her.”
paragraphs.zh: “我尽力保护他，”母亲说。“我一直试图保护他免受伤害。至少我可以尽力保护她。”

paragraphs.en: “How sleepin in dis room gwine hurt her, I like to know,” Dilsey says.
paragraphs.zh: “我想知道，在房间里睡觉对她造成了怎样的伤害，”迪尔西说。

paragraphs.en: “I cant help it,” Mother says. “I know I’m just a troublesome old woman. But I know that people cannot flout God’s laws with impunity.”
paragraphs.zh: “我忍不住，”母亲说。“我知道我只是一个麻烦的老太婆。但我知道人们不能藐视上帝的律法而不受惩罚。”

paragraphs.en: “Nonsense,” Father said. “Fix it in Miss Caroline’s room then, Dilsey.”
paragraphs.zh: “胡说，”父亲说。“那就去卡罗琳小姐的房间里解决吧，迪尔西。”

paragraphs.en: “You can say nonsense,” Mother says. “But she must never know. She must never even learn that name. Dilsey, I forbid you ever to speak that name in her hearing. If she could grow up never to know that she had a mother, I would thank God.”
paragraphs.zh: “你可以胡说八道，”母亲说。“但她永远不能知道。她甚至永远不能知道这个名字。迪尔西，我禁止你在她的耳边说出这个名字。如果她长大后永远不知道她有一个母亲，我会感谢上帝。”

paragraphs.en: “Dont be a fool,” Father says.
paragraphs.zh: “别犯傻了，”父亲说。

paragraphs.en: “I have never interfered with the way you brought them up,” Mother says, “But now I cannot stand anymore. We must decide this now, tonight. Either that name is never to be spoken in her hearing, or she must go, or I will go. Take your choice.”
paragraphs.zh: “我从来没有干涉过你养育他们的方式，”母亲说，“但现在我再也忍受不了了。我们必须在今晚做出决定。要么永远不要在她耳边说出这个名字，要么她必须走，要么我走。你选择吧。”

paragraphs.en: “Hush,” Father says, “You’re just upset. Fix it in here, Dilsey.”
paragraphs.zh: “嘘，”父亲说，“你只是不高兴。在这儿解决它，迪尔西。”

paragraphs.en: “En you’s about sick too,” Dilsey says. “You looks like a hant. You git in bed and I’ll fix you a toddy and see kin you sleep. I bet you aint had a full night’s sleep since you lef.”
paragraphs.zh: “嗯，你也病了，”迪尔西说。“你看起来像个汉子。你上床睡觉，我会给你泡一杯棕榈酒，然后看你睡觉。我敢打赌，自从你离开后，你就没有睡过一整夜。”

paragraphs.en: “No,” Mother says, “Dont you know what the doctor says? Why must you encourage him to drink? That’s what’s the matter with him now. Look at me, I suffer too, but I’m not so weak that I must kill myself with whiskey.”
paragraphs.zh: “不，”妈妈说，“你难道不知道医生怎么说吗？你为什么一定要鼓励他喝酒？这就是他现在的问题。看看我，我也很痛苦，但我还没有弱到必须用威士忌自杀的程度。”

paragraphs.en: “Fiddlesticks,” Father says, “What do doctors know? They make their livings advising people to do whatever they are not doing at the time, which is the extent of anyone’s knowledge of the degenerate ape. You’ll have a minister in to hold my hand next.” Then Mother cried, and he went out. Went down stairs, and then I heard the sideboard. I woke up and heard him going down again. Mother had gone to sleep or something, because the house was quiet at last. He was trying to be quiet too, because I couldn’t hear him, only the bottom of his nightshirt and his bare legs in front of the sideboard.
paragraphs.zh: “胡说八道，”父亲说，“医生知道什么？他们靠建议人们做他们当时没有做的事情来谋生，这就是任何人对堕落猿的了解程度。接下来你会有一位牧师来握住我的手。”妈妈哭了，他就出去了。下了楼梯，然后我听到了餐具柜的声音。我醒了，听到他又倒下了。妈妈已经睡着了，因为家里终于安静了。他也试图保持安静，因为我听不到他的声音，只能听到他睡衣的下摆和他光着腿放在餐具柜前的声音。

paragraphs.en: Dilsey fixed the cradle and undressed her and put her in it. She never had waked up since he brought her in the house.
paragraphs.zh: 迪尔西修好摇篮，脱掉她的衣服，把她放进去。自从他把她带进屋后，她就再也没有醒过。

paragraphs.en: “She pretty near too big fer hit,” Dilsey says. “Dar now. I gwine spread me a pallet right acrost de hall, so you wont need to git up in de night.”
paragraphs.zh: “她几乎太大了，无法击中，”迪尔西说。“现在。我在大厅对面铺了一个托盘，这样你就不需要在晚上起床了。”

paragraphs.en: “I wont sleep,” Mother says. “You go on home. I wont mind. I’ll be happy to give the rest of my life to her, if I can just prevent—”
paragraphs.zh: “我睡不着，”妈妈说。“你回家吧。我不介意。我很乐意把我的余生交给她，如果我能阻止——”

paragraphs.en: “Hush, now,” Dilsey says. “We gwine take keer of her. En you go on to bed too,” she says to me, “You got to go to school tomorrow.”
paragraphs.zh: “嘘，现在，”迪尔西说。“我们都讨厌她。那么你也去睡觉吧，”她对我说，“你明天还得去上学。”

paragraphs.en: So I went out, then Mother called me back and cried on me awhile.
paragraphs.zh: 于是我就出去了，然后妈妈把我叫回来，哭了一会儿。

paragraphs.en: “You are my only hope,” she says. “Every night I thank God for you.” While we were waiting there for them to start she says Thank God if he had to be taken too, it is you left me and not Quentin. Thank God you are not a Compson, because all I have left now is you and Maury and I says, Well I could spare Uncle Maury myself. Well, he kept on patting her hand with his black glove, talking away from her. He took them off when his turn with the shovel came. He got up near the first, where they were holding the umbrellas over them, stamping every now and then and trying to kick the mud off their feet and sticking to the shovels so they’d have to knock it off, making a hollow sound when it fell on it, and when I stepped back around the hack I could see him behind a tombstone, taking another one out of a bottle. I thought he never was going to stop because I had on my new suit too, but it happened that there wasn’t much mud on the wheels yet, only Mother saw it and says I dont know when you’ll ever have another one and Uncle Maury says, “Now, now. Dont you worry at all. You have me to depend on, always.”
paragraphs.zh: “你是我唯一的希望，”她说。“每天晚上我都为你感谢上帝。”当我们在那里等待他们开始时，她说感谢上帝，如果他也必须被带走，是你离开了我，而不是昆丁。感谢上帝，你不是康普生，因为我现在只剩下你和莫里了，我说，好吧，我可以自己饶过莫里舅舅。好吧，他继续用黑色手套拍着她的手，不再说话。当轮到他用铲子时，他把它们脱下来。他在第一处附近站起来，他们把雨伞撑在雨伞上，时不时地跺脚，试图把脚上的泥踢掉，并粘在铲子上，这样他们就必须把泥铲掉，当泥落在铲子上时发出空洞的声音，当我绕过墓碑后退时，我可以看到他在一块墓碑后面，从一个瓶子里取出另一个。我以为他永远不会停下来，因为我也穿上了新衣服，但碰巧轮子上还没有多少泥，只有妈妈看到了，说我不知道​​你什么时候才能再有一套，莫里舅舅说：“现在，现在。你别担心。你有我可以依靠，永远。”

paragraphs.en: And we have. Always. The fourth letter was from him. But there wasn’t any need to open it. I could have written it myself, or recited it to her from memory, adding ten dollars just to be safe. But I had a hunch about that other letter. I just felt that it was about time she was up to some of her tricks again. She got pretty wise after that first time. She found out pretty quick that I was a different breed of cat from Father. When they begun to get it filled up toward the top Mother started crying sure enough, so Uncle Maury got in with her and drove off. He says You can come in with somebody; they’ll be glad to give you a lift. I’ll have to take your mother on and I thought about saying, Yes you ought to brought two bottles instead of just one only I thought about where we were, so I let them go on. Little they cared how wet I got, because then Mother could have a whale of a time being afraid I was taking pneumonia.
paragraphs.zh: 我们有。总是。第四封信是他写的。但没有必要打开它。我可以自己写，或者凭记忆背诵给她听，为了安全起见，再加上十美元。但我对另一封信有一种预感。我只是觉得她是时候再次施展她的伎俩了。第一次之后她就变得很聪明了。她很快就发现我和父亲是不同品种的猫。当他们开始往山顶加满油时，母亲果然开始哭了，所以莫里舅舅和她一起上车然后开车走了。他说你可以和某人一起进来；他们会很高兴载你一程。我得带你妈妈去，我想说，是的，你应该带两瓶，而不是只带一瓶，只是我想到了我们在哪里，所以我让他们继续。他们很少关心我被淋湿了多少，因为这样一来，母亲就会因为担心我得了肺炎而大吃一惊。

paragraphs.en: Well, I got to thinking about that and watching them throwing dirt into it, slapping it on anyway like they were making mortar or something or building a fence, and I began to feel sort of funny and so I decided to walk around a while. I thought that if I went toward town they’d catch up and be trying to make me get in one of them, so I went on back toward the nigger graveyard. I got under some cedars, where the rain didn’t come much, only dripping now and then, where I could see when they got through and went away. After a while they were all gone and I waited a minute and came out.
paragraphs.zh: 好吧，我开始思考这一点，看着他们往里面扔泥土，拍打它，就像他们在制造迫击炮或其他东西或建造栅栏一样，我开始觉得有点有趣，所以我决定四处走走。我想，如果我进城，他们会追上来，并试图让我进入其中，所以我又朝黑鬼墓地走去。我躲到了一些雪松树下，那里下的雨不多，只是时不时地滴下，我可以看到它们什么时候穿过去，什么时候走开。过了一会儿，他们都走了，我等了一会儿就出来了。

paragraphs.en: I had to follow the path to keep out of the wet grass so I didn’t see her until I was pretty near there, standing there in a black cloak, looking at the flowers. I knew who it was right off, before she turned and looked at me and lifted up her veil.
paragraphs.zh: 我必须沿着小路走，避开潮湿的草地，所以直到我很靠近那里才看到她，穿着黑色斗篷站在那里，看着花朵。在她转过身来看着我并掀起面纱之前，我立刻就知道是谁了。

paragraphs.en: “Hello, Jason,” she says, holding out her hand. We shook hands.
paragraphs.zh: “你好，杰生，”她伸出手说道。我们握手了。

paragraphs.en: “What are you doing here?” I says. “I thought you promised her you wouldn’t come back here. I thought you had more sense than that.”
paragraphs.zh: “你在这里做什么？”我说。“我以为你答应过她不会再来这里了。我以为你比那更有道理。”

paragraphs.en: “Yes?” she says. She looked at the flowers again. There must have been fifty dollars’ worth. Somebody had put one bunch on Quentin’s. “You did?” she says.
paragraphs.zh: “是吗？”她说。她又看了看花。肯定有五十美元的价值。有人在昆丁的身上放了一束。“你做到了？”她说。

paragraphs.en: “I’m not surprised though,” I says. “I wouldn’t put anything past you. You dont mind anybody. You dont give a damn about anybody.”
paragraphs.zh: “不过我并不感到惊讶，”我说。“我不会把任何事情放在你身上。你不介意任何人。你不在乎任何人。”

paragraphs.en: “Oh,” she says, “that job.” She looked at the grave. “I’m sorry about that, Jason.”
paragraphs.zh: “哦，”她说，“那份工作。”她看着坟墓。“对此我很抱歉，杰生。”

paragraphs.en: “I bet you are,” I says. “You’ll talk mighty meek now. But you needn’t have come back. There’s not anything left. Ask Uncle Maury, if you dont believe me.”
paragraphs.zh: “我打赌你是的，”我说。“你现在会说得很温顺了。不过你不必回来了。什么都没有了。不信就问莫里舅舅吧。”

paragraphs.en: “I dont want anything,” she says. She looked at the grave. “Why didn’t they let me know?” she says. “I just happened to see it in the paper. On the back page. Just happened to.”
paragraphs.zh: “我什么都不想要，”她说。她看着坟墓。“他们为什么不通知我？”她说。“我只是碰巧在报纸上看到了它。在背面。只是碰巧。”

paragraphs.en: I didn’t say anything. We stood there, looking at the grave, and then I got to thinking about when we were little and one thing and another and I got to feeling funny again, kind of mad or something, thinking about now we’d have Uncle Maury around the house all the time, running things like the way he left me to come home in the rain by myself. I says,
paragraphs.zh: 我什么也没说。我们站在那里，看着坟墓，然后我开始回想起我们小的时候，一件事又另一件事，我又开始感到有趣，有点生气什么的，想着现在我们有莫里舅舅一直在房子周围，做一些事情，就像他让我一个人在雨中回家一样。我说，

paragraphs.en: “A fine lot you care, sneaking in here soon as he’s dead. But it wont do you any good. Dont think that you can take advantage of this to come sneaking back. If you cant stay on the horse you’ve got, you’ll have to walk,” I says. “We dont even know your name at that house,” I says. “Do you know that? We don’t even know you with him and Quentin,” I says. “Do you know that?”
paragraphs.zh: “你很关心，他一死就偷偷溜进来。但这对你没有任何好处。别以为你可以利用这个机会偷偷回来。如果你不能留在你的马上，你就只能步行了，”我说。“我们甚至不知道你在那所房子的名字，”我说。“你知道吗？我们甚至都不认识你和他还有昆丁，”我说。“你知道吗？”

paragraphs.en: “I know it,” she says. “Jason,” she says, looking at the grave, “if you’ll fix it so I can see her a minute I’ll give you fifty dollars.”
paragraphs.zh: “我知道，”她说。“杰生，”她看着坟墓说道，“如果你能修好它，让我能见见她，我就给你五十美元。”

paragraphs.en: “You haven’t got fifty dollars,” I says.
paragraphs.zh: “你没有五十美元，”我说。

paragraphs.en: “Will you?” she says, not looking at me.
paragraphs.zh: “你愿意吗？”她说，没有看我。

paragraphs.en: “Let’s see it,” I says. “I dont believe you’ve got fifty dollars.”
paragraphs.zh: “让我们看看，”我说。“我不相信你有五十美元。”

paragraphs.en: I could see where her hands were moving under her cloak, then she held her hand out. Damn if it wasn’t full of money. I could see two or three yellow ones.
paragraphs.zh: 我可以看到她的手在斗篷下移动，然后她伸出了手。如果不是装满了钱就该死。我可以看到两三个黄色的。

paragraphs.en: “Does he still give you money?” I says. “How much does he send you?”
paragraphs.zh: “他还给你钱吗？”我说。“他寄给你多少钱？”

paragraphs.en: “I’ll give you a hundred,” she says. “Will you?”
paragraphs.zh: “我给你一百，”她说。“你会？”

paragraphs.en: “Just a minute,” I says, “And just like I say. I wouldn’t have her know it for a thousand dollars.”
paragraphs.zh: “等一下，”我说，“就像我说的。即使花一千块钱，我也不会让她知道。”

paragraphs.en: “Yes,” she says. “Just like you say do it. Just so I see her a minute. I wont beg or do anything. I’ll go right on away.”
paragraphs.zh: “是的，”她说。“就像你说的那样做。让我见见她一分钟。我不会乞求或做任何事情。我会马上走。”

paragraphs.en: “Give me the money,” I says.
paragraphs.zh: “给我钱，”我说。

paragraphs.en: “I’ll give it to you afterward,” she says.
paragraphs.zh: “稍后我会把它给你，”她说。

paragraphs.en: “Dont you trust me?” I says.
paragraphs.zh: “你不相信我吗？”我说。

paragraphs.en: “No,” she says. “I know you. I grew up with you.”
paragraphs.zh: “不，”她说。“我认识你。我和你一起长大。”

paragraphs.en: “You’re a fine one to talk about trusting people,” I says. “Well,” I says, “I got to get on out of the rain. Goodbye.” I made to go away.
paragraphs.zh: “你是一个善于谈论信任别人的人，”我说。“好吧，”我说，“我得出去避雨。再见。”我只好走开。

paragraphs.en: “Jason,” she says. I stopped.
paragraphs.zh: “杰生，”她说。我停了下来。

paragraphs.en: “Yes?” I says. “Hurry up. I’m getting wet.”
paragraphs.zh: “是吗？”我说。“快点，我都湿透了。”

paragraphs.en: “All right,” she says. “Here.” There wasn’t anybody in sight. I went back and took the money. She still held to it. “You’ll do it?” she says, looking at me from under the veil, “You promise?”
paragraphs.zh: “好吧，”她说。“这里。”看不见任何人。我回去拿了钱。她依然坚持着。“你会做吗？”她从面纱下看着我说，“你保证吗？”

paragraphs.en: “Let go,” I says, “You want somebody to come along and see us?”
paragraphs.zh: “放手吧，”我说，“你想让人过来看看我们吗？”

paragraphs.en: She let go. I put the money in my pocket. “You’ll do it, Jason?” she says. “I wouldn’t ask you, if there was any other way.”
paragraphs.zh: 她放开了。我把钱放进口袋里。“你会做到吗，杰生？”她说。“我不会问你，如果还有别的办法。”

paragraphs.en: “You’re damn right there’s no other way,” I says. “Sure I’ll do it. I said I would, didn’t I? Only you’ll have to do just like I say, now.”
paragraphs.zh: “你说得对，没有其他办法，”我说。“我当然会做。我说过我会的，不是吗？只是你现在必须按照我说的去做。”

paragraphs.en: “Yes,” she says, “I will.” So I told her where to be, and went to the livery stable. I hurried and got there just as they were unhitching the hack. I asked if they had paid for it yet and he said No and I said Mrs Compson forgot something and wanted it again, so they let me take it. Mink was driving. I bought him a cigar, so we drove around until it begun to get dark on the back streets where they wouldn’t see him. Then Mink said he’d have to take the team on back and so I said I’d buy him another cigar and so we drove into the lane and I went across the yard to the house. I stopped in the hall until I could hear Mother and Uncle Maury upstairs, then I went on back to the kitchen. She and Ben were there with Dilsey. I said Mother wanted her and I took her into the house. I found Uncle Maury’s raincoat and put it around her and picked her up and went back to the lane and got in the hack. I told Mink to drive to the depot. He was afraid to pass the stable, so we had to go the back way and I saw her standing on the corner under the light and I told Mink to drive close to the walk and when I said Go on, to give the team a bat. Then I took the raincoat off of her and held her to the window and Caddy saw her and sort of jumped forward.
paragraphs.zh: “是的，”她说，“我会的。”于是我告诉她要去哪里，然后去了马厩。当他们解开黑客的时候，我赶紧赶到了那里。我问他们付钱了吗，他说没有，我说康普生夫人忘记了一些东西，又想要它，所以他们让我拿了。明克正在开车。我给他买了一支雪茄，所以我们开车兜风，直到天黑在后街上他们就看不到他了。然后明克说他必须带球队回来，所以我说我要再给他买一支雪茄，所以我们开车进入小巷，我穿过院子回到房子。我在大厅里停了下来，直到听到楼上妈妈和莫里舅舅的声音，然后我又回到厨房。她和本和迪尔西一起在那里。我说妈妈想要她，然后我就把她带进了屋子。我找到莫里舅舅的雨衣，给她披上，抱起她，回到巷子里，钻进了小屋。我告诉明克开车去车站。他害怕经过马厩，所以我们不得不往后走，我看到她站在灯下的拐角处，我告诉明克把车开到人行道附近，当我说继续前进时，给团队一个球棒。然后我脱下她的雨衣，把她抱到窗边，凯蒂看到了她，有点向前跳了。

paragraphs.en: “Hit ’em, Mink!” I says, and Mink gave them a cut and we went past her like a fire engine. “Now get on that train like you promised,” I says. I could see her running after us through the back window. “Hit ’em again,” I says, “Let’s get on home.” When we turned the corner she was still running.
paragraphs.zh: “打他们，明克！”我说，明克给了他们一刀，我们像消防车一样从她身边经过。“现在就像你答应的那样上火车吧，”我说。我可以透过后窗看到她追赶我们。“再打他们一次，”我说，“我们回家吧。”当我们拐过街角时，她还在跑。

paragraphs.en: And so I counted the money again that night and put it away, and I didn’t feel so bad. I says I reckon that’ll show you. I reckon you’ll know now that you cant beat me out of a job and get away with it. It never occurred to me she wouldn’t keep her promise and take that train. But I didn’t know much about them then; I didn’t have any more sense than to believe what they said, because the next morning damn if she didn’t walk right into the store, only she had sense enough to wear the veil and not speak to anybody. It was Saturday morning, because I was at the store, and she came right on back to the desk where I was, walking fast.
paragraphs.zh: 于是那天晚上我又数了数钱，把它收了起来，心里也没那么难受了。我说我想这会告诉你。我想你现在就会知道，你不可能把我丢掉工作并侥幸逃脱。我从来没有想到她不会遵守诺言并乘坐那趟火车。但当时我对他们了解不多；我没有任何理智，只能相信他们说的话，因为第二天早上，该死的，如果她没有直接走进商店，只有她有足够的理智戴上面纱，不和任何人说话。那是星期六早上，因为我在商店，她快步走回我所在的办公桌旁。

paragraphs.en: “Liar,” she says, “Liar.”
paragraphs.zh: “骗子，”她说，“骗子。”

paragraphs.en: “Are you crazy?” I says. “What do you mean? coming in here like this?” She started in, but I shut her off. I says, “You already cost me one job; do you want me to lose this one too? If you’ve got anything to say to me, I’ll meet you somewhere after dark. What have you got to say to me?” I says, “Didn’t I do everything I said? I said see her a minute, didn’t I? Well, didn’t you?” She just stood there looking at me, shaking like an ague-fit, her hands clenched and kind of jerking. “I did just what I said I would,” I says, “You’re the one that lied. You promised to take that train. Didn’t you Didn’t you promise? If you think you can get that money back, just try it,” I says. “If it’d been a thousand dollars, you’d still owe me after the risk I took. And if I see or hear you’re still in town after number 17 runs,” I says, “I’ll tell Mother and Uncle Maury. Then hold your breath until you see her again.” She just stood there, looking at me, twisting her hands together.
paragraphs.zh: “你疯了吗？”我说。“什么意思？就这样进来了？”她开始说话，但我阻止了她。我说：“你已经让我失去了一份工作；你想让我也失去这份工作吗？如果你有什么话要对我说，我会在天黑后某个地方与你见面。你有什么话要对我说的吗？”我说：“我不是已经做到了我所说的一切吗？我说过见她一下，不是吗？那么，你不是吗？”她只是站在那里看着我，浑身发抖，双手紧握，有些抽搐。“我就按照我说的做了，”我说，“你是撒谎的人。你答应乘坐那趟火车。你不是答应了吗？如果你认为你能拿回那笔钱，就试试吧，”我说。“如果是一千美元，在我冒了这个风险之后，你仍然欠我。如果我看到或听到你在第 17 次跑步后还在城里，”我说，“我会告诉妈妈和莫里舅舅。然后屏住呼吸，直到你再次见到她。”她只是站在那里，看着我，双手绞在一起。

paragraphs.en: “Damn you,” she says, “Damn you.”
paragraphs.zh: “该死的，”她说，“该死的。”

paragraphs.en: “Sure,” I says, “That’s all right too. Mind what I say, now. After number 17, and I tell them.”
paragraphs.zh: “当然，”我说，“那也没关系。现在注意我说的话。17 号之后，我会告诉他们。”

paragraphs.en: After she was gone I felt better. I says I reckon you’ll think twice before you deprive me of a job that was promised me. I was a kid then. I believed folks when they said they’d do things. I’ve learned better since. Besides, like I say I guess I dont need any man’s help to get along I can stand on my own feet like I always have. Then all of a sudden I thought of Dilsey and Uncle Maury. I thought how she’d get around Dilsey and that Uncle Maury would do anything for ten dollars. And there I was, couldn’t even get away from the store to protect my own Mother. Like she says, if one of you had to be taken, thank God it was you left me I can depend on you and I says well I dont reckon I’ll ever get far enough from the store to get out of your reach. Somebody’s got to hold on to what little we have left, I reckon.
paragraphs.zh: 她走后我感觉好多了。我说我想你在剥夺我答应给我的工作之前会三思而后行。那时我还是个孩子。当人们说他们会做事时，我相信他们。从那以后我学得更好了。此外，就像我说的，我想我不需要任何男人的帮助就能相处，我可以像往常一样自力更生。然后突然我想到了迪尔西和莫里舅舅。我想她会如何绕过迪尔西，莫里舅舅会为了十美元做任何事。我什至无法离开商店来保护我自己的母亲。就像她说的，如果你们中的一个人必须被带走，感谢上帝，是你离开了我，我可以依靠你，我说好吧，我认为我永远不会离开商店足够远的距离来摆脱你的影响。我想，必须有人保住我们所剩无几的东西。

paragraphs.en: So as soon as I got home I fixed Dilsey. I told Dilsey she had leprosy and I got the bible and read where a man’s flesh rotted off and I told her that if she ever looked at her or Ben or Quentin they’d catch it too. So I thought I had everything all fixed until that day when I came home and found Ben bellowing. Raising hell and nobody could quiet him. Mother said, Well, get him the slipper then. Dilsey made out she didn’t hear. Mother said it again and I says I’d go I couldn’t stand that damn noise. Like I say I can stand lots of things I dont expect much from them but if I have to work all day long in a damn store damn if I dont think I deserve a little peace and quiet to eat dinner in. So I says I’d go and Dilsey says quick, “Jason!”
paragraphs.zh: 所以我一回到家就修好了迪尔西。我告诉迪尔西她得了麻风病，我拿了圣经，读到了一个男人的肉腐烂的地方，我告诉她，如果她看她、本或昆丁，他们也会染上麻风病。所以我以为我已经把一切都修好了，直到那天我回到家，发现本在吼叫。引起地狱，没有人能让他安静下来。妈妈说，好吧，那就给他拿拖鞋吧。迪尔西装作没听见。妈妈又说了一遍，我说我要走了，我受不了那该死的噪音。就像我说的，我可以忍受很多事情，我对他们的期望并不高，但如果我必须在一家该死的商店里工作一整天，如果我不认为我应该有一点和平和安静的地方吃晚饭，那该死的。所以我说我会去，迪尔西很快说，“杰生！”

paragraphs.en: Well, like a flash I knew what was up, but just to make sure I went and got the slipper and brought it back, and just like I thought, when he saw it you’d thought we were killing him. So I made Dilsey own up, then I told Mother. We had to take her up to bed then, and after things got quieted down a little I put the fear of God into Dilsey. As much as you can into a nigger, that is. That’s the trouble with nigger servants, when they’ve been with you for a long time they get so full of self importance that they’re not worth a damn. Think they run the whole family.
paragraphs.zh: 好吧，就像一瞬间我知道发生了什么，但只是为了确保我去拿了拖鞋并将其带回来，就像我想的那样，当他看到它时，你会认为我们要杀了他。所以我让迪尔西坦白了，然后我告诉了妈妈。然后我们不得不带她上床睡觉，等事情稍微平静下来后，我把对上帝的敬畏带入了迪尔西。就是说，尽可能多地变成一个黑鬼。这就是黑鬼仆人的麻烦，当他们和你在一起很长一段时间后，他们就会变得非常自以为是，以至于一文不值。认为他们经营着整个家庭。

paragraphs.en: “I like to know whut’s de hurt in lettin dat po chile see her own baby,” Dilsey says. “If Mr Jason was still here hit ud be different.”
paragraphs.zh: “我想知道让智利人看到自己的孩子有什么伤害，”迪尔西说。“如果杰生先生还在这里，情况就会不同。”

paragraphs.en: “Only Mr Jason’s not here,” I says. “I know you wont pay me any mind, but I reckon you’ll do what Mother says. You keep on worrying her like this until you get her into the graveyard too, then you can fill the whole house full of ragtag and bobtail. But what did you want to let that damn idiot see her for?”
paragraphs.zh: “只有杰生先生不在这里，”我说。“我知道你不会理我，但我想你会照妈妈说的做的。你一直这样担心她，直到你把她也带进墓地，然后你就可以让整个房子都充满了乌合之众和短尾辫。但你想让那个该死的白痴看到她做什么？”

paragraphs.en: “You’s a cold man, Jason, if man you is,” she says. “I thank de Lawd I got mo heart dan dat, even ef hit is black.”
paragraphs.zh: “杰生，如果你是个冷酷的男人的话，”她说。“我感谢德·劳德，我有一颗心，但即使击中的是黑色的。”

paragraphs.en: “At least I’m man enough to keep that flour barrel full,” I says. “And if you do that again, you wont be eating out of it either.”
paragraphs.zh: “至少我有足够的男子气概，可以把面粉桶装满，”我说。“如果你再这样做，你也不会再吃它了。”

paragraphs.en: So the next time I told her that if she tried Dilsey again, Mother was going to fire Dilsey and send Ben to Jackson and take Quentin and go away. She looked at me for a while. There wasn’t any street light close and I couldn’t see her face much. But I could feel her looking at me. When we were little when she’d get mad and couldn’t do anything about it her upper lip would begin to jump. Everytime it jumped it would leave a little more of her teeth showing, and all the time she’d be as still as a post, not a muscle moving except her lip jerking higher and higher up her teeth. But she didn’t say anything. She just said,
paragraphs.zh: 所以下次我告诉她，如果她再尝试迪尔西，妈妈就会解雇迪尔西，然后把本送到杰克逊，然后带着昆丁走开。她看了我一会儿。附近没有路灯，我看不清她的脸。但我能感觉到她在看着我。当我们还小的时候，当她生气却无能为力时，她的上嘴唇就会开始跳动。每次它跳起来，她的牙齿都会露出来，而她一直都像一根柱子一样一动不动，除了她的嘴唇在牙齿上越来越高地跳动之外，没有任何肌肉在移动。但她什么也没说。她只是说，

paragraphs.en: “All right. How much?”
paragraphs.zh: “好吧。多少钱？”

paragraphs.en: “Well, if one look through a hack window was worth a hundred,” I says. So after that she behaved pretty well, only one time she asked to see a statement of the bank account.
paragraphs.zh: “好吧，如果透过黑客窗口看一眼就值一百美元，”我说。所以后来她表现得还不错，只有一次她要求看银行账户的对账单。

paragraphs.en: “I know they have Mother’s indorsement on them,” she says, “But I want to see the bank statement. I want to see myself where those checks go.”
paragraphs.zh: “我知道他们有母亲的背书，”她说，“但我想看看银行对账单。我想看看我自己那些支票去了哪里。”

paragraphs.en: “That’s in Mother’s private business,” I says. “If you think you have any right to pry into her private affairs I’ll tell her you believe those checks are being misappropriated and you want an audit because you dont trust her.”
paragraphs.zh: “那是母亲的私事，”我说。“如果你认为你有权利窥探她的私人事务，我会告诉她你认为这些支票被挪用了，你想要接受审计，因为你不信任她。”

paragraphs.en: She didn’t say anything or move. I could hear her whispering Damn you oh damn you oh damn you.
paragraphs.zh: 她什么也没说，也没有动。我能听到她低声说该死的你，该死的你，该死的你。

paragraphs.en: “Say it out,” I says, “I dont reckon it’s any secret what you and I think of one another. Maybe you want the money back,” I says.
paragraphs.zh: “说出来，”我说，“我不认为你和我对彼此的看法有什么秘密。也许你想要回钱，”我说。

paragraphs.en: “Listen, Jason,” she says, “Dont lie to me now. About her. I wont ask to see anything. If that isn’t enough, I’ll send more each month. Just promise that she’ll—that she—You can do that. Things for her. Be kind to her. Little things that I cant, they wont let. . . . But you wont. You never had a drop of warm blood in you. Listen,” she says, “If you’ll get Mother to let me have her back, I’ll give you a thousand dollars.”
paragraphs.zh: “听着，杰生，”她说，“现在别对我撒谎。关于她的事。我不会要求看任何东西。如果这还不够，我每个月都会寄更多。只要保证她会——她——你能做到。为她做事。善待她。我做不到的小事，他们不会让……但你不会的。你身上从来没有一滴热血。听着，”她说，“如果你能让妈妈为了让她回来，我给你一千块钱。”

paragraphs.en: “You haven’t got a thousand dollars,” I says, “I know you’re lying now.”
paragraphs.zh: “你没有一千美元，”我说，“我知道你现在在撒谎。”

paragraphs.en: “Yes I have. I will have. I can get it.”
paragraphs.zh: “是的，我有。我会的。我能得到它。”

paragraphs.en: “And I know how you’ll get it,” I says, “You’ll get it the same way you got her. And when she gets big enough—” Then I thought she really was going to hit at me, and then I didn’t know what she was going to do. She acted for a minute like some kind of a toy that’s wound up too tight and about to burst all to pieces.
paragraphs.zh: “我知道你会怎样得到它，”我说，“你会得到它，就像你得到她一样。当她变得足够大时——”然后我以为她真的要打我，然后我不知道她会做什么。有那么一分钟，她表现得就像一个被卷得太紧、快要炸成碎片的玩具。

paragraphs.en: “Oh, I’m crazy,” she says, “I’m insane. I can’t take her. Keep her. What am I thinking of. Jason,” she says, grabbing my arm. Her hands were hot as fever. “You’ll have to promise to take care of her, to—She’s kin to you; your own flesh and blood. Promise, Jason. You have Father’s name: do you think I’d have to ask him twice? once, even?”
paragraphs.zh: “哦，我疯了，”她说，“我疯了。我不能带走她。留下她。我在想什么。杰生，”她说，抓住了我的手臂。她的手像发烧一样滚烫。“你必须答应照顾她，到——她是你的亲人；你的骨肉。答应我，杰生。你有父亲的名字：你认为我需要问他两次吗？甚至一次？”

paragraphs.en: “That’s so,” I says, “He did leave me something. What do you want me to do,” I says, “Buy an apron and a go-cart? I never got you into this,” I says. “I run more risk than you do, because you haven’t got anything at stake. So if you expect—”
paragraphs.zh: “是这样的，”我说，“他确实给我留下了一些东西。你想让我做什么，”我说，“买一条围裙和一辆卡丁车？我从来没有让你参与过这个，”我说。“我比你冒更大的风险，因为你没有任何危险。所以如果你期望——”

paragraphs.en: “No,” she says, then she begun to laugh and to try to hold it back all at the same time. “No. I have nothing at stake,” she says, making that noise, putting her hands to her mouth, “Nuh-nuh-nothing,” she says.
paragraphs.zh: “不，”她说，然后她开始笑，同时又试图忍住。“不。我没有任何危险，”她说，用手捂住嘴，发出声音，“没什么，没什么，”她说。

paragraphs.en: “Here,” I says, “Stop that!”
paragraphs.zh: “在这里，”我说，“别这样！”

paragraphs.en: “I’m tr-trying to,” she says, holding her hands over her mouth. “Oh God, oh God.”
paragraphs.zh: “我正在努力，”她用手捂住嘴说道。“天啊，天啊。”

paragraphs.en: “I’m going away from here,” I says, “I cant be seen here. You get on out of town now, you hear?”
paragraphs.zh: “我要离开这里，”我说，“这里看不见我。你现在就出城吧，听到了吗？”

paragraphs.en: “Wait,” she says, catching my arm. “I’ve stopped. I wont again. You promise, Jason?” she says, and me feeling her eyes almost like they were touching my face, “You promise? Mother—that money—if sometimes she needs things—If I send checks for her to you, other ones besides those, you’ll give them to her? You wont tell? You’ll see that she has things like other girls?”
paragraphs.zh: “等等，”她抓住我的手臂说道。“我已经戒了。我不会再这样了。杰生，你保证吗？”她说，我感觉到她的眼睛几乎像是在抚摸我的脸，“你保证？妈妈——那笔钱——如果她有时需要东西的话——如果我给她寄支票给你，除了这些之外，你也会给她？你不会告诉吗？你会看到她和其他女孩一样有东西吗？”

paragraphs.en: “Sure,” I says, “As long as you behave and do like I tell you.”
paragraphs.zh: “当然，”我说，“只要你表现得像我告诉你的那样。”

paragraphs.en: And so when Earl came up front with his hat on he says, “I’m going to step up to Rogers’ and get a snack. We wont have time to go home to dinner, I reckon.”
paragraphs.zh: 因此，当厄尔戴着帽子走到前面时，他说：“我要去罗杰斯家吃点零食。我想我们没有时间回家吃晚饭了。”

paragraphs.en: “What’s the matter we wont have time?” I says.
paragraphs.zh: “怎么了，我们没有时间？”我说。

paragraphs.en: “With this show in town and all,” he says. “They’re going to give an afternoon performance too, and they’ll all want to get done trading in time to go to it. So we’d better just run up to Rogers’.”
paragraphs.zh: “随着镇上的这场演出等等，”他说。“他们也将进行下午的表演，他们都希望及时完成交易才能参加。所以我们最好跑到罗杰斯那里去。”

paragraphs.en: “All right,” I says, “It’s your stomach. If you want to make a slave of yourself to your business, it’s all right with me.”
paragraphs.zh: “好吧，”我说，“这是你的胃。如果你想让自己成为你事业的奴隶，我没意见。”

paragraphs.en: “I reckon you’ll never be a slave to any business,” he says.
paragraphs.zh: “我认为你永远不会成为任何企业的奴隶，”他说。

paragraphs.en: “Not unless it’s Jason Compson’s business,” I says.
paragraphs.zh: “除非这是杰生康普生的事，”我说。

paragraphs.en: So when I went back and opened it the only thing that surprised me was it was a money order not a check. Yes, sir. You cant trust a one of them. After all the risk I’d taken, risking Mother finding out about her coming down here once or twice a year sometimes, and me having to tell Mother lies about it. That’s gratitude for you. And I wouldn’t put it past her to try to notify the postoffice not to let anyone except her cash it. Giving a kid like that fifty dollars. Why I never saw fifty dollars until I was twenty-one years old, with all the other boys with the afternoon off and all day Saturday and me working in a store. Like I say, how can they expect anybody to control her, with her giving her money behind our backs. She has the same home you had I says, and the same raising. I reckon Mother is a better judge of what she needs than you are, that haven’t even got a home. “If you want to give her money,” I says, “You send it to Mother, dont be giving it to her. If I’ve got to run this risk every few months, you’ll have to do like I say, or it’s out.”
paragraphs.zh: 所以当我回去打开它时，唯一让我惊讶的是这是一张汇票而不是支票。是的，先生。你不能相信他们中的任何一个。毕竟我冒了那么多风险，冒着让母亲发现她每年来这里一两次的风险，而我不得不向母亲撒谎。这就是对你的感激之情。我不会让她尝试通知邮局除了她之外不要让任何人兑现。给这样的孩子五十美元。为什么我从来没有见过五十美元，直到我二十一岁时，和其他男孩一起下午休息，星期六一整天，而我在一家商店工作。就像我说的，她在背后给她钱，他们怎么能指望任何人控制她呢。我说她和你有同样的家，同样的成长环境。我认为母亲比你更能判断自己的需要，因为你甚至还没有家。“如果你想给她钱，”我说，“你把钱寄给妈妈，而不是给她。如果我每隔几个月就得冒这个风险，你就必须按照我说的去做，否则就完了。”

paragraphs.en: And just about the time I got ready to begin on it because if Earl thought I was going to dash up the street and gobble two bits worth of indigestion on his account he was bad fooled. I may not be sitting with my feet on a mahogany desk but I am being paid for what I do inside this building and if I cant manage to live a civilised life outside of it I’ll go where I can. I can stand on my own feet; I dont need any man’s mahogany desk to prop me up. So just about the time I got ready to start I’d have to drop everything and run to sell some redneck a dime’s worth of nails or something, and Earl up there gobbling a sandwich and half way back already, like as not, and then I found that all the blanks were gone. I remembered then that I had aimed to get some more, but it was too late now, and then I looked up and there Quentin came. In the back door. I heard her asking old Job if I was there. I just had time to stick them in the drawer and close it.
paragraphs.zh: 就在我准备开始做这件事的时候，因为如果厄尔以为我会冲到街上，为了他的缘故狼吞虎咽地吃掉两块消化不良的东西，那他就上当了。我可能不会把脚放在红木桌子上，但我在这栋大楼里所做的事情是有报酬的，如果我不能在大楼外过上文明的生活，我会去我能去的地方。我能自立；我不需要任何男人的红木桌子来支撑我。所以就在我准备开始的时候，我不得不放下一切，跑去卖一些乡下人一角钱的钉子什么的，厄尔在那里狼吞虎咽地吃着三明治，已经回来了一半，就像没有一样，然后我发现所有的空白都消失了。我这才想起来，本来还想多拿一些，但现在已经晚了，抬头一看，昆丁来了。在后门。我听到她问老乔布我是否在场。我刚好有时间把它们放进抽屉里并关上它。

paragraphs.en: She came around to the desk. I looked at my watch.
paragraphs.zh: 她走到办公桌前。我看了看手表。

paragraphs.en: “You been to dinner already?” I says. “It’s just twelve; I just heard it strike. You must have flown home and back.”
paragraphs.zh: “你已经吃过晚饭了吗？”我说。“才十二点，我刚刚听到钟声敲响了。你肯定已经飞回家了。”

paragraphs.en: “I’m not going home to dinner,” she says. “Did I get a letter today?”
paragraphs.zh: “我不会回家吃晚饭，”她说。“今天收到信了吗？”

paragraphs.en: “Were you expecting one?” I says. “Have you got a sweetie that can write?”
paragraphs.zh: “你在等一个吗？”我说。“你有一个会写字的甜心吗？”

paragraphs.en: “From Mother,” she says. “Did I get a letter from Mother?” she says, looking at me.
paragraphs.zh: “来自母亲，”她说。“我收到妈妈的信了吗？”她看着我说道。

paragraphs.en: “Mother got one from her,” I says. “I haven’t opened it. You’ll have to wait until she opens it. She’ll let you see it, I imagine.”
paragraphs.zh: “妈妈从她那里得到了一个，”我说。“我还没打开。你得等她打开。我想她会让你看到的。”

paragraphs.en: “Please, Jason,” she says, not paying any attention, “Did I get one?”
paragraphs.zh: “请问，杰生，”她没有理睬，“我得到一个了吗？”

paragraphs.en: “What’s the matter?” I says. “I never knew you to be this anxious about anybody. You must expect some money from her.”
paragraphs.zh: “怎么了？”我说。“我从来不知道你会对任何人如此焦虑。你一定指望从她那里得到一些钱。”

paragraphs.en: “She said she—” she says. “Please, Jason,” she says, “Did I?”
paragraphs.zh: “她说她——”她说。“请问，杰生，”她说，“是吗？”

paragraphs.en: “You must have been to school today, after all,” I says, “Somewhere where they taught you to say please. Wait a minute, while I wait on that customer.”
paragraphs.zh: “毕竟你今天一定去了学校，”我说，“他们教你说‘请’的地方。等一下，我去侍候那个顾客。”

paragraphs.en: I went and waited on him. When I turned to come back she was out of sight behind the desk. I ran. I ran around the desk and caught her as she jerked her hand out of the drawer. I took the letter away from her, beating her knuckles on the desk until she let go.
paragraphs.zh: 我去伺候他。当我转身回来时，她已经消失在桌子后面了。我跑了。我绕着桌子跑去，当她把手从抽屉里抽出来时，我抓住了她。我把信从她手中夺走，用指关节敲打桌子直到她松开。

paragraphs.en: “You would, would you?” I says.
paragraphs.zh: “你会的，会吗？”我说。

paragraphs.en: “Give it to me,” she says, “You’ve already opened it. Give it to me. Please, Jason. It’s mine. I saw the name.”
paragraphs.zh: “把它给我，”她说，“你已经打开了。把它给我。杰生，求你了。它是我的。我看到了名字。”

paragraphs.en: “I’ll take a hame string to you,” I says. “That’s what I’ll give you. Going into my papers.”
paragraphs.zh: “我会给你一根绳子，”我说。“这就是我要给你的。查看我的文件。”

paragraphs.en: “Is there some money in it?” she says, reaching for it. “She said she would send me some money. She promised she would. Give it to me.”
paragraphs.zh: “里面有钱吗？”她一边说，一边伸手去拿。“她说她会给我一些钱。她答应过。给我吧。”

paragraphs.en: “What do you want with money?” I says.
paragraphs.zh: “你要钱做什么？”我说。

paragraphs.en: “She said she would,” she says, “Give it to me. Please, Jason. I wont ever ask you anything again, if you’ll give it to me this time.”
paragraphs.zh: “她说她会的，”她说，“把它给我。求你了，杰生。如果你这次把它给我，我就不会再问你任何事了。”

paragraphs.en: “I’m going to, if you’ll give me time,” I says. I took the letter and the money order out and gave her the letter. She reached for the money order, not hardly glancing at the letter. “You’ll have to sign it first,” I says.
paragraphs.zh: “如果你给我时间，我会的。”我说。我把信和汇票拿出来，把信交给了她。她伸手去拿汇票，几乎没有看那封信。“你必须先签字，”我说。

paragraphs.en: “How much is it?” she says.
paragraphs.zh: “多少钱？”她说。

paragraphs.en: “Read the letter,” I says. “I reckon it’ll say.”
paragraphs.zh: “读一下这封信，”我说。“我想它会说的。”

paragraphs.en: She read it fast, in about two looks.
paragraphs.zh: 她读得很快，大约看了两眼。

paragraphs.en: “It dont say,” she says, looking up. She dropped the letter to the floor. “How much is it?”
paragraphs.zh: “它没有说，”她抬起头说道。她把信扔到了地板上。“多少钱？”

paragraphs.en: “It’s ten dollars,” I says.
paragraphs.zh: “十美元，”我说。

paragraphs.en: “Ten dollars?” she says, staring at me.
paragraphs.zh: “十块钱？”她盯着我说道。

paragraphs.en: “And you ought to be damn glad to get that,” I says, “A kid like you. What are you in such a rush for money all of a sudden for?”
paragraphs.zh: “你应该很高兴得到这个，”我说，“像你这样的孩子。你突然这么急着要钱干什么？”

paragraphs.en: “Ten dollars?” she says, like she was talking in her sleep, “Just ten dollars?” She made a grab at the money order. “You’re lying,” she says. “Thief!” she says, “Thief!”
paragraphs.zh: “十块钱？”她就像在说梦话一样说道：“只要十块钱？”她抓起汇票。“你在撒谎，”她说。“贼！”她说：“小偷！”

paragraphs.en: “You would, would you?” I says, holding her off.
paragraphs.zh: “你会的，会吗？”我一边说着，一边拦住了她。

paragraphs.en: “Give it to me!” she says, “It’s mine. She sent it to me. I will see it. I will.”
paragraphs.zh: “给我吧！”她说：“这是我的。她寄给我的。我会看到的。我会的。”

paragraphs.en: “You will?” I says, holding her, “How’re you going to do it?”
paragraphs.zh: “你会吗？”我抱着她说：“你打算怎么做？”

paragraphs.en: “Just let me see it, Jason,” she says, “Please. I wont ask you for anything again.”
paragraphs.zh: “杰生，就让我看看吧，”她说，“拜托了。我不会再向你要任何东西了。”

paragraphs.en: “Think I’m lying, do you?” I says. “Just for that you wont see it.”
paragraphs.zh: “你认为我在撒谎，是吗？”我说。“只是为了这个你不会看到它。”

paragraphs.en: “But just ten dollars,” she says, “She told me she—she told me—Jason, please please please. I’ve got to have some money. I’ve just got to. Give it to me, Jason. I’ll do anything if you will.”
paragraphs.zh: “但是只要十块钱，”她说，“她告诉我她——她告诉我——杰生，拜托拜托拜托。我必须有一些钱。我就是必须。给我，杰生。如果你愿意，我会做任何事。”

paragraphs.en: “Tell me what you’ve got to have money for,” I says.
paragraphs.zh: “告诉我你有钱做什么，”我说。

paragraphs.en: “I’ve got to have it,” she says. She was looking at me. Then all of a sudden she quit looking at me without moving her eyes at all. I knew she was going to lie. “It’s some money I owe,” she says. “I’ve got to pay it. I’ve got to pay it today.”
paragraphs.zh: “我必须拥有它，”她说。她正在看着我。然后突然她不再看我了，眼睛也没有移动。我知道她会撒谎。“这是我欠的一些钱，”她说。“我必须付钱。我今天就必须付。”

paragraphs.en: “Who to?” I says. Her hands were sort of twisting. I could watch her trying to think of a lie to tell. “Have you been charging things at stores again?” I says. “You needn’t bother to tell me that. If you can find anybody in this town that’ll charge anything to you after what I told them, I’ll eat it.”
paragraphs.zh: “给谁？”我说。她的手有点扭曲。我可以看到她试图想出一个谎言来说。“你又去商店收费了吗？”我说。“你不用费心告诉我这个。如果你能在这个镇上找到一个在我告诉他们之后向你收取任何费用的人，我就吃掉它。”

paragraphs.en: “It’s a girl,” she says, “It’s a girl. I borrowed some money from a girl. I’ve got to pay it back. Jason, give it to me. Please. I’ll do anything. I’ve got to have it. Mother will pay you. I’ll write to her to pay you and that I wont ever ask her for anything again. You can see the letter. Please, Jason. I’ve got to have it.”
paragraphs.zh: “这是一个女孩，”她说，“这是一个女孩。我向一个女孩借了一些钱。我必须还。杰生，把它给我。求你了。我会做任何事。我必须得到它。妈妈会付钱给你。我会写信给她付给你，我不会再向她要任何东西。你可以看看这封信。求你了，杰生。我必须得到它。”

paragraphs.en: “Tell me what you want with it, and I’ll see about it,” I says. “Tell me.” She just stood there, with her hands working against her dress. “All right,” I says, “If ten dollars is too little for you, I’ll just take it home to Mother, and you know what’ll happen to it then. Of course, if you’re so rich you dont need ten dollars—”
paragraphs.zh: “告诉我你想要什么，我会看看，”我说。“告诉我。”她只是站在那里，双手抚摸着裙子。“好吧，”我说，“如果十块钱对你来说太少了，我就把它带回家给妈妈，然后你知道会发生什么。当然，如果你这么有钱，你就不需要十块——”

paragraphs.en: She stood there, looking at the floor, kind of mumbling to herself. “She said she would send me some money. She said she sends money here and you say she dont send any. She said she’s sent a lot of money here. She says it’s for me. That it’s for me to have some of it. And you say we haven’t got any money.”
paragraphs.zh: 她站在那里，看着地板，自言自语。“她说她要寄给我一些钱。她说她寄了钱到这里，而你却说她不寄钱。她说她寄了很多钱到这里。她说这是给我的。我应该得到一些。而你却说我们没有钱。”

paragraphs.en: “You know as much about that as I do,” I says. “You’ve seen what happens to those checks.”
paragraphs.zh: “你和我一样了解这一点，”我说。“你已经看到了这些支票会发生什么。”

paragraphs.en: “Yes,” she says, looking at the floor. “Ten dollars,” she says, “Ten dollars.”
paragraphs.zh: “是的，”她看着地板说道。“十美元，”她说，“十美元。”

paragraphs.en: “And you’d better thank your stars it’s ten dollars,” I says. “Here,” I says. I put the money order face down on the desk, holding my hand on it, “Sign it.”
paragraphs.zh: “你最好感谢你的明星，这是十美元，”我说。“在这里，”我说。我把汇票面朝下放在桌子上，把手放在上面，“签字。”

paragraphs.en: “Will you let me see it?” she says. “I just want to look at it. Whatever it says, I wont ask for but ten dollars. You can have the rest. I just want to see it.”
paragraphs.zh: “你能让我看看吗？”她说。“我就是想看看，不管上面写的是什么，我只要十块钱，剩下的你就可以了，我就是想看看。”

paragraphs.en: “Not after the way you’ve acted,” I says. “You’ve got to learn one thing, and that is that when I tell you to do something, you’ve got it to do. You sign your name on that line.”
paragraphs.zh: “按照你的行为方式，不会。”我说。“你必须学会​​一件事，那就是当我告诉你做某事时，你必须去做。你在那一行签上你的名字。”

paragraphs.en: She took the pen, but instead of signing it she just stood there with her head bent and the pen shaking in her hand. Just like her mother. “Oh, God,” she says, “oh, God.”
paragraphs.zh: 她接过笔，但没有签字，只是低着头站在那里，手中的笔颤抖着。就像她的母亲一样。“哦，上帝，”她说，“哦，上帝。”

paragraphs.en: “Yes,” I says, “That’s one thing you’ll have to learn if you never learn anything else. Sign it now, and get on out of here.”
paragraphs.zh: “是的，”我说，“如果你永远学不到其他东西，那这是你必须学习的一件事。现在就签名，然后离开这里。”

paragraphs.en: She signed it. “Where’s the money?” she says. I took the order and blotted it and put it in my pocket. Then I gave her the ten dollars.
paragraphs.zh: 她签了字。“钱呢？”她说。我接过订单，把它吸干，然后放进口袋里。然后我就把十块钱给了她。

paragraphs.en: “Now you go on back to school this afternoon, you hear?” I says. She didn’t answer. She crumpled the bill up in her hand like it was a rag or something and went on out the front door just as Earl came in. A customer came in with him and they stopped up front. I gathered up the things and put on my hat and went up front.
paragraphs.zh: “现在下午你就回学校了，听到了吗？”我说。她没有回答。当厄尔进来时，她把钞票揉成一团，就像是一块抹布什么的，然后走出前门。一位顾客和他一起进来，他们在前面停了下来。我收拾好东西，戴上帽子，走到前面。

paragraphs.en: “Been much busy?” Earl says.
paragraphs.zh: “很忙吗？”厄尔说。

paragraphs.en: “Not much,” I says. He looked out the door.
paragraphs.zh: “不多，”我说。他朝门外望去。

paragraphs.en: “That your car over yonder?” he says. “Better not try to go out home to dinner. We’ll likely have another rush just before the show opens. Get you a lunch at Rogers’ and put a ticker in the drawer.”
paragraphs.zh: “那边是你的车吗？”他说。“最好不要尝试回家吃晚饭。演出开始前我们可能会再次赶时间。在罗杰斯餐厅给你吃顿午餐，然后在抽屉里放一张收报机。”

paragraphs.en: “Much obliged,” I says. “I can still manage to feed myself, I reckon.”
paragraphs.zh: “非常感谢，”我说。“我想我还能养活自己。”

paragraphs.en: And right there he’d stay, watching that door like a hawk until I came through it again. Well, he’d just have to watch it for a while; I was doing the best I could. The time before I says that’s the last one now; you’ll have to remember to get some more right away. But who can remember anything in all this hurrah. And now this damn show had to come here the one day I’d have to hunt all over town for a blank check, besides all the other things I had to do to keep the house running, and Earl watching the door like a hawk.
paragraphs.zh: 他会呆在那里，像鹰一样盯着那扇门，直到我再次穿过它。好吧，他只需要看一会儿就可以了；我已经尽力了。我说之前的时间现在已经是最后一次了；你必须记住立即多买一些。但谁能记住这一切欢呼声中的任何事情。现在，有一天，除了我必须做的所有其他事情来维持房子运转之外，我还得满城寻找一张空白支票，而厄尔则像鹰一样盯着门，这该死的节目必须来到这里。

paragraphs.en: I went to the printing shop and told him I wanted to play a joke on a fellow, but he didn’t have anything. Then he told me to have a look in the old opera house, where somebody had stored a lot of papers and junk out of the old Merchants’ and Farmers’ Bank when it failed, so I dodged up a few more alleys so Earl couldn’t see me and finally found old man Simmons and got the key from him and went up there and dug around. At last I found a pad on a Saint Louis bank. And of course she’d pick this one time to look at it close. Well, it would have to do. I couldn’t waste any more time now.
paragraphs.zh: 我去了印刷厂，告诉他我想跟一个家伙开个玩笑，但他什么也没有。然后他让我去老歌剧院看看，老招农银行倒闭时，有人在那里存放了很多文件和垃圾，所以我又躲了几条小巷，不让厄尔看到我，最后找到了老西蒙斯，从他那里拿到了钥匙，然后上去挖了一圈。最后我在圣路易斯的一家银行找到了一本本子。当然，她会选择这一次仔细观察。好吧，这是必须要做的。我现在不能再浪费时间了。

paragraphs.en: I went back to the store. “Forgot some papers Mother wants to go to the bank,” I says. I went back to the desk and fixed the check. Trying to hurry and all, I says to myself it’s a good thing her eyes are giving out, with that little whore in the house, a Christian forbearing woman like Mother. I says you know just as well as I do what she’s going to grow up into but I says that’s your business, if you want to keep her and raise her in your house just because of Father. Then she would begin to cry and say it was her own flesh and blood so I just says All right. Have it your way. I can stand it if you can.
paragraphs.zh: 我回到商店。“忘记了一些文件，妈妈要去银行，”我说。我回到办公桌前，核对了支票。我尽力加快速度，对自己说，她的眼睛流露出来是一件好事，家里有那个小妓女，一个像母亲一样隐忍的基督教女人。我说你和我一样知道她会长大成什么样子，但我说那是你的事，如果你只是因为父亲而想把她留在家里抚养。然后她会开始哭泣并说这是她自己的骨肉，所以我只是说好吧。随心所欲。如果你可以的话我可以忍受。

paragraphs.en: I fixed the letter up again and glued it back and went out.
paragraphs.zh: 我又把信粘好，然后出去了。

paragraphs.en: “Try not to be gone any longer than you can help,” Earl says.
paragraphs.zh: “尽量不要离开太久，”厄尔说。

paragraphs.en: “All right,” I says. I went to the telegraph office. The smart boys were all there.
paragraphs.zh: “好吧，”我说。我去了电报局。聪明的男孩都在那里。

paragraphs.en: “Any of you boys made a million yet?” I says.
paragraphs.zh: “你们有谁赚了一百万了吗？”我说。

paragraphs.en: “Who can do anything, with a market like that?” Doc says.
paragraphs.zh: “在这样的市场下，谁能做任何事情呢？”医生说。

paragraphs.en: “What’s it doing?” I says. I went in and looked. It was three points under the opening. “You boys are not going to let a little thing like the cotton market beat you, are you?” I says. “I thought you were too smart for that.”
paragraphs.zh: “它在做什么？”我说。我进去看了看。开局落后三分。“你们小伙子不会让像棉花市场这样的小事打败你们的，是吗？”我说。“我以为你太聪明了，不会这么做。”

paragraphs.en: “Smart, hell,” Doc says. “It was down twelve points at twelve o’clock. Cleaned me out.”
paragraphs.zh: “聪明啊，”医生说。“十二点钟下降了十二点。把我清理干净了。”

paragraphs.en: “Twelve points?” I says. “Why the hell didn’t somebody let me know? Why didn’t you let me know?” I says to the operator.
paragraphs.zh: “十二分？”我说。“到底为什么没人让我知道？你为什么不让我知道？”我对接线员说。

paragraphs.en: “I take it as it comes in,” he says. “I’m not running a bucket shop.”
paragraphs.zh: “我接受它，”他说。“我不是在经营对赌行。”

paragraphs.en: “You’re smart, aren’t you?” I says. “Seems to me, with the money I spend with you, you could take time to call me up. Or maybe your damn company’s in a conspiracy with those damn eastern sharks.”
paragraphs.zh: “你很聪明，不是吗？”我说。“在我看来，用我和你一起花的钱，你可以花点时间给我打电话。或者也许你该死的公司正在与那些该死的东方鲨鱼密谋。”

paragraphs.en: He didn’t say anything. He made like he was busy.
paragraphs.zh: 他什么也没说。他表现得好像很忙。

paragraphs.en: “You’re getting a little too big for your pants,” I says. “First thing you know you’ll be working for a living.”
paragraphs.zh: “你的裤子有点太大了，”我说。“首先你知道你会为了谋生而工作。”

paragraphs.en: “What’s the matter with you?” Doc says. “You’re still three points to the good.”
paragraphs.zh: “你怎么了？”医生说。“你还差三分。”

paragraphs.en: “Yes,” I says, “If I happened to be selling. I haven’t mentioned that yet, I think. You boys all cleaned out?”
paragraphs.zh: “是的，”我说，“如果我碰巧要卖的话。我想我还没有提到这一点。你们都清理干净了吗？”

paragraphs.en: “I got caught twice,” Doc says. “I switched just in time.”
paragraphs.zh: “我被抓了两次，”医生说。“我换得真及时。”

paragraphs.en: “Well,” I. O. Snopes says, “I’ve picked hit; I reckon taint no more than fair fer hit to pick me once in a while.”
paragraphs.zh: “好吧，”I.O.斯诺普斯说，“我选择了热门；我认为污点偶尔会选择我。”

paragraphs.en: So I left them buying and selling among themselves at a nickel a point. I found a nigger and sent him for my car and stood on the corner and waited. I couldn’t see Earl looking up and down the street, with one eye on the clock, because I couldn’t see the door from here. After about a week he got back with it.
paragraphs.zh: 所以我让他们以每分钱的价格进行买卖。我找到了一个黑鬼，派他去我的车上，然后站在街角等待。我看不到厄尔一只眼睛盯着时钟，在街上上下打量，因为我从这里看不到门。大约一周后，他回来了。

paragraphs.en: “Where the hell have you been?” I says, “Riding around where the wenches could see you?”
paragraphs.zh: “你到底去哪儿了？”我说：“骑到那些姑娘们能看到你的地方去？”

paragraphs.en: “I come straight as I could,” he says, “I had to drive clean around the square, wid all dem wagons.”
paragraphs.zh: “我尽可能笔直地走来，”他说，“我必须带着所有的马车干净地绕着广场行驶。”

paragraphs.en: I never found a nigger yet that didn’t have an airtight alibi for whatever he did. But just turn one loose in a car and he’s bound to show off. I got in and went on around the square. I caught a glimpse of Earl in the door across the square.
paragraphs.zh: 我还没有发现哪个黑鬼无论做什么都没有无懈可击的不在场证据。但只要在车里放松一下，他就一定会炫耀。我上了车，继续绕着广场走。我在广场对面的门口瞥见了厄尔。

paragraphs.en: I went straight to the kitchen and told Dilsey to hurry up with dinner.
paragraphs.zh: 我径直去了厨房，吩咐迪尔西赶紧吃晚饭。

paragraphs.en: “Quentin aint come yit,” she says.
paragraphs.zh: “昆丁不会来的，”她说。

paragraphs.en: “What of that?” I says. “You’ll be telling me next that Luster’s not quite ready to eat yet. Quentin knows when meals are served in this house. Hurry up with it, now.”
paragraphs.zh: “那又怎样？”我说。“接下来你会告诉我，勒斯特还没准备好吃饭。昆丁知道这所房子什么时候开饭。现在就快点吧。”

paragraphs.en: Mother was in her room. I gave her the letter. She opened it and took the check out and sat holding it in her hand. I went and got the shovel from the corner and gave her a match. “Come on,” I says, “Get it over with. You’ll be crying in a minute.”
paragraphs.zh: 母亲在她的房间里。我把信给了她。她打开门，取出支票，坐在手里，手里拿着它。我从角落里拿出铲子，给了她一根火柴。“来吧，”我说，“快点结束吧。一会儿你就会哭了。”

paragraphs.en: She took the match, but she didn’t strike it. She sat there, looking at the check. Just like I said it would be.
paragraphs.zh: 她接过了火柴，但没有擦亮。她坐在那里，看着支票。就像我说的那样。

paragraphs.en: “I hate to do it,” she says, “To increase your burden by adding Quentin. . . .”
paragraphs.zh: “我讨厌这样做，”她说，“增加昆丁的负担……”

paragraphs.en: “I guess we’ll get along,” I says. “Come on. Get it over with.”
paragraphs.zh: “我想我们会相处得很好，”我说。“来吧。结束吧。”

paragraphs.en: But she just sat there, holding the check.
paragraphs.zh: 但她只是坐在那里，拿着支票。

paragraphs.en: “This one is on a different bank,” she says. “They have been on an Indianapolis bank.”
paragraphs.zh: “这个是在另一家银行，”她说。“他们一直在印第安纳波利斯的一家银行工作。”

paragraphs.en: “Yes,” I says. “Women are allowed to do that too.”
paragraphs.zh: “是的，”我说。“女性也可以这样做。”

paragraphs.en: “Do what?” she says.
paragraphs.zh: “做什么？”她说。

paragraphs.en: “Keep money in two different banks,” I says.
paragraphs.zh: “把钱存入两家不同的银行，”我说。

paragraphs.en: “Oh,” she says. She looked at the check a while. “I’m glad to know she’s so . . . she has so much . . . God sees that I am doing right,” she says.
paragraphs.zh: “哦，”她说。她看了一会儿支票。“我很高兴知道她是如此......她拥有如此多......上帝看到我做得对，”她说。

paragraphs.en: “Come on,” I says, “Finish it. Get the fun over.”
paragraphs.zh: “来吧，”我说，“完成它。享受乐趣吧。”

paragraphs.en: “Fun?” she says, “When I think—”
paragraphs.zh: “好玩吗？”她说，“当我想到——”

paragraphs.en: “I thought you were burning this two hundred dollars a month for fun,” I says. “Come on, now. Want me to strike the match?”
paragraphs.zh: “我以为你每个月花掉两百美元是为了好玩，”我说。“来吧，现在。要我擦火柴吗？”
