paragraphs.en: “I could bring myself to accept them,” she says, “For my childrens’ sake. I have no pride.”
paragraphs.zh: “为了我的孩子们，我可以接受它们。”她说，“我没有骄傲。”

paragraphs.en: “You’d never be satisfied,” I says, “You know you wouldn’t. You’ve settled that once, let it stay settled. We can get along.”
paragraphs.zh: “你永远不会满足，”我说，“你知道你不会满足。你已经解决了一次，就让它保持稳定吧。我们可以和睦相处。”

paragraphs.en: “I leave everything to you,” she says. “But sometimes I become afraid that in doing this I am depriving you all of what is rightfully yours. Perhaps I shall be punished for it. If you want me to, I will smother my pride and accept them.”
paragraphs.zh: “我把一切都交给你了，”她说。“但有时我会害怕这样做会剥夺你所有应得的东西。也许我会因此受到惩罚。如果你愿意，我会压抑我的自尊并接受它们。”

paragraphs.en: “What would be the good in beginning now, when you’ve been destroying them for fifteen years?” I says. “If you keep on doing it, you have lost nothing, but if you’d begin to take them now, you’ll have lost fifty thousand dollars. We’ve got along so far, haven’t we?” I says. “I haven’t seen you in the poorhouse yet.”
paragraphs.zh: “十五年来你一直在摧毁它们，现在开始有什么好处呢？”我说。“如果你继续这样做，你不会损失什么，但如果你现在开始接受它们，你就会损失五万美元。到目前为止，我们相处得很好，不是吗？”我说。“我还没在济贫院见过你呢。”

paragraphs.en: “Yes,” she says, “We Bascombs need nobody’s charity. Certainly not that of a fallen woman.”
paragraphs.zh: “是的，”她说，“我们巴斯库姆人不需要任何人的施舍。当然不需要一个堕落女人的施舍。”

paragraphs.en: She struck the match and lit the check and put it in the shovel, and then the envelope, and watched them burn.
paragraphs.zh: 她擦亮火柴，点燃支票，把它放进铲子，然后放进信封，看着它们燃烧。

paragraphs.en: “You dont know what it is,” she says, “Thank God you will never know what a mother feels.”
paragraphs.zh: “你不知道那是什么，”她说，“感谢上帝，你永远不会知道母亲的感受。”

paragraphs.en: “There are lots of women in this world no better than her,” I says.
paragraphs.zh: “这个世界上有很多女人并不比她更好，”我说。

paragraphs.en: “But they are not my daughters,” she says. “It’s not myself,” she says, “I’d gladly take her back, sins and all, because she is my flesh and blood. It’s for Quentin’s sake.”
paragraphs.zh: “但她们不是我的女儿，”她说。“这不是我自己，”她说，“我很乐意把她带回来，尽管有罪和一切，因为她是我的骨肉。这是为了昆丁。”

paragraphs.en: Well, I could have said it wasn’t much chance of anybody hurting Quentin much, but like I say I dont expect much but I do want to eat and sleep without a couple of women squabbling and crying in the house.
paragraphs.zh: 好吧，我本可以说任何人伤害昆丁的可能性不大，但就像我说的，我并没有期望太多，但我确实想吃饭和睡觉，而没有几个女人在家里争吵和哭泣。

paragraphs.en: “And yours,” she says. “I know how you feel toward her.”
paragraphs.zh: “还有你的，”她说。“我知道你对她的感觉。”

paragraphs.en: “Let her come back,” I says, “far as I’m concerned.”
paragraphs.zh: “让她回来吧，”我说，“就我而言。”

paragraphs.en: “No,” she says. “I owe that to your father’s memory.”
paragraphs.zh: “不，”她说。“这要归功于你父亲的记忆。”

paragraphs.en: “When he was trying all the time to persuade you to let her come home when Herbert threw her out?” I says.
paragraphs.zh: “当他一直试图说服你让她回家时，赫伯特把她赶了出去？”我说。

paragraphs.en: “You dont understand,” she says. “I know you dont intend to make it more difficult for me. But it’s my place to suffer for my children,” she says. “I can bear it.”
paragraphs.zh: “你不明白，”她说。“我知道你不想让我的处境变得更加困难。但这是我为我的孩子们受苦的地方，”她说。“我能忍受。”

paragraphs.en: “Seems to me you go to a lot of unnecessary trouble doing it,” I says. The paper burned out. I carried it to the grate and put it in. “It just seems a shame to me to burn up good money,” I says.
paragraphs.zh: “在我看来，这样做会带来很多不必要的麻烦，”我说。纸烧坏了。我把它拿到炉边，放进去。“烧掉好钱对我来说似乎是一种耻辱，”我说。

paragraphs.en: “Let me never see the day when my children will have to accept that, the wages of sin,” she says. “I’d rather see even you dead in your coffin first.”
paragraphs.zh: “让我永远不要看到我的孩子们不得不接受罪恶的工价的那一天，”她说。“我宁愿先看到你死在棺材里。”

paragraphs.en: “Have it your way,” I says. “Are we going to have dinner soon?” I says, “Because if we’re not, I’ll have to go on back. We’re pretty busy today.” She got up. “I’ve told her once,” I says. “It seems she’s waiting on Quentin or Luster or somebody. Here, I’ll call her. Wait.” But she went to the head of the stairs and called.
paragraphs.zh: “随你便吧，”我说。“我们很快就要去吃晚饭了吗？”我说：“因为如果我们不去的话，我就得回去了。我们今天很忙。”她站了起来。“我已经告诉过她一次了，”我说。“她好像在等昆丁或者勒斯特或者什么人。来，我给她打电话。等等。”但她走到楼梯口喊了一声。

paragraphs.en: “Quentin aint come yit,” Dilsey says.
paragraphs.zh: “昆丁不会来的，”迪尔西说。

paragraphs.en: “Well, I’ll have to get on back,” I says. “I can get a sandwich downtown. I dont want to interfere with Dilsey’s arrangements,” I says. Well, that got her started again, with Dilsey hobbling and mumbling back and forth, saying,
paragraphs.zh: “好吧，我得回去了，”我说。“我可以在市中心买个三明治。我不想干涉迪尔西的安排。”我说。好吧，这让她又开始了，迪尔西一瘸一拐地来回咕哝着说：

paragraphs.en: “All right, all right, Ise puttin hit on fast as I kin.”
paragraphs.zh: 「好吧好吧，一诚说得很快。」

paragraphs.en: “I try to please you all,” Mother says, “I try to make things as easy for you as I can.”
paragraphs.zh: “我尽力取悦你们所有人，”母亲说，“我尽力让你们的事情变得简单。”

paragraphs.en: “I’m not complaining, am I?” I says. “Have I said a word except I had to go back to work?”
paragraphs.zh: “我没有抱怨，不是吗？”我说。“我除了必须回去工作之外还说过一句话吗？”

paragraphs.en: “I know,” she says, “I know you haven’t had the chance the others had, that you’ve had to bury yourself in a little country store. I wanted you to get ahead. I knew your father would never realise that you were the only one who had any business sense, and then when everything else failed I believed that when she married, and Herbert . . . after his promise . . .”
paragraphs.zh: “我知道，”她说，“我知道你没有其他人有的机会，你不得不把自己埋在一家乡村小商店里。我希望你能出人头地。我知道你父亲永远不会意识到你是唯一有商业头脑的人，然后当其他一切都失败时，我相信当她结婚时，赫伯特……在他的承诺之后……”

paragraphs.en: “Well, he was probably lying too,” I says. “He may not have even had a bank. And if he had, I dont reckon he’d have to come all the way to Mississippi to get a man for it.”
paragraphs.zh: “嗯，他可能也在撒谎，”我说。“他可能连银行都没有。如果他有的话，我想他也不必大老远跑到密西西比州来找人。”

paragraphs.en: We ate awhile. I could hear Ben in the kitchen, where Luster was feeding him. Like I say, if we’ve got to feed another mouth and she wont take that money, why not send him down to Jackson. He’ll be happier there, with people like him. I says God knows there’s little enough room for pride in this family, but it dont take much pride to not like to see a thirty year old man playing around the yard with a nigger boy, running up and down the fence and lowing like a cow whenever they play golf over there. I says if they’d sent him to Jackson at first we’d all be better off today. I says, you’ve done your duty by him; you’ve done all anybody can expect of you and more than most folks would do, so why not send him there and get that much benefit out of the taxes we pay. Then she says, “I’ll be gone soon. I know I’m just a burden to you” and I says “You’ve been saying that so long that I’m beginning to believe you” only I says you’d better be sure and not let me know you’re gone because I’ll sure have him on number seventeen that night and I says I think I know a place where they’ll take her too and the name of it’s not Milk street and Honey avenue either. Then she begun to cry and I says All right all right I have as much pride about my kinfolks as anybody even if I dont always know where they come from.
paragraphs.zh: 我们吃了一会儿。我能听见本在厨房里的声音，勒斯特正在那里喂他。就像我说的，如果我们要养活另一张嘴，而她不肯拿那笔钱，为什么不把他送到杰克逊那里呢。和像他这样的人在一起，他会更快乐。我说上帝知道这个家庭没有足够的骄傲空间，但只要他们在那边打高尔夫球，就不会喜欢看到一个三十岁的男人和一个黑男孩在院子里玩耍，在栅栏上跑来跑去，像牛一样哞哞叫，这并不需要太多的骄傲。我说如果他们一开始就把他送到杰克逊，我们今天都会过得更好。我说，你已经尽到了他的义务；你已经做到了所有人对你的期望，而且比大多数人会做的还要多，所以为什么不把他送到那里，从我们缴纳的税款中获得这么多好处。然后她说，“我很快就会离开。我知道我对你来说只是一个负担”，我说“你这么说已经很久了，我开始相信你了”，只是我说你最好确定，不要让我知道你走了，因为那天晚上我肯定会让他在十七号，我说我想我知道一个地方，他们也会带她去，而且名字也不是牛奶街和蜂蜜大道。然后她开始哭，我说好吧好吧，我和任何人一样为我的家人感到自豪，即使我并不总是知道他们来自哪里。

paragraphs.en: We ate for awhile. Mother sent Dilsey to the front to look for Quentin again.
paragraphs.zh: 我们吃了一会儿。母亲又派迪尔西去前线寻找昆丁。

paragraphs.en: “I keep telling you she’s not coming to dinner,” I says.
paragraphs.zh: “我一直告诉你她不会来吃晚饭了，”我说。

paragraphs.en: “She knows better than that,” Mother says, “She knows I dont permit her to run about the streets and not come home at meal time. Did you look good, Dilsey?”
paragraphs.zh: “她比这更清楚，”妈妈说，“她知道我不允许她在街上跑来跑去，而且吃饭时不回家。迪尔西，你看起来不错吗？”

paragraphs.en: “Dont let her, then,” I says.
paragraphs.zh: “那就别让她了，”我说。

paragraphs.en: “What can I do,” she says. “You have all of you flouted me. Always.”
paragraphs.zh: “我能做什么，”她说。“你们所有人都蔑视我。一直都是。”

paragraphs.en: “If you wouldn’t come interfering, I’d make her mind,” I says. “It wouldn’t take me but about one day to straighten her out.”
paragraphs.zh: “如果你不来干涉，我会让她决定的。”我说。“我只需要大约一天的时间就能纠正她的错误。”

paragraphs.en: “You’d be too brutal with her,” she says. “You have your Uncle Maury’s temper.”
paragraphs.zh: “你对她太残酷了，”她说。“你的脾气就是你莫里舅舅的脾气。”

paragraphs.en: That reminded me of the letter. I took it out and handed it to her. “You wont have to open it,” I says. “The bank will let you know how much it is this time.”
paragraphs.zh: 这让我想起了那封信。我拿出来递给她。“你不必打开它，”我说。“银行会告诉你这次的金额是多少。”

paragraphs.en: “It’s addressed to you,” she says.
paragraphs.zh: “这是写给你的，”她说。

paragraphs.en: “Go on and open it,” I says. She opened it and read it and handed it to me.
paragraphs.zh: “继续打开它，”我说。她打开它读了一遍然后递给了我。

paragraphs.en: “ ‘My dear young nephew,’ it says,
paragraphs.zh: “‘我亲爱的小侄子，’它说，

paragraphs.en: ‘You will be glad to learn that I am now in a position to avail myself of an opportunity regarding which, for reasons which I shall make obvious to you, I shall not go into details until I have an opportunity to divulge it to you in a more secure manner. My business experience has taught me to be chary of committing anything of a confidential nature to any more concrete medium than speech, and my extreme precaution in this instance should give you some inkling of its value. Needless to say, I have just completed a most exhaustive examination of all its phases, and I feel no hesitancy in telling you that it is that sort of golden chance that comes but once in a lifetime, and I now see clearly before me that goal toward which I have long and unflaggingly striven: i.e., the ultimate solidification of my affairs by which I may restore to its rightful position that family of which I have the honour to be the sole remaining male descendant; that family in which I have ever included your lady mother and her children.
paragraphs.zh: “你会很高兴得知我现在能够利用这个机会，出于我将向你说明的原因，在我有机会以更安全的方式向你透露之前，我不会透露细节。我的商业经验告诉我，在任何比言语更具体的媒介上提交任何机密性质的事情都要小心谨慎，在这种情况下我的极端谨慎应该会让你对它的价值有所了解。不用说，我刚刚完成了对其所有阶段的最详尽的审查，我毫不犹豫地告诉你，这是一生中只有一次的黄金机会，我现在清楚地看到我长期以来不懈努力的目标：即，最终巩固我的事务，使我有幸成为唯一幸存的男性后裔的家庭恢复其应有的地位；我曾把你的母亲和她的孩子们纳入其中。

paragraphs.en: ‘As it so happens, I am not quite in a position to avail myself of this opportunity to the uttermost which it warrants, but rather than go out of the family to do so, I am today drawing upon your Mother’s bank for the small sum necessary to complement my own initial investment, for which I herewith enclose, as a matter of formality, my note of hand at eight percent per annum. Needless to say, this is merely a formality, to secure your Mother in the event of that circumstance of which man is ever the plaything and sport. For naturally I shall employ this sum as though it were my own and so permit your Mother to avail herself of this opportunity which my exhaustive investigation has shown to be a bonanza—if you will permit the vulgarism—of the first water and purest ray serene.
paragraphs.zh: “碰巧的是，我不太能充分利用这个机会，但我并没有走出家庭去这样做，而是今天从你母亲的银行提取一小笔必要的资金来补充我自己的初始投资，作为正式问题，我特此附上我的年利率百分之八的手头票据。不用说，这只是一种形式，为了在男人永远成为玩物和游戏的情况下保护你的母亲。因为自然地，我会像使用我自己的钱一样使用这笔钱，因此允许你的母亲利用这个机会，我的详尽调查表明，如果你允许粗俗的话，这是一笔财富，第一水和最纯净的光线宁静。

paragraphs.en: ‘This is in confidence, you will understand, from one business man to another; we will harvest our own vineyards, eh? And knowing your Mother’s delicate health and that timorousness which such delicately nutured Southern ladies would naturally feel regarding matters of business, and their charming proneness to divulge unwittingly such matters in conversation, I would suggest that you do not mention it to her at all. On second thought, I advise you not to do so. It might be better to simply restore this sum to the bank at some future date, say, in a lump sum with the other small sums for which I am indebted to her, and say nothing about it at all. It is our duty to shield her from the crass material world as much as possible.
paragraphs.zh: “你会明白，这是一个商人对另一个商人的秘密；我们将收获我们自己的葡萄园，是吗？我知道你母亲身体不好，而且这些天生娇弱的南方女士在处理公事时自然会感到胆怯，而且她们在谈话中很容易无意中泄露这些事情，所以我建议你根本不要向她提起这件事。转念一想，我建议你不要这样做。最好是在将来的某个日期将这笔款项与我欠她的其他小额款项一次性归还给银行，并且对此只字不提。我们有责任尽可能地保护她免受粗俗的物质世界的影响。

paragraphs.en: ‘Your affectionate Uncle,
paragraphs.zh: ‘你慈爱的叔叔，

paragraphs.en: ‘Maury L. Bascomb.’ ”
paragraphs.zh: ‘莫里·L·巴斯科姆。’”

paragraphs.en: “What do you want to do about it?” I says, flipping it across the table.
paragraphs.zh: “你想对此做什么？”我一边说，一边把它翻过桌子。

paragraphs.en: “I know you grudge what I give him,” she says.
paragraphs.zh: “我知道你对我给他的东西感到不满，”她说。

paragraphs.en: “It’s your money,” I says. “If you want to throw it to the birds even, it’s your business.”
paragraphs.zh: “这是你的钱，”我说。“如果你想把它扔给鸟儿，那是你的事。”

paragraphs.en: “He’s my own brother,” Mother says. “He’s the last Bascomb. When we are gone there wont be any more of them.”
paragraphs.zh: “他是我自己的兄弟，”母亲说。“他是最后一个巴斯科姆人。我们走了之后，就不会再有他们了。”

paragraphs.en: “That’ll be hard on somebody, I guess,” I says. “All right, all right,” I says, “It’s your money. Do as you please with it. You want me to tell the bank to pay it?”
paragraphs.zh: “我想这对某人来说会很困难，”我说。“好吧，好吧，”我说，“这是你的钱。你想怎么花就怎么花。你想让我告诉银行付款吗？”

paragraphs.en: “I know you begrudge him,” she says. “I realise the burden on your shoulders. When I’m gone it will be easier on you.”
paragraphs.zh: “我知道你嫉妒他，”她说。“我意识到你肩上的重担。当我离开后，你就会轻松一些。”

paragraphs.en: “I could make it easier right now,” I says. “All right, all right, I wont mention it again. Move all bedlam in here if you want to.”
paragraphs.zh: “我现在可以让事情变得更容易，”我说。“好吧，好吧，我不再提了。如果你愿意的话，把所有的混乱都搬到这里来。”

paragraphs.en: “He’s your own brother,” she says, “Even if he is afflicted.”
paragraphs.zh: “他是你自己的兄弟，”她说，“即使他很痛苦。”

paragraphs.en: “I’ll take your bank book,” I says. “I’ll draw my check today.”
paragraphs.zh: “我会拿走你的银行存折，”我说。“我今天就开支票。”

paragraphs.en: “He kept you waiting six days,” she says. “Are you sure the business is sound? It seems strange to me that a solvent business cannot pay its employees promptly.”
paragraphs.zh: “他让你等了六天，”她说。“你确定公司经营状况良好吗？在我看来，有偿付能力的公司无法及时向员工支付工资，这似乎很奇怪。”

paragraphs.en: “He’s all right,” I says, “Safe as a bank. I tell him not to bother about mine until we get done collecting every month. That’s why it’s late sometimes.”
paragraphs.zh: “他很好，”我说，“像银行一样安全。我告诉他在我们完成每个月的收款之前不要担心我的事情。这就是为什么有时会迟到的原因。”

paragraphs.en: “I just couldn’t bear to have you lose the little I had to invest for you,” she says. “I’ve often thought that Earl is not a good business man. I know he doesn’t take you into his confidence to the extent that your investment in the business should warrant. I’m going to speak to him.”
paragraphs.zh: “我只是无法忍受让你失去我为你投资的一点点，”她说。“我经常认为厄尔不是一个优秀的商人。我知道他并没有将你置于他的信任范围内，以至于你对公司的投资应该得到保证。我要和他谈谈。”

paragraphs.en: “No, you let him alone,” I says. “It’s his business.”
paragraphs.zh: “不，你让他一个人呆着，”我说。“这是他的事。”

paragraphs.en: “You have a thousand dollars in it.”
paragraphs.zh: “你里面有一千块钱。”

paragraphs.en: “You let him alone,” I says, “I’m watching things. I have your power of attorney. It’ll be all right.”
paragraphs.zh: “你别管他，”我说，“我在看着事情。我有你的授权书。不会有事的。”

paragraphs.en: “You dont know what a comfort you are to me,” she says. “You have always been my pride and joy, but when you came to me of your own accord and insisted on banking your salary each month in my name, I thanked God it was you left me if they had to be taken.”
paragraphs.zh: “你不知道你对我来说是多么的安慰，”她说。“你一直是我的骄傲和喜悦，但当你主动来找我并坚持将每个月的薪水存入我的名下时，我感谢上帝，如果他们必须被带走，那就是你离开了我。”

paragraphs.en: “They were all right,” I says. “They did the best they could, I reckon.”
paragraphs.zh: “他们都很好，”我说。“我认为他们已经尽力了。”

paragraphs.en: “When you talk that way I know you are thinking bitterly of your father’s memory,” she says. “You have a right to, I suppose. But it breaks my heart to hear you.”
paragraphs.zh: “当你这样说话时，我知道你正在痛苦地回忆你父亲的记忆，”她说。“我想你有权利这样做。但听到你的声音让我心碎。”

paragraphs.en: I got up. “If you’ve got any crying to do,” I says, “you’ll have to do it alone, because I’ve got to get on back. I’ll get the bank book.”
paragraphs.zh: 我站了起来。“如果你有事要哭，”我说，“你就得独自哭，因为我得回去。我去拿银行存折。”

paragraphs.en: “I’ll get it,” she says.
paragraphs.zh: “我会得到它，”她说。

paragraphs.en: “Keep still,” I says, “I’ll get it.” I went upstairs and got the bank book out of her desk and went back to town. I went to the bank and deposited the check and the money order and the other ten, and stopped at the telegraph office. It was one point above the opening. I had already lost thirteen points, all because she had to come helling in there at twelve, worrying me about that letter.
paragraphs.zh: “别动，”我说，“我会明白的。”我上楼从她桌上取出银行存折，然后回到城里。我去银行存了支票、汇票和另外十张，然后在电报局停了下来。比开盘价高出一分。我已经丢了十三分，全是因为她必须在十二点赶到那里，让我担心那封信。

paragraphs.en: “What time did that report come in?” I says.
paragraphs.zh: “那份报告什么时候送来的？”我说。

paragraphs.en: “About an hour ago,” he says.
paragraphs.zh: “大约一个小时前，”他说。

paragraphs.en: “An hour ago?” I says. “What are we paying you for?” I says, “Weekly reports? How do you expect a man to do anything? The whole damn top could blow off and we’d not know it.”
paragraphs.zh: “一小时前？”我说。“我们付钱给你做什么？”我说：“每周报告？你怎么指望一个人会做任何事？整个该死的顶部可能会被炸掉，而我们却浑然不知道。”

paragraphs.en: “I dont expect you to do anything,” he says. “They changed that law making folks play the cotton market.”
paragraphs.zh: “我不指望你做任何事，”他说。“他们改变了法律，让人们参与棉花市场。”

paragraphs.en: “They have?” I says. “I hadn’t heard. They must have sent the news out over the Western Union.”
paragraphs.zh: “他们有吗？”我说。“我没听说。他们一定是通过西联汇款把消息发出来的。”

paragraphs.en: I went back to the store. Thirteen points. Damn if I believe anybody knows anything about the damn thing except the ones that sit back in those New York offices and watch the country suckers come up and beg them to take their money. Well, a man that just calls shows he has no faith in himself, and like I say if you aren’t going to take the advice, what’s the use in paying money for it. Besides, these people are right up there on the ground; they know everything that’s going on. I could feel the telegram in my pocket. I’d just have to prove that they were using the telegraph company to defraud. That would constitute a bucket shop. And I wouldn’t hesitate that long, either. Only be damned if it doesn’t look like a company as big and rich as the Western Union could get a market report out on time. Half as quick as they’ll get a wire to you saying Your account closed out. But what the hell do they care about the people. They’re hand in glove with that New York crowd. Anybody could see that.
paragraphs.zh: 我回到商店。十三分。如果我相信除了那些坐在纽约办公室里看着乡村傻瓜上来乞求他们拿走他们的钱的人之外，还有人对这该死的事情一无所知的话，那该死的。好吧，一个男人只是打电话表明他对自己没有信心，就像我说的，如果你不接受建议，付钱有什么用。而且，这些人就在地面上；他们知道正在发生的一切。我能感觉到电报在我的口袋里。我只需要证明他们正在利用电报公司进行诈骗。那将构成一个对赌行。我也不会犹豫那么久。如果它看起来不像西联汇款这样大而富有的公司能够按时发布市场报告，那就见鬼了。他们会以一半的速度给您发电报，说您的帐户已关闭。但他们到底关心人民什么？他们与纽约人群密切相关。任何人都可以看到这一点。

paragraphs.en: When I came in Earl looked at his watch. But he didn’t say anything until the customer was gone. Then he says,
paragraphs.zh: 当我进来时，厄尔看了看手表。但直到顾客走后，他才说什么。然后他说，

paragraphs.en: “You go home to dinner?”
paragraphs.zh: “你回家吃饭吗？”

paragraphs.en: “I had to go to the dentist,” I says because it’s not any of his business where I eat but I’ve got to be in the store with him all the afternoon. And with his jaw running off after all I’ve stood. You take a little two by four country storekeeper like I say it takes a man with just five hundred dollars to worry about it fifty thousand dollars’ worth.
paragraphs.zh: “我必须去看牙医，”我说，因为我在哪里吃饭不关他的事，但我整个下午都得和他一起呆在商店里。在我站起来之后，他的下巴都快掉下来了。就像我说的那样，一个二乘四的乡村店主需要一个只有五百美元的人才能担心价值五万美元的东西。

paragraphs.en: “You might have told me,” he says. “I expected you back right away.”
paragraphs.zh: “你可能已经告诉过我了，”他说。“我还以为你马上就回来呢。”

paragraphs.en: “I’ll trade you this tooth and give you ten dollars to boot, any time,” I says. “Our agreement was an hour for dinner,” I says, “and if you dont like the way I do, you know what you can do about it.”
paragraphs.zh: “我随时都可以用这颗牙齿交换你，并给你十美元。”我说。“我们的协议是吃一个小时的晚餐，”我说，“如果你不喜欢我的方式，你知道你能做什么。”

paragraphs.en: “I’ve known that some time,” he says. “If it hadn’t been for your mother I’d have done it before now, too. She’s a lady I’ve got a lot of sympathy for, Jason. Too bad some other folks I know cant say as much.”
paragraphs.zh: “我早就知道这一点了，”他说。“如果不是你妈妈，我早就这么做了。杰生，我非常同情她。可惜我认识的其他人不能这么说。”

paragraphs.en: “Then you can keep it,” I says. “When we need any sympathy I’ll let you know in plenty of time.”
paragraphs.zh: “那你就可以保留它了，”我说。“当我们需要任何同情时，我会及时通知你。”

paragraphs.en: “I’ve protected you about that business a long time, Jason,” he says.
paragraphs.zh: “杰生，我长期以来一直在这件事上保护你，”他说。

paragraphs.en: “Yes?” I says, letting him go on. Listening to what he would say before I shut him up.
paragraphs.zh: “是吗？”我说，让他继续说。在我让他闭嘴之前听听他会说什么。

paragraphs.en: “I believe I know more about where that automobile came from than she does.”
paragraphs.zh: “我相信我比她更了解那辆车的来源。”

paragraphs.en: “You think so, do you?” I says. “When are you going to spread the news that I stole it from my mother?”
paragraphs.zh: “你也这么认为，是吗？”我说。“你什么时候要把我从妈妈那里偷来的消息传出去？”

paragraphs.en: “I dont say anything,” he says, “I know you have her power of attorney. And I know she still believes that thousand dollars is in this business.”
paragraphs.zh: “我什么也没说，”他说，“我知道你有她的授权书。而且我知道她仍然相信这个行业能赚到一千美元。”

paragraphs.en: “All right,” I says, “Since you know so much, I’ll tell you a little more: go to the bank and ask them whose account I’ve been depositing a hundred and sixty dollars on the first of every month for twelve years.”
paragraphs.zh: “好吧，”我说，“既然你知道这么多，那我就多告诉你一点：去银行问问他们，十二年来，我每个月的一号都在谁的账户上存了一百六十美元。”

paragraphs.en: “I dont say anything,” he says, “I just ask you to be a little more careful after this.”
paragraphs.zh: “我什么也没说，”他说，“我只是请你以后要小心一点。”

paragraphs.en: I never said anything more. It doesn’t do any good. I’ve found that when a man gets into a rut the best thing you can do is let him stay there. And when a man gets it in his head that he’s got to tell something on you for your own good, good-night. I’m glad I haven’t got the sort of conscience I’ve got to nurse like a sick puppy all the time. If I’d ever be as careful over anything as he is to keep his little shirt tail full of business from making him more then eight percent. I reckon he thinks they’d get him on the usury law if he netted more than eight percent. What the hell chance has a man got, tied down in a town like this and to a business like this. Why I could take his business in one year and fix him so he’d never have to work again, only he’d give it all away to the church or something. If there’s one thing gets under my skin, it’s a damn hypocrite. A man that thinks anything he dont understand all about must be crooked and that first chance he gets he’s morally bound to tell the third party what’s none of his business to tell. Like I say if I thought every time a man did something I didn’t know all about he was bound to be a crook, I reckon I wouldn’t have any trouble finding something back there on those books that you wouldn’t see any use for running and telling somebody I thought ought to know about it, when for all I knew they might know a damn sight more about it now than I did, and if they didn’t it was damn little of my business anyway and he says, “My books are open to anybody. Anybody that has any claim or believes she has any claim on this business can go back there and welcome.”
paragraphs.zh: 我再也没有说过任何话。这没有任何好处。我发现，当一个人陷入困境时，你能做的最好的事情就是让他呆在那里。当一个男人心里想他必须告诉你一些关于你的事情，为了你好，晚安。我很高兴我没有像一只生病的小狗一样一直需要护理的良知。如果我能像他一样对任何事情都小心翼翼，别让他的小衬衫尾部充满生意，不要让他的收入超过百分之八。我认为，如果他的净收入超过百分之八，他们就会根据高利贷法对他进行处罚。一个人到底有什么机会，被束缚在这样的小镇和这样的生意上。为什么我可以在一年内接手他的生意并修复他，这样他就再也不用工作了，只是他会把所有的钱都捐给教堂之类的。如果有一件事让我恼火，那就是一个该死的伪君子。一个认为自己完全不了解的事情的人一定是骗人的，一旦有机会，他在道德上就有义务告诉第三方那些与他无关的事情。就像我说的，如果我认为每当一个人做了一些我不完全了解的事情时，他一定是个骗子，我想我不会有任何麻烦，在那些书上找到一些东西，你不会看到跑去告诉别人我认为应该知道这件事有什么用处，尽管我知道他们现在可能比我更了解这件事，如果他们不这样做，那也与我无关，他说，“我的书对任何人开放。任何人任何主张或认为她对这项业务有任何主张都可以回到那里并受到欢迎。”

paragraphs.en: “Sure, you wont tell,” I says, “You couldn’t square your conscience with that. You’ll just take her back there and let her find it. You wont tell, yourself.”
paragraphs.zh: “当然，你不会说出来，”我说，“你不能平复自己的良心。你只能带她回去，让她找到它。你自己也不会说出来。”

paragraphs.en: “I’m not trying to meddle in your business,” he says. “I know you missed out on some things like Quentin had. But your mother has had a misfortunate life too, and if she was to come in here and ask me why you quit, I’d have to tell her. It aint that thousand dollars. You know that. It’s because a man never gets anywhere if fact and his ledgers dont square. And I’m not going to lie to anybody, for myself or anybody else.”
paragraphs.zh: “我并不是想干涉你的事，”他说。“我知道你错过了像昆丁那样的一些事情。但你母亲也有过不幸的生活，如果她来这里问我为什么辞职，我就必须告诉她。那不是那一千美元。你知道的。这是因为如果事实和他的账本不一致，一个人永远不会有任何进展。而且我不会对任何人撒谎，无论是为了我自己还是其他任何人。”

paragraphs.en: “Well, then,” I says, “I reckon that conscience of yours is a more valuable clerk than I am; it dont have to go home at noon to eat. Only dont let it interfere with my appetite,” I says, because how the hell can I do anything right, with that damn family and her not making any effort to control her nor any of them, like that time when she happened to see one of them kissing Caddy and all next day she went around the house in a black dress and a veil and even Father couldn’t get her to say a word except crying and saying her little daughter was dead and Caddy about fifteen then only in three years she’d been wearing haircloth or probably sandpaper at that rate. Do you think I can afford to have her running bout the streets with every drummer that comes to town, I says, and them telling the new ones up and down the road where to pick up a hot one when they made Jefferson. I haven’t got much pride, I can’t afford it with a kitchen full of niggers to feed and robbing the state asylum of its star freshman. Blood, I says, governors and generals. It’s a damn good thing we never had any kings and presidents; we’d all be down there at Jackson chasing butterflies. I say it’d be bad enough if it was mine; I’d at least be sure it was a bastard to begin with, and now even the Lord doesn’t know that for certain probably.
paragraphs.zh: “好吧，那么，”我说，“我认为你的良心比我更有价值；它不必在中午回家吃饭。只要别让它影响我的胃口，”我说，因为那个该死的家庭和她没有做出任何努力来控制她或他们中的任何人，我到底怎么能做正确的事情，就像那次她碰巧看到他们中的一个亲吻凯蒂，第二天她就穿着黑色连衣裙和一身黑衣在房子里走来走去。就连父亲也无法让她说一句话，只能哭着说她的小女儿死了，而凯蒂大约十五岁，仅仅在三年内，她就一直戴着发布或可能是砂纸。你认为我能负担得起让她和每一个进城的鼓手一起在街上跑来跑去吗？我说，他们告诉新来的鼓手，当他们制作杰斐逊时，在哪里可以找到一个热门的鼓手。我没有太多的骄傲，我负担不起厨房里满是黑鬼的食物，并抢走了州立收容所的明星新生。血统，我说，州长和将军。我们从来没有过国王和总统，这真是一件好事。我们都会在杰克逊追逐蝴蝶。我说如果是我的就已经够糟糕了；我至少一开始就确定那是个私生子，但现在连上帝都不确定了。

paragraphs.en: So after awhile I heard the band start up, and then they begun to clear out. Headed for the show, every one of them. Haggling over a twenty cent hame string to save fifteen cents, so they can give it to a bunch of Yankees that come in and pay maybe ten dollars for the privilege. I went on out to the back.
paragraphs.zh: 过了一会儿，我听到乐队开始演奏，然后他们开始散场。他们每个人都前往演出。为一根二十美分的火腿绳讨价还价，节省了十五美分，这样他们就可以把它送给一群进来并支付十美元的特权的北方基队。我走到后面。

paragraphs.en: “Well,” I says, “If you dont look out, that bolt will grow into your hand. And then I’m going to take an axe and chop it out. What do you reckon the boll-weevils’ll eat if you dont get those cultivators in shape to raise them a crop?” I says, “sage grass?”
paragraphs.zh: “好吧，”我说，“如果你不小心，那根螺栓会长到你的手上。然后我会拿一把斧头把它砍下来。如果你不让那些耕耘机恢复收成，你认为棉铃象鼻虫会吃什么？”我说：“鼠尾草？”

paragraphs.en: “Dem folks sho do play dem horns,” he says. “Tell me man in dat show kin play a tune on a handsaw. Pick hit like a banjo.”
paragraphs.zh: “人们应该吹响号角，”他说。“告诉我那个表演中的人用手锯演奏一首曲子。像班卓琴一样敲击。”

paragraphs.en: “Listen,” I says. “Do you know how much that show’ll spend in this town? About ten dollars,” I says. “The ten dollars Buck Turpin has in his pocket right now.”
paragraphs.zh: “听着，”我说。“你知道这个节目在这个镇上要花多少钱吗？大约十美元，”我说。“巴克·特平现在口袋里有十美元。”

paragraphs.en: “Whut dey give Mr Buck ten dollars fer?” he says.
paragraphs.zh: “他们为什么给巴克先生十美元？”他说。

paragraphs.en: “For the privilege of showing here,” I says. “You can put the balance of what they’ll spend in your eye.”
paragraphs.zh: “我有幸在这里展示，”我说。“你可以把他们的支出余额放在你的眼睛里。”

paragraphs.en: “You mean dey pays ten dollars jest to give dey show here?” he says.
paragraphs.zh: “你的意思是他们花十美元在这里表演？”他说。

paragraphs.en: “That’s all,” I says. “And how much do you reckon . . .”
paragraphs.zh: “仅此而已，”我说。“那你觉得有多少……”

paragraphs.en: “Gret day,” he says, “You mean to tell me dey chargin um to let um show here? I’d pay ten dollars to see dat man pick dat saw, ef I had to. I figures dat tomorrow mawnin I be still owin um nine dollars and six bits at dat rate.”
paragraphs.zh: “天哪，”他说，“你的意思是告诉我，让我在这里展示？我愿意付十美元让那个人挑选那把锯子，如果我不得不这样做的话。我想明天我仍然欠着嗯九美元和六比特。”

paragraphs.en: And then a Yankee will talk your head off about niggers getting ahead. Get them ahead, what I say. Get them so far ahead you cant find one south of Louisville with a blood hound. Because when I told him about how they’d pick up Saturday night and carry off at least a thousand dollars out of the county, he says,
paragraphs.zh: 然后一个北方佬就会喋喋不休地谈论黑人的成功。让他们领先，照我说的。让他们走得太远，你在路易斯维尔南部找不到一只带着猎犬的狗。因为当我告诉他他们周六晚上如何接货并将至少一千美元带出县城时，他说，

paragraphs.en: “I don’t begrudge um. I kin sho afford my two bits.”
paragraphs.zh: “我不吝惜嗯。我肯定能负担得起我的两块钱。”

paragraphs.en: “Two bits hell,” I says. “That dont begin it. How about the dime or fifteen cents you’ll spend for a damn two cent box of candy or something. How about the time you’re wasting right now, listening to that band.”
paragraphs.zh: “两点地狱，”我说。“这还不是开始。你花一毛钱或十五美分买一盒该死的两美分糖果之类的怎么样？你现在浪费在听乐队演奏的时间怎么样？”

paragraphs.en: “Dat’s de troof,” he says. “Well, ef I lives twell night hit’s gwine to be two bits mo dey takin out of town, dat’s sho.”
paragraphs.zh: “就是这样，”他说。“好吧，如果我今晚住两晚就要出城，那就好了。”

paragraphs.en: “Then you’re a fool,” I says.
paragraphs.zh: “那你就是个傻瓜，”我说。

paragraphs.en: “Well,” he says, “I dont spute dat neither. Ef dat uz a crime, all chain-gangs wouldn’t be black.”
paragraphs.zh: “好吧，”他说，“我也不怀疑这一点。如果这是一种犯罪，那么所有的铁链帮派都不会是黑人。”

paragraphs.en: Well, just about that time I happened to look up the alley and saw her. When I stepped back and looked at my watch I didn’t notice at the time who he was because I was looking at the watch. It was just two thirty, forty-five minutes before anybody but me expected her to be out. So when I looked around the door the first thing I saw was the red tie he had on and I was thinking what the hell kind of a man would wear a red tie. But she was sneaking along the alley, watching the door, so I wasn’t thinking anything about him until they had gone past. I was wondering if she’d have so little respect for me that she’d not only play out of school when I told her not to, but would walk right past the store, daring me not to see her. Only she couldn’t see into the door because the sun fell straight into it and it was like trying to see through an automobile searchlight, so I stood there and watched her go on past, with her face painted up like a damn clown’s and her hair all gummed and twisted and a dress that if a woman had come out doors even on Gayoso or Beale street when I was a young fellow with no more than that to cover her legs and behind, she’d been thrown in jail. I’ll be damned if they dont dress like they were trying to make every man they passed on the street want to reach out and clap his hand on it. And so I was thinking what kind of a damn man would wear a red tie when all of a sudden I knew he was one of those show folks well as if she’d told me. Well, I can stand a lot; if I couldn’t, damn if I wouldn’t be in a hell of a fix, so when they turned the corner I jumped down and followed. Me, without any hat, in the middle of the afternoon, having to chase up and down back alleys because of my mother’s good name. Like I say you cant do anything with a woman like that, if she’s got it in her. If it’s in her blood, you cant do anything with her. The only thing you can do is to get rid of her, let her go on and live with her own sort.
paragraphs.zh: 就在那时，我碰巧朝小巷望去，看到了她。当我退后一步看手表时，我当时没有注意到他是谁，因为我正在看手表。距离除了我之外的任何人都预计她会出去的时间只有两点三十分、四十五分钟。所以当我环视门时，我首先看到的是他打的红领带，我在想什么样的男人才会打红领带。但她正沿着小巷偷偷溜走，注视着门口，所以在他们经过之前我并没有想到他。我想知道她是否对我太不尊重了，以至于当我告诉她不要去学校玩时，她不仅会去学校玩，而且会径直走过商店，不敢让我看到她。只是她看不到门里面，因为阳光直接照进门里，就像试图透过汽车探照灯看东西一样，所以我站在那里，看着她走过去，她的脸涂得像个该死的小丑，头发粘满了胶，扭曲着，穿着一件衣服，如果一个女人在我还是个年轻人的时候，即使是在加约索街或比尔街走出家门，除了覆盖她的腿和后面，她也会被扔进监狱。如果他们穿得不像他们试图让街上经过的每个人都想伸出手来拍拍它，我就该死了。所以我在想什么样的该死的男人会戴红领带，突然间我知道他是那些表演者之一，就像她告诉我的一样。好吧，我可以忍受很多；如果我不能，该死的如果我不会陷入困境，所以当他们转过拐角时，我跳了下来，跟着。我，没戴帽子，在下午的时候，为了母亲的好名声，不得不在后巷里来回追逐。就像我说的，如果她有这样的想法，你就不能对她做任何事。如果这是她的血液，你就不能对她做任何事。你唯一能做的就是摆脱她，让她继续和她自己的同类生活。

paragraphs.en: I went on to the street, but they were out of sight. And there I was, without any hat, looking like I was crazy too. Like a man would naturally think, one of them is crazy and another one drowned himself and the other one was turned out into the street by her husband, what’s the reason the rest of them are not crazy too. All the time I could see them watching me like a hawk, waiting for a chance to say Well I’m not surprised I expected it all the time the whole family’s crazy. Selling land to send him to Harvard and paying taxes to support a state University all the time that I never saw except twice at a baseball game and not letting her daughter’s name be spoken on the place until after a while Father wouldn’t even come down town anymore but just sat there all day with the decanter I could see the bottom of his nightshirt and his bare legs and hear the decanter clinking until finally T. P. had to pour it for him and she says You have no respect for your Father’s memory and I says I dont know why not it sure is preserved well enough to last only if I’m crazy too God knows what I’ll do about it just to look at water makes me sick and I’d just as soon swallow gasoline as a glass of whiskey and Lorraine telling them he may not drink but if you dont believe he’s a man I can tell you how to find out she says If I catch you fooling with any of these whores you know what I’ll do she says I’ll whip her grabbing at her I’ll whip her as long as I can find her she says and I says if I dont drink that’s my business but have you ever found me short I says I’ll buy you enough beer to take a bath in if you want it because I’ve got every respect for a good honest whore because with Mother’s health and the position I try to uphold to have her with no more respect for what I try to do for her than to make her name and my name and my Mother’s name a byword in the town.
paragraphs.zh: 我走到街上，但他们已经看不见了。我就在那里，没有戴帽子，看起来我也疯了。就像一个男人自然会想的那样，其中一个疯了，另一个淹死了，另一个被她丈夫赶到了街上，为什么其他人也不疯。我一直看到他们像老鹰一样看着我，等待着一个机会说：好吧，我并不感到惊讶，我一直都在预料到这一点，全家人都疯了。卖地送他去哈佛，纳税来资助一所州立大学，我从来没有见过，除了两次棒球比赛，直到一段时间后，才让她女儿的名字在这个地方被提及，直到一段时间之后，父亲甚至不再进城了，只是整天拿着酒瓶坐在那儿，我可以看到他睡衣的底部和他光着的腿，听到酒瓶叮当作响，直到最后蒂·皮不得不为他倒酒，她说你不尊重你父亲的记忆，我说我不知道为什么它肯定保存得足够好，只有当我也疯了的时候天知道我会怎么做，只是看到水就让我恶心，我会像喝一杯威士忌一样吞下汽油，洛兰告诉他们他可能不喝酒，但如果你不相信他是一个男人，我可以告诉你如何找出她说如果我抓住你和这些妓女中的任何一个愚弄你知道我会做什么她说我会鞭打她抓住她我会鞭打她她说只要我能找到她，我说如果我不喝酒那是我的事，但你有没有发现我矮了我说如果你想要的话我会给你买足够的啤酒洗澡，因为我非常尊重一个诚实的好妓女，因为母亲的健康和我努力维护的地位，而不是尊重我为她做的事情，就像让她的名字、我的名字和我母亲的名字成为镇上的一个代名词一样。

paragraphs.en: She had dodged out of sight somewhere. Saw me coming and dodged into another alley, running up and down the alleys with a damn show man in a red tie that everybody would look at and think what kind of a damn man would wear a red tie. Well, the boy kept speaking to me and so I took the telegram without knowing I had taken it. I didn’t realise what it was until I was signing for it, and I tore it open without even caring much what it was. I knew all the time what it would be, I reckon. That was the only thing else that could happen, especially holding it up until I had already had the check entered on the pass book.
paragraphs.zh: 她已经躲到看不见的地方了。看到我来了，就躲到另一条巷子里，和一个系着红领带的该死的表演者在巷子里跑来跑去，每个人都会看着并思考什么样的该死的男人会系着红领带。嗯，那个男孩一直跟我说话，所以我在不知道自己已经收到电报的情况下接了它。直到我签字时我才意识到那是什么，我什至不在乎它是什么，就把它撕开了。我想我一直都知道那会是什么。这是唯一可能发生的事情，尤其是在我将支票记入存折之前一直拖延。

paragraphs.en: I dont see how a city no bigger than New York can hold enough people to take the money away from us country suckers. Work like hell all day every day, send them your money and get a little piece of paper back, Your account closed at 20.62. Teasing you along, letting you pile up a little paper profit, then bang! Your account closed at 20.62. And if that wasn’t enough, paying ten dollars a month to somebody to tell you how to lose it fast, that either dont know anything about it or is in cahoots with the telegraph company. Well, I’m done with them. They’ve sucked me in for the last time. Any fool except a fellow that hasn’t got any more sense than to take a jew’s word for anything could tell the market was going up all the time, with the whole damn delta about to be flooded again and the cotton washed right out of the ground like it was last year. Let it wash a man’s crop out of the ground year after year, and them up there in Washington spending fifty thousand dollars a day keeping an army in Nicaragua or some place. Of course it’ll overflow again, and then cotton’ll be worth thirty cents a pound. Well, I just want to hit them one time and get my money back. I don’t want a killing; only these small town gamblers are out for that, I just want my money back that these damn jews have gotten with all their guaranteed inside dope. Then I’m through; they can kiss my foot for every other red cent of mine they get.
paragraphs.zh: 我不明白一个不比纽约大的城市怎么能容纳足够多的人口来从我们乡下人手中夺走金钱。每天拼命工作，把钱寄给他们，然后拿回一张小纸条，你的账户在 20.62 关闭。逗你玩，让你积累一点账面利润，然后砰！您的账户于 20.62 关闭。如果这还不够，每月向某人支付十美元，告诉你如何快速失去它，这个人要么对此一无所知，要么与电报公司勾结。好吧，我已经受够了。他们最后一次把我吸进去了。任何一个傻瓜，除了一个不相信犹太人的话的人，都可以看出市场一直在上涨，整个该死的三角洲将再次被洪水淹没，棉花像去年一样从地里被冲走。让它年复一年地把人们的庄稼从地里冲走，华盛顿的人每天花五万美元在尼加拉瓜或其他地方养一支军队。当然，它会再次溢出，然后棉花将值三十美分一磅。好吧，我只是想打他们一次，把我的钱拿回来。我不想杀人；只有这些小镇的赌徒才愿意这么做，我只是想拿回这些该死的犹太人用他们所有保证的内幕毒品得到的钱。然后我就结束了；他们可以亲吻我的脚，以换取我的每一个红分。

paragraphs.en: I went back to the store. It was half past three almost. Damn little time to do anything in, but then I am used to that. I never had to go to Harvard to learn that. The band had quit playing. Got them all inside now, and they wouldn’t have to waste any more wind. Earl says,
paragraphs.zh: 我回到商店。时间已经快三点半了。真是太少时间做任何事了，但后来我就习惯了。我从来不需要去哈佛就可以学到这一点。乐队已经停止演奏了。现在把他们都放进去，他们就不用再浪费风了。厄尔说，

paragraphs.en: “He found you, did he? He was in here with it a while ago. I thought you were out back somewhere.”
paragraphs.zh: “他找到了你，是吗？他不久前还带着它来过这里。我以为你在外面的某个地方。”

paragraphs.en: “Yes,” I says, “I got it. They couldn’t keep it away from me all afternoon. The town’s too small. I’ve got to go out home a minute,” I says. “You can dock me if it’ll make you feel any better.”
paragraphs.zh: “是的，”我说，“我明白了。他们整个下午都无法把它从我身边带走。这个小镇太小了。我得回家一会儿，”我说。“如果能让你感觉好一点的话，你可以停靠我。”

paragraphs.en: “Go ahead,” he says, “I can handle it now. No bad news, I hope.”
paragraphs.zh: “继续吧，”他说，“我现在可以处理了。我希望没有坏消息。”

paragraphs.en: “You’ll have to go to the telegraph office and find that out,” I says. “They’ll have time to tell you. I haven’t.”
paragraphs.zh: “你必须去电报局才能找到答案，”我说。“他们会有时间告诉你的。我还没有。”

paragraphs.en: “I just asked,” he says. “Your mother knows she can depend on me.”
paragraphs.zh: “我只是问了，”他说。“你妈妈知道她可以依靠我。”

paragraphs.en: “She’ll appreciate it,” I says. “I wont be gone any longer than I have to.”
paragraphs.zh: “她会很感激的，”我说。“我不会离开的时间超过必要的时间。”

paragraphs.en: “Take your time,” he says. “I can handle it now. You go ahead.”
paragraphs.zh: “慢慢来，”他说。“我现在可以处理了，你尽管吧。”

paragraphs.en: I got the car and went home. Once this morning, twice at noon, and now again, with her and having to chase all over town and having to beg them to let me eat a little of the food I am paying for. Sometimes I think what’s the use of anything. With the precedent I’ve been set I must be crazy to keep on. And now I reckon I’ll get home just in time to take a nice long drive after a basket of tomatoes or something and then have to go back to town smelling like a camphor factory so my head wont explode right on my shoulders. I keep telling her there’s not a damn thing in that aspirin except flour and water for imaginary invalids. I says you dont know what a headache is. I says you think I’d fool with that damn car at all if it depended on me. I says I can get along without one I’ve learned to get along without lots of things but if you want to risk yourself in that old wornout surrey with a halfgrown nigger boy all right because I says God looks after Ben’s kind, God knows He ought to do something for him but if you think I’m going to trust a thousand dollars’ worth of delicate machinery to a halfgrown nigger or a grown one either, you’d better buy him one yourself because I says you like to ride in the car and you know you do.
paragraphs.zh: 我拿到车就回家了。今天早上一次，中午两次，现在又是一次，和她一起，不得不满城追赶，不得不恳求他们让我吃一点我付钱的食物。有时候我会想，什么都有什么用呢？有了先例，我再坚持下去一定是疯了。现在我想我会及时回家，买一篮西红柿什么的，然后开长途车，然后回到镇上，闻起来像樟脑工厂，这样我的头就不会在我的肩膀上爆炸。我一直告诉她，阿司匹林里除了面粉和水之外什么也没有，是给想象中的病人用的。我说你不知道什么是头痛。我说你认为如果那辆该死的车取决于我的话我就会去愚弄它。我说我可以在没有一个人的情况下相处，我已经学会了在没有很多东西的情况下相处，但是如果你想和一个半成年的黑鬼男孩一起冒险在那辆破旧的萨里车里，好吧，因为我说上帝会照顾本的同类，上帝知道他应该为他做点什么，但如果你认为我会把价值一千美元的精密机械托付给一个半成年的黑鬼或一个成年的人，你最好自己给他买一个，因为我说你喜欢坐汽车，你知道你会的。

paragraphs.en: Dilsey said Mother was in the house. I went on into the hall and listened, but I didn’t hear anything. I went up stairs, but just as I passed her door she called me.
paragraphs.zh: 迪尔西说妈妈在家里。我走进大厅听着，但什么也没听到。我上了楼梯，但当我经过她的门时，她叫了我。

paragraphs.en: “I just wanted to know who it was,” she says. “I’m here alone so much that I hear every sound.”
paragraphs.zh: “我只是想知道是谁，”她说。“我一个人在这里，所以我能听到所有的声音。”

paragraphs.en: “You dont have to stay here,” I says. “You could spend the whole day visiting like other women, if you wanted to.” She came to the door.
paragraphs.zh: “你不必留在这里，”我说。“如果你愿意的话，你可以像其他女人一样花一整天的时间来拜访。”她来到门口。

paragraphs.en: “I thought maybe you were sick,” she says. “Having to hurry through your dinner like you did.”
paragraphs.zh: “我以为你可能病了，”她说。“必须像你一样快点吃完晚饭。”

paragraphs.en: “Better luck next time,” I says. “What do you want?”
paragraphs.zh: “下次祝你好运。”我说。“你想要什么？”

paragraphs.en: “Is anything wrong?” she says.
paragraphs.zh: “有什么事吗？”她说。

paragraphs.en: “What could be?” I says. “Cant I come home in the middle of the afternoon without upsetting the whole house?”
paragraphs.zh: “可能是什么？”我说。“我能在下午回家的时候不把整个房子弄乱吗？”

paragraphs.en: “Have you seen Quentin?” she says.
paragraphs.zh: “你见过昆丁吗？”她说。

paragraphs.en: “She’s in school,” I says.
paragraphs.zh: “她在学校，”我说。

paragraphs.en: “It’s after three,” she says. “I heard the clock strike at least a half an hour ago. She ought to be home by now.”
paragraphs.zh: “已经三点了，”她说。“我至少在半小时前听到钟声了。她现在应该到家了。”

paragraphs.en: “Ought she?” I says. “When have you ever seen her before dark?”
paragraphs.zh: “她应该吗？”我说。“天黑前你什么时候见过她？”

paragraphs.en: “She ought to be home,” she says. “When I was a girl . . .”
paragraphs.zh: “她应该回家了，”她说。“当我还是个女孩的时候……”

paragraphs.en: “You had somebody to make you behave yourself,” I says. “She hasn’t.”
paragraphs.zh: “有人让你规规矩矩，”我说。“她没有。”

paragraphs.en: “I can’t do anything with her,” she says. “I’ve tried and I’ve tried.”
paragraphs.zh: “我对她无能为力，”她说。“我已经尝试过了，我已经尝试过了。”

paragraphs.en: “And you wont let me, for some reason,” I says, “So you ought to be satisfied.” I went on to my room. I turned the key easy and stood there until the knob turned. Then she says,
paragraphs.zh: “但出于某种原因，你不让我这么做，”我说，“所以你应该感到满意。”我继续往自己的房间走去。我轻松转动钥匙，站在那里直到旋钮转动。然后她说，

paragraphs.en: “Jason.”
paragraphs.zh: “杰生。”

paragraphs.en: “What,” I says.
paragraphs.zh: “什么，”我说。

paragraphs.en: “I just thought something was wrong.”
paragraphs.zh: “我只是觉得出了什么问题。”

paragraphs.en: “Not in here,” I says. “You’ve come to the wrong place.”
paragraphs.zh: “不在这里，”我说。“你来错地方了。”

paragraphs.en: “I dont mean to worry you,” she says.
paragraphs.zh: “我不想让你担心，”她说。

paragraphs.en: “I’m glad to hear that,” I says. “I wasn’t sure. I thought I might have been mistaken. Do you want anything?”
paragraphs.zh: “我很高兴听到这个消息，”我说。“我不确定。我想我可能弄错了。你想要什么吗？”

paragraphs.en: After awhile she says, “No. Not any thing.” Then she went away. I took the box down and counted out the money and hid the box again and unlocked the door and went out. I thought about the camphor, but it would be too late now, anyway. And I’d just have one more round trip. She was at her door, waiting.
paragraphs.zh: 过了一会儿，她说：“不。没什么。”然后她就走了。我把盒子拿下来，数了钱，又把盒子藏起来，打开门出去了。我想到了樟脑，但无论如何现在已经太晚了。我只想再多来一次往返。她就在门口等着。

paragraphs.en: “You want anything from town?” I says.
paragraphs.zh: “你想要镇上的东西吗？”我说。

paragraphs.en: “No,” she says. “I dont mean to meddle in your affairs. But I dont know what I’d do if anything happened to you, Jason.”
paragraphs.zh: “不，”她说。“我无意插手你的事情，但杰生，如果你出了什么事，我不知道该怎么办。”

paragraphs.en: “I’m all right,” I says. “Just a headache.”
paragraphs.zh: “我没事，”我说。“就是头疼。”

paragraphs.en: “I wish you’d take some aspirin,” she says. “I know you’re not going to stop using the car.”
paragraphs.zh: “我希望你服用一些阿司匹林，”她说。“我知道你不会停止使用这辆车。”

paragraphs.en: “What’s the car got to do with it?” I says. “How can a car give a man a headache?”
paragraphs.zh: “这和车有什么关系？”我说。“汽车怎么能让人头疼呢？”

paragraphs.en: “You know gasoline always made you sick,” she says. “Ever since you were a child. I wish you’d take some aspirin.”
paragraphs.zh: “你知道汽油总是会让你生病，”她说。“从小到大，我希望你能吃点阿司匹林。”

paragraphs.en: “Keep on wishing it,” I says. “It wont hurt you.”
paragraphs.zh: “继续希望吧，”我说。“它不会伤害你。”

paragraphs.en: I got in the car and started back to town. I had just turned onto the street when I saw a ford coming helling toward me. All of a sudden it stopped. I could hear the wheels sliding and it slewed around and backed and whirled and just as I was thinking what the hell they were up to, I saw that red tie. Then I recognised her face looking back through the window. It whirled into the alley. I saw it turn again, but when I got to the back street it was just disappearing, running like hell.
paragraphs.zh: 我上了车，开始回城。我刚拐到街上，就看见一辆福特车向我猛冲过来。突然它停了下来。我能听到车轮滑动的声音，它旋转、后退、旋转，正当我思考他们到底在做什么时，我看到了那条红色领带。然后我认出了她透过窗户回头看去的脸。它旋转着进入了小巷。我看到它又转动了，但当我到达后街时，它就消失了，拼命奔跑。

paragraphs.en: I saw red. When I recognised that red tie, after all I had told her, I forgot about everything. I never thought about my head even until I came to the first forks and had to stop. Yet we spend money and spend money on roads and damn if it isn’t like trying to drive over a sheet of corrugated iron roofing. I’d like to know how a man could be expected to keep up with even a wheelbarrow. I think too much of my car; I’m not going to hammer it to pieces like it was a ford. Chances were they had stolen it, anyway, so why should they give a damn. Like I say blood always tells. If you’ve got blood like that in you, you’ll do anything. I says whatever claim you believe she has on you has already been discharged; I says from now on you have only yourself to blame because you know what any sensible person would do. I says if I’ve got to spend half my time being a damn detective, at least I’ll go where I can get paid for it.
paragraphs.zh: 我看到了红色。当我认出那条红领带时，在我告诉她一切之后，我忘记了一切。直到我来到第一个岔路口并不得不停下来时，我才考虑过自己的头脑。然而，我们在道路上花了很多钱，如果这不像试图开车驶过一层波纹铁皮屋顶，那该死的。我想知道一个人怎样才能跟上一辆独轮车。我太看重我的车了；我不会像对待福特一样把它砸成碎片。无论如何，很可能他们已经偷了它，所以他们为什么要在乎呢？就像我说的，血总能说明一切。如果你体内有这样的血液，你就会做任何事。我想说的是，无论你认为她对你有什么要求，都已经被解除了；我说从现在起你就只能怪你自己了，因为你知道任何明智的人都会做什么。我说，如果我必须花一半的时间当一名该死的侦探，至少我会去能得到报酬的地方。

paragraphs.en: So I had to stop there at the forks. Then I remembered it. It felt like somebody was inside with a hammer, beating on it. I says I’ve tried to keep you from being worried by her; I says far as I’m concerned, let her go to hell as fast as she pleases and the sooner the better. I says what else do you expect except every drummer and cheap show that comes to town because even these town jellybeans give her the go-by now. You dont know what goes on I says, you dont hear the talk that I hear and you can just bet I shut them up too. I says my people owned slaves here when you all were running little shirt tail country stores and farming land no nigger would look at on shares.
paragraphs.zh: 所以我不得不在岔路口停下来。然后我就想起来了。感觉就像有人拿着锤子在里面敲打。我说我已经尽力不让你为她担心了；我说就我而言，让她尽快下地狱吧，越快越好。我说除了来到镇上的每个鼓手和廉价表演之外，你还能期待什么，因为即使是这些镇上的软心豆粒糖现在也让她过去了。你不知道我在说什么，你听不到我听到的谈话，你可以打赌我也让他们闭嘴了。我说我的人民在这里拥有奴隶，而你们都在经营小衬衫尾巴乡村商店和耕地，没有黑鬼会看股票。

paragraphs.en: If they ever farmed it. It’s a good thing the Lord did something for this country; the folks that live on it never have. Friday afternoon, and from right here I could see three miles of land that hadn’t even been broken, and every able bodied man in the county in town at that show. I might have been a stranger starving to death, and there wasn’t a soul in sight to ask which way to town even. And she trying to get me to take aspirin. I says when I eat bread I’ll do it at the table. I says you always talking about how much you give up for us when you could buy ten new dresses a year on the money you spend for those damn patent medicines. It’s not something to cure it I need it’s just an even break not to have to have them but as long as I have to work ten hours a day to support a kitchen full of niggers in the style they’re accustomed to and send them to the show with every other nigger in the county, only he was late already. By the time he got there it would be over.
paragraphs.zh: 如果他们曾经种植过它。主为这个国家做了一些事情，这是一件好事；住在上面的人们从来没有。星期五下午，从这里我可以看到三英里尚未被破坏的土地，以及县城里每一个身体健全的人都在观看那场演出。我可能是一个快要饿死的陌生人，而且看不到一个人来问去镇上的路。她试图让我服用阿司匹林。我说当我吃面包时我会在餐桌上做。我说你总是在谈论你为我们放弃了多少，当你每年可以用买那些该死的专利药品的钱购买十件新衣服时。这不是治愈它的东西，我需要的只是一个平衡的休息，不必拥有他们，但只要我必须每天工作十个小时，以他们习惯的方式支持一个满是黑鬼的厨房，并把他们和县里其他黑鬼一起送去演出，只有他已经迟到了。等他到了那里，事情就已经结束了。

paragraphs.en: After awhile he got up to the car and when I finally got it through his head if two people in a ford had passed him, he said yes. So I went on, and when I came to where the wagon road turned off I could see the tire tracks. Ab Russell was in his lot, but I didn’t bother to ask him and I hadn’t got out of sight of his barn hardly when I saw the ford. They had tried to hide it. Done about as well at it as she did at everything else she did. Like I say it’s not that I object to so much; maybe she cant help that, it’s because she hasn’t even got enough consideration for her own family to have any discretion. I’m afraid all the time I’ll run into them right in the middle of the street or under a wagon on the square, like a couple of dogs.
paragraphs.zh: 过了一会儿，他走到车前，当我终于明白他的脑子里是否有两个人在福特车里经过他时，他说是的。于是我继续前行，当我来到马车路岔路的地方时，我可以看到轮胎痕迹。阿布·拉塞尔也在他的地盘上，但我懒得去问他，当我看到浅滩时，我还没有离开他的谷仓。他们曾试图隐藏它。她在这件事上做得和她做的其他事情一样好。就像我说的那样，我并不是那么反对；而是我非常反对。或许她也无可奈何，因为她连自己的家人都没有考虑到，没有足够的自由裁量权。我总是担心我会在街中央或广场的马车底下遇到它们，就像两只狗一样。

paragraphs.en: I parked and got out. And now I’d have to go way around and cross a plowed field, the only one I had seen since I left town, with every step like somebody was walking along behind me, hitting me on the head with a club. I kept thinking that when I got across the field at least I’d have something level to walk on, that wouldn’t jolt me every step, but when I got into the woods it was full of underbrush and I had to twist around through it, and then I came to a ditch full of briers. I went along it for awhile, but it got thicker and thicker, and all the time Earl probably telephoning home about where I was and getting Mother all upset again.
paragraphs.zh: 我停好车然后下车。现在我必须绕一圈，穿过一片犁过的田地，这是我离开小镇以来唯一见过的田地，每一步都像是有人在我后面走，用棍子打我的头。我一直在想，当我穿过田野时，至少我有一个平坦的地方可以行走，这样我就不会每一步都摇摇欲坠，但当我进入树林时，那里充满了灌木丛，我不得不绕过它，然后我来到了一条长满荆棘的沟渠。我顺着它走了一会儿，但它变得越来越厚，厄尔可能一直打电话回家询问我在哪里，这又让母亲感到不安。

paragraphs.en: When I finally got through I had had to wind around so much that I had to stop and figure out just where the car would be. I knew they wouldn’t be far from it, just under the closest bush, so I turned and worked back toward the road. Then I couldn’t tell just how far I was, so I’d have to stop and listen, and then with my legs not using so much blood, it all would go into my head like it would explode any minute, and the sun getting down just to where it could shine straight into my eyes and my ears ringing so I couldn’t hear anything. I went on, trying to move quiet, then I heard a dog or something and I knew that when he scented me he’d have to come helling up, then it would be all off.
paragraphs.zh: 当我终于通过时，我不得不绕得很远，以至于我不得不停下来弄清楚汽车到底在哪里。我知道他们离它不远，就在最近的灌木丛下，所以我转身朝路走去。然后我不知道自己到底有多远，所以我必须停下来听听，然后我的腿没有用那么多血，一切都会进入我的脑海，就像随时会爆炸一样，太阳落山到可以直接照进我眼睛的地方，我的耳朵嗡嗡作响，所以我听不到任何声音。我继续往前走，试图保持安静，然后我听到了狗的叫声或其他什么声音，我知道当他闻到我的气味时，他一定会惊慌失措，然后一切就都结束了。

paragraphs.en: I had gotten beggar lice and twigs and stuff all over me, inside my clothes and shoes and all, and then I happened to look around and I had my hand right on a bunch of poison oak. The only thing I couldn’t understand was why it was just poison oak and not a snake or something. So I didn’t even bother to move it. I just stood there until the dog went away. Then I went on.
paragraphs.zh: 我身上沾满了乞丐虱子、树枝之类的东西，衣服里、鞋子里等等，然后我碰巧环顾四周，发现我的手正好放在一棵毒橡树上。我唯一不明白的是为什么它只是毒橡树而不是蛇什么的。所以我什至懒得去动它。我就站在那里，直到狗走开。然后我继续说。

paragraphs.en: I didn’t have any idea where the car was now. I couldn’t think about anything except my head, and I’d just stand in one place and sort of wonder if I had really seen a ford even, and I didn’t even care much whether I had or not. Like I say, let her lay out all day and all night with everything in town that wears pants, what do I care. I dont owe anything to anybody that has no more consideration for me, that wouldn’t be a damn bit above planting that ford there and making me spend a whole afternoon and Earl taking her back there and showing her the books just because he’s too damn virtuous for this world. I says you’ll have one hell of a time in heaven, without anybody’s business to meddle in only dont you ever let me catch you at it I says, I close my eyes to it because of your grandmother, but just you let me catch you doing it one time on this place, where my mother lives. These damn little slick haired squirts, thinking they are raising so much hell, I’ll show them something about hell I says, and you too. I’ll make him think that damn red tie is the latch string to hell, if he thinks he can run the woods with my niece.
paragraphs.zh: 我不知道车现在在哪里。除了脑子之外，我无法思考任何事情，我只是站在一个地方，想知道我是否真的看到了一辆福特，而且我什至不太关心我是否看到过。就像我说的，让她整天整夜地和城里所有穿裤子的东西摆在一起，我在乎什么。我不欠任何不再关心我的人任何东西，这不会比在那里种植那辆福特并让我度过整个下午而厄尔带她回到那里并向她展示书籍只是因为他对这个世界来说太他妈的善良了。我说你会在天堂度过一段地狱般的时光，没有任何人干涉，只是别让我抓住你，我说，因为你的祖母，我闭上了眼睛，但只要你让我抓住你在这个地方，我母亲住的地方，一次。这些该死的光滑头发的小水鬼，认为他们正在引发如此多的地狱，我将向他们展示一些我所说的关于地狱的东西，还有你。如果他认为他可以和我侄女一起在树林里奔跑，我会让他认为那条该死的红领带是通往地狱的闩锁。

paragraphs.en: With the sun and all in my eyes and my blood going so I kept thinking every time my head would go on and burst and get it over with, with briers and things grabbing at me, then I came onto the sand ditch where they had been and I recognised the tree where the car was, and just as I got out of the ditch and started running I heard the car start. It went off fast, blowing the horn. They kept on blowing it, like it was saying Yah. Yah. Yaaahhhhhhhh, going out of sight. I got to the road just in time to see it go out of sight.
paragraphs.zh: 阳光和一切都在我的眼睛里，我的血液在流淌，所以我一直在想，每次我的头会继续前进，爆裂，结束，荆棘和其他东西抓住我，然后我来到沙沟，他们曾经在那里，我认出了汽车所在的那棵树，正当我从沟里出来并开始奔跑时，我听到汽车发动了。它很快就响了，吹响了喇叭。他们继续吹它，就像在说“是的”。嗯。啊啊啊啊啊，消失不见了。我及时赶到了路边，看到它消失在视线之外。

paragraphs.en: By the time I got up to where my car was, they were clean out of sight, the horn still blowing. Well, I never thought anything about it except I was saying Run. Run back to town. Run home and try to convince Mother that I never saw you in that car. Try to make her believe that I dont know who he was. Try to make her believe that I didn’t miss ten feet of catching you in that ditch. Try to make her believe you were standing up, too.
paragraphs.zh: 当我到达我的车所在的地方时，它们已经消失在我的视线之外，喇叭还在吹。好吧，除了我说“跑”之外，我从来没有想过任何事情。跑回城里。跑回家，试着让妈妈相信我从来没有在那辆车里见过你。试着让她相信我不知道他是谁。试着让她相信我没有错过在沟里抓住你的十英尺。试着让她相信你也站起来了。

paragraphs.en: It kept on saying Yahhhhh, Yahhhhh, Yaaahhhhhhhhh, getting fainter and fainter. Then it quit, and I could hear a cow lowing up at Russell’s barn. And still I never thought. I went up to the door and opened it and raised my foot. I kind of thought then that the car was leaning a little more than the slant of the road would be, but I never found it out until I got in and started off.
paragraphs.zh: It kept on saying Yahhhhh, Yahhhhh, Yaaahhhhhhhhh, getting fainter and fainter.然后声音停止了，我能听到一头牛在拉塞尔的谷仓里鸣叫。但我仍然没有想到。我走到门口，打开门，抬起脚。当时我觉得车子的倾斜度比路面的倾斜度还要大一点，但直到上车出发后我才发现。

paragraphs.en: Well, I just sat there. It was getting on toward sundown, and town was about five miles. They never even had guts enough to puncture it, to jab a hole in it. They just let the air out. I just stood there for awhile, thinking about that kitchen full of niggers and not one of them had time to lift a tire onto the rack and screw up a couple of bolts. It was kind of funny because even she couldn’t have seen far enough ahead to take the pump out on purpose, unless she thought about it while he was letting out the air maybe. But what it probably was, was somebody took it out and gave it to Ben to play with for a squirt gun because they’d take the whole car to pieces if he wanted it and Dilsey says, Aint nobody teched yo car. What we want to fool with hit fer? and I says You’re a nigger. You’re lucky, do you know it? I says I’ll swap with you any day because it takes a white man not to have anymore sense than to worry about what a little slut of a girl does.
paragraphs.zh: 嗯，我只是坐在那里。太阳快要落山了，小镇距离这里大约有五英里。他们甚至没有足够的勇气去刺穿它，在上面戳一个洞。他们只是把空气放出去。我只是在那里站了一会儿，想着厨房里挤满了黑鬼，但他们中没有人有时间把轮胎举到架子上并拧紧几个螺栓。这有点有趣，因为即使她也看不到足够远的前方，无法故意将泵取出，除非她在他放气时想到这一点。但可能是有人把它拿出来给本当水枪玩，因为如果他想要的话，他们会把整辆车拆成碎片，迪尔西说，没有人对你的车进行技术改造。我们想用hit fer来愚弄什么？我说你是个黑鬼。你很幸运，你知道吗？我说我随时都会和你交换，因为一个白人除了担心一个小荡妇的所作所为之外，没有任何理智。

paragraphs.en: I walked up to Russell’s. He had a pump. That was just an oversight on their part, I reckon. Only I still couldn’t believe she’d have had the nerve to. I kept thinking that. I dont know why it is I cant seem to learn that a woman’ll do anything. I kept thinking, Let’s forget for awhile how I feel toward you and how you feel toward me: I just wouldn’t do you this way. I wouldn’t do you this way no matter what you had done to me. Because like I say blood is blood and you cant get around it. It’s not playing a joke that any eight year old boy could have thought of, it’s letting your own uncle be laughed at by a man that would wear a red tie. They come into town and call us all a bunch of hicks and think it’s too small to hold them. Well he doesn’t know just how right he is. And her too. If that’s the way she feels about it, she’d better keep right on going and a damn good riddance.
paragraphs.zh: 我走到拉塞尔家。他有一个泵。我认为这只是他们的疏忽。只是我仍然不敢相信她有勇气这样做。我一直这么想。我不知道为什么我似乎无法了解到女人会做任何事情。我一直在想，让我们暂时忘记我对你的感觉以及你对我的感觉：我只是不会这样对待你。无论你对我做了什么，我都不会这样对你。因为就像我说的，血就是血，你无法回避它。这不是一个八岁男孩能想到的玩笑，而是让你自己的叔叔被一个系红领带的男人嘲笑。他们来到城里，称我们为一群乡巴佬，并认为城太小，容不下他们。好吧，他不知道自己是多么正确。还有她。如果她就是这么想的，那么她最好继续前进，彻底摆脱困境。

paragraphs.en: I stopped and returned Russell’s pump and drove on to town. I went to the drugstore and got a coca-cola and then I went to the telegraph office. It had closed at 12.21, forty points down. Forty times five dollars; buy something with that if you can, and she’ll say, I’ve got to have it I’ve just got to and I’ll say that’s too bad you’ll have to try somebody else, I haven’t got any money; I’ve been too busy to make any.
paragraphs.zh: 我停下来，归还拉塞尔的泵，然后开车进城。我去药店买了一瓶可口可乐，然后去了电报局。收盘价为 12.21，下跌 40 点。五美元的四十倍；如果可以的话，用它买点东西，她会说，我必须拥有它，我必须拥有它，我会说这太糟糕了，你必须尝试其他人，我没有钱;我太忙了，没时间做任何事。

paragraphs.en: I just looked at him.
paragraphs.zh: 我只是看着他。

paragraphs.en: “I’ll tell you some news,” I says, “You’ll be astonished to learn that I am interested in the cotton market,” I says. “That never occurred to you, did it?”
paragraphs.zh: “我会告诉你一些消息，”我说，“你会惊讶地发现我对棉花市场感兴趣。”我说。“你从来没有想到过这一点，是吗？”

paragraphs.en: “I did my best to deliver it,” he says. “I tried the store twice and called up your house, but they didn’t know where you were,” he says, digging in the drawer.
paragraphs.zh: “我尽了最大努力来实现它，”他说。“我去了商店两次，还给你家打了电话，但他们不知道你在哪里，”他一边说，一边在抽屉里翻手。

paragraphs.en: “Deliver what?” I says. He handed me a telegram. “What time did this come?” I says.
paragraphs.zh: “送什么？”我说。他递给我一份电报。“这是什么时候来的？”我说。

paragraphs.en: “About half past three,” he says.
paragraphs.zh: “大约三点半，”他说。

paragraphs.en: “And now it’s ten minutes past five,” I says.
paragraphs.zh: “现在是五点十分，”我说。

paragraphs.en: “I tried to deliver it,” he says. “I couldn’t find you.”
paragraphs.zh: “我试图交付它，”他说。“我找不到你。”

paragraphs.en: “That’s not my fault, is it?” I says. I opened it, just to see what kind of a lie they’d tell me this time. They must be in one hell of a shape if they’ve got to come all the way to Mississippi to steal ten dollars a month. Sell, it says. The market will be unstable, with a general downward tendency. Do not be alarmed following government report.
paragraphs.zh: “这不是我的错，是吗？”我说。我打开它，只是想看看他们这次会告诉我什么样的谎言。如果他们每个月都要千里迢迢来到密西西比州偷十美元，那他们的处境一定很糟糕。卖吧，它说。市场将不稳定，总体呈下降趋势。看到政府报告后不要惊慌。

paragraphs.en: “How much would a message like this cost?” I says. He told me.
paragraphs.zh: “这样的消息要花多少钱？”我说。他告诉我。

paragraphs.en: “They paid it,” he says.
paragraphs.zh: “他们付了钱，”他说。

paragraphs.en: “Then I owe them that much,” I says. “I already knew this. Send this collect,” I says, taking a blank. Buy, I wrote, Market just on point of blowing its head off. Occasional flurries for purpose of hooking a few more country suckers who haven’t got in to the telegraph office yet. Do not be alarmed. “Send that collect,” I says.
paragraphs.zh: “那我欠他们太多了，”我说。“我已经知道了这一点。发送此收款，”我茫然地说。我写道，买入，市场即将崩溃。偶尔会出现一阵骚乱，目的是为了吸引更多尚未进入电报局的乡村傻瓜。不要惊慌。“发送那个收集，”我说。

paragraphs.en: He looked at the message, then he looked at the clock. “Market closed an hour ago,” he says.
paragraphs.zh: 他看了看消息，然后又看了看时钟。“市场一小时前关闭，”他说。

paragraphs.en: “Well,” I says, “That’s not my fault either. I didn’t invent it; I just bought a little of it while under the impression that the telegraph company would keep me informed as to what it was doing.”
paragraphs.zh: “好吧，”我说，“这也不是我的错。它不是我发明的；我只是买了一点它，当时我以为电报公司会让我知道它在做什么。”

paragraphs.en: “A report is posted whenever it comes in,” he says.
paragraphs.zh: “只要有报告出现，就会发布，”他说。

paragraphs.en: “Yes,” I says, “And in Memphis they have it on a blackboard every ten seconds,” I says. “I was within sixty-seven miles of there once this afternoon.”
paragraphs.zh: “是的，”我说，“在孟菲斯，他们每十秒就把它写在黑板上，”我说。“今天下午我曾到过距那里六十七英里以内的地方。”

paragraphs.en: He looked at the message. “You want to send this?” he says.
paragraphs.zh: 他看着消息。“你想寄这个吗？”他说。

paragraphs.en: “I still haven’t changed my mind,” I says. I wrote the other one out and counted the money. “And this one too, if you’re sure you can spell b-u-y.”
paragraphs.zh: “我仍然没有改变主意，”我说。我把另一张写下来，数了数钱。“还有这个，如果你确定你能拼出 b-u-y。”

paragraphs.en: I went back to the store. I could hear the band from down the street. Prohibition’s a fine thing. Used to be they’d come in Saturday with just one pair of shoes in the family and him wearing them, and they’d go down to the express office and get his package; now they all go to the show barefooted, with the merchants in the door like a row of tigers or something in a cage, watching them pass. Earl says,
paragraphs.zh: 我回到商店。我能听到街上传来乐队的声音。禁止是件好事。以前他们周六来的时候家里只有一双鞋，而他也穿着这双鞋，他们会去快递办公室取他的包裹；现在，他们会去快递办公室拿他的包裹。现在他们都赤脚去看演出，门口的商人就像一排老虎或者笼子里的什么东西，看着他们经过。厄尔说，

paragraphs.en: “I hope it wasn’t anything serious.”
paragraphs.zh: “我希望这不是什么严重的事情。”

paragraphs.en: “What?” I says. He looked at his watch. Then he went to the door and looked at the courthouse clock. “You ought to have a dollar watch,” I says. “It wont cost you so much to believe it’s lying each time.”
paragraphs.zh: “什么？”我说。他看了看手表。然后他走到门口，看了看法院的时钟。“你应该有一块一美元的手表，”我说。“你不会花太多钱去相信它每次都在撒谎。”

paragraphs.en: “What?” he says.
paragraphs.zh: “什么？”他说。

paragraphs.en: “Nothing,” I says. “Hope I haven’t inconvenienced you.”
paragraphs.zh: “没什么，”我说。“希望我没有给你带来不便。”

paragraphs.en: “We were not busy much,” he says. “They all went to the show. It’s all right.”
paragraphs.zh: “我们并不忙，”他说。“他们都去看演出了。没关系。”

paragraphs.en: “If it’s not all right,” I says, “You know what you can do about it.”
paragraphs.zh: “如果不行，”我说，“你知道你能做些什么。”

paragraphs.en: “I said it was all right,” he says.
paragraphs.zh: “我说没关系，”他说。

paragraphs.en: “I heard you,” I says. “And if it’s not all right, you know what you can do about it.”
paragraphs.zh: “我听到了，”我说。“如果情况不好，你知道你能做些什么。”

paragraphs.en: “Do you want to quit?” he says.
paragraphs.zh: “你想退出吗？”他说。

paragraphs.en: “It’s not my business,” I says. “My wishes dont matter. But dont get the idea that you are protecting me by keeping me.”
paragraphs.zh: “这不关我的事，”我说。“我的愿望并不重要。但别以为你留住我是在保护我。”

paragraphs.en: “You’d be a good business man if you’d let yourself, Jason,” he says.
paragraphs.zh: “杰生，如果你愿意的话，你就会成为一名优秀的商人。”他说。

paragraphs.en: “At least I can tend to my own business and let other peoples’ alone,” I says.
paragraphs.zh: “至少我可以专注于我自己的事情，而不管其他人的事情，”我说。

paragraphs.en: “I dont know why you are trying to make me fire you,” he says. “You know you could quit anytime and there wouldn’t be any hard feelings between us.”
paragraphs.zh: “我不知道你为什么要让我解雇你，”他说。“你知道你可以随时退出，我们之间不会有任何不愉快的感觉。”

paragraphs.en: “Maybe that’s why I dont quit,” I says. “As long as I tend to my job, that’s what you are paying me for.” I went on to the back and got a drink of water and went on out to the back door. Job had the cultivators all set up at last. It was quiet there, and pretty soon my head got a little easier. I could hear them singing now, and then the band played again. Well, let them get every quarter and dime in the county; it was no skin off my back. I’ve done what I could; a man that can live as long as I have and not know when to quit is a fool. Especially as it’s no business of mine. If it was my own daughter now it would be different, because she wouldn’t have time to; she’d have to work some to feed a few invalids and idiots and niggers, because how could I have the face to bring anybody there. I’ve too much respect for anybody to do that. I’m a man, I can stand it, it’s my own flesh and blood and I’d like to see the colour of the man’s eyes that would speak disrespectful of any woman that was my friend it’s these damn good women that do it I’d like to see the good, church-going woman that’s half as square as Lorraine, whore or no whore. Like I say if I was to get married you’d go up like a balloon and you know it and she says I want you to be happy to have a family of your own not to slave your life away for us. But I’ll be gone soon and then you can take a wife but you’ll never find a woman who is worthy of you and I says yes I could. You’d get right up out of your grave you know you would. I says no thank you I have all the women I can take care of now if I married a wife she’d probably turn out to be a hophead or something. That’s all we lack in this family, I says.
paragraphs.zh: “也许这就是我不放弃的原因，”我说。“只要我专注于我的工作，这就是你付钱给我的原因。”我走到后面喝了口水，然后走到后门。约伯终于把耕种者都安置好了。那里很安静，很快我的头脑就轻松了一些。我现在可以听到他们唱歌，然后乐队又演奏了。好吧，让他们得到县里的每一分钱；我的背上一点皮也没有。我已经尽力了；一个人能活得和我一样长，却不知道什么时候该放弃，他就是个傻瓜。尤其是这不关我的事。如果现在是我自己的女儿，那就不一样了，因为她没有时间；她必须工作一些来养活一些病人、白痴和黑鬼，因为我怎么有脸带任何人去那里。我非常尊重任何人这样做。我是个男人，我能忍受，这是我自己的血肉，我想看看那个男人眼睛的颜色会说出对我朋友的任何女人的不尊重，是这些该死的好女人做的，我想看到那个善良的，有洛兰一半方形的女人，无论是妓女还是不是妓女。就像我说的，如果我要结婚，你会像气球一样上升，你知道这一点，她说我希望你快乐地拥有自己的家庭，而不是为了我们而牺牲你的生活。但我很快就会离开，然后你可以娶个妻子，但你永远找不到一个配得上你的女人，我说是的，我可以。你会从坟墓里爬起来，你知道你会的。我说不，谢谢，我现在有所有我能照顾的女人，如果我娶了一个妻子，她可能会变成一个啤酒花头什么的。我说，这就是我们这个家庭所缺乏的。

paragraphs.en: The sun was down beyond the Methodist church now, and the pigeons were flying back and forth around the steeple, and when the band stopped I could hear them cooing. It hadn’t been four months since Christmas, and yet they were almost as thick as ever. I reckon Parson Walthall was getting a belly full of them now. You’d have thought we were shooting people, with him making speeches and even holding onto a man’s gun when they came over. Talking about peace on earth good will toward all and not a sparrow can fall to earth. But what does he care how thick they get, he hasn’t got anything to do; what does he care what time it is. He pays no taxes, he doesn’t have to see his money going every year to have the courthouse clock cleaned to where it’ll run. They had to pay a man forty-five dollars to clean it. I counted over a hundred half-hatched pigeons on the ground. You’d think they’d have sense enough to leave town. It’s a good thing I dont have any more ties than a pigeon, I’ll say that.
paragraphs.zh: 现在太阳已经落到了卫理公会教堂的后面，鸽子在尖塔周围来回飞翔，当乐队停下来时，我能听到它们咕咕叫。距离圣诞节还不到四个月，但它们却几乎和以前一样浓密。我估计帕森·沃尔索尔现在已经吃饱了。你可能以为我们在向人开枪，而他则发表演讲，甚至在他们过来时还拿着一个人的枪。谈论地球和平，向所有人表达善意，没有一只麻雀能落到地球上。但他不在乎它们变得多厚，他无事可做；他没有事可做。他关心现在几点了。他不用缴税，也不必每年都花他的钱来把法院的时钟清理到正常运行的地方。他们必须付给一个人四十五美元来清理它。我数了数地上有一百多只半孵出的鸽子。你可能认为他们有足够的理智离开城镇。我会这么说，幸好我没有比鸽子更多的领带。

paragraphs.en: The band was playing again, a loud fast tune, like they were breaking up. I reckon they’d be satisfied now. Maybe they’d have enough music to entertain them while they drove fourteen or fifteen miles home and unharnessed in the dark and fed the stock and milked. All they’d have to do would be to whistle the music and tell the jokes to the live stock in the barn, and then they could count up how much they’d made by not taking the stock to the show too. They could figure that if a man had five children and seven mules, he cleared a quarter by taking his family to the show. Just like that. Earl came back with a couple of packages.
paragraphs.zh: 乐队又开始演奏，是响亮的快节奏，就像他们要解散一样。我想他们现在应该很满意了。也许他们有足够的音乐来娱乐他们，而他们开车十四或十五英里回家，在黑暗中解开马具，喂养牲畜并挤奶。他们所要做的就是吹口哨音乐，给谷仓里的牲畜讲笑话，然后他们就可以计算出如果不把牲畜也带到展会上，他们赚了多少钱。他们可以算出，如果一个男人有五个孩子和七头骡子，他带家人去看演出就可以赚到四分之一。就这样。厄尔带着几个包裹回来了。

paragraphs.en: “Here’s some more stuff going out,” he says. “Where’s Uncle Job?”
paragraphs.zh: “还有更多的东西要出去，”他说。“乔布叔叔在哪儿？”

paragraphs.en: “Gone to the show, I imagine,” I says. “Unless you watched him.”
paragraphs.zh: “我想是去看演出了，”我说。“除非你看着他。”

paragraphs.en: “He doesn’t slip off,” he says. “I can depend on him.”
paragraphs.zh: “他不会滑倒，”他说。“我可以依靠他。”

paragraphs.en: “Meaning me by that,” I says.
paragraphs.zh: “这指的是我，”我说。

paragraphs.en: He went to the door and looked out, listening.
paragraphs.zh: 他走到门口，向外张望，侧耳倾听。

paragraphs.en: “That’s a good band,” he says. “It’s about time they were breaking up, I’d say.”
paragraphs.zh: “这是一支很好的乐队，”他说。“我想说，他们是时候分手了。”

paragraphs.en: “Unless they’re going to spend the night there,” I says. The swallows had begun, and I could hear the sparrows beginning to swarm in the trees in the courthouse yard. Every once in a while a bunch of them would come swirling around in sight above the roof, then go away. They are as big a nuisance as the pigeons, to my notion. You cant even sit in the courthouse yard for them. First thing you know, bing. Right on your hat. But it would take a millionaire to afford to shoot them at five cents a shot. If they’d just put a little poison out there in the square, they’d get rid of them in a day, because if a merchant cant keep his stock from running around the square, he’d better try to deal in something besides chickens, something that dont eat, like plows or onions. And if a man dont keep his dogs up, he either dont want it or he hasn’t any business with one. Like I say if all the businesses in a town are run like country businesses, you’re going to have a country town.
paragraphs.zh: “除非他们要在那里过夜，”我说。燕子开始了，我能听到麻雀开始在法院院子里的树上成群结队。每隔一段时间，就会有一群人在屋顶上方盘旋，然后消失。在我看来，它们和鸽子一样令人讨厌。你甚至不能为他们坐在法院院子里。首先你要知道，bing。就在你的帽子上。但只有百万富翁才能以五美分的价格进行射击。如果他们在广场上放一点毒药，一天之内就会把它们处理掉，因为如果商人不能阻止他的货物在广场上乱跑，他最好尝试经营鸡以外的东西，一些不吃的东西，比如犁或洋葱。如果一个人不养他的狗，他要么不想要它，要么他与狗没有任何关系。就像我说的，如果一个城镇中的所有企业都像乡村企业一样经营，那么你就会拥有一个乡村小镇。

paragraphs.en: “It wont do you any good if they have broke up,” I says. “They’ll have to hitch up and take out to get home by midnight as it is.”
paragraphs.zh: “如果他们分手了，对你没有任何好处，”我说。“他们必须搭便车，在午夜之前回家。”

paragraphs.en: “Well,” he says, “They enjoy it. Let them spend a little money on a show now and then. A hill farmer works pretty hard and gets mighty little for it.”
paragraphs.zh: “嗯，”他说，“他们喜欢这样。让他们时不时地花一点钱看一场演出。山里的农民工作很辛苦，但得到的却很少。”

paragraphs.en: “There’s no law making them farm in the hills,” I says, “Or anywhere else.”
paragraphs.zh: “没有法律规定他们在山上耕种，”我说，“或者在其他地方。”

paragraphs.en: “Where would you and me be, if it wasn’t for the farmers?” he says.
paragraphs.zh: “如果没有农民，你和我会在哪里？”他说。

paragraphs.en: “I’d be home right now,” I says, “Lying down, with an ice pack on my head.”
paragraphs.zh: “我现在就到家了，”我说，“躺着，头上放着冰袋。”

paragraphs.en: “You have these headaches too often,” he says. “Why dont you have your teeth examined good? Did he go over them all this morning?”
paragraphs.zh: “你经常会感到这些头痛，”他说。“你为什么不检查一下你的牙齿？他今天早上检查了吗？”

paragraphs.en: “Did who?” I says.
paragraphs.zh: “谁干的？”我说。

paragraphs.en: “You said you went to the dentist this morning.”
paragraphs.zh: “你说你今天早上去看牙医了。”

paragraphs.en: “Do you object to my having the headache on your time?” I says. “Is that it?” They were crossing the alley now, coming up from the show.
paragraphs.zh: “你反对我打扰你的时间吗？”我说。“是这样吗？”他们现在正在穿过小巷，从演出中走来。

paragraphs.en: “There they come,” he says. “I reckon I better get up front.” He went on. It’s a curious thing how no matter what’s wrong with you, a man’ll tell you to have your teeth examined and a woman’ll tell you to get married. It always takes a man that never made much at any thing to tell you how to run your business, though. Like these college professors without a whole pair of socks to their name, telling you how to make a million in ten years, and a woman that couldn’t even get a husband can always tell you how to raise a family.
paragraphs.zh: “他们来了，”他说。“我想我最好先走在前面。”他继续说下去。奇怪的是，无论你有什么问题，男人都会让你检查牙齿，女人会让你结婚。然而，总是需要一个从来没有赚过太多钱的人来告诉你如何经营你的生意。就像那些连一双袜子都没有的大学教授，告诉你如何在十年内赚到一百万，而一个连丈夫都找不到的女人却总能告诉你如何养家糊口。

paragraphs.en: Old man Job came up with the wagon. After a while he got through wrapping the lines around the whip socket.
paragraphs.zh: 约伯老人开来了马车。过了一会儿，他把绳子绕在鞭子插座上。

paragraphs.en: “Well,” I says, “Was it a good show?”
paragraphs.zh: “嗯，”我说，“这是一场精彩的表演吗？”

paragraphs.en: “I aint been yit,” he says. “But I kin be arrested in dat tent tonight, dough.”
paragraphs.zh: “我不是这样的，”他说。“但今晚我可能会在那个帐篷里被捕，面团。”

paragraphs.en: “Like hell you haven’t,” I says. “You’ve been away from here since three oclock. Mr Earl was just back here looking for you.”
paragraphs.zh: “见鬼，你没有，”我说。“你从三点钟就离开了这里。厄尔先生刚刚回来找你。”

paragraphs.en: “I been tendin to my business,” he says. “Mr Earl knows whar I been.”
paragraphs.zh: “我一直专注于我的生意，”他说。“厄尔先生知道我在哪儿。”

paragraphs.en: “You may can fool him,” I says. “I wont tell on you.”
paragraphs.zh: “你也许可以愚弄他，”我说。“我不会告发你的。”

paragraphs.en: “Den he’s de onliest man here I’d try to fool,” he says. “Whut I want to waste my time foolin a man whut I dont keer whether I sees him Sat’dy night er not? I wont try to fool you,” he says. “You too smart fer me. Yes, suh,” he says, looking busy as hell, putting five or six little packages into the wagon, “You’s too smart fer me. Aint a man in dis town kin keep up wid you fer smartness. You fools a man whut so smart he cant even keep up wid hisself,” he says, getting in the wagon and unwrapping the reins.
paragraphs.zh: “他是这里我唯一想愚弄的人，”他说。“我为什么要浪费时间去愚弄一个我不关心周六晚上是否能见到他的人呢？我不会试图愚弄你，”他说。“你对我来说太聪明了。是的，先生，”他说，看上去很忙，把五六个小包裹放进马车里，“对我来说你太聪明了。镇上没有一个人能跟上你的聪明。你愚弄了一个如此聪明的人，他甚至无法跟上自己，”他说，上了马车，解开缰绳。

paragraphs.en: “Who’s that?” I says.
paragraphs.zh: “那是谁？”我说。

paragraphs.en: “Dat’s Mr Jason Compson,” he says. “Git up dar, Dan!”
paragraphs.zh: “那是杰生康普生先生，”他说。“站起来，丹！”

paragraphs.en: One of the wheels was just about to come off. I watched to see if he’d get out of the alley before it did. Just turn any vehicle over to a nigger, though. I says that old rattletrap’s just an eyesore, yet you’ll keep it standing there in the carriage house a hundred years just so that boy can ride to the cemetery once a week. I says he’s not the first fellow that’ll have to do things he doesn’t want to. I’d make him ride in that car like a civilised man or stay at home. What does he know about where he goes or what he goes in, and us keeping a carriage and a horse so he can take a ride on Sunday afternoon.
paragraphs.zh: 其中一个轮子即将脱落。我观察着他是否能在这之前走出小巷。不过，只要把任何车辆交给黑鬼就可以了。我说那个老响尾蛇只是碍眼，但你却要把它在马车房里放一百年，只是为了让那个男孩每周能骑车去墓地一次。我说他不是第一个不得不做他不想做的事情的人。我会让他像个文明人一样坐那辆车，或者呆在家里。他知道他要去哪里或进去什么，以及我们保留一辆马车和一匹马，以便他可以在周日下午乘坐。

paragraphs.en: A lot Job cared whether the wheel came off or not, long as he wouldn’t have too far to walk back. Like I say the only place for them is in the field, where they’d have to work from sunup to sundown. They cant stand prosperity or an easy job. Let one stay around white people for a while and he’s not worth killing. They get so they can outguess you about work before your very eyes, like Roskus the only mistake he ever made was he got careless one day and died. Shirking and stealing and giving you a little more lip and a little more lip until some day you have to lay them out with a scantling or something. Well, it’s Earl’s business. But I’d hate to have my business advertised over this town by an old doddering nigger and a wagon that you thought every time it turned a corner it would come all to pieces.
paragraphs.zh: 约伯非常关心轮子是否脱落，只要他走回去的路不会太远。就像我说的，他们唯一的地方就是田野里，他们必须从日出工作到日落。他们无法忍受繁荣或轻松的工作。让一个人在白人身边待一段时间，他就不值得被杀。他们这样做是为了在你眼前胜过你对工作的猜测，就像罗斯库斯一样，他犯过的唯一错误就是有一天他粗心大意而死了。偷懒，偷窃，给你多一点的嘴唇和多一点的嘴唇，直到有一天你不得不用小尺寸或其他东西把它们摆出来。好吧，这是厄尔的事。但我不想让一个老态龙钟的黑鬼和一辆马车在这个小镇上为我的生意做广告，你以为它每次转弯都会散架。

paragraphs.en: The sun was all high up in the air now, and inside it was beginning to get dark. I went up front. The square was empty. Earl was back closing the safe, and then the clock begun to strike.
paragraphs.zh: 太阳已经高高挂在空中了，而里面已经开始变黑了。我走到前面。广场上空无一人。厄尔回来关上保险箱，然后时钟开始敲响。

paragraphs.en: “You lock the back door,” he says. I went back and locked it and came back. “I suppose you’re going to the show tonight,” he says. “I gave you those passes yesterday, didn’t I?”
paragraphs.zh: “你锁上后门，”他说。我回去锁了门就回来了。“我想你今晚会去看演出，”他说。“我昨天给了你那些通行证，不是吗？”

paragraphs.en: “Yes,” I said. “You want them back?”
paragraphs.zh: “是的，”我说。“你想让他们回来吗？”

paragraphs.en: “No, no,” he says, “I just forgot whether I gave them to you or not. No sense in wasting them.”
paragraphs.zh: “不，不，”他说，“我只是忘了我是否把它们给了你。浪费它们没有意义。”

paragraphs.en: He locked the door and said Goodnight and went on. The sparrows were still rattling away in the trees, but the square was empty except for a few cars. There was a ford in front of the drugstore, but I didn’t even look at it. I know when I’ve had enough of anything. I dont mind trying to help her, but I know when I’ve had enough. I guess I could teach Luster to drive it, then they could chase her all day long if they wanted to, and I could stay home and play with Ben.
paragraphs.zh: 他锁上门，说了声晚安，然后继续前行。麻雀还在树上叽叽喳喳地叫着，但广场上除了几辆车外空无一人。药店前面有一辆福特车，但我连看都没看。我知道什么时候我已经受够了。我不介意尝试帮助她，但我知道什么时候我已经受够了。我想我可以教勒斯特开车，然后如果他们愿意的话，他们可以整天追她，而我可以呆在家里和本一起玩。

paragraphs.en: I went in and got a couple of cigars. Then I thought I’d have another headache shot for luck, and I stood and talked with them awhile.
paragraphs.zh: 我进去拿了几支雪茄。然后我想我可能会再头痛一次，于是我站起来和他们聊了一会儿。

paragraphs.en: “Well,” Mac says, “I reckon you’ve got your money on the Yankees this year.”
paragraphs.zh: “好吧，”麦克说，“我想你今年已经在洋基队身上赚到了钱。”

paragraphs.en: “What for?” I says.
paragraphs.zh: “干什么？”我说。

paragraphs.en: “The Pennant,” he says. “Not anything in the League can beat them.”
paragraphs.zh: “三角旗，”他说。“联盟中没有任何球队可以击败他们。”

paragraphs.en: “Like hell there’s not,” I says. “They’re shot,” I says. “You think a team can be that lucky forever?”
paragraphs.zh: “根本就没有，”我说。“他们被枪杀了，”我说。“你认为一支球队可以永远这么幸运吗？”

paragraphs.en: “I dont call it luck,” Mac says.
paragraphs.zh: “我不称之为运气，”麦克说。

paragraphs.en: “I wouldn’t bet on any team that fellow Ruth played on,” I says. “Even if I knew it was going to win.”
paragraphs.zh: “我不会在露丝同伴效力的任何球队上打赌，”我说。“即使我知道它会赢。”

paragraphs.en: “Yes?” Mac says.
paragraphs.zh: “是吗？”麦克说。

paragraphs.en: “I can name you a dozen men in either League who’re more valuable than he is,” I says.
paragraphs.zh: “我可以给你说出两个联盟中比他更有价值的十几个人的名字，”我说。

paragraphs.en: “What have you got against Ruth?” Mac says.
paragraphs.zh: “你跟露丝有什么仇？”麦克说。

paragraphs.en: “Nothing,” I says. “I haven’t got any thing against him. I dont even like to look at his picture.” I went on out.
