The lights were coming on, and people going along the streets toward home. Sometimes the sparrows never got still until full dark. The night they turned on the new lights around the courthouse it waked them up and they were flying around and blundering into the lights all night long. They kept it up two or three nights, then one morning they were all gone. Then after about two months they all came back again.
paragraphs.zh: “没什么，”我说。“我对他没有任何怨言。我什至不喜欢看他的照片。”我继续往外走。灯亮了，人们沿着街道朝家走去。有时，麻雀直到天黑才安静下来。那天晚上，他们打开法院周围的新灯，这把他们吵醒了，他们整夜都在飞来飞去，跌跌撞撞地撞进灯光里。他们持续了两三个晚上，然后有一天早上他们都走了。大约两个月后，他们又全部回来了。

paragraphs.en: I drove on home. There were no lights in the house yet, but they’d all be looking out the windows, and Dilsey jawing away in the kitchen like it was her own food she was having to keep hot until I got there. You’d think to hear her that there wasn’t but one supper in the world, and that was the one she had to keep back a few minutes on my account. Well at least I could come home one time without finding Ben and that nigger hanging on the gate like a bear and a monkey in the same cage. Just let it come toward sundown and he’d head for the gate like a cow for the barn, hanging onto it and bobbing his head and sort of moaning to himself. That’s a hog for punishment for you. If what had happened to him for fooling with open gates had happened to me, I never would want to see another one. I often wondered what he’d be thinking about, down there at the gate, watching the girls going home from school, trying to want something he couldn’t even remember he didn’t and couldn’t want any longer. And what he’d think when they’d be undressing him and he’d happen to take a look at himself and begin to cry like he’d do. But like I say they never did enough of that. I says I know what you need, you need what they did to Ben then you’d behave. And if you dont know what that was I says, ask Dilsey to tell you.
paragraphs.zh: 我开车回家。房子里还没有开灯，但他们都会看着窗外，迪尔西在厨房里喋喋不休，好像这是她自己的食物，她必须保持热度，直到我到达那里。你可能会认为，听她说，世界上只有一顿晚餐，而她却因为我的原因而不得不推迟几分钟。好吧，至少我可以回家一次，而不会发现本和那个黑鬼像一只熊和一只猴子关在同一个笼子里一样挂在大门上。只要让它在日落时分到来，他就会像一头牛走向谷仓一样走向大门，抓住大门，摇摇头，自言自语。那是对你的惩罚。如果他愚弄敞开的大门所发生的事情发生在我身上，我就再也不想看到另一扇门了。我经常想知道，在大门口，看着女孩们放学回家，他会在想什么，试图想要一些他甚至不记得他不想要也不再想要的东西。当他们给他脱衣服时，他碰巧看了一眼自己，然后像他一样开始哭泣，他会怎么想。但就像我说的，他们在这方面做得还不够。我说我知道你需要什么，你需要他们对本所做的事情，然后你就会表现得很好。如果你不知道我说的是什么，请让迪尔西告诉你。

paragraphs.en: There was a light in Mother’s room. I put the car up and went on into the kitchen. Luster and Ben were there.
paragraphs.zh: 母亲的房间里亮着灯。我把车停好，走进厨房。勒斯特和本也在场。

paragraphs.en: “Where’s Dilsey?” I says. “Putting supper on?”
paragraphs.zh: “迪尔西在哪儿？”我说。“准备晚饭了吗？”

paragraphs.en: “She upstairs wid Miss Cahline,” Luster says. “Dey been goin hit. Ever since Miss Quentin come home. Mammy up there keepin um fum fightin. Is dat show come, Mr Jason?”
paragraphs.zh: “她和卡琳小姐在楼上，”勒斯特说。“他们被打了。自从昆丁小姐回家后，妈妈就一直在吵架。杰生先生，演出来了吗？”

paragraphs.en: “Yes,” I says.
paragraphs.zh: “是的，”我说。

paragraphs.en: “I thought I heard de band,” he says. “Wish I could go,” he says. “I could ef I jes had a quarter.”
paragraphs.zh: “我以为我听到了乐队的声音，”他说。“希望我能去，”他说。“只要我有 25 美分，我就可以了。”

paragraphs.en: Dilsey came in. “You come, is you?” she says. “Whut you been up to dis evenin? You knows how much work I got to do; whyn’t you git here on time?”
paragraphs.zh: 迪尔西进来了。“你来了，是吗？”她说。“你今天晚上都在忙什么？你知道我要做多少工作；你为什么不准时到这里呢？”

paragraphs.en: “Maybe I went to the show,” I says. “Is supper ready?”
paragraphs.zh: “也许我去看了演出，”我说。“晚饭准备好了吗？”

paragraphs.en: “Wish I could go,” Luster said. “I could ef I jes had a quarter.”
paragraphs.zh: “希望我能去，”勒斯特说。“只要我有 25 美分，我就可以了。”

paragraphs.en: “You aint got no business at no show,” Dilsey says. “You go on in de house and set down,” she says. “Dont you go up stairs and git um started again, now.”
paragraphs.zh: “不演出你就没有生意，”迪尔西说。“你继续在屋子里走，然后坐下来，”她说。“你现在不要上楼然后重新开始。”

paragraphs.en: “What’s the matter?” I says.
paragraphs.zh: “怎么了？”我说。

paragraphs.en: “Quentin come in a while ago and says you been follerin her around all evenin and den Miss Cahline jumped on her. Whyn’t you let her alone? Cant you live in de same house wid you own blood niece widout quoilin?”
paragraphs.zh: “昆丁不久前进来，说你整个晚上都跟着她，卡林小姐就扑到了她身上。你为什么不让她一个人呆着？你就不能和你的亲生侄女住在同一栋房子里，没有奎林吗？”

paragraphs.en: “I cant quarrel with her,” I says, “because I haven’t seen her since this morning. What does she say I’ve done now? made her go to school? That’s pretty bad,” I says.
paragraphs.zh: “我不能和她吵架，”我说，“因为从今天早上起我就没见过她。她说我现在做了什么？让她去上学？那太糟糕了，”我说。

paragraphs.en: “Well, you tend to yo business and let her alone,” Dilsey says, “I’ll take keer of her ef you’n Miss Cahline’ll let me. Go on in dar now and behave yoself twell I get supper on.”
paragraphs.zh: “好吧，你管好自己的事，别打扰她，”迪尔西说，“如果你和卡林小姐不让我的话，我会照顾她的。现在就去达尔吧，在我吃晚饭之前表现得很好。”

paragraphs.en: “Ef I jes had a quarter,” Luster says, “I could go to dat show.”
paragraphs.zh: “如果我有 25 美分，”勒斯特说，“我就可以去看那个演出。”

paragraphs.en: “En ef you had wings you could fly to heaven,” Dilsey says. “I dont want to hear another word about dat show.”
paragraphs.zh: “如果你有翅膀，你就可以飞向天堂，”迪尔西说。“我不想再听到有关该节目的任何消息。”

paragraphs.en: “That reminds me,” I says, “I’ve got a couple of tickets they gave me.” I took them out of my coat.
paragraphs.zh: “这让我想起了，”我说，“我有几张他们给我的票。”我把它们从外套里拿出来。

paragraphs.en: “You fixin to use um?” Luster says.
paragraphs.zh: “你决定使用嗯吗？”勒斯特说。

paragraphs.en: “Not me,” I says. “I wouldn’t go to it for ten dollars.”
paragraphs.zh: “不是我，”我说。“我不会为了十美元就去那里。”

paragraphs.en: “Gimme one of um, Mr Jason,” he says.
paragraphs.zh: “杰生先生，给我一份，”他说。

paragraphs.en: “I’ll sell you one,” I says. “How about it?”
paragraphs.zh: “我卖给你一个，”我说。“怎么样？”

paragraphs.en: “I aint got no money,” he says.
paragraphs.zh: “我没有钱，”他说。

paragraphs.en: “That’s too bad,” I says. I made to go out.
paragraphs.zh: “那太糟糕了，”我说。我决定出去。

paragraphs.en: “Gimme one of um, Mr Jason,” he says. “You aint gwine need um bofe.”
paragraphs.zh: “杰生先生，给我一份，”他说。“你不需要恩哥。”

paragraphs.en: “Hush yo mouf,” Dilsey says, “Dont you know he aint gwine give nothing away?”
paragraphs.zh: “嘘，穆夫，”迪尔西说，“你不知道他不会透露任何信息吗？”

paragraphs.en: “How much you want fer hit?” he says.
paragraphs.zh: “你想要多少命中率？”他说。

paragraphs.en: “Five cents,” I says.
paragraphs.zh: “五美分，”我说。

paragraphs.en: “I aint got dat much,” he says.
paragraphs.zh: “我知道的不多，”他说。

paragraphs.en: “How much you got?” I says.
paragraphs.zh: “你有多少钱？”我说。

paragraphs.en: “I aint got nothing,” he says.
paragraphs.zh: “我什么也没得到，”他说。

paragraphs.en: “All right,” I says. I went on.
paragraphs.zh: “好吧，”我说。我继续说下去。

paragraphs.en: “Mr Jason,” he says.
paragraphs.zh: “杰生先生，”他说。

paragraphs.en: “Whyn’t you hush up?” Dilsey says. “He jes teasin you. He fixin to use dem tickets hisself. Go on, Jason, and let him lone.”
paragraphs.zh: “你为什么不小声点？”迪尔西说道。“他是在逗你。他自己想用这些票。继续吧，杰生，别打扰他了。”

paragraphs.en: “I dont want them,” I says. I came back to the stove. “I came in here to burn them up. But if you want to buy one for a nickel?” I says, looking at him and opening the stove lid.
paragraphs.zh: “我不想要它们，”我说。我又回到了炉子边。“我来这里是为了烧掉它们。但是你想花五分钱买一个吗？”我一边说，一边看着他，打开炉盖。

paragraphs.en: “I aint got dat much,” he says.
paragraphs.zh: “我知道的不多，”他说。

paragraphs.en: “All right,” I says. I dropped one of them in the stove.
paragraphs.zh: “好吧，”我说。我把其中一个掉进了炉子里。

paragraphs.en: “You, Jason,” Dilsey says, “Aint you shamed?”
paragraphs.zh: “你，杰生，”迪尔西说，“你不感到羞耻吗？”

paragraphs.en: “Mr Jason,” he says, “Please, suh. I’ll fix dem tires ev’ry day fer a mont’.”
paragraphs.zh: “杰生先生，”他说，“拜托了，先生。我会在一个月内每天修理他们的轮胎。”

paragraphs.en: “I need the cash,” I says. “You can have it for a nickel.”
paragraphs.zh: “我需要现金，”我说。“你花五分钱就可以得到它。”

paragraphs.en: “Hush, Luster,” Dilsey says. She jerked him back. “Go on,” she says, “Drop hit in. Go on. Git hit over with.”
paragraphs.zh: “嘘，勒斯特，”迪尔西说。她猛地把他拉了回来。“继续，”她说，“插话。继续。Git 结束了。”

paragraphs.en: “You can have it for a nickel,” I says.
paragraphs.zh: “你花五分钱就可以得到它，”我说。

paragraphs.en: “Go on,” Dilsey says. “He aint got no nickel. Go on. Drop hit in.”
paragraphs.zh: “继续，”迪尔西说。“他连五分钱都没有。继续吧。快点进来吧。”

paragraphs.en: “All right,” I says. I dropped it in and Dilsey shut the stove.
paragraphs.zh: “好吧，”我说。我把它放进去，迪尔西关上了炉子。

paragraphs.en: “A big growed man like you,” she says. “Git on outen my kitchen. Hush,” she says to Luster. “Dont you git Benjy started. I’ll git you a quarter fum Frony tonight and you kin go tomorrow night. Hush up, now.”
paragraphs.zh: “像你这样的大男人，”她说。“出去我的厨房。嘘，”她对勒斯特说。“你别开始班吉了。今晚我会给你四分之一的弗罗妮，你明天晚上就可以走了。现在安静点。”

paragraphs.en: I went on into the living room. I couldn’t hear anything from upstairs. I opened the paper. After awhile Ben and Luster came in. Ben went to the dark place on the wall where the mirror used to be, rubbing his hands on it and slobbering and moaning. Luster begun punching at the fire.
paragraphs.zh: 我继续走进客厅。我听不到楼上有任何声音。我打开纸。过了一会儿，本和勒斯特进来了。本走到墙上原来放镜子的那个黑暗地方，用手擦着镜子，流着口水，呻吟着。勒斯特开始扑灭火。

paragraphs.en: “What’re you doing?” I says. “We dont need any fire tonight.”
paragraphs.zh: “你在做什么？”我说。“今晚我们不需要生火。”

paragraphs.en: “I trying to keep him quiet,” he says. “Hit always cold Easter,” he says.
paragraphs.zh: “我试图让他保持安静，”他说。“复活节总是很冷，”他说。

paragraphs.en: “Only this is not Easter,” I says. “Let it alone.”
paragraphs.zh: “只不过这不是复活节，”我说。“别管它了。”

paragraphs.en: He put the poker back and got the cushion out of Mother’s chair and gave it to Ben, and he hunkered down in front of the fireplace and got quiet.
paragraphs.zh: 他把拨火棍放回原处，从母亲的椅子上拿出垫子，递给本，然后他在壁炉前蹲下来，安静下来。

paragraphs.en: I read the paper. There hadn’t been a sound from upstairs when Dilsey came in and sent Ben and Luster on to the kitchen and said supper was ready.
paragraphs.zh: 我读了报纸。当迪尔西进来并把本和勒斯特送到厨房并说晚饭准备好了时，楼上没有发出任何声音。

paragraphs.en: “All right,” I says. She went out. I sat there, reading the paper. After a while I heard Dilsey looking in at the door.
paragraphs.zh: “好吧，”我说。她出去了。我坐在那里，读着报纸。过了一会儿，我听见迪尔西向门口张望。

paragraphs.en: “Whyn’t you come on and eat?” she says.
paragraphs.zh: “你怎么不过来吃饭？”她说。

paragraphs.en: “I’m waiting for supper,” I says.
paragraphs.zh: “我在等晚饭。”我说。

paragraphs.en: “Hit’s on the table,” she says. “I done told you.”
paragraphs.zh: “一切都在桌面上，”她说。“我已经告诉过你了。”

paragraphs.en: “Is it?” I says. “Excuse me. I didn’t hear anybody come down.”
paragraphs.zh: “是吗？”我说。“对不起。我没有听到有人下来。”

paragraphs.en: “They aint comin,” she says. “You come on and eat, so I can take something up to them.”
paragraphs.zh: “他们不会来，”她说。“你过来吃点东西吧，我去给他们带点东西。”

paragraphs.en: “Are they sick?” I says. “What did the doctor say it was? Not Smallpox, I hope.”
paragraphs.zh: “他们生病了吗？”我说。“医生说那是什么？我希望不是天花。”

paragraphs.en: “Come on here, Jason,” she says, “So I kin git done.”
paragraphs.zh: “杰生，过来吧，”她说，“这样我就可以完成任务了。”

paragraphs.en: “All right,” I says, raising the paper again. “I’m waiting for supper now.”
paragraphs.zh: “好吧，”我说，再次举起报纸。“我现在正在等晚饭。”

paragraphs.en: I could feel her watching me at the door. I read the paper.
paragraphs.zh: 我能感觉到她在门口看着我。我读了报纸。

paragraphs.en: “Whut you want to act like this fer?” she says. “When you knows how much bother I has anyway.”
paragraphs.zh: “你为什么要表现得像这样？”她说。“当你知道我有多么麻烦的时候。”

paragraphs.en: “If Mother is any sicker than she was when she came down to dinner, all right,” I says. “But as long as I am buying food for people younger than I am, they’ll have to come down to the table to eat it. Let me know when supper’s ready,” I says, reading the paper again. I heard her climbing the stairs, dragging her feet and grunting and groaning like they were straight up and three feet apart. I heard her at Mother’s door, then I heard her calling Quentin, like the door was locked, then she went back to Mother’s room and then Mother went and talked to Quentin. Then they came down stairs. I read the paper.
paragraphs.zh: “如果母亲的病情比她下楼吃晚饭时更严重的话，那好吧，”我说。“但只要我为比我年轻的人买食物，他们就必须到餐桌上吃。晚饭准备好时请告诉我，”我一边说，一边再次读着报纸。我听见她爬上楼梯，拖着脚步，咕哝着，呻吟着，就好像他们笔直地站着，相距三英尺。我听到她在妈妈门口，然后我听到她叫昆丁，就像门锁着一样，然后她回到妈妈的房间，然后妈妈就去和昆丁说话。然后他们下了楼梯。我读了报纸。

paragraphs.en: Dilsey came back to the door. “Come on,” she says, “fo you kin think up some mo devilment. You just tryin yoself tonight.”
paragraphs.zh: 迪尔西回到门口。“来吧，”她说，“你可以想出一些恶作剧。今晚你自己试试吧。”

paragraphs.en: I went to the diningroom. Quentin was sitting with her head bent. She had painted her face again. Her nose looked like a porcelain insulator.
paragraphs.zh: 我去了餐厅。昆丁低着头坐着。她又重新画了脸。她的鼻子看起来就像一个瓷绝缘体。

paragraphs.en: “I’m glad you feel well enough to come down,” I says to Mother.
paragraphs.zh: “我很高兴你感觉好起来了，”我对母亲说。

paragraphs.en: “It’s little enough I can do for you, to come to the table,” she says. “No matter how I feel. I realise that when a man works all day he likes to be surrounded by his family at the supper table. I want to please you. I only wish you and Quentin got along better. It would be easier for me.”
paragraphs.zh: “我能为你做的还不够，只能坐到谈判桌前，”她说。“不管我的感受如何。我知道，当一个男人工作了一整天时，他喜欢在晚饭桌上被家人围着。我想让你高兴。我只希望你和昆丁相处得更好。这对我来说会更容易。”

paragraphs.en: “We get along all right,” I says. “I dont mind her staying locked up in her room all day if she wants to. But I cant have all this whoop-de-do and sulking at mealtimes. I know that’s a lot to ask her, but I’m that way in my own house. Your house, I meant to say.”
paragraphs.zh: “我们相处得很好，”我说。“如果她愿意的话，我不介意她整天把自己锁在房间里。但我不能让她在吃饭的时候大喊大叫、生闷气。我知道要问她很多，但我在自己家里就是这样。我想说的是，你的房子。”

paragraphs.en: “It’s yours,” Mother says, “You are the head of it now.”
paragraphs.zh: “它是你的了，”母亲说，“你现在是它的负责人了。”

paragraphs.en: Quentin hadn’t looked up. I helped the plates and she begun to eat.
paragraphs.zh: 昆丁没有抬头。我帮她收拾盘子，她开始吃饭。

paragraphs.en: “Did you get a good piece of meat?” I says. “If you didn’t, I’ll try to find you a better one.”
paragraphs.zh: “你吃到一块好肉了吗？”我说。“如果你没有，我会尽力为你找到一个更好的。”

paragraphs.en: She didn’t say anything.
paragraphs.zh: 她什么也没说。

paragraphs.en: “I say, did you get a good piece of meat?” I says.
paragraphs.zh: “我说，你有块好肉吗？”我说。

paragraphs.en: “What?” she says. “Yes. It’s all right.”
paragraphs.zh: “什么？”她说。“是的。没关系。”

paragraphs.en: “Will you have some more rice?” I says.
paragraphs.zh: “还要再吃点米饭吗？”我说。

paragraphs.en: “No,” she says.
paragraphs.zh: “不，”她说。

paragraphs.en: “Better let me give you some more,” I says.
paragraphs.zh: “最好让我再给你一些，”我说。

paragraphs.en: “I dont want any more,” she says.
paragraphs.zh: “我不再想要了，”她说。

paragraphs.en: “Not at all,” I says, “You’re welcome.”
paragraphs.zh: “一点也不，”我说，“不客气。”

paragraphs.en: “Is your headache gone?” Mother says.
paragraphs.zh: “你的头痛消失了吗？”妈妈说。

paragraphs.en: “Headache?” I says.
paragraphs.zh: “头痛？”我说。

paragraphs.en: “I was afraid you were developing one,” she says. “When you came in this afternoon.”
paragraphs.zh: “我担心你正在开发一款，”她说。“今天下午你进来的时候。”

paragraphs.en: “Oh,” I says. “No, it didn’t show up. We stayed so busy this afternoon I forgot about it.”
paragraphs.zh: “哦，”我说。“没有，没有出现。今天下午我们太忙了，我都忘了这件事了。”

paragraphs.en: “Was that why you were late?” Mother says. I could see Quentin listening. I looked at her. Her knife and fork were still going, but I caught her looking at me, then she looked at her plate again. I says,
paragraphs.zh: “这就是你迟到的原因吗？”妈妈说。我可以看到昆丁在听。我看着她。她的刀叉还在继续，但我发现她在看着我，然后她又看了看她的盘子。我说，

paragraphs.en: “No. I loaned my car to a fellow about three o’clock and I had to wait until he got back with it.” I ate for a while.
paragraphs.zh: “没有。三点左右我把车借给了一个人，我得等他回来才行。”我吃了一会儿。

paragraphs.en: “Who was it?” Mother says.
paragraphs.zh: “是谁？”妈妈说。

paragraphs.en: “It was one of those show men,” I says. “It seems his sister’s husband was out riding with some town woman, and he was chasing them.”
paragraphs.zh: “这是那些表演者之一，”我说。“看来他姐姐的丈夫和镇上的某个女人一起出去骑马，他正在追他们。”

paragraphs.en: Quentin sat perfectly still, chewing.
paragraphs.zh: 昆丁一动不动地坐着，咀嚼着。

paragraphs.en: “You ought not to lend your car to people like that,” Mother says. “You are too generous with it. That’s why I never call on you for it if I can help it.”
paragraphs.zh: “你不应该把你的车借给这样的人，”母亲说。“你太慷慨了。所以，如果我能帮忙的话，我从来不会找你帮忙。”

paragraphs.en: “I was beginning to think that myself, for awhile,” I says. “But he got back, all right. He says he found what he was looking for.”
paragraphs.zh: “有一段时间我自己也开始这么想，”我说。“但是他回来了，好吧。他说他找到了他要找的东西。”

paragraphs.en: “Who was the woman?” Mother says.
paragraphs.zh: “那个女人是谁？”妈妈说。

paragraphs.en: “I’ll tell you later,” I says. “I dont like to talk about such things before Quentin.”
paragraphs.zh: “我稍后告诉你，”我说。“我不喜欢在昆丁之前谈论这些事情。”

paragraphs.en: Quentin had quit eating. Every once in a while she’d take a drink of water, then she’d sit there crumbling a biscuit up, her face bent over her plate.
paragraphs.zh: 昆丁已经不吃东西了。每隔一段时间，她就会喝一杯水，然后坐在那里，把一块饼干弄碎，脸埋在盘子上。

paragraphs.en: “Yes,” Mother says, “I suppose women who stay shut up like I do have no idea what goes on in this town.”
paragraphs.zh: “是的，”母亲说，“我想像我一样闭嘴的女人根本不知道这个镇上发生了什么。”

paragraphs.en: “Yes,” I says, “They dont.”
paragraphs.zh: “是的，”我说，“他们不知道。”

paragraphs.en: “My life has been so different from that,” Mother says. “Thank God I dont know about such wickedness. I dont even want to know about it. I’m not like most people.”
paragraphs.zh: “我的生活与那时大不相同，”母亲说。“感谢上帝，我不知道有这样的邪恶。我什至不想知道。我不像大多数人。”

paragraphs.en: I didn’t say any more. Quentin sat there, crumbling the biscuit until I quit eating, then she says,
paragraphs.zh: 我没有再说什么。昆丁坐在那里，把饼干弄碎，直到我不吃为止，然后她说：

paragraphs.en: “Can I go now?” without looking at anybody.
paragraphs.zh: “我现在可以走了吗？”不看任何人。

paragraphs.en: “What?” I says. “Sure, you can go. Were you waiting on us?”
paragraphs.zh: “什么？”我说。“当然，你可以走了。你在等我们吗？”

paragraphs.en: She looked at me. She had crumbled all the biscuit, but her hands still went on like they were crumbling it yet and her eyes looked like they were cornered or something and then she started biting her mouth like it ought to have poisoned her, with all that red lead.
paragraphs.zh: 她看着我。她已经把所有的饼干都弄碎了，但她的手仍然继续，好像还在弄碎它，她的眼睛看起来像是陷入了角落或什么的，然后她开始咬自己的嘴，就像它应该毒死她一样，所有的红铅。

paragraphs.en: “Grandmother,” she says, “Grandmother—”
paragraphs.zh: “祖母，”她说，“祖母——”

paragraphs.en: “Did you want something else to eat?” I says.
paragraphs.zh: “你还想吃点别的吗？”我说。

paragraphs.en: “Why does he treat me like this, Grandmother?” she says. “I never hurt him.”
paragraphs.zh: “奶奶，他为什么这样对我？”她说。“我从来没有伤害过他。”

paragraphs.en: “I want you all to get along with one another,” Mother says, “You are all that’s left now, and I do want you all to get along better.”
paragraphs.zh: “我希望你们都能和睦相处，”母亲说，“现在只剩下你们了，我确实希望你们能相处得更好。”

paragraphs.en: “It’s his fault,” she says, “He wont let me alone, and I have to. If he doesn’t want me here, why wont he let me go back to—”
paragraphs.zh: “这是他的错，”她说，“他不让我孤单，而我必须这样做。如果他不想让我在这里，为什么他不让我回去——”

paragraphs.en: “That’s enough,” I says, “Not another word.”
paragraphs.zh: “够了，”我说，“不用再说了。”

paragraphs.en: “Then why wont he let me alone?” she says. “He—he just—”
paragraphs.zh: “那他为什么不放过我呢？”她说。“他——他只是——”

paragraphs.en: “He is the nearest thing to a father you’ve ever had,” Mother says. “It’s his bread you and I eat. It’s only right that he should expect obedience from you.”
paragraphs.zh: “他是你所拥有的最接近父亲的人，”母亲说。“你我吃的是他的面包。他理应期望你服从，这是理所当然的。”

paragraphs.en: “It’s his fault,” she says. She jumped up. “He makes me do it. If he would just—” she looked at us, her eyes cornered, kind of jerking her arms against her sides.
paragraphs.zh: “这是他的错，”她说。她跳了起来。“他让我这么做。如果他愿意——”她看着我们，眼睛眯了起来，双臂猛地靠在身体两侧。

paragraphs.en: “If I would just what?” I says.
paragraphs.zh: “如果我愿意呢？”我说。

paragraphs.en: “Whatever I do, it’s your fault,” she says. “If I’m bad, it’s because I had to be. You made me. I wish I was dead. I wish we were all dead.” Then she ran. We heard her run up the stairs. Then a door slammed.
paragraphs.zh: “无论我做什么，都是你的错，”她说。“如果我很糟糕，那是因为我不得不如此。是你创造了我。我希望我死了。我希望我们都死了。”然后她跑了。我们听到她跑上楼梯的声音。然后一扇门砰地关上。

paragraphs.en: “That’s the first sensible thing she ever said,” I says.
paragraphs.zh: “这是她说的第一句话，”我说。

paragraphs.en: “She didn’t go to school today,” Mother says.
paragraphs.zh: “她今天没有去上学，”妈妈说。

paragraphs.en: “How do you know?” I says. “Were you down town?”
paragraphs.zh: “你怎么知道？”我说。“你在城里吗？”

paragraphs.en: “I just know,” she says. “I wish you could be kinder to her.”
paragraphs.zh: “我只知道，”她说。“我希望你能对她好一点。”

paragraphs.en: “If I did that I’d have to arrange to see her more than once a day,” I says. “You’ll have to make her come to the table every meal. Then I could give her an extra piece of meat every time.”
paragraphs.zh: “如果我这样做，我就必须安排每天不止一次见到她，”我说。“每顿饭你都得让她到餐桌上来，这样我每次都可以多给她一块肉。”

paragraphs.en: “There are little things you could do,” she says.
paragraphs.zh: “你可以做一些小事情，”她说。

paragraphs.en: “Like not paying any attention when you ask me to see that she goes to school?” I says.
paragraphs.zh: “就像你让我看看她上学时没有注意一样吗？”我说。

paragraphs.en: “She didn’t go to school today,” she says. “I just know she didn’t. She says she went for a car ride with one of the boys this afternoon and you followed her.”
paragraphs.zh: “她今天没有去上学，”她说。“我只知道她没有。她说今天下午她和一个男孩一起去兜风，而你却跟着她。”

paragraphs.en: “How could I,” I says, “When somebody had my car all afternoon? Whether or not she was in school today is already past,” I says, “If you’ve got to worry about it, worry about next Monday.”
paragraphs.zh: “我怎么可能，”我说，“当有人整个下午都拿走我的车时？她今天是否上学都已经过去了，”我说，“如果你必须担心它，那就担心下周一吧。”

paragraphs.en: “I wanted you and she to get along with one another,” she says. “But she has inherited all of the headstrong traits. Quentin’s too. I thought at the time, with the heritage she would already have, to give her that name, too. Sometimes I think she is the judgment of Caddy and Quentin upon me.”
paragraphs.zh: “我希望你和她和睦相处，”她说。“但她继承了所有任性的特质。昆丁也是如此。我当时想，凭借她已经拥有的遗产，也给她起这个名字。有时我认为她是凯蒂和昆丁对我的判断。”

paragraphs.en: “Good Lord,” I says, “You’ve got a fine mind. No wonder you kept yourself sick all the time.”
paragraphs.zh: “上帝啊，”我说，“你的头脑很好。难怪你总是生病。”

paragraphs.en: “What?” she says. “I dont understand.”
paragraphs.zh: “什么？”她说。“我不明白。”

paragraphs.en: “I hope not,” I says. “A good woman misses a lot she’s better off without knowing.”
paragraphs.zh: “我希望不会，”我说。“一个好女人会错过很多她不知道的事情。”

paragraphs.en: “They were both that way,” she says, “They would make interest with your father against me when I tried to correct them. He was always saying they didn’t need controlling, that they already knew what cleanliness and honesty were, which was all that anyone could hope to be taught. And now I hope he’s satisfied.”
paragraphs.zh: “他们都是这样的，”她说，“当我试图纠正他们时，他们就会对你的父亲感兴趣。他总是说他们不需要控制，他们已经知道什么是清洁和诚实，这是任何人都希望被教导的。现在我希望他满意。”

paragraphs.en: “You’ve got Ben to depend on,” I says, “Cheer up.”
paragraphs.zh: “你有本可以依靠，”我说，“振作起来。”

paragraphs.en: “They deliberately shut me out of their lives,” she says, “It was always her and Quentin. They were always conspiring against me. Against you too, though you were too young to realise it. They always looked on you and me as outsiders, like they did your Uncle Maury. I always told your father that they were allowed too much freedom, to be together too much. When Quentin started to school we had to let her go the next year, so she could be with him. She couldn’t bear for any of you to do anything she couldn’t. It was vanity in her, vanity and false pride. And then when her troubles began I knew that Quentin would feel that he had to do something just as bad. But I didn’t believe that he would have been so selfish as to—I didn’t dream that he—”
paragraphs.zh: “他们故意把我排除在他们的生活之外，”她说，“总是她和昆丁。他们总是密谋反对我。也反对你，尽管你还太小，还没有意识到这一点。他们总是把你和我视为局外人，就像他们对待你莫里舅舅一样。我总是告诉你父亲，他们被允许太多自由，在一起太多了。昆丁开始上学的时候，我们必须让她第二年离开，这样她才能和他在一起。她无法忍受任何事情。”她做不到的事情都是虚荣心，虚荣心和虚假的骄傲，然后当她遇到麻烦时，我知道昆丁会觉得他必须做一些同样糟糕的事情，但我不相信他会如此自私——我做梦也没想到他——”

paragraphs.en: “Maybe he knew it was going to be a girl,” I says, “And that one more of them would be more than he could stand.”
paragraphs.zh: “也许他知道那将是一个女孩，”我说，“而且如果再多一个女孩，他就无法忍受了。”

paragraphs.en: “He could have controlled her,” she says. “He seemed to be the only person she had any consideration for. But that is a part of the judgment too, I suppose.”
paragraphs.zh: “他本可以控制她，”她说。“他似乎是她唯一考虑的人。但我想这也是判断的一部分。”

paragraphs.en: “Yes,” I says, “Too bad it wasn’t me instead of him. You’d be a lot better off.”
paragraphs.zh: “是的，”我说，“可惜不是我，而是他。你会过得更好。”

paragraphs.en: “You say things like that to hurt me,” she says. “I deserve it though. When they began to sell the land to send Quentin to Harvard I told your father that he must make an equal provision for you. Then when Herbert offered to take you into the bank I said, Jason is provided for now, and when all the expense began to pile up and I was forced to sell our furniture and the rest of the pasture, I wrote her at once because I said she will realise that she and Quentin have had their share and part of Jason’s too and that it depends on her now to compensate him. I said she will do that out of respect for her father. I believed that, then. But I’m just a poor old woman; I was raised to believe that people would deny themselves for their own flesh and blood. It’s my fault. You were right to reproach me.”
paragraphs.zh: “你说这样的话是为了伤害我，”她说。“不过这是我应得的。当他们开始卖掉土地送昆丁去哈佛时，我告诉你父亲，他必须为你提供同等的生活保障。然后，当赫伯特提出带你去银行时，我说，杰生现在已经有了，当所有的费用开始堆积起来，我被迫卖掉我们的家具和剩下的牧场时，我立即写信给她，因为我说她会意识到，她和昆丁也得到了杰生的份额和一部分，这取决于我说她会这样做是出于对她父亲的尊重，但我只是一个可怜的老妇人；我从小就相信人们会为了自己的血肉而否定自己，你责备我是对的。

paragraphs.en: “Do you think I need any man’s help to stand on my feet?” I says, “Let alone a woman that cant name the father of her own child.”
paragraphs.zh: “你认为我需要任何人的帮助才能站起来吗？”我说：“更不用说一个连自己孩子的父亲都叫不出名字的女人了。”

paragraphs.en: “Jason,” she says.
paragraphs.zh: “杰生，”她说。

paragraphs.en: “All right,” I says. “I didn’t mean that. Of course not.”
paragraphs.zh: “好吧，”我说。“我不是那个意思。当然不是。”

paragraphs.en: “If I believed that were possible, after all my suffering.”
paragraphs.zh: “如果我相信这是可能的，在经历了所有的痛苦之后。”

paragraphs.en: “Of course it’s not,” I says. “I didn’t mean it.”
paragraphs.zh: “当然不是，”我说。“我不是故意的。”

paragraphs.en: “I hope that at least is spared me,” she says.
paragraphs.zh: “我希望至少我能幸免，”她说。

paragraphs.en: “Sure it is,” I says, “She’s too much like both of them to doubt that.”
paragraphs.zh: “当然是这样，”我说，“她太像他们了，所以不会怀疑这一点。”

paragraphs.en: “I couldn’t bear that,” she says.
paragraphs.zh: “我无法忍受，”她说。

paragraphs.en: “Then quit thinking about it,” I says. “Has she been worrying you any more about getting out at night?”
paragraphs.zh: “那就别再想了，”我说。“她还担心你晚上出去吗？”

paragraphs.en: “No. I made her realise that it was for her own good and that she’d thank me for it some day. She takes her books with her and studies after I lock the door. I see the light on as late as eleven oclock some nights.”
paragraphs.zh: “不。我让她意识到这是为了她好，有一天她会为此感谢我。我锁上门后，她就带着书本开始学习。有些晚上我看到灯亮到十一点。”

paragraphs.en: “How do you know she’s studying?” I says.
paragraphs.zh: “你怎么知道她在学习？”我说。

paragraphs.en: “I don’t know what else she’d do in there alone,” she says. “She never did read any.”
paragraphs.zh: “我不知道她一个人在那里还能做什么，”她说。“她从来没有读过任何书。”

paragraphs.en: “No,” I says, “You wouldn’t know. And you can thank your stars for that,” I says. Only what would be the use in saying it aloud. It would just have her crying on me again.
paragraphs.zh: “不，”我说，“你不会知道。你可以为此感谢你的明星，”我说。只是大声说出来有什么用呢。这只会让她再次向我哭泣。

paragraphs.en: I heard her go up stairs. Then she called Quentin and Quentin says What? through the door. “Goodnight,” Mother says. Then I heard the key in the lock, and Mother went back to her room.
paragraphs.zh: 我听到她上楼梯的声音。然后她打电话给昆丁，昆丁说什么？穿过门。“晚安，”妈妈说。然后我听到钥匙插锁的声音，母亲就回到了她的房间。

paragraphs.en: When I finished my cigar and went up, the light was still on. I could see the empty keyhole, but I couldn’t hear a sound. She studied quiet. Maybe she learned that in school. I told Mother goodnight and went on to my room and got the box out and counted it again. I could hear the Great American Gelding snoring away like a planing mill. I read somewhere they’d fix men that way to give them women’s voices. But maybe he didn’t know what they’d done to him. I dont reckon he even knew what he had been trying to do, or why Mr Burgess knocked him out with the fence picket. And if they’d just sent him on to Jackson while he was under the ether, he’d never have known the difference. But that would have been too simple for a Compson to think of. Not half complex enough. Having to wait to do it at all until he broke out and tried to run a little girl down on the street with her own father looking at him. Well, like I say they never started soon enough with their cutting, and they quit too quick. I know at least two more that needed something like that, and one of them not over a mile away, either. But then I dont reckon even that would do any good. Like I say once a bitch always a bitch. And just let me have twenty-four hours without any damn New York jew to advise me what it’s going to do. I dont want to make a killing; save that to suck in the smart gamblers with. I just want an even chance to get my money back. And once I’ve done that they can bring all Beale Street and all bedlam in here and two of them can sleep in my bed and another one can have my place at the table too.
paragraphs.zh: 当我抽完雪茄上楼时，灯还亮着。我可以看到空的钥匙孔，但听不到任何声音。她安静地学习。也许她在学校学到了这一点。我跟妈妈道晚安，然后走进自己的房间，把盒子拿出来，又数了一遍。我能听到伟大的美国骟马像刨木机一样的鼾声。我在某处读到过，他们会用这种方式修复男性，让他们拥有女性的声音。但也许他不知道他们对他做了什么。我认为他甚至不知道自己一直想做什么，也不知道伯吉斯先生为什么用栅栏纠察队把他打倒。如果他们在他处于乙醚状态时把他送到杰克逊，他永远不会知道其中的区别。但这对一个康普生来说就太简单了。还不够复杂。必须等到他爆发并试图在街上追赶一个小女孩，而她自己的父亲正在看着他时，才采取行动。好吧，就像我说的，他们开始剪辑的速度不够快，而且退出得太快。我知道至少还有两个需要类似的东西，其中一个距离也不超过一英里。但我认为即使这样也没有什么好处。就像我说的，一旦是婊子，永远是婊子。让我有二十四小时的时间，没有任何该死的纽约犹太人告诉我它将做什么。我不想杀人；留着它来吸引聪明的赌徒。我只是想要一个均匀的机会拿回我的钱。一旦我完成了这件事，他们就可以把所有比尔街和所有的混乱都带到这里，其中两个人可以睡在我的床上，另一个人也可以在桌子上占据我的位置。

paragraphs.en: The day dawned bleak and chill, a moving wall of grey light out of the northeast which, instead of dissolving into moisture, seemed to disintegrate into minute and venomous particles, like dust that, when Dilsey opened the door of the cabin and emerged, needled laterally into her flesh, precipitating not so much a moisture as a substance partaking of the quality of thin, not quite congealed oil. She wore a stiff black straw hat perched upon her turban, and a maroon velvet cape with a border of mangy and anonymous fur above a dress of purple silk, and she stood in the door for awhile with her myriad and sunken face lifted to the weather, and one gaunt hand flac-soled as the belly of a fish, then she moved the cape aside and examined the bosom of her gown.
paragraphs.zh: 天亮了，阴沉而寒冷，一堵灰色光墙从东北方移动过来，仿佛没有融成水汽，却碎成了细小而狠毒的微粒，像尘埃一样；迪尔西打开小屋的门走出来时，那些微粒从侧面针一般刺进她的皮肉，落下的与其说是水汽，不如说是一种薄薄的、尚未完全凝固的油状物。她的头巾上扣着一顶硬挺的黑草帽，紫色丝绸长裙外面披着栗色天鹅绒斗篷，边缘镶着秃了毛、辨不出是什么兽皮的毛皮。她站在门口一会儿，把那张布满岁月痕迹、凹陷的脸迎向风雨，一只瘦骨嶙峋的手，掌心像鱼肚那样松软；随后她拨开斗篷，察看长裙的胸襟。

paragraphs.en: The gown fell gauntly from her shoulders, across her fallen breasts, then tightened upon her paunch and fell again, ballooning a little above the nether garments which she would remove layer by layer as the spring accomplished and the warm days, in colour regal and moribund. She had been a big woman once but now her skeleton rose, draped loosely in unpadded skin that tightened again upon a paunch almost dropsical, as though muscle and tissue had been courage or fortitude which the days or the years had consumed until only the indomitable skeleton was left rising like a ruin or a landmark above the somnolent and impervious guts, and above that the collapsed face that gave the impression of the bones themselves being outside the flesh, lifted into the driving day with an expression at once fatalistic and of a child’s astonished disappointment, until she turned and entered the house again and closed the door.
paragraphs.zh: 长裙从她肩头干瘦地垂下，掠过下垂的乳房，在大肚子上绷紧，又垂下去，罩在层层内衣外面，微微鼓起；随着春天和暖日的来临，她会把那些内衣一层层脱去，长裙的颜色既显得高贵，又显得衰败。她从前是个魁梧的女人，如今只剩骨架高高撑起，松松披着没有脂肉衬垫的皮肤，皮肤到了几乎浮肿的大肚子上又绷紧了，仿佛肌肉和组织原来都是勇气和坚忍，被一天又一天、一年又一年的岁月消耗，直到只剩那副不屈的骨架，像废墟或地标一般耸立在昏昏欲睡、麻木不仁的肚肠上；再上面，是塌陷的脸，叫人觉得骨头竟露在皮肉之外。她仰起那张脸迎着扑来的风雨，神情既认命，又带着孩子般惊讶的失望，直到她转身重新进屋，关上门。

paragraphs.en: The earth immediately about the door was bare. It had a patina, as though from the soles of bare feet in generations, like old silver or the walls of Mexican houses which have been plastered by hand. Beside the house, shading it in summer, stood three mulberry trees, the fledged leaves that would later be broad and placid as the palms of hands streaming flatly undulant upon the driving air. A pair of jaybirds came up from nowhere, whirled up on the blast like gaudy scraps of cloth or paper and lodged in the mulberries, where they swung in raucous tilt and recover, screaming into the wind that ripped their harsh cries onward and away like scraps of paper or of cloth in turn. Then three more joined them and they swung and tilted in the wrung branches for a time, screaming. The door of the cabin opened and Dilsey emerged once more, this time in a man’s felt hat and an army overcoat, beneath the frayed skirts of which her blue gingham dress fell in uneven balloonings, streaming too about her as she crossed the yard and mounted the steps to the kitchen door.
paragraphs.zh: 门周围的土地是光秃秃的。它有一种古铜色，仿佛是几代人赤脚的脚底留下的痕迹，就像古老的银器或墨西哥房屋的手工抹灰的墙壁。房子旁边矗立着三棵桑树，在夏天给房子遮荫，长出羽毛的叶子后来变得宽阔而平静，就像手掌在强劲的空气中平坦地起伏一样。一对松鸦不知从哪里冒了出来，像花哨的布片或纸片一样在狂风中旋转起来，停在桑葚里，它们在桑葚里倾斜地摇晃着，然后恢复原状，在风中尖叫着，风把它们刺耳的叫声像纸片或布片一样依次撕扯着前进和远去。然后另外三个人加入了他们，他们在扭曲的树枝上摇摆、倾斜了一段时间，尖叫着。小屋的门打开了，迪尔西再次出现，这次她戴着一顶男士毡帽，穿着一件军大衣，在磨损的裙子下面，她的蓝色格子连衣裙呈不均匀的气球形状，当她穿过院子，登上通向厨房门的台阶时，她的裙子也在她周围流动。

paragraphs.en: A moment later she emerged, carrying an open umbrella now, which she slanted ahead into the wind, and crossed to the woodpile and laid the umbrella down, still open. Immediately she caught at it and arrested it and held to it for a while, looking about her. Then she closed it and laid it down and stacked stovewood into her crooked arm, against her breast, and picked up the umbrella and got it open at last and returned to the steps and held the wood precariously balanced while she contrived to close the umbrella, which she propped in the corner just within the door. She dumped the wood into the box behind the stove. Then she removed the overcoat and hat and took a soiled apron down from the wall and put it on and built a fire in the stove. While she was doing so, rattling the grate bars and clattering the lids, Mrs Compson began to call her from the head of the stairs.
paragraphs.zh: 过了一会儿，她出现了，手里拿着一把打开的雨伞，她把雨伞斜向前方，迎着风，走到柴堆旁，把雨伞放下，雨伞还开着。她立刻抓住了它，抓住了它，抓住了它一会儿，环顾四周。然后她把它合上，放下，把柴火堆在她弯曲的手臂上，靠在胸前，然后拿起雨伞，最后把它打开，回到台阶上，在她设法合上雨伞的同时，把木头摇摇晃晃地保持平衡，把雨伞撑在门内的角落里。她把木头倒进炉子后面的盒子里。然后她脱下大衣和帽子，从墙上取下一条脏围裙穿上，在炉子里生了火。当她这样做时，炉栅格子嘎嘎作响，盖子嘎嘎作响，康普生夫人开始在楼梯口喊她。

paragraphs.en: She wore a dressing gown of quilted black satin, holding it close under her chin. In the other hand she held a red rubber hot water bottle and she stood at the head of the back stairway, calling “Dilsey” at steady and inflectionless intervals into the quiet stairwell that descended into complete darkness, then opened again where a grey window fell across it. “Dilsey,” she called, without inflection or emphasis or haste, as though she were not listening for a reply at all. “Dilsey.”
paragraphs.zh: 她穿着一件黑色绗缝缎面晨衣，将它紧贴在下巴下面。她另一只手拿着一个红色的橡胶热水瓶，站在后楼梯的尽头，以稳定而无语调的间隔喊着“迪尔西”，进入安静的楼梯间，楼梯间下降到完全黑暗中，然后再次打开，一扇灰色的窗户掉下来。“迪尔西，”她喊道，没有语调变化，没有强调，也没有匆忙，就好像她根本没有在听回应。“迪尔西。”

paragraphs.en: Dilsey answered and ceased clattering the stove, but before she could cross the kitchen Mrs Compson called her again, and before she crossed the diningroom and brought her head into relief against the grey splash of the window, still again.
paragraphs.zh: 迪尔西接了电话，停止了敲打炉子的声音，但在她穿过厨房之前，康普生太太又叫了她一声，在她穿过餐厅，把头靠在窗户的灰色飞溅上之前，又再次叫了她一声。

paragraphs.en: “All right,” Dilsey said, “All right, here I is. I’ll fill hit soon ez I git some hot water.” She gathered up her skirts and mounted the stairs, wholly blotting the grey light. “Put hit down dar en g’awn back to bed.”
paragraphs.zh: “好吧，”迪尔西说，“好吧，我来了。我很快就会加满水，我会弄点热水。”她卷起裙子，登上楼梯，完全遮住了灰色的光芒。“把被击中的达恩·加恩放回床上。”

paragraphs.en: “I couldn’t understand what was the matter,” Mrs Compson said. “I’ve been lying awake for an hour at least, without hearing a sound from the kitchen.”
paragraphs.zh: “我不明白发生了什么事，”康普生夫人说。“我至少已经醒了一个小时了，没有听到厨房里有任何声音。”

paragraphs.en: “You put hit down and g’awn back to bed,” Dilsey said. She toiled painfully up the steps, shapeless, breathing heavily. “I’ll have de fire gwine in a minute, en de water hot in two mo.”
paragraphs.zh: “你把击倒的东西放下，让格恩回到床上，”迪尔西说。她费力地爬上台阶，身形模糊，呼吸粗重。“一分钟后我就会把火烧开，两分钟后我就会把水烧热。”

paragraphs.en: “I’ve been lying there for an hour, at least,” Mrs Compson said. “I thought maybe you were waiting for me to come down and start the fire.”
paragraphs.zh: “至少我已经在那里躺了一个小时了，”康普生夫人说。“我以为你可能在等我下来生火。”

paragraphs.en: Dilsey reached the top of the stairs and took the water bottle. “I’ll fix hit in a minute,” she said. “Luster overslep dis mawnin, up half de night at dat show. I gwine build de fire myself. Go on now, so you wont wake de others twell I ready.”
paragraphs.zh: 迪尔西到达楼梯顶，拿走了水瓶。“我会在一分钟内修复命中，”她说。“勒斯特在这场演出中睡过头了。我自己生火。现在继续吧，这样你就不会在我准备好时吵醒其他人了。”

paragraphs.en: “If you permit Luster to do things that interfere with his work, you’ll have to suffer for it yourself,” Mrs Compson said. “Jason wont like this if he hears about it. You know he wont.”
paragraphs.zh: “如果你允许勒斯特做干扰他工作的事情，你自己就得受苦，”康普生夫人说。“如果杰生听到这件事，他不会喜欢的。你知道他不会的。”

paragraphs.en: “Twusn’t none of Jason’s money he went on,” Dilsey said. “Dat’s one thing sho.” She went on down the stairs. Mrs Compson returned to her room. As she got into bed again she could hear Dilsey yet descending the stairs with a sort of painful and terrific slowness that would have become maddening had it not presently ceased beyond the flapping diminishment of the pantry door.
paragraphs.zh: “杰生的钱他都没有花，”迪尔西说。“那是一回事。”她继续走下楼梯。康普生夫人回到自己的房间。当她再次上床时，她能听到迪尔西以一种痛苦而可怕的速度走下楼梯的声音，如果不是在食品储藏室门的拍打声消失之后，这种速度很快就会变得令人发狂。

paragraphs.en: She entered the kitchen and built up the fire and began to prepare breakfast. In the midst of this she ceased and went to the window and looked out toward her cabin, then she went to the door and opened it and shouted into the driving weather.
paragraphs.zh: 她走进厨房，生起火，开始准备早餐。就在这中间，她停了下来，走到窗前，朝她的小屋望去，然后她走到门边，打开门，对着恶劣的天气大声喊道。

paragraphs.en: “Luster!” she shouted, standing to listen, tilting her face from the wind, “You, Luster?” She listened, then as she prepared to shout again Luster appeared around the corner of the kitchen.
paragraphs.zh: “勒斯特！”她站着听，侧着脸迎风喊道，“你，勒斯特？”她听着，然后当她准备再次喊叫时，勒斯特出现在厨房的拐角处。

paragraphs.en: “Ma’am?” he said innocently, so innocently that Dilsey looked down at him, for a moment motionless, with something more than mere surprise.
paragraphs.zh: “女士？”他天真地说道，天真得迪尔西低头看着他，一动不动，其中的表情不仅仅是惊讶。

paragraphs.en: “Whar you at?” she said.
paragraphs.zh: “你在做什么？”她说。

paragraphs.en: “Nowhere,” he said. “Jes in de cellar.”
paragraphs.zh: “无处可去，”他说。“杰斯在地窖里。”

paragraphs.en: “Whut you doin in de cellar?” she said. “Dont stand dar in de rain, fool,” she said.
paragraphs.zh: “你在地窖里做什么？”她说。“别站在雨里，傻瓜，”她说。

paragraphs.en: “Aint doin nothin,” he said. He came up the steps.
paragraphs.zh: “什么也没做，”他说。他走上台阶。

paragraphs.en: “Dont you dare come in dis do widout a armful of wood,” she said. “Here I done had to tote yo wood en build yo fire bofe. Didn’t I tole you not to leave dis place last night befo dat woodbox wus full to de top?”
paragraphs.zh: “你不带一抱木头就敢进来吗？”她说。“我得把木头搬到消防站去。昨晚我不是告诉过你在木箱装满之前不要离开这个地方吗？”

paragraphs.en: “I did,” Luster said, “I filled hit.”
paragraphs.zh: “我做到了，”勒斯特说，“我很成功。”

paragraphs.en: “Whar hit gone to, den?”
paragraphs.zh: “去哪儿了，书房？”

paragraphs.en: “I dont know’m. I aint teched hit.”
paragraphs.zh: “我不知道。我没有被技术击中。”

paragraphs.en: “Well, you git hit full up now,” she said. “And git on up den en see bout Benjy.”
paragraphs.zh: “好吧，你现在已经很兴奋了，”她说。“然后到书房去看看班吉。”

paragraphs.en: She shut the door. Luster went to the woodpile. The five jaybirds whirled over the house, screaming, and into the mulberries again. He watched them. He picked up a rock and threw it. “Whoo,” he said, “Git on back to hell, whar you belong at. ’Taint Monday yit.”
paragraphs.zh: 她关上了门。勒斯特走向柴堆。五只松鸦尖叫着在房子上空盘旋，又飞进桑葚里。他看着他们。他捡起一块石头并扔了出去。“哇哦，”他说，“滚回地狱去吧，你属于哪里。‘玷污星期一吧。’”

paragraphs.en: He loaded himself mountainously with stove wood. He could not see over it, and he staggered to the steps and up them and blundered crashing against the door, shedding billets. Then Dilsey came and opened the door for him and he blundered across the kitchen. “You, Luster!” she shouted, but he had already hurled the wood into the box with a thunderous crash. “Hah!” he said.
paragraphs.zh: 他给自己装满了大量的柴火。他看不到门外的情况，摇摇晃晃地走到台阶上，爬上台阶，跌跌撞撞地撞在门上，钢坯掉落。然后迪尔西过来为他打开门，他跌跌撞撞地穿过厨房。“你，勒斯特！”她喊道，但他已经把木头扔进盒子里，发出一声雷鸣般的撞击声。“哈！”他说。

paragraphs.en: “Is you tryin to wake up de whole house?” Dilsey said. She hit him on the back of his head with the flat of her hand. “Go on up dar and git Benjy dressed, now.”
paragraphs.zh: “你想唤醒整个房子吗？”迪尔西说道。她用手掌击打他的后脑勺。“现在就上楼去，把班吉穿好衣服。”

paragraphs.en: “Yessum,” he said. He went toward the outer door.
paragraphs.zh: “是的，”他说。他朝外门走去。

paragraphs.en: “Whar you gwine?” Dilsey said.
paragraphs.zh: “你怎么了？”迪尔西说道。

paragraphs.en: “I thought I better go round de house en in by de front, so I wont wake up Miss Cahline en dem.”
paragraphs.zh: “我想我最好从前面绕着房子走一圈，这样我就不会吵醒卡琳小姐了。”

paragraphs.en: “You go on up dem backstairs like I tole you en git Benjy’s clothes on him,” Dilsey said. “Go on, now.”
paragraphs.zh: “就像我告诉你的那样，你到后楼去，把班吉的衣服穿在他身上，”迪尔西说。“继续吧，现在。”

paragraphs.en: “Yessum,” Luster said. He returned and left by the diningroom door. After awhile it ceased to flap. Dilsey prepared to make biscuit. As she ground the sifter steadily above the bread board, she sang, to herself at first, something without particular tune or words, repetitive, mournful and plaintive, austere, as she ground a faint, steady snowing of flour onto the bread board. The stove had begun to heat the room and to fill it with murmurous minors of the fire, and presently she was singing louder, as if her voice too had been thawed out by the growing warmth, and then Mrs Compson called her name again from within the house. Dilsey raised her face as if her eyes could and did penetrate the walls and ceiling and saw the old woman in her quilted dressing gown at the head of the stairs, calling her name with machinelike regularity.
paragraphs.zh: “是的，”勒斯特说。他回来了，又从餐厅门口离开。过了一会儿，它不再拍动了。迪尔西准备做饼干。当她把筛子在面包板上稳定地磨碎时，她一开始自言自语地唱着一些没有特殊曲调或歌词的东西，重复、悲伤、哀伤、严肃，同时她把一层微弱的、稳定的面粉雪落在面包板上。炉子开始给房间加热，房间里充满了低语的小火苗，不久她唱得更大声了，仿佛她的声音也被日益增长的温暖融化了，然后康普生夫人在屋里再次叫她的名字。迪尔西抬起脸，仿佛她的眼睛能够而且确实能穿透墙壁和天花板，看到楼梯口穿着绗缝晨衣的老妇人，像机器一样有规律地喊着她的名字。

paragraphs.en: “Oh, Lawd,” Dilsey said. She set the sifter down and swept up the hem of her apron and wiped her hands and caught up the bottle from the chair on which she had laid it and gathered her apron about the handle of the kettle which was now jetting faintly. “Jes a minute,” she called, “De water jes dis minute got hot.”
paragraphs.zh: “哦，劳德，”迪尔西说。她放下筛子，扫起围裙的下摆，擦了擦手，从椅子上拿起瓶子，用围裙围住正在微弱喷水的水壶把手。“等一下，”她喊道，“水快变热了。”

paragraphs.en: It was not the bottle which Mrs Compson wanted, however, and clutching it by the neck like a dead hen Dilsey went to the foot of the stairs and looked upward.
paragraphs.zh: 然而，这并不是康普生夫人想要的瓶子，迪尔西像死母鸡一样抓住它的脖子，走到楼梯脚下，向上看。

paragraphs.en: “Aint Luster up dar wid him?” she said.
paragraphs.zh: “勒斯特在他身边吗？”她说。

paragraphs.en: “Luster hasn’t been in the house. I’ve been lying here listening for him. I knew he would be late, but I did hope he’d come in time to keep Benjamin from disturbing Jason on Jason’s one day in the week to sleep in the morning.”
paragraphs.zh: “勒斯特不在屋里。我一直躺在这里听他的声音。我知道他会迟到，但我确实希望他能及时赶到，以免本杰明在一周中的某一天打扰杰生睡觉。”

paragraphs.en: “I dont see how you expect anybody to sleep, wid you standin in de hall, holl’in at folks fum de crack of dawn,” Dilsey said. She began to mount the stairs, toiling heavily. “I sont dat boy up dar half hour ago.”
paragraphs.zh: “如果你站在大厅里，在黎明时分向人们大喊大叫，我不明白你希望别人怎么睡觉，”迪尔西说。她开始爬楼梯，吃力地吃力。“半小时前我还没起床。”

paragraphs.en: Mrs Compson watched her, holding the dressing gown under her chin. “What are you going to do?” she said.
paragraphs.zh: 康普生夫人看着她，把睡袍夹在下巴下面。“你会怎样做？”她说。

paragraphs.en: “Gwine git Benjy dressed en bring him down to de kitchen, whar he wont wake Jason en Quentin,” Dilsey said.
paragraphs.zh: “班吉穿好衣服，带他去厨房，这样他就不会吵醒昆丁的杰生，”迪尔西说。

paragraphs.en: “Haven’t you started breakfast yet?”
paragraphs.zh: “你还没开始吃早餐吗？”

paragraphs.en: “I’ll tend to dat too,” Dilsey said. “You better git back in bed twell Luster make yo fire. Hit cold dis mawnin.”
paragraphs.zh: “我也会倾向于这样做，”迪尔西说。“你最好回到床上，等勒斯特给你生火。把寒冷打醒。”

paragraphs.en: “I know it,” Mrs Compson said. “My feet are like ice. They were so cold they waked me up.” She watched Dilsey mount the stairs. It took her a long while. “You know how it frets Jason when breakfast is late,” Mrs Compson said.
paragraphs.zh: “我知道，”康普生夫人说。“我的脚像冰一样。太冷了，把我吵醒了。”她看着迪尔西走上楼梯。她花了很长时间。“你知道早餐迟到时杰生会多么烦恼，”康普生夫人说。

paragraphs.en: “I cant do but one thing at a time,” Dilsey said. “You git on back to bed, fo I has you on my hands dis mawnin too.”
paragraphs.zh: “我一次只能做一件事，”迪尔西说。“你回到床上去吧，因为我也把你抱在怀里了。”

paragraphs.en: “If you’re going to drop everything to dress Benjamin, I’d better come down and get breakfast. You know as well as I do how Jason acts when it’s late.”
paragraphs.zh: “如果你要放下一切给本杰明穿衣服，我最好下来吃早餐。你和我一样清楚杰生天色已晚时的表现。”

paragraphs.en: “En who gwine eat yo messin?” Dilsey said. “Tell me dat. Go on now,” she said, toiling upward. Mrs Compson stood watching her as she mounted, steadying herself against the wall with one hand, holding her skirts up with the other.
paragraphs.zh: “谁吃你的饭？”迪尔西说道。“告诉我这些。现在继续，”她一边说，一边艰难地向上爬。康普生夫人站在那儿看着她上马，一只手靠在墙上，另一只手提着裙子。

paragraphs.en: “Are you going to wake him up just to dress him?” she said.
paragraphs.zh: “你要叫醒他只是为了给他穿衣服吗？”她说。

paragraphs.en: Dilsey stopped. With her foot lifted to the next step she stood there, her hand against the wall and the grey splash of the window behind her, motionless and shapeless she loomed.
paragraphs.zh: 迪尔西停了下来。她抬起脚迈向下一步，手扶着墙，身后灰色的窗户映衬着她，一动不动、毫无形状，她站在那儿。

paragraphs.en: “He aint awake den?” she said.
paragraphs.zh: “他还没醒吗？”她说。

paragraphs.en: “He wasn’t when I looked in,” Mrs Compson said. “But it’s past his time. He never does sleep after half past seven. You know he doesn’t.”
paragraphs.zh: “我进去的时候他不在，”康普生夫人说。“但他的时代已经过去了。他七点半之后就不再睡觉了。你知道他不睡觉。”

paragraphs.en: Dilsey said nothing. She made no further move, but though she could not see her save as a blobby shape without depth, Mrs Compson knew that she had lowered her face a little and that she stood now like a cow in the rain, as she held the empty water bottle by its neck.
paragraphs.zh: 迪尔西什么也没说。她没有再动，虽然她看不到她，只看到她是一个没有深度的斑点，但康普生夫人知道她已经把脸低了一点，她现在像雨中的牛一样站着，手里捏着空水瓶的脖子。

paragraphs.en: “You’re not the one who has to bear it,” Mrs Compson said. “It’s not your responsibility. You can go away. You dont have to bear the brunt of it day in and day out. You owe nothing to them, to Mr Compson’s memory. I know you have never had any tenderness for Jason. You’ve never tried to conceal it.”
paragraphs.zh: “你不是必须承受的人。”康普生夫人说道。“这不是你的责任。你可以走开。你不必日复一日地承受着。你不欠他们，也不欠康普生先生的记忆。我知道你对杰生从来没有任何温柔。你从来没有试图隐瞒这一点。”

paragraphs.en: Dilsey said nothing. She turned slowly and descended, lowering her body from step to step, as a small child does, her hand against the wall. “You go on and let him alone,” she said. “Dont go in dar no mo, now. I’ll send Luster up soon as I find him. Let him alone, now.”
paragraphs.zh: 迪尔西什么也没说。她慢慢地转身下降，一步一步地降低身体，就像一个小孩子一样，她的手抵在墙上。“你继续吧，别管他了，”她说。“现在别进去。我一找到勒斯特就派他上去。现在就别管他了。”

paragraphs.en: She returned to the kitchen. She looked into the stove, then she drew her apron over her head and donned the overcoat and opened the outer door and looked up and down the yard. The weather drove upon her flesh, harsh and minute, but the scene was empty of all else that moved. She descended the steps, gingerly, as if for silence, and went around the corner of the kitchen. As she did so Luster emerged quickly and innocently from the cellar door.
paragraphs.zh: 她回到厨房。她朝炉子里看了看，然后把围裙拉到头上，穿上大衣，打开外门，上下打量着院子。天气严酷而微小地压在她的肉体上，但场景中却没有任何其他移动的东西。她小心翼翼地走下台阶，仿佛是为了保持安静，然后绕过厨房的拐角处。当她这样做时，勒斯特迅速而天真地从地窖门口走了出来。

paragraphs.en: Dilsey stopped. “Whut you up to?” she said.
paragraphs.zh: 迪尔西停了下来。“你在忙什么？”她说。

paragraphs.en: “Nothin,” Luster said, “Mr Jason say fer me to find out whar dat water leak in de cellar fum.”
paragraphs.zh: “没什么，”勒斯特说，“杰生先生让我去查一下地窖里漏水的地方。”

paragraphs.en: “En when wus hit he say fer you to do dat?” Dilsey said. “Last New Year’s day, wasn’t hit?”
paragraphs.zh: “嗯，我们打的时候他说让你这么做？”迪尔西说道。“去年元旦，没被击中吧？”

paragraphs.en: “I thought I jes be lookin whiles dey sleep,” Luster said. Dilsey went to the cellar door. He stood aside and she peered down into the obscurity odorous of dank earth and mould and rubber.
paragraphs.zh: “我想我应该在他们睡觉的时候看看，”勒斯特说。迪尔西走到地窖门口。他站在一旁，她低头凝视着潮湿的泥土、霉菌和橡胶的模糊气味。

paragraphs.en: “Huh,” Dilsey said. She looked at Luster again. He met her gaze blandly, innocent and open. “I dont know whut you up to, but you aint got no business doin hit. You jes tryin me too dis mawnin cause de others is, aint you? You git on up dar en see to Benjy, you hear?”
paragraphs.zh: “嗯，”迪尔西说。她又看了看勒斯特。他温和地、天真地、开放地与她对视。“我不知道你在做什么，但你没有任何事可做。你也想试探我，因为其他人也是如此，不是吗？你继续看班吉，听到了吗？”

paragraphs.en: “Yessum,” Luster said. He went on toward the kitchen steps, swiftly.
paragraphs.zh: “是的，”勒斯特说。他快步朝厨房的台阶走去。

paragraphs.en: “Here,” Dilsey said, “You git me another armful of wood while I got you.”
paragraphs.zh: “给你，”迪尔西说，“我抓到你的时候，你再给我一抱木头。”

paragraphs.en: “Yessum,” he said. He passed her on the steps and went to the woodpile. When he blundered again at the door a moment later, again invisible and blind within and beyond his wooden avatar, Dilsey opened the door and guided him across the kitchen with a firm hand.
paragraphs.zh: “是的，”他说。他在台阶上越过她，朝柴堆走去。片刻之后，当他再次在门口绊倒时，他的木制化身内外再次变得隐形和盲目，迪尔西打开了门，用坚定的手引导他穿过厨房。

paragraphs.en: “Jes thow hit at dat box again,” she said, “Jes thow hit.”
paragraphs.zh: “天啊，你又击中了那个盒子，”她说，“天啊，你又击中了。”

paragraphs.en: “I got to,” Luster said, panting, “I cant put hit down no other way.”
paragraphs.zh: “我必须这样做，”勒斯特气喘吁吁地说，“我没有其他办法可以把打击击倒。”

paragraphs.en: “Den you stand dar en hold hit a while,” Dilsey said. She unloaded him a stick at a time. “Whut got into you dis mawnin? Here I sont you fer wood en you aint never brought mo’n six sticks at a time to save yo life twell today. Whut you fixin to ax me kin you do now? Aint dat show lef town yit?”
paragraphs.zh: “你站稳了，打一会儿，”迪尔西说。她一次给他卸下一根棍子。“你怎么了？我在这里给你提供木头，你今天从来没有一次带六根棍子来救你的命。你现在想用斧头砍我吗？这不是表明离开了城镇吗？”

paragraphs.en: “Yessum. Hit done gone.”
paragraphs.zh: “是的，成功了。”

paragraphs.en: She put the last stick into the box. “Now you go on up dar wid Benjy, like I tole you befo,” she said. “And I dont want nobody else yellin down dem stairs at me twell I rings de bell. You hear me.”
paragraphs.zh: 她把最后一根棍子放进盒子里。“现在你继续往班吉走，就像我之前告诉你的那样，”她说。“我不希望别人在我按响门铃时在楼梯下对我大喊大叫。你听我说。”

paragraphs.en: “Yessum,” Luster said. He vanished through the swing door. Dilsey put some more wood in the stove and returned to the bread board. Presently she began to sing again.
paragraphs.zh: “是的，”勒斯特说。他从旋转门消失了。迪尔西又往炉子里放了一些木头，然后又回到了面包板旁。不久她又开始唱歌了。

paragraphs.en: The room grew warmer. Soon Dilsey’s skin had taken on a rich, lustrous quality as compared with that as of a faint dusting of wood ashes which both it and Luster’s had worn, as she moved about the kitchen, gathering about her the raw materials of food, coordinating the meal. On the wall above a cupboard, invisible save at night, by lamp light and even then evincing an enigmatic profundity because it had but one hand, a cabinet clock ticked, then with a preliminary sound as if it had cleared its throat, struck five times.
paragraphs.zh: 房间变得温暖起来。很快，迪尔西的皮肤就呈现出丰富而有光泽的质感，与她和勒斯特的皮肤相比，她的皮肤就像一层淡淡的木灰，当她在厨房里走来走去，收集食物的原材料，协调膳食时。橱柜上方的墙上，除了在晚上，在灯光下是看不见的，即使在那时，因为只有一只手，柜子的钟也表现出一种神秘的深邃，滴答作响，然后伴随着一声初步的声音，好像它清了嗓子，敲响了五下。

paragraphs.en: “Eight oclock,” Dilsey said. She ceased and tilted her head upward, listening. But there was no sound save the clock and the fire. She opened the oven and looked at the pan of bread, then stooping she paused while someone descended the stairs. She heard the feet cross the diningroom, then the swing door opened and Luster entered, followed by a big man who appeared to have been shaped of some substance whose particles would not or did not cohere to one another or to the frame which supported it. His skin was dead looking and hairless; dropsical too, he moved with a shambling gait like a trained bear. His hair was pale and fine. It had been brushed smoothly down upon his brow like that of children in daguerreotypes. His eyes were clear, of the pale sweet blue of cornflowers, his thick mouth hung open, drooling a little.
paragraphs.zh: “八点，”迪尔西说。她停下来，抬起头，听着。但除了时钟和火之外，没有任何声音。她打开烤箱，看着那盘面包，然后弯下腰，在有人走下楼梯时停了下来。她听到脚步声穿过餐厅，然后旋转门打开，勒斯特走了进来，后面跟着一个大个子，他似乎是由某种物质制成的，这种物质的颗粒不会或不会相互粘连或与支撑它的框架粘连。他的皮肤看起来毫无生气，没有毛发。他也患有水肿，走路时步态蹒跚，就像一只训练有素的熊。他的头发苍白而细腻。它被光滑地刷在他的额头上，就像银版照片中的孩子一样。他的眼睛清澈，呈矢车菊般淡甜的蓝色，厚厚的嘴巴张开，流着一点口水。

paragraphs.en: “Is he cold?” Dilsey said. She wiped her hands on her apron and touched his hand.
paragraphs.zh: “他冷吗？”迪尔西说道。她在围裙上擦了擦手，摸了摸他的手。

paragraphs.en: “Ef he aint, I is,” Luster said. “Always cold Easter. Aint never seen hit fail. Miss Cahline say ef you aint got time to fix her hot water bottle to never mind about hit.”
paragraphs.zh: “如果他不是，我就是，”勒斯特说。“复活节总是很冷。从未见过撞车失败。卡林小姐说，如果你没有时间修理她的热水袋，就不用担心撞车了。”

paragraphs.en: “Oh, Lawd,” Dilsey said. She drew a chair into the corner between the woodbox and the stove. The man went obediently and sat in it. “Look in de dinin room and see whar I laid dat bottle down,” Dilsey said. Luster fetched the bottle from the diningroom and Dilsey filled it and give it to him. “Hurry up, now,” she said. “See ef Jason wake now. Tell em hit’s all ready.”
paragraphs.zh: “哦，劳德，”迪尔西说。她把一把椅子拉到木箱和炉子之间的角落里。那人听话的走了进去，坐了进去。“看看餐厅，看看我把瓶子放在哪里，”迪尔西说。勒斯特从餐厅拿来瓶子，迪尔西装满它并交给他。“快点，现在，”她说。“杰生快醒来吧。告诉他们一切准备就绪。”

paragraphs.en: Luster went out. Ben sat beside the stove. He sat loosely, utterly motionless save for his head, which made a continual bobbing sort of movement as he watched Dilsey with his sweet vague gaze as she moved about. Luster returned.
paragraphs.zh: 勒斯特出去了。本坐在炉子旁边。他松松垮垮地坐着，一动不动，除了他的头，当他用甜蜜而模糊的目光注视着迪尔西走动时，她的头不断地摆动。勒斯特回来了。

paragraphs.en: “He up,” he said, “Miss Cahline say put hit on de table.” He came to the stove and spread his hands palm down above the firebox. “He up, too,” He said, “Gwine hit wid bofe feet dis mawnin.”
paragraphs.zh: “他站起来，”他说，“卡琳小姐说把击球放在桌子上。”他来到炉子前，将手掌摊开在火箱上方。“他也起来了，”他说，“格温用他的脚踢了下去。”

paragraphs.en: “Whut’s de matter now?” Dilsey said. “Git away fum dar. How kin I do anything wid you standin over de stove?”
paragraphs.zh: “现在有什么事吗？”迪尔西说道。“滚开吧，你站在炉子旁边我怎么办？”

paragraphs.en: “I cold,” Luster said.
paragraphs.zh: “我冷，”勒斯特说。

paragraphs.en: “You ought to thought about dat whiles you wus down dar in dat cellar,” Dilsey said. “Whut de matter wid Jason?”
paragraphs.zh: “当你在那个地窖里的时候，你应该想想那个，”迪尔西说。“杰生有什么关系？”

paragraphs.en: “Sayin me en Benjy broke dat winder in his room.”
paragraphs.zh: “说我班吉在他的房间里打破了那个缠绕者。”

paragraphs.en: “Is dey one broke?” Dilsey said.
paragraphs.zh: “他们破产了吗？”迪尔西说道。

paragraphs.en: “Dat’s whut he sayin,” Luster said. “Say I broke hit.”
paragraphs.zh: “他就是这么说的，”勒斯特说。“说我打破了打击。”

paragraphs.en: “How could you, when he keep hit locked all day en night?”
paragraphs.zh: “他整天整夜都被锁定，你怎么能这样呢？”

paragraphs.en: “Say I broke hit chunkin rocks at hit,” Luster said.
paragraphs.zh: “假设我在击球时打破了大块岩石，”勒斯特说。

paragraphs.en: “En did you?”
paragraphs.zh: “嗯，是吗？”

paragraphs.en: “Nome,” Luster said.
paragraphs.zh: “不，”勒斯特说。

paragraphs.en: “Dont lie to me, boy,” Dilsey said.
paragraphs.zh: “别对我撒谎，孩子，”迪尔西说。

paragraphs.en: “I never done hit,” Luster said. “Ask Benjy ef I did. I aint stud’in dat winder.”
paragraphs.zh: “我从来没有打过球，”勒斯特说。“如果我问过的话，就去问班吉吧。我不是那个上链者。”

paragraphs.en: “Who could a broke hit, den?” Dilsey said. “He jes tryin hisself, to wake Quentin up,” she said, taking the pan of biscuits out of the stove.
paragraphs.zh: “谁能打出一记破发，书房？”迪尔西说道。“他正在尝试自己叫醒昆丁，”她一边说，一边从炉子里拿出一盘饼干。

paragraphs.en: “Reckin so,” Luster said. “Dese is funny folks. Glad I aint none of em.”
paragraphs.zh: “我想是这样，”勒斯特说。“德塞是一群有趣的人。很高兴我不是他们中的任何一个。”

paragraphs.en: “Aint none of who?” Dilsey said. “Lemme tell you somethin, nigger boy, you got jes es much Compson devilment in you es any of em. Is you right sho you never broke dat window?”
paragraphs.zh: “谁都没有吗？”迪尔西说道。“让我告诉你一件事，黑鬼男孩，你们每个人身上都有很多康普生的恶魔。你说得对吗，你从来没有打破过那扇窗户？”

paragraphs.en: “Whut I want to break hit fur?”
paragraphs.zh: “我为什么要打碎皮毛？”

paragraphs.en: “Whut you do any of yo devilment fur?” Dilsey said. “Watch him now, so he cant burn his hand again twell I git de table set.”
paragraphs.zh: “你们这些魔鬼毛皮干什么？”迪尔西说道。“现在看着他，这样他就不会在我摆好桌子后再次烧伤他的手。”

paragraphs.en: She went to the diningroom, where they heard her moving about, then she returned and set a plate at the kitchen table and set food there. Ben watched her, slobbering, making a faint, eager sound.
paragraphs.zh: 她去了餐厅，他们听到她走动的声音，然后她回来，在厨房的桌子上放了一个盘子，放了食物。本看着她，流着口水，发出微弱而急切的声音。

paragraphs.en: “All right, honey,” she said, “Here yo breakfast. Bring his chair, Luster.” Luster moved the chair up and Ben sat down, whimpering and slobbering. Dilsey tied a cloth about his neck and wiped his mouth with the end of it. “And see kin you kep fum messin up his clothes one time,” she said, handing Luster a spoon.
paragraphs.zh: “好吧，亲爱的，”她说，“早餐来了。勒斯特，把他的椅子拿来。”勒斯特把椅子移了上去，本坐下来，呜咽着流着口水。迪尔西在脖子上绑了一块布，用布的一端擦了擦嘴。“你看你有一次把他的衣服弄脏了，”她说，递给勒斯特一把勺子。

paragraphs.en: Ben ceased whimpering. He watched the spoon as it rose to his mouth. It was as if even eagerness were muscle-bound in him too, and hunger itself inarticulate, not knowing it is hunger. Luster fed him with skill and detachment. Now and then his attention would return long enough to enable him to feint the spoon and cause Ben to close his mouth upon the empty air, but it was apparent that Luster’s mind was elsewhere. His other hand lay on the back of the chair and upon that dead surface it moved tentatively, delicately, as if he were picking an inaudible tune out of the dead void, and once he even forgot to tease Ben with the spoon while his fingers teased out of the slain wood a soundless and involved arpeggio until Ben recalled him by whimpering again.
paragraphs.zh: 本停止了呜咽。他看着勺子升到嘴边。就好像连渴望也让他肌肉僵硬，而饥饿本身却无法言喻，不知道那是饥饿。勒斯特以技巧和超然的态度培养了他。时不时地，他的注意力会回来足够长的时间，使他能够佯装拿勺子，让本在空虚的空气中闭上嘴，但很明显，勒斯特的心思在别处。他的另一只手放在椅背上，在死气沉沉的表面上试探性地、微妙地移动，仿佛他正在从死寂的虚空中挑选出一首听不见的曲子，有一次他甚至忘记用勺子逗弄本，而他的手指从被杀死的木头上逗弄出无声的、复杂的琶音，直到本再次呜咽着回忆起他。

paragraphs.en: In the diningroom Dilsey moved back and forth. Presently she rang a small clear bell, then in the kitchen Luster heard Mrs Compson and Jason descending, and Jason’s voice, and he rolled his eyes whitely with listening.
paragraphs.zh: 迪尔西在餐厅里来回走动。不久，她按响了一声清脆的小门铃，然后勒斯特听到厨房里康普生太太和杰生走下来，还有杰生的声音，他听着，翻白眼。

paragraphs.en: “Sure, I know they didn’t break it,” Jason said. “Sure, I know that. Maybe the change of weather broke it.”
paragraphs.zh: “当然，我知道他们没有打破它，”杰生说。“当然，我知道。也许天气的变化打破了它。”

paragraphs.en: “I dont see how it could have,” Mrs Compson said. “Your room stays locked all day long, just as you leave it when you go to town. None of us ever go in there except Sunday, to clean it. I dont want you to think that I would go where I’m not wanted, or that I would permit anyone else to.”
paragraphs.zh: “我不明白怎么会这样，”康普生夫人说。“你的房间整天都锁着，就像你进城时离开它一样。除了周日，我们没有人进去那里打扫房间。我不想让你认为我会去我不想要的地方，或者我会允许其他人去。”

paragraphs.en: “I never said you broke it, did I?” Jason said.
paragraphs.zh: “我从来没有说过你弄坏了它，是吗？”杰生说道。

paragraphs.en: “I dont want to go in your room,” Mrs Compson said. “I respect anybody’s private affairs. I wouldn’t put my foot over the threshold, even if I had a key.”
paragraphs.zh: “我不想进你的房间，”康普生夫人说。“我尊重任何人的私人事务。即使我有钥匙，我也不会跨过门槛。”

paragraphs.en: “Yes,” Jason said, “I know your keys wont fit. That’s why I had the lock changed. What I want to know is, how that window got broken.”
paragraphs.zh: “是的，”杰生说，“我知道你的钥匙插不进去，所以我才换了锁。我想知道的是，那扇窗户是怎么被打破的。”

paragraphs.en: “Luster say he didn’t do hit,” Dilsey said.
paragraphs.zh: “勒斯特说他没有击中，”迪尔西说。

paragraphs.en: “I knew that without asking him,” Jason said. “Where’s Quentin?” he said.
paragraphs.zh: “我不用问他就知道了，”杰生说。“昆丁在哪儿？”他说。

paragraphs.en: “Where she is ev’y Sunday mawnin,” Dilsey said. “Whut got into you de last few days, anyhow?”
paragraphs.zh: “她每个星期天都在那个地方，”迪尔西说。“最近几天你到底发生了什么事情？”

paragraphs.en: “Well, we’re going to change all that,” Jason said. “Go up and tell her breakfast is ready.”
paragraphs.zh: “好吧，我们要改变这一切，”杰生说。“上去告诉她早餐准备好了。”

paragraphs.en: “You leave her alone now, Jason,” Dilsey said. “She gits up fer breakfast ev’y week mawnin, en Cahline lets her stay in bed ev’y Sunday. You knows dat.”
paragraphs.zh: “杰生，你现在别管她了，”迪尔西说。“她每周都会起床吃早餐，而卡林则让她每周日都躺在床上。你知道这一点。”

paragraphs.en: “I cant keep a kitchen full of niggers to wait on her pleasure, much as I’d like to,” Jason said. “Go and tell her to come down to breakfast.”
paragraphs.zh: “我不能让厨房里全是黑鬼来伺候她高兴，尽管我很想这么做，”杰生说。“去叫她下来吃早餐。”

paragraphs.en: “Aint nobody have to wait on her,” Dilsey said. “I puts her breakfast in de warmer en she—”
paragraphs.zh: “没有人需要伺候她，”迪尔西说。“我把她的早餐放在保温箱里，让她——”

paragraphs.en: “Did you hear me?” Jason said.
paragraphs.zh: “你听到我说话了吗？”杰生说道。

paragraphs.en: “I hears you,” Dilsey said. “All I been hearin, when you in de house. Ef hit aint Quentin er yo maw, hit’s Luster en Benjy. Whut you let him go on dat way fer, Miss Cahline?”
paragraphs.zh: “我听到了，”迪尔西说。“当你在家里的时候，我一直听到的都是。Ef hit a not 昆丁 er yo maw, hit's 勒斯特 en班吉. Cahline 小姐，你为什么让他继续那条路？”

paragraphs.en: “You’d better do as he says,” Mrs Compson said, “He’s head of the house now. It’s his right to require us to respect his wishes. I try to do it, and if I can, you can too.”
paragraphs.zh: “你最好按照他说的去做，”康普生太太说，“他现在是一家之主，要求我们尊重他的意愿是他的权利。我尽力做到这一点，如果我能做到，你也能做到。”

paragraphs.en: “’Taint no sense in him bein so bad tempered he got to make Quentin git up jes to suit him,” Dilsey said. “Maybe you think she broke dat window.”
paragraphs.zh: “他脾气这么坏，他必须让昆丁振作起来以适应他，这毫无意义，”迪尔西说。“也许你认为她打破了那扇窗户。”

paragraphs.en: “She would, if she happened to think of it,” Jason said. “You go and do what I told you.”
paragraphs.zh: “如果她碰巧想到的话，她会的，”杰生说。“你去照我说的做。”

paragraphs.en: “En I wouldn’t blame her none ef she did,” Dilsey said, going toward the stairs. “Wid you naggin at her all de blessed time you in de house.”
paragraphs.zh: “嗯，如果她这么做了，我也不会责怪她。”迪尔西一边说，一边朝楼梯走去。“如果你在家里的时候一直对她唠叨的话。”

paragraphs.en: “Hush, Dilsey,” Mrs Compson said, “It’s neither your place nor mine to tell Jason what to do. Sometimes I think he is wrong, but I try to obey his wishes for you alls’ sakes. If I’m strong enough to come to the table, Quentin can too.”
paragraphs.zh: “嘘，迪尔西，”康普生夫人说道，“你和我都没有资格告诉杰生该怎么做。有时我认为他是错的，但为了你们大家，我会尽量遵守他的意愿。如果我有足够的力量参加谈判，昆丁也可以。”

paragraphs.en: Dilsey went out. They heard her mounting the stairs. They heard her a long while on the stairs.
paragraphs.zh: 迪尔西出去了。他们听到她上楼梯的声音。他们在楼梯上听到了她的声音。

paragraphs.en: “You’ve got a prize set of servants,” Jason said. He helped his mother and himself to food. “Did you ever have one that was worth killing? You must have had some before I was big enough to remember.”
paragraphs.zh: “你有一套奖品仆人，”杰生说。他帮助他的母亲和他自己吃饭。“你曾经有过值得杀死的东西吗？在我长大到能记住之前，你一定有过一些。”

paragraphs.en: “I have to humour them,” Mrs Compson said. “I have to depend on them so completely. It’s not as if I were strong. I wish I were. I wish I could do all the house work myself. I could at least take that much off your shoulders.”
paragraphs.zh: “我必须迁就他们，”康普生夫人说。“我必须完全依赖他们。我并不坚强。我希望我是。我希望我能自己做所有的家务。我至少可以减轻你的负担。”

paragraphs.en: “And a fine pigsty we’d live in, too,” Jason said. “Hurry up, Dilsey,” he shouted.
paragraphs.zh: “我们也可以住在一个漂亮的猪圈里，”杰生说。“快点，迪尔西，”他喊道。

paragraphs.en: “I know you blame me,” Mrs Compson said, “for letting them off to go to church today.”
paragraphs.zh: “我知道你责怪我，”康普生夫人说，“今天让他们去教堂。”

paragraphs.en: “Go where?” Jason said. “Hasn’t that damn show left yet?”
paragraphs.zh: “去哪儿？”杰生说道。“那个该死的节目还没结束吗？”

paragraphs.en: “To church,” Mrs Compson said. “The darkies are having a special Easter service. I promised Dilsey two weeks ago that they could get off.”
paragraphs.zh: “去教堂，”康普生夫人说。“黑人正在举行特别的复活节仪式。两周前我向迪尔西保证他们可以下车。”

paragraphs.en: “Which means we’ll eat cold dinner,” Jason said, “or none at all.”
paragraphs.zh: “这意味着我们会吃冷晚餐，”杰生说，“或者根本不吃。”

paragraphs.en: “I know it’s my fault,” Mrs Compson said. “I know you blame me.”
paragraphs.zh: “我知道这是我的错，”康普生夫人说。“我知道你怪我。”

paragraphs.en: “For what?” Jason said. “You never resurrected Christ, did you?”
paragraphs.zh: “为了什么？”杰生说道。“你从来没有复活基督，是吗？”

paragraphs.en: They heard Dilsey mount the final stair, then her slow feet overhead.
paragraphs.zh: 他们听到迪尔西爬上最后一层楼梯的声音，然后她的脚步缓慢地迈过头顶。

paragraphs.en: “Quentin,” she said. When she called the first time Jason laid his knife and fork down and he and his mother appeared to wait across the table from one another, in identical attitudes; the one cold and shrewd, with close-thatched brown hair curled into two stubborn hooks, one on either side of his forehead like a bartender in caricature, and hazel eyes with black-ringed irises like marbles, the other cold and querulous, with perfectly white hair and eyes pouched and baffled and so dark as to appear to be all pupil or all iris.
paragraphs.zh: “昆丁，”她说。当她第一次打电话时，杰生放下了刀叉，他和他的母亲似乎隔着桌子等着，态度一模一样。一个冷酷而精明，一头浓密的茅草棕色头发卷成两个顽固的钩子，一个在额头两侧，像漫画中的酒保，淡褐色的眼睛，黑圈虹膜像大理石一样；另一个冷酷而爱发牢骚，有着纯白的头发和眼袋，眼袋茫然，颜色深邃，看起来全是瞳孔或虹膜。

paragraphs.en: “Quentin,” Dilsey said, “Get up, honey. Dey waitin breakfast on you.”
paragraphs.zh: “昆丁，”迪尔西说，“起来吧，亲爱的。他们在等你吃早餐。”

paragraphs.en: “I cant understand how that window got broken,” Mrs Compson said. “Are you sure it was done yesterday? It could have been like that a long time, with the warm weather. The upper sash, behind the shade like that.”
paragraphs.zh: “我不明白那扇窗户是怎么被打破的，”康普生夫人说。“你确定是昨天做的吗？天气暖和的话，可能已经这样很久了。上层窗框，在遮阳帘后面就是这样。”

paragraphs.en: “I’ve told you for the last time that it happened yesterday,” Jason said. “Dont you reckon I know the room I live in? Do you reckon I could have lived in it a week with a hole in the window you could stick your hand—” his voice ceased, ebbed, left him staring at his mother with eyes that for an instant were quite empty of anything. It was as though his eyes were holding their breath, while his mother looked at him, her face flaccid and querulous, interminable, clairvoyant yet obtuse. As they sat so Dilsey said,
paragraphs.zh: “我最后一次告诉你，这件事是昨天发生的。”杰生说道。“你不认为我知道我住的房间吗？你认为我可以在窗户上有一个洞，你可以把手伸进去吗？你认为我可以在里面住一个星期吗？”他的声音停止了，减弱了，留下他用一瞬间空洞的眼睛盯着他的母亲。他的眼睛仿佛屏住了呼吸，而他的母亲则看着他，表情软弱而抱怨，没完没了，有洞察力却又迟钝。当他们这样坐着时，迪尔西说道：

paragraphs.en: “Quentin. Dont play wid me, honey. Come on to breakfast, honey. Dey waitin fer you.”
paragraphs.zh: “昆丁。别跟我玩了，亲爱的。来吃早餐吧，亲爱的。他们在等你。”

paragraphs.en: “I cant understand it,” Mrs Compson said, “It’s just as if somebody had tried to break into the house—” Jason sprang up. His chair crashed over backward. “What—” Mrs Compson said, staring at him as he ran past her and went jumping up the stairs, where he met Dilsey. His face was now in shadow, and Dilsey said,
paragraphs.zh: “我无法理解，”康普生太太说，“就好像有人试图闯入房子一样——”杰生跳了起来。他的椅子向后翻倒了。“什么——”康普生夫人盯着他说，他跑过她身边，跳上楼梯，在那里他遇见了迪尔西。他的脸现在处于阴影之中，迪尔西说道：

paragraphs.en: “She sullin. Yo ma aint unlocked—” But Jason ran on past her and along the corridor to a door. He didn’t call. He grasped the knob and tried it, then he stood with the knob in his hand and his head bent a little, as if he were listening to something much further away than the dimensioned room beyond the door, and which he already heard. His attitude was that of one who goes through the motions of listening in order to deceive himself as to what he already hears. Behind him Mrs Compson mounted the stairs, calling his name. Then she saw Dilsey and she quit calling him and began to call Dilsey instead.
paragraphs.zh: “她闷闷不乐。你没开锁——”但是杰生跑过她身边，沿着走廊跑到一扇门前。他没有打电话。他抓住门把手，试了一下，然后他手里拿着门把手站着，头微微低着，仿佛他正在聆听比门外那个宽敞的房间更远的声音，而他已经听到了。他的态度是一种假装倾听的态度，目的是为了欺骗自己相信他已经听到了什么。在他身后，康普生夫人走上楼梯，喊着他的名字。然后她看到了迪尔西，她不再给他打电话，而是开始打电话给迪尔西。

paragraphs.en: “I told you she aint unlocked dat do’ yit,” Dilsey said.
paragraphs.zh: “我告诉过你，她没有解锁，”迪尔西说。

paragraphs.en: When she spoke he turned and ran toward her, but his voice was quiet, matter of fact. “She carry the key with her?” he said. “Has she got it now, I mean, or will she have—”
paragraphs.zh: 当她说话时，他转身朝她跑来，但他的声音实际上很平静。“她随身带着钥匙吗？”他说。“我是说，她现在明白了吗，或者她会——”

paragraphs.en: “Dilsey,” Mrs Compson said on the stairs.
paragraphs.zh: “迪尔西，”康普生夫人在楼梯上说道。

paragraphs.en: “Is which?” Dilsey said. “Whyn’t you let—”
paragraphs.zh: “是哪个？”迪尔西说道。“你为什么不让——”

paragraphs.en: “The key,” Jason said, “To that room. Does she carry it with her all the time. Mother.” Then he saw Mrs Compson and he went down the stairs and met her. “Give me the key,” he said. He fell to pawing at the pockets of the rusty black dressing sacque she wore. She resisted.
paragraphs.zh: “钥匙，”杰生说，“那个房间的钥匙。她一直带着它吗？妈妈。”然后他看到了康普生夫人，便走下楼梯遇见了她。“把钥匙给我，”他说。他用爪子抓她穿的生锈的黑色敷料囊的口袋。她反抗了。

paragraphs.en: “Jason,” she said, “Jason! Are you and Dilsey trying to put me to bed again?” she said, trying to fend him off, “Cant you even let me have Sunday in peace?”
paragraphs.zh: “杰生，”她说，“杰生！你和迪尔西又想把我送上床睡觉吗？”她试图挡开他，说道：“你就不能让我安静地过个周日吗？”

paragraphs.en: “The key,” Jason said, pawing at her, “Give it here.” He looked back at the door, as if he expected it to fly open before he could get back to it with the key he did not yet have.
paragraphs.zh: “钥匙，”杰生用爪子抓着她，“给我吧。”他回头看了看门，好像他希望在他用尚未拿到的钥匙回到门之前门会飞开。

paragraphs.en: “You, Dilsey!” Mrs Compson said, clutching her sacque about her.
paragraphs.zh: “你，迪尔西！”康普生夫人一边说，一边紧紧地抓着她的囊。

paragraphs.en: “Give me the key, you old fool!” Jason cried suddenly. From her pocket he tugged a huge bunch of rusted keys on an iron ring like a mediaeval jailer’s and ran back up the hall with the two women behind him.
paragraphs.zh: “把钥匙给我，你这个老笨蛋！”杰生突然哭了起来。他从她的口袋里掏出一大串生锈的钥匙，就像中世纪狱卒的铁环一样，然后跑回大厅，身后跟着两个女人。

paragraphs.en: “You, Jason!” Mrs Compson said. “He will never find the right one,” she said, “You know I never let anyone take my keys, Dilsey,” she said. She began to wail.
paragraphs.zh: “你，杰生！”康普生夫人说道。“他永远找不到合适的人，”她说，“你知道我从来不让任何人拿走我的钥匙，迪尔西，”她说。她开始哭泣。

paragraphs.en: “Hush,” Dilsey said, “He aint gwine do nothin to her. I aint gwine let him.”
paragraphs.zh: “嘘，”迪尔西说，“他不会对她做任何事。我不会让他这么做的。”

paragraphs.en: “But on Sunday morning, in my own house,” Mrs Compson said, “When I’ve tried so hard to raise them Christians. Let me find the right key, Jason,” she said. She put her hand on his arm. Then she began to struggle with him, but he flung her aside with a motion of his elbow and looked around at her for a moment, his eyes cold and harried, then he turned to the door again and the unwieldy keys.
paragraphs.zh: “但是周日早上，在我自己家里，”康普生夫人说，“当我竭尽全力把他们培养成基督徒时。让我找到正确的钥匙，杰生，”她说。她把手放在他的手臂上。然后她开始与他挣扎，但他用手肘一挥，把她推到一边，环视了她一会儿，目光冰冷而忙碌，然后他又转向门和笨重的钥匙。

paragraphs.en: “Hush,” Dilsey said, “You, Jason!”
paragraphs.zh: “嘘，”迪尔西说，“你，杰生！”

paragraphs.en: “Something terrible has happened,” Mrs Compson said, wailing again, “I know it has. You, Jason,” she said, grasping at him again. “He wont even let me find the key to a room in my own house!”
paragraphs.zh: “发生了可怕的事情，”康普生夫人再次哭泣，“我知道发生了。你，杰生，”她说，再次抓住了他。“他连我自己家里房间的钥匙都不让我找到！”

paragraphs.en: “Now, now,” Dilsey said, “Whut kin happen? I right here. I aint gwine let him hurt her. Quentin,” she said, raising her voice, “dont you be skeered, honey, I’se right here.”
paragraphs.zh: “现在，现在，”迪尔西说，“发生什么事了？我就在这里。我不会让他伤害她。昆丁，”她提高了声音说，“亲爱的，你别生气，我就在这里。”

paragraphs.en: The door opened, swung inward. He stood in it for a moment, hiding the room, then he stepped aside. “Go in,” he said in a thick, light voice. They went in. It was not a girl’s room. It was not anybody’s room, and the faint scent of cheap cosmetics and the few feminine objects and the other evidences of crude and hopeless efforts to feminize it but added to its anonymity, giving it that dead and stereotyped transience of rooms in assignation houses. The bed had not been disturbed. On the floor lay a soiled undergarment of cheap silk a little too pink; from a half open bureau drawer dangled a single stocking. The window was open. A pear tree grew there, close against the house. It was in bloom and the branches scraped and rasped against the house and the myriad air, driving in the window, brought into the room the forlorn scent of the blossoms.
paragraphs.zh: 门打开了，向内转动。他在里面站了一会儿，把房间藏起来，然后退到一边。“进去吧。”他用低沉而轻盈的声音说道。他们进去了。这不是女孩的房间。这不是任何人的房间，廉价化妆品的淡淡气味和为数不多的女性物品以及其他粗暴而无望的女性化努力的证据，但增加了它的匿名性，赋予它死气沉沉和刻板的转瞬即逝的分配房屋的房间。床没有被打扰。地板上放着一件脏兮兮的廉价丝绸内衣，颜色有点太粉红了。半开的抽屉里挂着一只袜子。窗户是开着的。那里长着一棵梨树，靠近房子。正值花开之际，树枝刮擦着房子，无数的空气从窗户吹进来，把花朵凄凉的香味带进房间。

paragraphs.en: “Dar now,” Dilsey said, “Didn’t I told you she all right?”
paragraphs.zh: “现在，”迪尔西说，“我不是告诉过你她没事吗？”

paragraphs.en: “All right?” Mrs Compson said. Dilsey followed her into the room and touched her.
paragraphs.zh: “好吧？”康普生夫人说道。迪尔西跟着她进了房间，抚摸着她。

paragraphs.en: “You come on and lay down, now,” she said. “I find her in ten minutes.”
paragraphs.zh: “现在你过来躺下，”她说。“十分钟后我就能找到她了。”

paragraphs.en: Mrs Compson shook her off. “Find the note,” she said. “Quentin left a note when he did it.”
paragraphs.zh: 康普生夫人甩开了她。“找到纸条，”她说。“昆丁做的时候留下了一张纸条。”

paragraphs.en: “All right,” Dilsey said, “I’ll find hit. You come on to yo room, now.”
paragraphs.zh: “好吧，”迪尔西说，“我会找到办法的。你现在就到你的房间去吧。”

paragraphs.en: “I knew the minute they named her Quentin this would happen,” Mrs Compson said. She went to the bureau and began to turn over the scattered objects there—scent bottles, a box of powder, a chewed pencil, a pair of scissors with one broken blade lying upon a darned scarf dusted with powder and stained with rouge. “Find the note,” she said.
paragraphs.zh: “从他们给她取名昆丁的那一刻起，我就知道这会发生，”康普生女士说。她走到写字台前，开始翻动那里散落的东西——香水瓶、一盒粉末、一支被咀嚼过的铅笔、一把剪刀，剪刀的刀片已经折断，放在一条沾满粉末和胭脂的破旧围巾上。“找到纸条，”她说。

paragraphs.en: “I is,” Dilsey said. “You come on, now. Me and Jason’ll find hit. You come on to yo room.”
paragraphs.zh: “我是，”迪尔西说。“现在你来吧。我和杰生会受到打击的。你到你的房间来。”

paragraphs.en: “Jason,” Mrs Compson said, “Where is he?” She went to the door. Dilsey followed her on down the hall, to another door. It was closed. “Jason,” she called through the door. There was no answer. She tried the knob, then she called him again. But there was still no answer, for he was hurling things backward out of the closet: garments, shoes, a suitcase. Then he emerged carrying a sawn section of tongue-and-groove planking and laid it down and entered the closet again and emerged with a metal box. He set it on the bed and stood looking at the broken lock while he dug a key ring from his pocket and selected a key, and for a time longer he stood with the selected key in his hand, looking at the broken lock, then he put the keys back in his pocket and carefully tilted the contents of the box out upon the bed. Still carefully he sorted the papers, taking them up one at a time and shaking them. Then he upended the box and shook it too and slowly replaced the papers and stood again, looking at the broken lock, with the box in his hands and his head bent. Outside the window he heard some jaybirds swirl shrieking past, and away, their cries whipping away along the wind, and an automobile passed somewhere and died away also. His mother spoke his name again beyond the door, but he didn’t move. He heard Dilsey lead her away up the hall, and then a door closed. Then he replaced the box in the closet and flung the garments back into it and went down stairs to the telephone. While he stood there with the receiver to his ear, waiting, Dilsey came down the stairs. She looked at him, without stopping, and went on.
paragraphs.zh: “杰生，”康普生太太说，“他在哪儿？”她走到门口。迪尔西跟着她穿过大厅，来到另一扇门前。它已经关门了。“杰生。”她在门外喊道。没有人回答。她试了一下门把手，然后又给他打电话。但仍然没有回应，因为他正把衣柜里的东西往后扔：衣服、鞋子、手提箱。然后他拿着一块锯好的榫槽木板出来，把它放下，再次进入壁橱，带着一个金属盒子出来。他把它放在床上，站着看着那把坏了的锁，同时从口袋里掏出一个钥匙圈，选了一把钥匙，又拿着选定的钥匙站了一会儿，看着那把坏了的锁，然后他把钥匙放回口袋里，小心翼翼地把盒子里的东西倒在床上。他仍然小心翼翼地将文件分类，一次拿起一张并摇晃它们。然后他把盒子倒过来，也摇了摇，慢慢地把文件放回原处，再次站起来，手里拿着盒子，低着头，看着那把坏了的锁。窗外，他听到一些松鸦尖叫着盘旋而过，然后飞走了，它们的叫声随风而去，一辆汽车从某处驶过，也消失了。他的母亲在门外再次叫了他的名字，但他没有动。他听到迪尔西领着她走上大厅，然后门关上了。然后他把盒子放回衣柜里，把衣服扔回里面，然后下楼去接电话。当他把听筒放在耳边等待时，迪尔西走下楼梯。她看了他一眼，没有停下，继续说道。

paragraphs.en: The wire opened. “This is Jason Compson,” he said, his voice so harsh and thick that he had to repeat himself. “Jason Compson,” he said, controlling his voice. “Have a car ready, with a deputy, if you cant go, in ten minutes. I’ll be there—What?—Robbery. My house. I know who it—Robbery, I say. Have a car read—What? Aren’t you a paid law enforcement—Yes, I’ll be there in five minutes. Have that car ready to leave at once. If you dont, I’ll report it to the governor.”
paragraphs.zh: 电线打开了。“这是杰生康普生，”他说，他的声音如此刺耳而粗重，以至于他不得不重复一遍。“杰生康普生，”他控制着自己的声音说道。“准备一辆汽车，如果你不能去的话，十分钟内。我会在那里——什么？——抢劫。我的房子。我知道是谁——抢劫，我说。让车读一下——什么？你不是受薪的执法人员吗——是的，我五分钟后就到了。让那辆车准备好立即离开。如果你不这样做，我会向州长报告。”

paragraphs.en: He clapped the receiver back and crossed the diningroom, where the scarce-broken meal now lay cold on the table, and entered the kitchen. Dilsey was filling the hot water bottle. Ben sat, tranquil and empty. Beside him Luster looked like a fice dog, brightly watchful. He was eating something. Jason went on across the kitchen.
paragraphs.zh: 他拍了一下听筒，穿过餐厅，几乎没有破碎的饭菜现在已经冷在桌子上，然后走进厨房。迪尔西正在给热水袋注水。本坐着，平静而空虚。在他身边，勒斯特看起来就像一只办公室狗，神情警惕。他正在吃东西。杰生继续穿过厨房。

paragraphs.en: “Aint you going to eat no breakfast?” Dilsey said. He paid her no attention. “Go on and eat yo breakfast, Jason.” He went on. The outer door banged behind him. Luster rose and went to the window and looked out.
paragraphs.zh: “你不吃早餐吗？”迪尔西说道。他没有理睬她。“杰生，去吃早饭吧。”他继续说下去。外门在他身后砰地一声关上。勒斯特站起身来，走到窗前向外看去。

paragraphs.en: “Whoo,” he said, “Whut happenin up dar? He been beatin’ Miss Quentin?”
paragraphs.zh: “哎哟，”他说，“怎么了？他打昆丁小姐了？”

paragraphs.en: “You hush yo mouf,” Dilsey said. “You git Benjy started now en I beat yo head off. You keep him quiet es you kin twell I get back, now.” She screwed the cap on the bottle and went out. They heard her go up the stairs, then they heard Jason pass the house in his car. Then there was no sound in the kitchen save the simmering murmur of the kettle and the clock.
paragraphs.zh: “你别出声，”迪尔西说。“你现在就开始班吉，我把你打得落花流水。你让他安静，我现在就回来。”她拧紧瓶盖，然后出去了。他们听到她上楼的声音，然后听到杰生开着车经过房子。然后厨房里就没有任何声音了，只有水壶和钟表沸腾的声音。

paragraphs.en: “You know whut I bet?” Luster said. “I bet he beat her. I bet he knock her in de head en now he gone fer de doctor. Dat’s whut I bet.” The clock tick-tocked, solemn and profound. It might have been the dry pulse of the decaying house itself; after a while it whirred and cleared its throat and struck six times. Ben looked up at it, then he looked at the bullet-like silhouette of Luster’s head in the window and he begun to bob his head again, drooling. He whimpered.
paragraphs.zh: “你知道我赌什么吗？”勒斯特说。“我打赌他打败了她。我打赌他把她的头撞到了，现在他去找医生了。我打赌就是这样。”时钟滴答作响，庄严而深邃。这可能是腐烂的房子本身的干燥脉动；过了一会儿，它发出呼呼声，清了清喉咙，敲击了六下。本抬头看了看，然后又看了看窗外勒斯特头部如子弹般的轮廓，他又开始摇头，流着口水。他呜咽着。

paragraphs.en: “Hush up, loony,” Luster said without turning. “Look like we aint gwine git to go to no church today.” But Ben sat in the chair, his big soft hands dangling between his knees, moaning faintly. Suddenly he wept, a slow bellowing sound, meaningless and sustained. “Hush,” Luster said. He turned and lifted his hand. “You want me to whup you?” But Ben looked at him, bellowing slowly with each expiration. Luster came and shook him. “You hush dis minute!” he shouted. “Here,” he said. He hauled Ben out of the chair and dragged the chair around facing the stove and opened the door to the firebox and shoved Ben into the chair. They looked like a tug nudging at a clumsy tanker in a narrow dock. Ben sat down again facing the rosy door. He hushed. Then they heard the clock again, and Dilsey slow on the stairs. When she entered he began to whimper again. Then he lifted his voice.
paragraphs.zh: “闭嘴，疯子，”勒斯特没有转身说道。“看来我们今天不去教堂了。”但本坐在椅子上，柔软的大手悬在膝盖之间，微弱地呻吟着。突然他哭了起来，声音缓慢而持续，毫无意义。“嘘，”勒斯特说。他转身举起了手。“你想让我打你吗？”但本看着他，每次呼气时都缓慢地吼叫。勒斯特过来摇晃他。“你安静点！”他喊道。“在这里，”他说。他把本从椅子上拖起来，把椅子拖到炉子对面，打开火箱的门，把本推到椅子上。它们看起来就像一艘拖船在狭窄的码头上推着一艘笨拙的油轮。本恩再次面向玫瑰色的门坐下。他沉默了。然后他们又听到了时钟的声音，迪尔西缓慢地走上楼梯。当她进来时，他又开始抽泣。然后他提高了声音。

paragraphs.en: “Whut you done to him?” Dilsey said. “Why cant you let him lone dis mawnin, of all times?”
paragraphs.zh: “你对他做了什么？”迪尔西说道。“为什么你不能让他一个人呆着，无论何时？”

paragraphs.en: “I aint doin nothin to him,” Luster said. “Mr Jason skeered him, dat’s whut hit is. He aint kilt Miss Quentin, is he?”
paragraphs.zh: “我没有对他做什么，”勒斯特说。“杰生先生踢了他一脚，这才是重点。他该不会是跟昆丁小姐打过交道吧？”
