paragraphs.en: “Hush, Benjy,” Dilsey said. He hushed. She went to the window and looked out. “Is it quit rainin?” she said.
paragraphs.zh: “嘘，班吉，”迪尔西说。他沉默了。她走到窗前向外看去。“雨停了吗？”她说。

paragraphs.en: “Yessum,” Luster said. “Quit long time ago.”
paragraphs.zh: “是的，”勒斯特说。“很久以前就戒掉了。”

paragraphs.en: “Den y’all go out do’s awhile,” she said. “I jes got Miss Cahline quiet now.”
paragraphs.zh: “你们都出去玩一会儿吧，”她说。“我现在已经让卡琳小姐安静了。”

paragraphs.en: “Is we gwine to church?” Luster said.
paragraphs.zh: “我们要去教堂吗？”勒斯特说。

paragraphs.en: “I let you know bout dat when de time come. You keep him away fum de house twell I calls you.”
paragraphs.zh: “到时候我会让你知道的。我打电话给你之前，你让他远离家里。”

paragraphs.en: “Kin we go to de pastuh?” Luster said.
paragraphs.zh: “我们可以去德巴斯图吗？”勒斯特说。

paragraphs.en: “All right. Only you keep him away fum de house. I done stood all I kin.”
paragraphs.zh: “好吧。只要你别让他进屋子。我所有的亲人都受不了了。”

paragraphs.en: “Yessum,” Luster said. “Whar Mr Jason gone, mammy?”
paragraphs.zh: “是的，”勒斯特说。“妈妈，杰生先生去哪儿了？”

paragraphs.en: “Dat’s some mo of yo business, aint it?” Dilsey said. She began to clear the table. “Hush, Benjy. Luster gwine take you out to play.”
paragraphs.zh: “那是你的事，不是吗？”迪尔西说道。她开始清理桌子。“嘘，班吉。勒斯特格温带你出去玩。”

paragraphs.en: “Whut he done to Miss Quentin, mammy?” Luster said.
paragraphs.zh: “妈咪，他对昆丁小姐做了什么？”勒斯特说。

paragraphs.en: “Aint done nothin to her. You all git on outen here?”
paragraphs.zh: “没有对她做什么。你们都在这儿混吗？”

paragraphs.en: “I bet she aint here,” Luster said.
paragraphs.zh: “我敢打赌她不在这里，”勒斯特说。

paragraphs.en: Dilsey looked at him. “How you know she aint here?”
paragraphs.zh: 迪尔西看着他。“你怎么知道她不在这里？”

paragraphs.en: “Me and Benjy seed her clamb out de window last night. Didn’t us, Benjy?”
paragraphs.zh: “昨晚我和班吉发现她从窗户爬了出去。不是吗，班吉？”

paragraphs.en: “You did?” Dilsey said, looking at him.
paragraphs.zh: “你做到了？”迪尔西看着他说道。

paragraphs.en: “We sees her doin hit ev’y night,” Luster said, “Clamb right down dat pear tree.”
paragraphs.zh: “我们每天晚上都看到她的所作所为，”勒斯特说，“从那棵梨树上爬下来。”

paragraphs.en: “Dont you lie to me, nigger boy,” Dilsey said.
paragraphs.zh: “你别对我撒谎，黑鬼小子，”迪尔西说。

paragraphs.en: “I aint lyin. Ask Benjy ef I is.”
paragraphs.zh: “我没有说谎。如果我是的话，去问班吉吧。”

paragraphs.en: “Whyn’t you say somethin about it, den?”
paragraphs.zh: “你为什么不说点什么呢，丹恩？”

paragraphs.en: “’Twarn’t none o my business,” Luster said. “I aint gwine git mixed up in white folks’ business. Come on here, Benjy, les go out do’s.”
paragraphs.zh: “别打扰我的事，”勒斯特说。“我不参与白人的事。来吧，班吉，我们出去吧。”

paragraphs.en: They went out. Dilsey stood for awhile at the table, then she went and cleared the breakfast things from the diningroom and ate her breakfast and cleaned up the kitchen. Then she removed her apron and hung it up and went to the foot of the stairs and listened for a moment. There was no sound. She donned the overcoat and the hat and went across to her cabin.
paragraphs.zh: 他们出去了。迪尔西在桌边站了一会儿，然后去把餐厅里的早餐用品收拾干净，吃完早餐，又把厨房打扫干净。然后她脱下围裙，挂起来，走到楼梯口听了一会儿。没有声音。她穿上大衣，戴上帽子，走进自己的小屋。

paragraphs.en: The rain had stopped. The air now drove out of the southeast, broken overhead into blue patches. Upon the crest of a hill beyond the trees and roofs and spires of town sunlight lay like a pale scrap of cloth, was blotted away. Upon the air a bell came, then as if at a signal, other bells took up the sound and repeated it.
paragraphs.zh: 雨已经停了。空气现在从东南方向吹出，在头顶上分裂成蓝色的斑块。在树木、屋顶和尖塔之外的山顶上，城镇的阳光像一块苍白的布片一样，被遮蔽了。空中传来一声钟声，然后就像收到信号一样，其他钟声也跟着响了起来并重复了一遍。

paragraphs.en: The cabin door opened and Dilsey emerged, again in the maroon cape and the purple gown, and wearing soiled white elbow-length gloves and minus her headcloth now. She came into the yard and called Luster. She waited awhile, then she went to the house and around it to the cellar door, moving close to the wall, and looked into the door. Ben sat on the steps. Before him Luster squatted on the damp floor. He held a saw in his left hand, the blade sprung a little by pressure of his hand, and he was in the act of striking the blade with the worn wooden mallet with which she had been making beaten biscuit for more than thirty years. The saw gave forth a single sluggish twang that ceased with lifeless alacrity, leaving the blade in a thin clean curve between Luster’s hand and the floor. Still, inscrutable, it bellied.
paragraphs.zh: 舱门打开，迪尔西出现了，她再次穿着栗色斗篷和紫色长袍，戴着脏兮兮的白色肘长手套，现在没有戴头巾。她走进院子，打电话给勒斯特。她等了一会儿，然后走到房子前，绕过地窖门，靠近墙壁，向门内看去。本坐在台阶上。勒斯特蹲在他面前潮湿的地板上。他左手握着一把锯子，手一用力，锯片就弹起一点，他正用她三十多年来用来打饼干的破旧木槌敲击锯片。锯子发出一声迟缓的声响，随后又毫无生气地迅速停止，锯片在勒斯特的手和地板之间留下了一条细细的、干净的曲线。尽管如此，它仍然令人费解，它鼓起肚子来。

paragraphs.en: “Dat’s de way he done hit,” Luster said. “I jes aint foun de right thing to hit it wid.”
paragraphs.zh: “他就是这样击球的，”勒斯特说。“我找不到合适的东西来击中它。”

paragraphs.en: “Dat’s whut you doin, is it?” Dilsey said. “Bring me dat mallet,” she said.
paragraphs.zh: “这就是你所做的，是吗？”迪尔西说道。“把那把木槌给我拿来，”她说。

paragraphs.en: “I aint hurt hit,” Luster said.
paragraphs.zh: “我没有受伤，”勒斯特说。

paragraphs.en: “Bring hit here,” Dilsey said. “Put dat saw whar you got hit first.”
paragraphs.zh: “来这里打吧，”迪尔西说道。“把它放在你最先被击中的地方。”

paragraphs.en: He put the saw away and brought the mallet to her. Then Ben wailed again, hopeless and prolonged. It was nothing. Just sound. It might have been all time and injustice and sorrow become vocal for an instant by a conjunction of planets.
paragraphs.zh: 他把锯子收起来，把木槌拿给她。然后本又哭了，绝望而长久。没什么。只是声音。也许一直以来，不公正和悲伤都因为行星的合相而瞬间变得大声起来。

paragraphs.en: “Listen at him,” Luster said, “He been gwine on dat way ev’y since you sont us outen de house. I dont know whut got in to him dis mawnin.”
paragraphs.zh: “听他说，”勒斯特说，“自从你把我们送出家门以来，他就一直在路上。我不知道他怎么了。”

paragraphs.en: “Bring him here,” Dilsey said.
paragraphs.zh: “把他带到这里来，”迪尔西说道。

paragraphs.en: “Come on, Benjy,” Luster said. He went back down the steps and took Ben’s arm. He came obediently, wailing, that slow hoarse sound that ships make, that seems to begin before the sound itself has started, seems to cease before the sound itself has stopped.
paragraphs.zh: “来吧，班吉，”勒斯特说。他走下台阶，挽起本的手臂。他顺从地来了，哀嚎着，船发出的那种缓慢而嘶哑的声音，似乎在声音本身开始之前就开始了，又似乎在声音本身停止之前就停止了。

paragraphs.en: “Run and git his cap,” Dilsey said. “Dont make no noise Miss Cahline kin hear. Hurry, now. We already late.”
paragraphs.zh: “跑去拿帽子，”迪尔西说。“别出声，卡琳小姐你能听见。快点，我们已经迟到了。”

paragraphs.en: “She gwine hear him anyhow, ef you dont stop him.” Luster said.
paragraphs.zh: “无论如何，如果你不阻止他，她就会听到他的声音。”勒斯特说。

paragraphs.en: “He stop when we git off de place,” Dilsey said. “He smellin hit. Dat’s whut hit is.”
paragraphs.zh: “当我们下车时，他停了下来，”迪尔西说。“他闻到了命中的味道。命中就是这样。”

paragraphs.en: “Smell whut, mammy?” Luster said.
paragraphs.zh: “闻什么味道，妈妈？”勒斯特说。

paragraphs.en: “You go git dat cap,” Dilsey said. Luster went on. They stood in the cellar door, Ben one step below her. The sky was broken now into scudding patches that dragged their swift shadows up out of the shabby garden, over the broken fence and across the yard. Dilsey stroked Ben’s head, slowly and steadily, smoothing the bang upon his brow. He wailed quietly, unhurriedly. “Hush,” Dilsey said, “Hush, now. We be gone in a minute. Hush, now.” He wailed quietly and steadily.
paragraphs.zh: “你去戴上帽子吧，”迪尔西说。勒斯特继续说道。他们站在地窖门口，本比她低一步。天空现在裂成碎片，拖着它们快速的影子从破旧的花园里爬出来，越过破碎的栅栏，穿过院子。迪尔西缓慢而稳定地抚摸着本的头，抚平他额头上的刘海。他低声哀嚎，不紧不慢。“嘘，”迪尔西说，“嘘，现在。我们一会儿就走。嘘，现在。”他低声地、稳定地哀号着。

paragraphs.en: Luster returned, wearing a stiff new straw hat with a coloured band and carrying a cloth cap. The hat seemed to isolate Luster’s skull, in the beholder’s eye as a spotlight would, in all its individual planes and angles. So peculiarly individual was its shape that at first glance the hat appeared to be on the head of someone standing immediately behind Luster. Dilsey looked at the hat.
paragraphs.zh: 勒斯特回来了，戴着一顶硬邦邦的新草帽，上面有彩色带子，戴着一顶布帽。在旁观者看来，这顶帽子似乎将勒斯特的头骨隔离开来，就像聚光灯一样，在各个平面和角度上。它的形状非常独特，乍一看，这顶帽子似乎戴在勒斯特身后某个人的头上。迪尔西看着帽子。

paragraphs.en: “Whyn’t you wear yo old hat?” she said.
paragraphs.zh: “你为什么不戴那顶旧帽子？”她说。

paragraphs.en: “Couldn’t find hit,” Luster said.
paragraphs.zh: “找不到命中，”勒斯特说。

paragraphs.en: “I bet you couldn’t. I bet you fixed hit last night so you couldn’t find hit. You fixin to ruin dat un.”
paragraphs.zh: “我打赌你不能。我打赌你昨晚修复了命中，所以你找不到命中。你修复了这个目标。”

paragraphs.en: “Aw, mammy,” Luster said, “Hit aint gwine rain.”
paragraphs.zh: “噢，妈妈，”勒斯特说，“下雨了。”

paragraphs.en: “How you know? You go git dat old hat en put dat new un away.”
paragraphs.zh: “你怎么知道？你把旧帽子收起来，把新帽子收起来。”

paragraphs.en: “Aw, mammy.”
paragraphs.zh: “噢，妈妈。”

paragraphs.en: “Den you go git de umbreller.”
paragraphs.zh: “你去拿伞吧。”

paragraphs.en: “Aw, mammy.”
paragraphs.zh: “噢，妈妈。”

paragraphs.en: “Take yo choice,” Dilsey said. “Git yo old hat, er de umbreller. I dont keer which.”
paragraphs.zh: “你自己选择吧，”迪尔西说。“你这老帽子，呃，雨伞人。我不喜欢哪个。”

paragraphs.en: Luster went to the cabin. Ben wailed quietly.
paragraphs.zh: 勒斯特走向小屋。本小声地哭了。

paragraphs.en: “Come on,” Dilsey said, “Dey kin ketch up wid us. We gwine to hear de singin.” They went around the house, toward the gate. “Hush,” Dilsey said from time to time as they went down the drive. They reached the gate. Dilsey opened it. Luster was coming down the drive behind them, carrying the umbrella. A woman was with him. “Here dey come,” Dilsey said. They passed out the gate. “Now, den,” she said. Ben ceased. Luster and his mother overtook them. Frony wore a dress of bright blue silk and a flowered hat. She was a thin woman, with a flat, pleasant face.
paragraphs.zh: “来吧，”迪尔西说，“他们会和我们一起上船。我们要听歌。”他们绕过房子，朝大门走去。“嘘，”他们沿着车道行驶时，迪尔西不时说道。他们到达了大门。迪尔西打开了它。勒斯特撑着雨伞从他们身后的车道走下来。一个女人和他在一起。“他们来了，”迪尔西说。他们走出了大门。“现在，书房，”她说。本停了下来。勒斯特和他的母亲追上了他们。弗罗妮穿着一件亮蓝色丝绸连衣裙，戴着一顶花帽。她是个瘦削的女人，有一张平坦而可爱的脸。

paragraphs.en: “You got six weeks’ work right dar on yo back,” Dilsey said. “Whut you gwine do ef hit rain?”
paragraphs.zh: “你已经完成了六周的工作了，”迪尔西说。“你怎么会下雨呢？”

paragraphs.en: “Git wet, I reckon,” Frony said. “I aint never stopped no rain yit.”
paragraphs.zh: “我想，湿透了，”弗罗妮说。“我从来没有停止过雨。”

paragraphs.en: “Mammy always talkin bout hit gwine rain,” Luster said.
paragraphs.zh: “妈妈总是谈论下雨，”勒斯特说。

paragraphs.en: “Ef I dont worry bout y’all, I dont know who is,” Dilsey said. “Come on, we already late.”
paragraphs.zh: “如果我不担心你们，我不知道是谁，”迪尔西说。“快点吧，我们已经迟到了。”

paragraphs.en: “Rev’un Shegog gwine preach today,” Frony said.
paragraphs.zh: “谢戈格牧师今天讲道，”弗罗妮说。

paragraphs.en: “Is?” Dilsey said. “Who him?”
paragraphs.zh: “是吗？”迪尔西说道。“他是谁？”

paragraphs.en: “He fum Saint Looey,” Frony said. “Dat big preacher.”
paragraphs.zh: “他对圣卢伊发脾气，”弗罗妮说。“那个大传教士。”

paragraphs.en: “Huh,” Dilsey said, “Whut dey needs is a man kin put de fear of God into dese here triflin young niggers.”
paragraphs.zh: “哈，”迪尔西说，“他们需要的是一个能够让这里的年轻黑鬼们敬畏上帝的人。”

paragraphs.en: “Rev’un Shegog gwine preach today,” Frony said. “So dey tells.”
paragraphs.zh: “谢戈格牧师今天讲道，”弗罗妮说。“他们是这么说的。”

paragraphs.en: They went on along the street. Along its quiet length white people in bright clumps moved churchward, under the windy bells, walking now and then in the random and tentative sun. The wind was gusty, out of the southeast, chill and raw after the warm days.
paragraphs.zh: 他们沿着街道继续前行。沿着安静的长度，白人成群结队地在风铃下朝教堂走去，时不时地在随机而试探性的阳光下行走。风从东南吹来，一阵阵阵阵阵阵阵风，带着温暖的日子过后的寒冷和刺骨的感觉。

paragraphs.en: “I wish you wouldn’t keep on bringin him to church, mammy,” Frony said. “Folks talkin.”
paragraphs.zh: “我希望你不要继续带他去教堂，妈妈，”弗罗妮说。“人们在说话。”

paragraphs.en: “Whut folks?” Dilsey said.
paragraphs.zh: “什么？伙计们？”迪尔西说道。

paragraphs.en: “I hears em,” Frony said.
paragraphs.zh: “我听到了，”弗罗妮说。

paragraphs.en: “And I knows whut kind of folks,” Dilsey said, “Trash white folks. Dat’s who it is. Thinks he aint good enough fer white church, but nigger church aint good enough fer him.”
paragraphs.zh: “我知道什么样的人，”迪尔西说，“垃圾白人。他们就是这样的人。认为他对白人教会不够好，但黑人教会对他来说不够好。”

paragraphs.en: “Dey talks, jes de same,” Frony said.
paragraphs.zh: “他们会说话，他们是一样的，”弗罗妮说。

paragraphs.en: “Den you send um to me,” Dilsey said. “Tell um de good Lawd dont keer whether he smart er not. Dont nobody but white trash keer dat.”
paragraphs.zh: “你把嗯发给我，”迪尔西说。“告诉好心的劳德，不要关心他是否聪明。除了白人垃圾之外，没有人会关心这一点。”

paragraphs.en: A street turned oil at right angles, descending, and became a dirt road. On either hand the land dropped more sharply; a broad flat dotted with small cabins whose weathered roofs were on a level with the crown of the road. They were set in small grassless plots littered with broken things, bricks, planks, crockery, things of a once utilitarian value. What growth there was consisted of rank weeds and the trees were mulberries and locusts and sycamores—trees that partook also of the foul desiccation which surrounded the houses; trees whose very burgeoning seemed to be the sad and stubborn remnant of September, as if even spring had passed them by, leaving them to feed upon the rich and unmistakable smell of negroes in which they grew.
paragraphs.zh: 一条街道变成了直角，向下倾斜，变成了一条土路。两边的土地下降得更厉害。宽阔的平地上散布着一些小木屋，它们饱经风霜的屋顶与路顶齐平。它们坐落在没有草的小地上，散落着破碎的东西、砖块、木板、陶器，以及曾经具有实用价值的东西。那里长满了杂草，树木是桑葚、蝗虫和无花果树——这些树也遭受了房屋周围恶臭干燥的影响。这些树木的蓬勃发展似乎是九月悲伤而顽固的残余，仿佛连春天都已经过去了，让它们以生长在其中的黑人浓郁而明确的气味为食。

paragraphs.en: From the doors negroes spoke to them as they passed, to Dilsey usually:
paragraphs.zh: 当他们经过时，黑人从门口对他们说话，通常是对迪尔西：

paragraphs.en: “Sis’ Gibson! How you dis mawnin?”
paragraphs.zh: “吉布森姐姐！你怎么样？”

paragraphs.en: “I’m well. Is you well?”
paragraphs.zh: “我很好。你还好吗？”

paragraphs.en: “I’m right well, I thank you.”
paragraphs.zh: “我很好，谢谢你。”

paragraphs.en: They emerged from the cabins and struggled up the shading levee to the road-men in staid, hard brown or black, with gold watch chains and now and then a stick; young men in cheap violent blues or stripes and swaggering hats; women a little stiffly sibilant, and children in garments bought second hand of white people, who looked at Ben with the covertness of nocturnal animals:
paragraphs.zh: 他们从小屋里出来，艰难地爬上遮荫的堤坝，来到修路人那里，他们穿着古板的硬棕色或黑色衣服，戴着金表链，时不时还拿着一根棍子。穿着廉价、暴力的蓝色或条纹衣服、戴着招摇的帽子的年轻人；女人们发出有点僵硬的嘶嘶声，穿着衣服的孩子们买了白人的二手货，他们用夜行动物般的狡猾眼神看着本：

paragraphs.en: “I bet you wont go up en tech him.”
paragraphs.zh: “我打赌你不会去科技他。”

paragraphs.en: “How come I wont?”
paragraphs.zh: “我怎么不肯呢？”

paragraphs.en: “I bet you wont. I bet you skeered to.”
paragraphs.zh: “我打赌你不会。我打赌你一定会这么做。”

paragraphs.en: “He wont hurt folks. He des a loony.”
paragraphs.zh: “他不会伤害别人。他是个疯子。”

paragraphs.en: “How come a loony wont hurt folks?”
paragraphs.zh: “疯子怎么不会伤害人呢？”

paragraphs.en: “Dat un wont. I teched him.”
paragraphs.zh: “那是不会的。我技术过他。”

paragraphs.en: “I bet you wont now.”
paragraphs.zh: “我打赌你现在不会了。”

paragraphs.en: “Case Miss Dilsey lookin.”
paragraphs.zh: “迪尔西小姐正在看。”

paragraphs.en: “You wont no ways.”
paragraphs.zh: “你没有办法。”

paragraphs.en: “He dont hurt folks. He des a loony.”
paragraphs.zh: “他不会伤害别人。他是个疯子。”

paragraphs.en: And steadily the older people speaking to Dilsey, though, unless they were quite old, Dilsey permitted Frony to respond.
paragraphs.zh: 渐渐地，老年人与迪尔西说话，除非他们已经很老了，否则迪尔西允许弗罗妮回应。

paragraphs.en: “Mammy aint feelin well dis mawnin.”
paragraphs.zh: “妈妈今天睡着了，感觉不太舒服。”

paragraphs.en: “Dat’s too bad. But Rev’un Shegog’ll cure dat. He’ll give her de comfort en de unburdenin.”
paragraphs.zh: “这太糟糕了。但谢戈格牧师会治愈这个问题。他会给她安慰和减轻负担。”

paragraphs.en: The road rose again, to a scene like a painted backdrop. Notched into a cut of red clay crowned with oaks the road appeared to stop short off, like a cut ribbon. Beside it a weathered church lifted its crazy steeple like a painted church, and the whole scene was as flat and without perspective as a painted cardboard set upon the ultimate edge of the flat earth, against the windy sunlight of space and April and a midmorning filled with bells. Toward the church they thronged with slow sabbath deliberation. The women and children went on in, the men stopped outside and talked in quiet groups until the bell ceased ringing. Then they too entered.
paragraphs.zh: 道路再次上升，呈现出一幅如彩绘背景般的景象。这条路在红粘土上开出一道缺口，上面长满了橡树，这条路似乎突然停了下来，就像一条剪断的丝带。在它旁边，一座饱经风霜的教堂耸立着疯狂的尖塔，就像一座彩绘教堂，整个场景就像一块彩绘纸板一样平坦，没有透视性，放置在平坦地球的最终边缘上，映衬着太空和四月的风和阳光，以及充满钟声的上午。他们涌向教堂，在安息日缓慢地商议。妇女和儿童继续进去，男人们在外面停下来，三五成群地小声交谈，直到铃声停止。然后他们也进去了。

paragraphs.en: The church had been decorated, with sparse flowers from kitchen gardens and hedgerows, and with streamers of coloured crepe paper. Above the pulpit hung a battered Christmas bell, the accordian sort that collapses. The pulpit was empty, though the choir was already in place, fanning themselves although it was not warm.
paragraphs.zh: 教堂里装饰着来自菜园和树篱的稀疏花朵，还有彩色皱纹纸的飘带。讲坛上方挂着一个破旧的圣诞钟声，是那种会倒塌的手风琴式的钟声。讲坛上空无一人，但唱诗班已经就位，虽然天气不热，但正在扇着扇子。

paragraphs.en: Most of the women were gathered on one side of the room. They were talking. Then the bell struck one time and they dispersed to their seats and the congregation sat for an instant, expectant. The bell struck again one time. The choir rose and began to sing and the congregation turned its head as one, as six small children—four girls with tight pigtails bound with small scraps of cloth like butterflies, and two boys with close napped heads,—entered and marched up the aisle, strung together in a harness of white ribbons and flowers, and followed by two men in single file. The second man was huge, of a light coffee colour, imposing in a frock coat and white tie. His head was magisterial and profound, his neck rolled above his collar in rich folds. But he was familiar to them, and so the heads were still reverted when he had passed, and it was not until the choir ceased singing that they realised that the visiting clergyman had already entered, and when they saw the man who had preceded their minister enter the pulpit still ahead of him an indescribable sound went up, a sigh, a sound of astonishment and disappointment.
paragraphs.zh: 大多数妇女聚集在房间的一侧。他们正在说话。然后铃声响起，他们分散到各自的座位上，会众坐了一会儿，满怀期待。钟声又敲响了一次。唱诗班起身开始唱歌，会众齐齐转过头来，六个小孩子——四个女孩扎着辫子，像蝴蝶一样用小布片绑着，两个男孩把头紧紧地扎在一起——走进来，沿着过道走，他们被一束白色丝带和鲜花串在一起，后面跟着两个男人排成一列。第二个男人身材高大，皮肤呈浅咖啡色，穿着长袍，系着白色领带，气势磅礴。他的头威严而深邃，脖子上的衣领上方有丰富的褶皱。但他对他们来说很熟悉，所以当他经过时，他们的头仍然转了回来，直到唱诗班停止歌唱，他们才意识到来访的牧师已经进来了，当他们看到在他们的牧师之前进入讲坛的那个人仍然在他前面时，一种难以形容的声音响起，一声叹息，一种惊讶和失望的声音。

paragraphs.en: The visitor was undersized, in a shabby alpaca coat. He had a wizened black face like a small, aged monkey. And all the while that the choir sang again and while the six children rose and sang in thin, frightened, tuneless whispers, they watched the insignificant looking man sitting dwarfed and countrified by the minister’s imposing bulk, with something like consternation. They were still looking at him with consternation and unbelief when the minister rose and introduced him in rich, rolling tones whose very unction served to increase the visitor’s insignificance.
paragraphs.zh: 来访者身材矮小，穿着一件破旧的羊驼毛外套。他有一张干瘪的黑脸，就像一只年迈的小猴子。在唱诗班再次歌唱的同时，六个孩子站起来，用细弱、恐惧、不合调的低声唱着歌，他们惊愕地看着那个相貌微不足道的男人坐在牧师那魁梧​​的身躯面前，显得矮小而乡土。当牧师站起身来，用浑厚而圆润的音调介绍他时，他们仍然用惊愕和难以置信的目光看着他，而他的这一举动却让这位来访者显得更加渺小。

paragraphs.en: “En dey brung dat all de way fum Saint Looey,” Frony whispered.
paragraphs.zh: “这些都是圣卢伊带来的，”弗罗妮低声说道。

paragraphs.en: “I’ve knowed de Lawd to use cuiser tools dan dat,” Dilsey said. “Hush, now,” she said to Ben, “Dey fixin to sing again in a minute.”
paragraphs.zh: “我知道 de Lawd 会使用 Cuiser 工具和 dat，”迪尔西说。“嘘，现在，”她对本说，“他们一会儿再唱歌。”

paragraphs.en: When the visitor rose to speak he sounded like a white man. His voice was level and cold. It sounded too big to have come from him and they listened at first through curiosity, as they would have to a monkey talking. They began to watch him as they would a man on a tight rope. They even forgot his insignificant appearance in the virtuosity with which he ran and poised and swooped upon the cold inflectionless wire of his voice, so that at last, when with a sort of swooping glide he came to rest again beside the reading desk with one arm resting upon it at shoulder height and his monkey body as reft of all motion as a mummy or an emptied vessel, the congregation sighed as if it waked from a collective dream and moved a little in its seats. Behind the pulpit the choir fanned steadily. Dilsey whispered, “Hush, now. Dey fixin to sing in a minute.”
paragraphs.zh: 当这位来访者站起来说话时，他听起来就像一个白人。他的声音平淡而冰冷。听起来太大了，不可能是他说的，他们一开始出于好奇而听，就像听猴子说话一样。他们开始观察他，就像观察一个被绳子拴住的人一样。他们甚至忘记了他那微不足道的外表，因为他奔跑、保持平衡、俯冲时声音冰冷、毫无变化，所以最后，当他以一种俯冲的滑翔方式再次停在阅读桌旁，一只手臂放在与肩同高的位置上，他的猴子身体像木乃伊或空容器一样没有任何运动时，会众叹了口气，仿佛从集体梦中醒来，稍微移动了一点。它的座位。讲坛后面，唱诗班的歌声稳定地响起。迪尔西低声说道：“嘘，一会儿。他们一会儿就唱歌。”

paragraphs.en: Then a voice said, “Brethren.”
paragraphs.zh: 然后一个声音说：“弟兄们。”

paragraphs.en: The preacher had not moved. His arm lay yet across the desk, and he still held that pose while the voice died in sonorous echoes between the walls. It was as different as day and dark from his former tone, with a sad, timbrous quality like an alto horn, sinking into their hearts and speaking there again when it had ceased in fading and cumulate echoes.
paragraphs.zh: 传教士没有动。他的手臂仍然放在桌子上，他仍然保持着那个姿势，而声音在墙壁之间的响亮回声中消失了。这与他以前的语气完全不同，带着一种悲伤、音色，像中音喇叭一样，沉入他们的心中，当它停止了消退和积聚的回声时，又在那里说话。

paragraphs.en: “Brethren and sisteren,” it said again. The preacher removed his arm and he began to walk back and forth before the desk, his hands clasped behind him, a meagre figure, hunched over upon itself like that of one long immured in striving with the implacable earth, “I got the recollection and the blood of the Lamb!” He tramped steadily back and forth beneath the twisted paper and the Christmas bell, hunched, his hands clasped behind him. He was like a worn small rock whelmed by the successive waves of his voice. With his body he seemed to feed the voice that, succubus like, had fleshed its teeth in him. And the congregation seemed to watch with its own eyes while the voice consumed him, until he was nothing and they were nothing and there was not even a voice but instead their hearts were speaking to one another in chanting measures beyond the need for words, so that when he came to rest against the reading desk, his monkey face lifted and his whole attitude that of a serene, tortured crucifix that transcended its shabbiness and insignificance and made it of no moment, a long moaning expulsion of breath rose from them, and a woman’s single soprano: “Yes, Jesus!”
paragraphs.zh: “弟兄姐妹们，”它又说道。传道人松开手臂，开始在讲台前来回走动，双手紧握在身后，身材瘦弱，弓着背，就像长期与无情的大地进行斗争的人一样：“我得到了记忆和羔羊的血！”他在扭曲的纸张和圣诞钟声下稳步地来回走动，弯着腰，双手紧握在身后。他就像一块磨损的小石头，被他连续不断的声音所压垮。他似乎用自己的身体来喂养那声音，那声音就像魅魔一样，在他体内充实了牙齿。当这个声音吞噬他时，会众似乎亲眼看着他，直到他什么都不是，他们什么也不是，甚至连声音都没有，而是他们的心在用超越语言的吟诵声互相交谈，因此，当他靠在阅读台上休息时，他的猴脸抬起来，他的整个态度就像一个宁静的、受折磨的十字架，超越了它的破旧和微不足道，使它不再是一个时刻，从那里升起一阵长长的呻吟式的呼吸。他们，还有一位女单女高音：“是的，耶稣！”

paragraphs.en: As the scudding day passed overhead the dingy windows glowed and faded in ghostly retrograde. A car passed along the road outside, labouring in the sand, died away. Dilsey sat bolt upright, her hand on Ben’s knee. Two tears slid down her fallen cheeks, in and out of the myriad coruscations of immolation and abnegation and time.
paragraphs.zh: 白天在头顶上疾驰而过，肮脏的窗户忽隐忽现，幽灵般地逆行着。一辆汽车沿着外面的道路行驶，在沙子里吃力，渐渐消失了。迪尔西坐直了身体，她的手放在本的膝盖上。两滴泪水顺着她垂下的脸颊滑落，在无数的牺牲、克制和时间的交响中落下。

paragraphs.en: “Brethren,” the minister said in a harsh whisper, without moving.
paragraphs.zh: “弟兄们，”牧师一动不动地低声说道。

paragraphs.en: “Yes, Jesus!” the woman’s voice said, hushed yet.
paragraphs.zh: “是的，耶稣！”女人的声音低沉地说道。

paragraphs.en: “Breddren en sistuhn!” His voice rang again, with the horns. He removed his arm and stood erect and raised his hands. “I got de ricklickshun en de blood of de Lamb!” They did not mark just when his intonation, his pronunciation, became negroid, they just sat swaying a little in their seats as the voice took them into itself.
paragraphs.zh: “Breddren en sistuhn！”他的声音再次响起，带着号角声。他松开手臂，站直身子，举起双手。“我得到了瑞克利顺和羔羊之血！”他们并没有注意到他的语调、他的发音何时变成了黑人，他们只是坐在座位上，随着声音将他们带入自己而微微摇晃。

paragraphs.en: “When de long, cold—Oh, I tells you, breddren, when de long, cold—I sees de light en I sees de word, po sinner! Dey passed away in Egypt, de swingin chariots; de generations passed away. Wus a rich man: whar he now, O breddren? Wus a po man: whar he now, O sistuhn? Oh I tells you, ef you aint got de milk en de dew of de old salvation when de long, cold years rolls away!”
paragraphs.zh: “当你寒冷时——哦，我告诉你，弟兄们，当你寒冷时——我看到了光，我看到了话语，罪人！他们在埃及去世了，旋转的战车；一代又一代的人去世了。他现在是个富翁吗，兄弟们？他现在是个穷人吗，西斯图恩？哦，我告诉你，如果你没有得到古老救恩的牛奶和露水，漫长而寒冷的岁月即将过去！”

paragraphs.en: “Yes, Jesus!”
paragraphs.zh: “是的，耶稣！”

paragraphs.en: “I tells you, breddren, en I tells you, sistuhn, dey’ll come a time. Po sinner sayin Let me lay down wid de Lawd, lemme lay down my load. Den whut Jesus gwine say, O breddren? O sistuhn? Is you got de ricklickshun en de Blood of de Lamb? Case I aint gwine load down heaven!”
paragraphs.zh: “我告诉你，兄弟们，我告诉你，西斯图恩，他们有一天会来。罪人说让我和德·劳德一起躺下，让我放下我的负担。耶稣说，兄弟们？哦西斯图恩？你得到了羔羊之血的瑞克利顺吗？如果我没有负载下天！”

paragraphs.en: He fumbled in his coat and took out a handkerchief and mopped his face. A low concerted sound rose from the congregation: “Mmmmmmmmmmmmm!” The woman’s voice said, “Yes, Jesus! Jesus!”
paragraphs.zh: 他摸索着外套，掏出手帕擦了擦脸。人群中齐声响起：“嗯嗯嗯嗯嗯！”女人的声音说：“是的，耶稣！耶稣！”

paragraphs.en: “Breddren! Look at dem little chillen settin dar. Jesus wus like dat once. He mammy suffered de glory en de pangs. Sometime maybe she helt him at de nightfall, whilst de angels singin him to sleep; maybe she look out de do’ en see de Roman po-lice passin.” He tramped back and forth, mopping his face. “Listen, breddren! I sees de day. Ma’y settin in de do’ wid Jesus on her lap, de little Jesus. Like dem chillen dar, de little Jesus. I hears de angels singin de peaceful songs en de glory; I sees de closin eyes; sees Mary jump up, sees de sojer face: We gwine to kill! We gwine to kill! We gwine to kill yo little Jesus! I hears de weepin en de lamentation of de po mammy widout de salvation en de word of God!”
paragraphs.zh: “布雷德伦！看看他们的小孩子们。耶稣曾经像这样。他妈妈遭受了荣耀和痛苦。有时，也许她在夜幕降临时扶着他，而天使们则在唱歌让他入睡；也许她在注视着罗马警察，看到了路过的罗马警察。”他来回走动，擦着脸。“听着，弟兄们！我看到了这一天。愿耶稣坐在她的腿上，小耶稣。就像小耶稣一样。我听到天使在荣耀中唱着和平的歌曲；我看到眼睛闭合；看到玛丽跳起来，看到苏耶尔的脸：我们要杀戮！我们要杀戮！我们要杀死你的小耶稣！我听到了为失去上帝话语的妈妈而哭泣和哀悼！”

paragraphs.en: “Mmmmmmmmmmmmmmmm! Jesus! Little Jesus!” and another voice, rising:
paragraphs.zh: “嗯嗯嗯嗯嗯嗯！耶稣！小耶稣！”另一个声音响起：

paragraphs.en: “I sees, O Jesus! Oh I sees!” and still another, without words, like bubbles rising in water.
paragraphs.zh: “我明白了，耶稣啊！哦，我明白了！”还有一种，没有言语，就像水中升起的气泡。

paragraphs.en: “I sees hit, breddren! I sees hit! Sees de blastin, blindin sight! I sees Calvary, wid de sacred trees, sees de thief en de murderer en de least of dese; I hears de boasting en de braggin: Ef you be Jesus, lif up yo tree en walk! I hears de wailin of women en de evenin lamentations; I hears de weepin en de cryin en de turnt-away face of God: dey done kilt Jesus; dey done kilt my Son!”
paragraphs.zh: “我看到击中，兄弟们！我看到击中！看到爆破，盲目的视线！我看到加略山，有圣树，看到小偷和杀人犯，至少是这样；我听到吹牛和吹牛：如果你是耶稣，把你的树抬起来行走！我晚上听到妇女的哀号；我听到哭泣和哭泣上帝转过脸来：他们已经杀了耶稣；他们已经杀了我的儿子！”

paragraphs.en: “Mmmmmmmmmmmmm. Jesus! I sees, O Jesus!”
paragraphs.zh: “嗯嗯嗯嗯嗯。耶稣啊！我明白了，耶稣啊！”

paragraphs.en: “O blind sinner! Breddren, I tells you; sistuhn, I says to you, when de Lawd did turn His mighty face, say, Aint gwine overload heaven! I can see de widowed God shet His do’; I sees de whelmin flood roll between; I sees de darkness en de death everlastin upon de generations. Den, lo! Breddren! Yes, breddren! Whut I see? Whut I see, O sinner? I sees de resurrection en de light; sees de meek Jesus sayin Dey kilt Me dat ye shall live again; I died dat dem whut sees en believes shall never die. Breddren, O breddren! I sees de doom crack en hears de golden horns shoutin down de glory, en de arisen dead whut got de blood en de ricklickshun of de Lamb!”
paragraphs.zh: “噢，盲目的罪人！布雷德伦，我告诉你；西斯图恩，我对你说，当德劳德转过他强大的面孔时，说，天堂不会超载！我可以看到寡妇的上帝施展他的作为”；我看到洪水在中间滚滚；我看到黑暗与死亡永远延续到一代又一代。天哪！布雷德伦！是的，兄弟们！我看到了什么？罪人啊，我看到了什么？我看到光明中的复活；看到温柔的耶稣说，你们将复活；我死了，但看到他们永远不会死，兄弟们，我看到末日破裂，听到荣耀的声音，死了，但羔羊的血被击倒了！

paragraphs.en: In the midst of the voices and the hands Ben sat, rapt in his sweet blue gaze. Dilsey sat bolt upright beside, crying rigidly and quietly in the annealment and the blood of the remembered Lamb.
paragraphs.zh: 本坐在声音和双手中间，全神贯注于他甜美的蓝色目光。迪尔西笔直地坐在旁边，在记忆中的羔羊的退火和鲜血中僵硬而安静地哭泣。

paragraphs.en: As they walked through the bright noon, up the sandy road with the dispersing congregation talking easily again group to group, she continued to weep, unmindful of the talk.
paragraphs.zh: 当他们穿过明亮的正午，沿着沙路走时，散去的会众又开始轻松地交谈，她继续哭泣，没有在意这些谈话。

paragraphs.en: “He sho a preacher, mon! He didn’t look like much at first, but hush!”
paragraphs.zh: “他对一个传教士开枪了，伙计！他一开始看起来不太像，但是嘘！”

paragraphs.en: “He seed de power en de glory.”
paragraphs.zh: “他播撒着权力和荣耀的种子。”

paragraphs.en: “Yes, suh. He seed hit. Face to face he seed hit.”
paragraphs.zh: “是的，先生。他击中了种子。他面对面击中了种子。”

paragraphs.en: Dilsey made no sound, her face did not quiver as the tears took their sunken and devious courses, walking with her head up, making no effort to dry them away even.
paragraphs.zh: 迪尔西没有出声，她的脸没有颤抖，泪水顺着凹陷而弯曲的轨迹，昂着头走着，甚至没有努力去擦干。

paragraphs.en: “Whyn’t you quit dat, mammy?” Frony said. “Wid all dese people lookin. We be passin white folks soon.”
paragraphs.zh: “妈妈，你为什么不放弃这个呢？”弗罗妮说。“所有这些人都在看着。我们很快就会超越白人。”

paragraphs.en: “I’ve seed de first en de last,” Dilsey said. “Never you mind me.”
paragraphs.zh: “我已经从第一个到最后一个种子了，”迪尔西说。“别管我。”

paragraphs.en: “First en last whut?” Frony said.
paragraphs.zh: “首先是最后什么？”弗罗妮说。

paragraphs.en: “Never you mind,” Dilsey said. “I seed de beginnin, en now I sees de endin.”
paragraphs.zh: “没关系，”迪尔西说。“我播种了开始，现在我看到了结束。”

paragraphs.en: Before they reached the street, though, she stopped and lifted her skirt and dried her eyes on the hem of her topmost underskirt. Then they went on. Ben shambled along beside Dilsey, watching Luster who anticked along ahead, the umbrella in his hand and his new straw hat slanted viciously in the sunlight, like a big foolish dog watching a small clever one. They reached the gate and entered. Immediately Ben began to whimper again, and for a while all of them looked up the drive at the square, paintless house with its rotting portico.
paragraphs.zh: 然而，在他们到达街道之前，她停下来，掀起裙子，在最上面的内衣下摆上擦干眼睛。然后他们继续前行。本在迪尔西身边摇摇晃晃地走着，看着前面走来的勒斯特，他手里的雨伞和他的新草帽在阳光下恶狠狠地倾斜着，就像一只大傻狗看着一只聪明的小狗。他们到达大门并进入。本立刻又开始呜咽起来，有一阵子，所有人都抬头望着车道上那座方形的、没有油漆、门廊腐烂的房子。

paragraphs.en: “Whut’s gwine on up dar today?” Frony said. “Something is.”
paragraphs.zh: “今天的 gwine 怎么样？”弗罗妮说。“有东西是。”

paragraphs.en: “Nothin,” Dilsey said. “You tend to yo business en let de white folks tend to deir’n.”
paragraphs.zh: “没什么，”迪尔西说。“你管你的事，让白人管他们的事。”

paragraphs.en: “Somethin is,” Frony said. “I heard him first thing dis mawnin. ’Taint none of my business, dough.”
paragraphs.zh: “有些东西是，”弗罗妮说。“我听到他说的第一句话就是‘别玷污我的事，面团。’”

paragraphs.en: “En I knows whut, too,” Luster said.
paragraphs.zh: “嗯，我也知道是什么，”勒斯特说。

paragraphs.en: “You knows mo dan you got any use fer,” Dilsey said. “Aint you jes heard Frony say hit aint none of yo business? You take Benjy on to de back and keep him quiet twell I put dinner on.”
paragraphs.zh: “你知道，但你有任何用处，”迪尔西说。“你没听到弗罗妮说打人不关你的事吗？你把班吉带回去，在我准备晚饭之前让他保持安静。”

paragraphs.en: “I knows whar Miss Quentin is,” Luster said.
paragraphs.zh: “我知道昆丁小姐是谁，”勒斯特说。

paragraphs.en: “Den jes keep hit,” Dilsey said. “Soon es Quentin need any of yo egvice, I’ll let you know. Y’all g’awn en play in de back, now.”
paragraphs.zh: “丹杰斯继续受到打击，”迪尔西说。“很快昆丁需要你们的任何建议，我会让你们知道的。你们现在就在后面玩吧。”

paragraphs.en: “You know whut gwine happen soon es dey start playin dat ball over yonder,” Luster said.
paragraphs.zh: “你知道，很快就会发生什么事，他们就会开始在那边打球，”勒斯特说。

paragraphs.en: “Dey wont start fer awhile yit. By dat time T.P. be here to take him ridin. Here, you gimme dat new hat.”
paragraphs.zh: “他们暂时还不会出发。到时候蒂·皮就来带他骑马了。给你，给我那顶新帽子。”

paragraphs.en: Luster gave her the hat and he and Ben went on across the back yard. Ben was still whimpering, though not loud. Dilsey and Frony went to the cabin. After a while Dilsey emerged, again in the faded calico dress, and went to the kitchen. The fire had died down. There was no sound in the house. She put on the apron and went up stairs. There was no sound anywhere. Quentin’s room was as they had left it. She entered and picked up the undergarment and put the stocking back in the drawer and closed it. Mrs Compson’s door was closed. Dilsey stood beside it for a moment, listening. Then she opened it and entered, entered a pervading reek of camphor. The shades were drawn, the room in halflight, and the bed, so that at first she thought Mrs Compson was asleep and was about to close the door when the other spoke.
paragraphs.zh: 勒斯特把帽子给了她，然后他和本继续穿过后院。本仍在呜咽，虽然声音不大。迪尔西和弗罗妮去了小屋。过了一会儿，迪尔西出现了，再次穿着褪色的印花布连衣裙，走进厨房。火已经熄灭了。屋子里没有声音。她系上围裙，上了楼梯。到处都没有声音。昆丁的房间还是他们离开时的样子。她走进去，拿起内衣，把袜子放回抽屉里，关上抽屉。康普生夫人的门关着。迪尔西在它旁边站了一会儿，倾听着。然后她打开门走了进去，进入了弥漫着樟脑气味的地方。窗帘拉上了，房间光线昏暗，床铺也昏暗，所以一开始她以为康普生太太睡着了，正要关门的时候，对方说话了。

paragraphs.en: “Well?” she said, “What is it?”
paragraphs.zh: “怎么样？”她说：“那是什么？”

paragraphs.en: “Hit’s me,” Dilsey said. “You want anything?”
paragraphs.zh: “打的是我，”迪尔西说。“你想要什么吗？”

paragraphs.en: Mrs Compson didn’t answer. After awhile, without moving her head at all, she said: “Where’s Jason?”
paragraphs.zh: 康普生夫人没有回答。过了一会儿，她头也不动地说道：“杰生呢？”

paragraphs.en: “He aint come back yit,” Dilsey said. “Whut you want?”
paragraphs.zh: “他不会回来了，”迪尔西说。“你想要什么？”

paragraphs.en: Mrs Compson said nothing. Like so many cold, weak people, when faced at last by the incontrovertible disaster she exhumed from somewhere a sort of fortitude, strength. In her case it was an unshakable conviction regarding the yet unplumbed event. “Well,” she said presently, “Did you find it?”
paragraphs.zh: 康普生夫人什么也没说。就像许多冷漠、软弱的人一样，当最终面对无可争议的灾难时，她从某处挖掘出一种坚韧和力量。就她而言，这是对尚未调查的事件的不可动摇的信念。“嗯，”她很快说道，“你找到了吗？”

paragraphs.en: “Find whut? Whut you talkin about?”
paragraphs.zh: “找到什么？你在说什么？”

paragraphs.en: “The note. At least she would have enough consideration to leave a note. Even Quentin did that.”
paragraphs.zh: “那张纸条，至少她有足够的体贴留张纸条，连昆丁都这么做了。”

paragraphs.en: “Whut you talkin about?” Dilsey said, “Dont you know she all right? I bet she be walkin right in dis do’ befo dark.”
paragraphs.zh: “你在说什么？”迪尔西说：“你不认识她吗？我打赌她一定会在天黑之前走路。”

paragraphs.en: “Fiddlesticks,” Mrs Compson said, “It’s in the blood. Like uncle, like niece. Or mother. I dont know which would be worse. I dont seem to care.”
paragraphs.zh: “胡闹，”康普生夫人说，“这是在血液里的。像叔叔，像侄女。或者母亲。我不知道哪个会更糟。我似乎不在乎。”

paragraphs.en: “Whut you keep on talkin that way fur?” Dilsey said. “Whut she want to do anything like that fur?”
paragraphs.zh: “你怎么还这么说话？”迪尔西说道。“她为什么想做那种毛皮之类的事情？”

paragraphs.en: “I dont know. What reason did Quentin have? Under God’s heaven what reason did he have? It cant be simply to flout and hurt me. Whoever God is, He would not permit that. I’m a lady. You might not believe that from my offspring, but I am.”
paragraphs.zh: “我不知道，昆丁有什么理由？天底下他有什么理由？不可能只是为了蔑视和伤害我。无论神是谁，他都不会允许这样做。我是一位女士，你可能不相信我的后代会这么说，但我是。”

paragraphs.en: “You des wait en see,” Dilsey said. “She be here by night, right dar in her bed.” Mrs Compson said nothing. The camphor-soaked cloth lay upon her brow. The black robe lay across the foot of the bed. Dilsey stood with her hand on the door knob.
paragraphs.zh: “你等着瞧，”迪尔西说。“她晚上就在这儿，就在床上。”康普生夫人什么也没说。浸过樟脑的布放在她的额头上。黑色长袍横放在床脚上。迪尔西站在那里，手放在门把手上。

paragraphs.en: “Well,” Mrs Compson said. “What do you want? Are you going to fix some dinner for Jason and Benjamin, or not?”
paragraphs.zh: “好吧，”康普生夫人说。“你想要什么？要不要给杰生和本杰明做顿饭？”

paragraphs.en: “Jason aint come yit,” Dilsey said. “I gwine fix somethin. You sho you dont want nothin? Yo bottle still hot enough?”
paragraphs.zh: “杰生不会来的，”迪尔西说。“我要修理一些东西。你确定你什么都不想要吗？你的瓶子还不够热吗？”

paragraphs.en: “You might hand me my Bible.”
paragraphs.zh: “你可以把我的圣经递给我。”

paragraphs.en: “I give hit to you dis mawnin, befo I left.”
paragraphs.zh: “在我离开之前，我给你打了一顿。”

paragraphs.en: “You laid it on the edge of the bed. How long did you expect it to stay there?”
paragraphs.zh: “你把它放在床边。你预计它会在那里呆多久？”

paragraphs.en: Dilsey crossed to the bed and groped among the shadows beneath the edge of it and found the Bible, face down. She smoothed the bent pages and laid the book on the bed again. Mrs Compson didn’t open her eyes. Her hair and the pillow were the same color, beneath the wimple of the medicated cloth she looked like an old nun praying. “Dont put it there again,” she said, without opening her eyes. “That’s where you put it before. Do you want me to have to get out of bed to pick it up?”
paragraphs.zh: 迪尔西走到床边，在床边的阴影中摸索，找到了圣经，面朝下。她抚平弯曲的书页，将书重新放在床上。康普生夫人没有睁开眼睛。她的头发和枕头是同一种颜色，药布头巾下的她看起来就像一位正在祈祷的老尼姑。“别再把它放在那里，”她说，没有睁开眼睛。“那是你之前放的。你想让我起床去捡吗？”

paragraphs.en: Dilsey reached the book across her and laid it on the broad side of the bed. “You cant see to read, noways,” she said. “You want me to raise de shade a little?”
paragraphs.zh: 迪尔西把书放在她身上，放在宽阔的床边。“无论如何，你看不到书，”她说。“你想让我把阴影提高一点吗？”

paragraphs.en: “No. Let them alone. Go on and fix Jason something to eat.”
paragraphs.zh: “不用了，别管他们了，去给杰生准备点吃的吧。”

paragraphs.en: Dilsey went out. She closed the door and returned to the kitchen. The stove was almost cold. While she stood there the clock above the cupboard struck ten times. “One oclock,” she said aloud, “Jason aint comin home. Ise seed de first en de last,” she said, looking at the cold stove, “I seed de first en de last.” She set out some cold food on a table. As she moved back and forth she sang a hymn. She sang the first two lines over and over to the complete tune. She arranged the meal and went to the door and called Luster, and after a time Luster and Ben entered. Ben was still moaning a little, as to himself.
paragraphs.zh: 迪尔西出去了。她关上门，回到厨房。炉子几乎冷了。当她站在那里时，柜子上方的钟敲响了十下。“一点了，”她大声说道，“杰生还没回家。我是第一个和最后一个种子，”她看着冰冷的炉子说，“我是第一个和最后一个种子。”她在桌子上摆了一些冷食。当她来回移动时，她唱着一首赞美诗。她一遍又一遍地唱着前两句歌词，完成了整首曲子。她安排好饭菜，走到门口给勒斯特打电话，过了一会儿，勒斯特和本进来了。本仍在轻微地呻吟，就像自言自语一样。

paragraphs.en: “He aint never quit,” Luster said.
paragraphs.zh: “他永远不会放弃，”勒斯特说。

paragraphs.en: “Y’all come on en eat,” Dilsey said. “Jason aint coming to dinner.” They sat down at the table. Ben could manage solid food pretty well for himself, though even now, with cold food before him, Dilsey tied a cloth about his neck. He and Luster ate. Dilsey moved about the kitchen, singing the two lines of the hymn which she remembered. “Yo’ll kin g’awn en eat,” she said, “Jason aint comin home.”
paragraphs.zh: “你们都来吃饭吧，”迪尔西说。“杰生不来吃晚饭了。”他们在桌边坐下。本自己可以很好地处理固体食物，尽管即使现在，在他面前有冷食，迪尔西还在他的脖子上绑了一块布。他和勒斯特一起吃饭。迪尔西在厨房里走来走去，唱着她记得的两句赞美诗。“你要吃饭了，”她说，“杰生还没回家。”

paragraphs.en: He was twenty miles away at that time. When he left the house he drove rapidly to town, overreaching the slow sabbath groups and the peremptory bells along the broken air. He crossed the empty square and turned into a narrow street that was abruptly quieter even yet, and stopped before a frame house and went up the flower-bordered walk to the porch.
paragraphs.zh: 当时他距离二十英里。当他离开家时，他迅速开车进城，超越了缓慢的安息日团体和沿着破碎的空气的专断的钟声。他穿过空荡荡的广场，拐进一条狭窄的街道，街道却突然安静下来，在一栋木屋前停了下来，沿着鲜花环绕的小道来到了门廊。

paragraphs.en: Beyond the screen door people were talking. As he lifted his hand to knock he heard steps, so he withheld his hand until a big man in black broadcloth trousers and a stiff-bosomed white shirt without collar opened the door. He had vigorous untidy iron-grey hair and his grey eyes were round and shiny like a little boy’s. He took Jason’s hand and drew him into the house, still shaking it.
paragraphs.zh: 纱门外人们正在说话。当他举手敲门时，听到了脚步声，于是他收回了手，直到一个穿着黑色阔布长裤和硬挺胸无领白衬衫的大个子男人打开了门。他有一头充满活力、凌乱的铁灰色头发，灰色的眼睛又圆又亮，像个小男孩的眼睛。他拉着杰生的手，把他拉进屋里，手还在颤抖。

paragraphs.en: “Come right in,” he said, “Come right in.”
paragraphs.zh: “请进来，”他说，“请进来。”

paragraphs.en: “You ready to go now?” Jason said.
paragraphs.zh: “你现在准备好了吗？”杰生说道。

paragraphs.en: “Walk right in,” the other said, propelling him by the elbow into a room where a man and a woman sat. “You know Myrtle’s husband, dont you? Jason Compson, Vernon.”
paragraphs.zh: “直接进去吧，”另一个说着，拉着他的胳膊肘，把他推进了一个房间，里面坐着一男一女。“你认识默特尔的丈夫，不是吗？杰生康普生，弗农。”

paragraphs.en: “Yes,” Jason said. He did not even look at the man, and as the sheriff drew a chair across the room the man said,
paragraphs.zh: “是的。”杰生说。他甚至没有看那个人，当治安官拉过一把椅子穿过房间时，那个人说道：

paragraphs.en: “We’ll go out so you can talk. Come on, Myrtle.”
paragraphs.zh: “我们出去，这样你就可以谈谈了。来吧，默特尔。”

paragraphs.en: “No, no,” the sheriff said, “You folks keep your seat. I reckon it aint that serious, Jason? Have a seat.”
paragraphs.zh: “不，不，”治安官说，“你们保持座位。我想事情没那么严重，杰生？坐吧。”

paragraphs.en: “I’ll tell you as we go along,” Jason said. “Get your hat and coat.”
paragraphs.zh: “我们一边走一边告诉你。”杰生说。“拿上你的帽子和外套。”

paragraphs.en: “We’ll go out,” the man said, rising.
paragraphs.zh: “我们出去吧。”男人站起身来说道。

paragraphs.en: “Keep your seat,” the sheriff said. “Me and Jason will go out on the porch.”
paragraphs.zh: “保持座位，”警长说。“我和杰生到门廊去。”

paragraphs.en: “You get your hat and coat,” Jason said. “They’ve already got a twelve hour start.” The sheriff led the way back to the porch. A man and a woman passing spoke to him. He responded with a hearty florid gesture. Bells were still ringing, from the direction of the section known as Nigger Hollow. “Get your hat, Sheriff,” Jason said. The sheriff drew up two chairs.
paragraphs.zh: “你去拿帽子和外套，”杰生说。“他们已经有十二个小时的出发时间了。”警长带路回到门廊。路过的一男一女对他说话。他以一个热情洋溢的姿态回应。钟声仍在响起，从被称为“黑鬼山谷”的那段方向传来。“戴上你的帽子，警长，”杰生说。治安官拉了两把椅子。

paragraphs.en: “Have a seat and tell me what the trouble is.”
paragraphs.zh: “坐下来，告诉我出了什么问题。”

paragraphs.en: “I told you over the phone,” Jason said, standing. “I did that to save time. Am I going to have to go to law to compel you to do your sworn duty?”
paragraphs.zh: “我在电话里告诉过你了。”杰生站起来说道。“我这样做是为了节省时间。我需要诉诸法律来强迫你履行你的宣誓职责吗？”

paragraphs.en: “You sit down and tell me about it,” the sheriff said. “I’ll take care of you all right.”
paragraphs.zh: “你坐下来告诉我这件事，”警长说。“我会好好照顾你的。”

paragraphs.en: “Care, hell,” Jason said. “Is this what you call taking care of me?”
paragraphs.zh: “小心点，见鬼，”杰生说。“这就是你所谓的照顾我吗？”

paragraphs.en: “You’re the one that’s holding us up,” the sheriff said. “You sit down and tell me about it.”
paragraphs.zh: “你是阻碍我们的人，”警长说。“你坐下来告诉我这件事。”

paragraphs.en: Jason told him, his sense of injury and impotence feeding upon its own sound, so that after a time he forgot his haste in the violent cumulation of his self justification and his outrage. The sheriff watched him steadily with his cold shiny eyes.
paragraphs.zh: 杰生告诉他，他的受伤感和无力感以自己的声音为食，所以过了一段时间，他忘记了自己在自我辩解和愤怒的猛烈积累中的匆忙。治安官用冰冷闪亮的眼睛定定地看着他。

paragraphs.en: “But you dont know they done it,” he said. “You just think so.”
paragraphs.zh: “但你不知道他们做到了，”他说。“你只是这么想而已。”

paragraphs.en: “Dont know?” Jason said. “When I spent two damn days chasing her through alleys, trying to keep her away from him, after I told her what I’d do to her if I ever caught her with him, and you say I dont know that that little b—”
paragraphs.zh: “不知道？”杰生说道。“当我花了两天的时间在小巷里追她，试图让她远离他时，在我告诉她如果我抓住她和他在一起我会对她做什么，而你却说我不知道那个小混蛋——”

paragraphs.en: “Now, then,” the sheriff said, “That’ll do. That’s enough of that.” He looked out across the street, his hands in his pockets.
paragraphs.zh: “那么，”治安官说道，“这样就可以了。够了。”他双手插在口袋里，看着街对面。

paragraphs.en: “And when I come to you, a commissioned officer of the law,” Jason said.
paragraphs.zh: “当我来找你时，你是一名法律军官，”杰生说。

paragraphs.en: “That show’s in Mottson this week,” the sheriff said.
paragraphs.zh: “这个节目本周在莫特森举行，”治安官说。

paragraphs.en: “Yes,” Jason said, “And if I could find a law officer that gave a solitary damn about protecting the people that elected him to office, I’d be there too by now.” He repeated his story, harshly recapitulant, seeming to get an actual pleasure out of his outrage and impotence. The sheriff did not appear to be listening at all.
paragraphs.zh: “是的，”杰生说，“如果我能找到一位真正关心保护选举他入职的人民的律师，我现在也会在那里。”他重复了他的故事，语气严厉地重述，似乎从他的愤怒和无能中得到了真正的快乐。警长似乎根本没有在听。

paragraphs.en: “Jason,” he said, “What were you doing with three thousand dollars hid in the house?”
paragraphs.zh: “杰生，”他说，“你把三千块钱藏在房子里做什么？”

paragraphs.en: “What?” Jason said. “That’s my business where I keep my money. Your business is to help me get it back.”
paragraphs.zh: “什么？”杰生说道。“我的钱就是我的事。你的事就是帮我把钱拿回来。”

paragraphs.en: “Did your mother know you had that much on the place?”
paragraphs.zh: “你妈妈知道你在这个地方有那么多东西吗？”

paragraphs.en: “Look here,” Jason said, “My house has been robbed. I know who did it and I know where they are. I come to you as the commissioned officer of the law, and I ask you once more, are you going to make any effort to recover my property, or not?”
paragraphs.zh: “你看，”杰生说，“我的房子被抢了，我知道是谁干的，我也知道他们在哪里。我作为法律的委托人来找你，我再问你一次，你会尽力追回我的财产吗？”

paragraphs.en: “What do you aim to do with that girl, if you catch them?”
paragraphs.zh: “如果你抓住了那个女孩，你打算对他们做什么？”

paragraphs.en: “Nothing,” Jason said, “Not anything. I wouldn’t lay my hand on her. The bitch that cost me a job, the one chance I ever had to get ahead, that killed my father and is shortening my mother’s life every day and made my name a laughing stock in the town. I wont do anything to her,” he said. “Not anything.”
paragraphs.zh: “没什么，”杰生说，“没什么。我不会对她下手。这个女人害了我一份工作，让我失去了一次出人头地的机会，她害死了我父亲，每天都在缩短我母亲的生命，让我的名字成为镇上的笑柄。我不会对她做任何事。”他说。“没什么。”

paragraphs.en: “You drove that girl into running off, Jason,” the sheriff said.
paragraphs.zh: “你让那个女孩跑了，杰生，”治安官说。

paragraphs.en: “How I conduct my family is no business of yours,” Jason said. “Are you going to help me or not?”
paragraphs.zh: 杰生说：“我如何管理我的家庭不关你的事。”“你到底帮不帮我？”

paragraphs.en: “You drove her away from home,” the sheriff said. “And I have some suspicions about who that money belongs to that I dont reckon I’ll ever know for certain.”
paragraphs.zh: “你把她赶出了家，”警长说。“我对这笔钱的归属有些怀疑，我认为我永远无法确定。”

paragraphs.en: Jason stood, slowly wringing the brim of his hat in his hands. He said quietly: “You’re not going to make any effort to catch them for me?”
paragraphs.zh: 杰生站了起来，双手慢慢地拧着帽檐。他低声说道：“你不打算费尽心思帮我抓到他们吗？”

paragraphs.en: “That’s not any of my business, Jason. If you had any actual proof, I’d have to act. But without that I dont figger it’s any of my business.”
paragraphs.zh: “这不关我的事，杰生。如果你有任何实际证据，我就必须采取行动。但如果没有证据，我认为这不关我的事。”

paragraphs.en: “That’s your answer, is it?” Jason said. “Think well, now.”
paragraphs.zh: “这就是你的答案，是吗？”杰生说道。“现在好好想想。”

paragraphs.en: “That’s it, Jason.”
paragraphs.zh: “就是这样，杰生。”

paragraphs.en: “All right,” Jason said. He put his hat on. “You’ll regret this. I wont be helpless. This is not Russia, where just because he wears a little metal badge, a man is immune to law.” He went down the steps and got in his car and started the engine. The sheriff watched him drive away, turn, and rush past the house toward town.
paragraphs.zh: “好吧。”杰生说。他戴上了帽子。“你会后悔的。我不会束手无策。这不是俄罗斯，在俄罗斯，一个人只要戴着一个小小的金属徽章，就可以免受法律的制裁。”他走下台阶，钻进车里，启动了引擎。治安官看着他开车离开，转身冲过房子朝镇上跑去。

paragraphs.en: The bells were ringing again, high in the scudding sunlight in bright disorderly tatters of sound. He stopped at a filling station and had his tires examined and the tank filled.
paragraphs.zh: 钟声再次响起，在猛烈的阳光照射下，发出明亮而杂乱的声音。他在一个加油站停下来检查轮胎并给油箱加满油。

paragraphs.en: “Gwine on a trip, is you?” the negro asked him. He didn’t answer. “Look like hit gwine fair off, after all,” the negro said.
paragraphs.zh: “Gwine 正在旅行，是吗？”黑人问他。他没有回答。“毕竟，看起来很公平，”黑人说。

paragraphs.en: “Fair off, hell,” Jason said, “It’ll be raining like hell by twelve oclock.” He looked at the sky, thinking about rain, about the slick clay roads, himself stalled somewhere miles from town. He thought about it with a sort of triumph, of the fact that he was going to miss dinner, that by starting now and so serving his compulsion of haste, he would be at the greatest possible distance from both towns when noon came. It seemed to him that, in this, circumstance was giving him a break, so he said to the negro:
paragraphs.zh: “好吧，见鬼，”杰生说，“到十二点就会下倾盆大雨。”他看着天空，想着下雨，想着光滑的粘土路，而自己却停在离城镇几英里的地方。他带着一种胜利的心情想到了这一点，事实上他将错过晚餐，通过现在出发，满足他匆忙的冲动，当中午到来时，他将尽可能远离这两个城镇。他觉得，在这种情况下，情况给了他喘息的机会，所以他对黑人说：

paragraphs.en: “What the hell are you doing? Has somebody paid you to keep this car standing here as long as you can?”
paragraphs.zh: “你到底在做什么？有人付钱给你让你把这辆车停在这里尽可能长时间吗？”

paragraphs.en: “Dis here ti’ aint got no air a-tall in hit,” the negro said.
paragraphs.zh: “在这里，你没有受到任何打击，”黑人说。

paragraphs.en: “Then get the hell away from there and let me have that tube,” Jason said.
paragraphs.zh: “那就滚开吧，把那根管子交给我，”杰生说。

paragraphs.en: “Hit up now,” the negro said, rising. “You kin ride now.”
paragraphs.zh: “现在就打吧，”黑人站起来说道。“你现在可以骑车了。”

paragraphs.en: Jason got in and started the engine and drove off. He went into second gear, the engine spluttering and gasping, and he raced the engine, jamming the throttle down and snapping the choker in and out savagely. “It’s goin to rain,” he said, “Get me half way there, and rain like hell.” And he drove on out of the bells and out of town, thinking of himself slogging through the mud, hunting a team. “And every damn one of them will be at church.” He thought of how he’d find a church at last and take a team and of the owner coming out, shouting at him and of himself striking the man down. “I’m Jason Compson. See if you can stop me. See if you can elect a man to office that can stop me,” he said, thinking of himself entering the courthouse with a file of soldiers and dragging the sheriff out. “Thinks he can sit with his hands folded and see me lose my job. I’ll show him about jobs.” Of his niece he did not think at all, nor of the arbitrary valuation of the money. Neither of them had had entity or individuality for him for ten years; together they merely symbolized the job in the bank of which he had been deprived before he ever got it.
paragraphs.zh: 杰生上了车，发动引擎，开走了。他挂入二档，发动机发出噼啪作响的喘息声，他加速发动机，猛踩油门，猛烈地把节流器猛地拉进拉出。“要下雨了，”他说，“让我走到一半，雨下得很大。”他开车离开钟声，出城，想着自己在泥泞中艰难前行，寻找一支队伍。“他们每个人都会去教堂。”他想到自己最终会找到一座教堂，并带领一支队伍，想到教堂的主人出来，对他大喊大叫，然后自己将那个人打倒。“我是杰生康普生。看看你能不能阻止我。看看你能不能选出一个能阻止我的人上任，”他说，想象着自己带着一队士兵走进法院，把治安官拖了出来。“他认为他可以袖手旁观，看着我失去工作。我会向他介绍工作。”他根本没有想到他的侄女，也没有想到对这笔钱的任意估价。十年来，他们两个对他来说都没有实体或个性；它们在一起只是象征着他在银行里的工作，而在他得到这份工作之前，他就被剥夺了这份工作。

paragraphs.en: The air brightened, the running shadow patches were not the obverse, and it seemed to him that the fact that the day was clearing was another cunning stroke on the part of the foe, the fresh battle toward which he was carrying ancient wounds. From time to time he passed churches, unpainted frame buildings with sheet iron steeples, surrounded by tethered teams and shabby motorcars, and it seemed to him that each of them was a picket-post where the rear guards of Circumstance peeped fleetingly back at him. “And damn You, too,” he said, “See if You can stop me,” thinking of himself, his file of soldiers with the manacled sheriff in the rear, dragging Omnipotence down from His throne, if necessary; of the embattled legions of both hell and heaven through which he tore his way and put his hands at last on his fleeing niece.
paragraphs.zh: 空气变亮了，反面的阴影斑驳不断，在他看来，天色晴朗这一事实是敌人的又一次狡猾的打击，他带着古老的伤口迎接新的战斗。他时不时地经过教堂，那些没有上漆、带有铁皮尖塔的框架建筑，周围都是系着绳索的队伍和破旧的汽车，在他看来，每一座教堂都是一个纠察队，环境的后卫们在其中飞快地向他窥视。“你也该死，”他说，“看看你能不能阻止我。”他想到了他自己，他的士兵队伍，后面还有戴着手铐的治安官，如果有必要，他会把全能者从他的宝座上拖下来；他在地狱和天堂的严阵以待的军团中杀出一条血路，最终把手放在了逃跑的侄女身上。

paragraphs.en: The wind was out of the southeast. It blew steadily upon his cheek. It seemed that he could feel the prolonged blow of it sinking through his skull, and suddenly with an old premonition he clapped the brakes on and stopped and sat perfectly still. Then he lifted his hand to his neck and began to curse, and sat there, cursing in a harsh whisper. When it was necessary for him to drive for any length of time he fortified himself with a handkerchief soaked in camphor, which he would tie about his throat when clear of town, thus inhaling the fumes, and he got out and lifted the seat cushion on the chance that there might be a forgotten one there. He looked beneath both seats and stood again for a while, cursing, seeing himself mocked by his own triumphing. He closed his eyes, leaning on the door. He could return and get the forgotten camphor, or he could go on. In either case, his head would be splitting, but at home he could be sure of finding camphor on Sunday, while if he went on he could not be sure. But if he went back, he would be an hour and a half later in reaching Mottson. “Maybe I can drive slow,” he said. “Maybe I can drive slow, thinking of something else—”
paragraphs.zh: 风是东南风。它稳定地吹在他的脸颊上。他似乎能感觉到那股持续不断的冲击力穿过他的头骨，突然带着一种古老的预感，他猛地踩下刹车，停了下来，一动不动地坐着。然后他把手举到脖子上开始咒骂，然后坐在那里，低声咒骂。当他需要开车走很长一段时间时，他都会用一块浸有樟脑的手帕来加强自己，出城时他会把手帕系在喉咙上，从而吸入烟雾，然后他下车并抬起座垫，以防那里可能有一个被遗忘的东西。他看了看两个座位下面，又站了一会儿，咒骂着，看到自己被自己的胜利所嘲笑。他闭上眼睛，靠在门上。他可以返回并取得被遗忘的樟脑，或者他可以继续前进。无论哪种情况，他的头都会裂开，但在家里，他可以肯定周日会找到樟脑，但如果他继续下去，他就不能确定了。但如果他回去，他将在一个半小时后到达莫特森。“也许我可以开慢一点，”他说。“也许我可以开慢一点，想想别的事——”

paragraphs.en: He got in and started. “I’ll think of something else,” he said, so he thought about Lorraine. He imagined himself in bed with her, only he was just lying beside her, pleading with her to help him, then he thought of the money again, and that he had been outwitted by a woman, a girl. If he could just believe it was the man who had robbed him. But to have been robbed of that which was to have compensated him for the lost job, which he had acquired through so much effort and risk, by the very symbol of the lost job itself, and worst of all, by a bitch of a girl. He drove on, shielding his face from the steady wind with the corner of his coat.
paragraphs.zh: 他上车开始。“我会想点别的事。”他说道，于是他想到了洛兰。他想象自己和她躺在床上，只是躺在她身边，恳求她帮助他，然后他又想到了那笔钱，想到了他被一个女人，一个女孩欺骗了。如果他能相信是那个男人抢劫了他就好了。但是，他通过如此多的努力和风险才获得的这份工作，本应补偿他失去的工作，却被失去工作本身的象征，最糟糕的是，被一个贱女孩剥夺了。他继续前行，用外套的一角遮住脸，挡住持续不断的风。

paragraphs.en: He could see the opposed forces of his destiny and his will drawing swiftly together now, toward a junction that would be irrevocable; he became cunning. I cant make a blunder, he told himself. There would be just one right thing, without alternatives: he must do that. He believed that both of them would know him on sight, while he’d have to trust to seeing her first, unless the man still wore the red tie. And the fact that he must depend on that red tie seemed to be the sum of the impending disaster; he could almost smell it, feel it above the throbbing of his head.
paragraphs.zh: 他可以看到他的命运和他的意志的对立力量现在迅速聚集在一起，走向一个不可逆转的交汇点；他变得狡猾。我不能犯错误，他告诉自己。只有一件事是正确的，没有其他选择：他必须这样做。他相信他们两人一见面就会认识他，而他必须相信自己先见到她，除非那个男人仍然戴着红色领带。事实上，他必须依赖那条红领带，这似乎是即将到来的灾难的总和。他几乎能闻到它的味道，感觉到它在他头顶的悸动之上。

paragraphs.en: He crested the final hill. Smoke lay in the valley, and roofs, a spire or two above trees. He drove down the hill and into the town, slowing, telling himself again of the need for caution, to find where the tent was located first. He could not see very well now, and he knew that it was the disaster which kept telling him to go directly and get something for his head. At a filling station they told him that the tent was not up yet, but that the show cars were on a siding at the station. He drove there.
paragraphs.zh: 他登上了最后一座山峰。山谷里浓烟滚滚，屋顶和树木上方有一两座尖塔。他开车下了山，进了镇子，放慢了速度，再次告诉自己需要小心，首先要找到帐篷所在的位置。他现在看得不太清楚了，他知道是灾难在不断地告诉他要直接去拿点东西来安抚他的脑袋。在加油站，他们告诉他帐篷还没有搭起来，但展示车已经停在加油站的支线上。他开车去那里。

paragraphs.en: Two gaudily painted pullman cars stood on the track. He reconnoitred them before he got out. He was trying to breathe shallowly, so that the blood would not beat so in his skull. He got out and went along the station wall, watching the cars. A few garments hung out of the windows, limp and crinkled, as though they had been recently laundered. On the earth beside the steps of one sat three canvas chairs. But he saw no sign of life at all until a man in a dirty apron came to the door and emptied a pan of dishwater with a broad gesture, the sunlight glinting on the metal belly of the pan, then entered the car again.
paragraphs.zh: 两辆涂装华丽的普尔曼汽车停在轨道上。他出去之前侦察了一下他们。他试着浅呼吸，这样血液就不会在他的头骨中剧烈跳动。他下了车，沿着车站围墙走去，观察着车厢。几件衣服挂在窗外，软塌塌的，皱巴巴的，好像刚洗过一样。台阶旁边的地上放着三张帆布椅。但他根本没有看到任何生命迹象，直到一个穿着脏围裙的男人走到门口，用一个大动作倒空一盆洗碗水，阳光在盘子的金属腹部上闪闪发光，然后又进了车。

paragraphs.en: Now I’ll have to take him by surprise, before he can warn them, he thought. It never occurred to him that they might not be there, in the car. That they should not be there, that the whole result should not hinge on whether he saw them first or they saw him first, would be opposed to all nature and contrary to the whole rhythm of events. And more than that: he must see them first, get the money back, then what they did would be of no importance to him, while otherwise the whole world would know that he, Jason Compson, had been robbed by Quentin, his niece, a bitch.
paragraphs.zh: 现在我必须让他措手不及，然后他才能警告他们，他想。他从来没有想到他们可能不在车里。他们不应该在那里，整个结果不应该取决于是他先看到他们还是他们先看到他，这将违背所有自然，也违背事件的整个节奏。更重要的是，他必须先见到他们，把钱拿回来，然后他们做了什么对他来说就不再重要了，否则全世界都会知道他杰生康普生被他侄女昆丁这个贱人抢了。

paragraphs.en: He reconnoitred again. Then he went to the car and mounted the steps, swiftly and quietly, and paused at the door. The galley was dark, rank with stale food. The man was a white blur, singing in a cracked, shaky tenor. An old man, he thought, and not as big as I am. He entered the car as the man looked up.
paragraphs.zh: 他再次侦察。然后他走到车旁，迅速而安静地走上台阶，在门口停了下来。厨房里漆黑一片，堆满了不新鲜的食物。这个男人是一个白色的模糊人影，用嘶哑、颤抖的男高音唱歌。一个老人，他想，而且没有我那么高大。当那人抬起头时，他走进了车里。

paragraphs.en: “Hey?” the man said, stopping his song.
paragraphs.zh: “嘿？”男人停下了歌声说道。

paragraphs.en: “Where are they?” Jason said. “Quick, now. In the sleeping car?”
paragraphs.zh: “他们在哪儿？”杰生说道。“快点，现在。在卧铺车厢里？”

paragraphs.en: “Where’s who?” the man said.
paragraphs.zh: “谁在哪儿？”那人说道。

paragraphs.en: “Dont lie to me,” Jason said. He blundered on in the cluttered obscurity.
paragraphs.zh: “别骗我。”杰生说。他在混乱的黑暗中跌跌撞撞地前行。

paragraphs.en: “What’s that?” the other said, “Who you calling a liar?” And when Jason grasped his shoulder he exclaimed, “Look out, fellow!”
paragraphs.zh: “那是什么？”另一个说：“你说谁是骗子？”当杰生抓住他的肩膀时，他喊道：“小心，伙计！”

paragraphs.en: “Dont lie,” Jason said, “Where are they?”
paragraphs.zh: “别撒谎了，”杰生说，“他们在哪儿？”

paragraphs.en: “Why, you bastard,” the man said. His arm was frail and thin in Jason’s grasp. He tried to wrench free, then he turned and fell to scrabbling on the littered table behind him.
paragraphs.zh: “为什么，你这个混蛋，”那人说。他的手臂在杰生的手里显得又瘦又弱。他试图挣脱，然后转身倒在身后乱七八糟的桌子上乱抓。

paragraphs.en: “Come on,” Jason said, “Where are they?”
paragraphs.zh: “快点，”杰生说，“他们在哪儿？”

paragraphs.en: “I’ll tell you where they are,” the man shrieked, “Lemme find my butcher knife.”
paragraphs.zh: “我会告诉你他们在哪里，”那人尖叫道，“让我找到我的屠刀。”

paragraphs.en: “Here,” Jason said, trying to hold the other, “I’m just asking you a question.”
paragraphs.zh: “在这里，”杰生试图抓住对方，“我只是问你一个问题。”

paragraphs.en: “You bastard,” the other shrieked, scrabbling at the table. Jason tried to grasp him in both arms, trying to prison the puny fury of him. The man’s body felt so old, so frail, yet so fatally single-purposed that for the first time Jason saw clear and unshadowed the disaster toward which he rushed.
paragraphs.zh: “你这个混蛋，”另一个尖叫着，在桌子上乱抓。杰生试图抓住他的双臂，试图囚禁他微不足道的愤怒。这个人的身体感觉如此苍老，如此虚弱，却又如此致命地单一，杰生第一次看清了他所面临的灾难。

paragraphs.en: “Quit it!” he said, “Here! Here! I’ll get out. Give me time, and I’ll get out.”
paragraphs.zh: “别说了！”他说：“这里！这里！我要出去了。给我时间，我会出去的。”

paragraphs.en: “Call me a liar,” the other wailed, “Lemme go. Lemme go just one minute. I’ll show you.”
paragraphs.zh: “叫我骗子吧，”另一个哭着说，“让我走。让我走一分钟。我给你看。”

paragraphs.en: Jason glared wildly about, holding the other. Outside it was now bright and sunny, swift and bright and empty, and he thought of the people soon to be going quietly home to Sunday dinner, decorously festive, and of himself trying to hold the fatal, furious little old man whom he dared not release long enough to turn his back and run.
paragraphs.zh: 杰生抓着另一只，疯狂地瞪着四周。外面现在阳光明媚，风雨无阻，空荡荡，他想到人们很快就要安静地回家吃周日的晚餐，举行庄严的节日，他想到自己试图抓住那个致命的、愤怒的小老头，他不敢放开他足够长的时间，以至于无法转身逃跑。

paragraphs.en: “Will you quit long enough for me to get out?” he said, “Will you?” But the other still struggled, and Jason freed one hand and struck him on the head. A clumsy, hurried blow, and not hard, but the other slumped immediately and slid clattering among pans and buckets to the floor. Jason stood above him, panting, listening. Then he turned and ran from the car. At the door he restrained himself and descended more slowly and stood there again. His breath made a hah hah hah sound and he stood there trying to repress it, darting his gaze this way and that, when at a scuffling sound behind him he turned in time to see the little old man leaping awkwardly and furiously from the vestibule, a rusty hatchet high in his hand.
paragraphs.zh: “你能放弃足够长的时间让我出去吗？”他说：“你愿意吗？”但另一人仍在挣扎，杰生腾出一只手，打在他的头上。笨拙而匆忙的一击，并不重，但另一个立即倒在了平底锅和水桶之间，叮当作响地滑到地板上。杰生站在他上方，气喘吁吁地听着。然后他转身跑下车。到了门口，他克制住自己，放慢了脚步，又站在那里。他的呼吸发出“哈哈哈”的声音，他站在那里试图压制住，目光东张西望，当身后传来一阵拖拉声时，他及时转过身，看到小老头笨拙而愤怒地从门厅里跳出来，手里高举着一把生锈的斧头。

paragraphs.en: He grasped at the hatchet, feeling no shock but knowing that he was falling, thinking So this is how it’ll end, and he believed that he was about to die and when something crashed against the back of his head he thought How did he hit me there? Only maybe he hit me a long time ago, he thought, And I just now felt it, and he thought Hurry. Hurry. Get it over with, and then a furious desire not to die seized him and he struggled, hearing the old man wailing and cursing in his cracked voice.
paragraphs.zh: 他抓住斧头，没有感到震惊，但知道自己正在坠落，心想这就是结局，他相信自己快要死了，当有东西撞到他的后脑勺时，他想他是怎么打到我那里的？只是也许他很久以前就打过我了，他想，而我现在才感觉到，他想快点。匆忙。把这一切都结束了，然后一种强烈的不想死的欲望抓住了他，他挣扎着，听到老人用嘶哑的声音哭泣和咒骂。

paragraphs.en: He still struggled when they hauled him to his feet, but they held him and he ceased.
paragraphs.zh: 当他们把他拉起来时，他仍在挣扎，但他们抓住了他，他停了下来。

paragraphs.en: “Am I bleeding much?” he said, “The back of my head. Am I bleeding?” He was still saying that while he felt himself being propelled rapidly away, heard the old man’s thin furious voice dying away behind him. “Look at my head,” he said, “Wait, I—”
paragraphs.zh: “我流血很多吗？”他说：“我的后脑勺。我流血了吗？”他正说着，就感觉自己被飞快地推开，身后传来老者微弱、愤怒的声音渐渐消失的声音。“看看我的头，”他说，“等等，我——”

paragraphs.en: “Wait, hell,” the man who held him said, “That damn little wasp’ll kill you. Keep going. You aint hurt.”
paragraphs.zh: “等等，见鬼，”抱着他的人说，“那只该死的小黄蜂会杀了你。继续走。你没有受伤。”

paragraphs.en: “He hit me,” Jason said. “Am I bleeding?”
paragraphs.zh: “他打了我，”杰生说。“我流血了吗？”

paragraphs.en: “Keep going,” the other said. He led Jason on around the corner of the station, to the empty platform where an express truck stood, where grass grew rigidly in a plot bordered with rigid flowers and a sign in electric lights: Keep your [Illustration: Eye] on Mottson, the gap filled by a human eye with an electric pupil. The man released him.
paragraphs.zh: “继续，”另一个说。他领着杰生绕过车站的拐角处，来到停着一辆快车的空站台，那里的草丛生硬地生长着，周围长满了僵硬的花朵，还有一个电灯标志：把你的[插图：眼睛]放在莫特森身上，这个间隙由一只带有电瞳孔的人眼填补。男人松开了他。

paragraphs.en: “Now,” he said, “You get on out of here and stay out. What were you trying to do? Commit suicide?”
paragraphs.zh: “现在，”他说，“你离开这里，呆在外面。你想做什么？自杀？”

paragraphs.en: “I was looking for two people,” Jason said. “I just asked him where they were.”
paragraphs.zh: “我正在找两个人，”杰生说。“我只是问他他们在哪里。”

paragraphs.en: “Who you looking for?”
paragraphs.zh: “你找谁？”

paragraphs.en: “It’s a girl,” Jason said. “And a man. He had on a red tie in Jefferson yesterday. With this show. They robbed me.”
paragraphs.zh: “是个女孩。”杰生说。“还有一个男人。他昨天在杰斐逊打着红色领带。在这个节目中。他们抢劫了我。”

paragraphs.en: “Oh,” the man said. “You’re the one, are you. Well, they aint here.”
paragraphs.zh: “哦，”男人说。“就是你，是吗。好吧，他们不在这里。”

paragraphs.en: “I reckon so,” Jason said. He leaned against the wall and put his hand to the back of his head and looked at his palm. “I thought I was bleeding,” he said. “I thought he hit me with that hatchet.”
paragraphs.zh: “我想是的。”杰生说。他靠在墙上，把手放在后脑勺上，看着自己的手掌。“我以为我在流血，”他说。“我以为他用斧头打了我。”

paragraphs.en: “You hit your head on the rail,” the man said. “You better go on. They aint here.”
paragraphs.zh: “你的头撞到了栏杆上，”那人说。“你最好继续说。他们不在这里。”

paragraphs.en: “Yes. He said they were not here. I thought he was lying.”
paragraphs.zh: “是的。他说他们不在这里。我以为他在撒谎。”

paragraphs.en: “Do you think I’m lying?” the man said.
paragraphs.zh: “你认为我在撒谎吗？”那人说道。

paragraphs.en: “No,” Jason said. “I know they’re not here.”
paragraphs.zh: “不，”杰生说。“我知道他们不在这里。”

paragraphs.en: “I told him to get the hell out of there, both of them,” the man said. “I wont have nothing like that in my show. I run a respectable show, with a respectable troupe.”
paragraphs.zh: “我告诉他，他们俩都赶紧离开那里，”那人说。“我的演出中不会有这样的东西。我经营着一场受人尊敬的演出，有一支受人尊敬的剧团。”

paragraphs.en: “Yes,” Jason said. “You dont know where they went?”
paragraphs.zh: “是的。”杰生说。“你不知道他们去了哪里？”

paragraphs.en: “No. And I dont want to know. No member of my show can pull a stunt like that. You her—brother?”
paragraphs.zh: “不。我也不想知道。我的节目中没有一个成员能做出这样的特技。你是她的——兄弟吗？”

paragraphs.en: “No,” Jason said. “It dont matter. I just wanted to see them. You sure he didn’t hit me? No blood, I mean.”
paragraphs.zh: “不，”杰生说。“没关系。我只是想看看他们。你确定他没有打我吗？我是说，没有流血。”

paragraphs.en: “There would have been blood if I hadn’t got there when I did. You stay away from here, now. That little bastard’ll kill you. That your car yonder?”
paragraphs.zh: “如果我当时没有赶到的话，那里就会有血迹。你现在就离开这里。那个小混蛋会杀了你。那边是你的车吗？”

paragraphs.en: “Yes.”
paragraphs.zh: “是的。”

paragraphs.en: “Well, you get in it and go back to Jefferson. If you find them, it wont be in my show. I run a respectable show. You say they robbed you?”
paragraphs.zh: “好吧，你进去然后回到杰斐逊。如果你找到他们，那不会出现在我的节目中。我经营着一个受人尊敬的节目。你说他们抢劫了你？”

paragraphs.en: “No,” Jason said, “It dont make any difference.” He went to the car and got in. What is it I must do? he thought. Then he remembered. He started the engine and drove slowly up the street until he found a drugstore. The door was locked. He stood for a while with his hand on the knob and his head bent a little. Then he turned away and when a man came along after a while he asked if there was a drugstore open anywhere, but there was not. Then he asked when the northbound train ran, and the man told him at two thirty. He crossed the pavement and got in the car again and sat there. After a while two negro lads passed. He called to them.
paragraphs.zh: “不，”杰生说，“这没有什么区别。”他走到车旁，上了车。我必须做什么？他想。然后他想起来了。他启动了引擎，慢慢地沿着街道行驶，直到找到一家药店。门锁着。他手放在把手上站了一会儿，头微微低着。然后他转过身去，过了一会儿，当一个男人走过来时，他问是否有药店开门，但没有。然后他问北行的火车什么时候开，那人告诉他是两点三十分。他穿过人行道，再次上车坐在那里。过了一会儿，两个黑人小伙子走过来。他呼唤他们。

paragraphs.en: “Can either of you boys drive a car?”
paragraphs.zh: “你们两个男孩会开车吗？”

paragraphs.en: “Yes, suh.”
paragraphs.zh: “是的，先生。”

paragraphs.en: “What’ll you charge to drive me to Jefferson right away?”
paragraphs.zh: “你马上开车送我去杰斐逊要多少钱？”

paragraphs.en: They looked at one another, murmuring.
paragraphs.zh: 他们互相看着对方，小声嘀咕着。

paragraphs.en: “I’ll pay a dollar,” Jason said.
paragraphs.zh: “我付一美元。”杰生说。

paragraphs.en: They murmured again. “Couldn’t go fer dat,” one said.
paragraphs.zh: 他们又低声议论起来。“无法前往，”其中一位说道。

paragraphs.en: “What will you go for?”
paragraphs.zh: “你去做什么？”

paragraphs.en: “Kin you go?” one said.
paragraphs.zh: “你去吗？”一个说。

paragraphs.en: “I cant git off,” the other said. “Whyn’t you drive him up dar? You aint got nothin to do.”
paragraphs.zh: “我下不了车，”另一个说。“你为什么不开车送他上去呢？你没什么可做的。”

paragraphs.en: “Yes I is.”
paragraphs.zh: “是的，我是。”

paragraphs.en: “Whut you got to do?”
paragraphs.zh: “你要做什么？”

paragraphs.en: They murmured again, laughing.
paragraphs.zh: 他们又低声笑了起来。

paragraphs.en: “I’ll give you two dollars,” Jason said. “Either of you.”
paragraphs.zh: “我给你两块钱。”杰生说。“你们两个都可以。”

paragraphs.en: “I cant git away neither,” the first said.
paragraphs.zh: “我也逃不掉，”第一个说。

paragraphs.en: “All right,” Jason said. “Go on.”
paragraphs.zh: “好吧。”杰生说。“继续。”

paragraphs.en: He sat there for sometime. He heard a clock strike the half hour, then people began to pass, in Sunday and Easter clothes. Some looked at him as they passed, at the man sitting quietly behind the wheel of a small car, with his invisible life ravelled out about him like a wornout sock. After a while a negro in overalls came up.
paragraphs.zh: 他在那里坐了一段时间。他听到钟声敲响了半点，然后人们开始走过，穿着周日和复活节的衣服。有些人在经过时看着他，看着那个安静地坐在一辆小汽车的方向盘后面的男人，他无形的生命像一只破旧的袜子一样在他周围散开。过了一会儿，一个穿着工作服的黑人走了过来。

paragraphs.en: “Is you de one wants to go to Jefferson?” he said.
paragraphs.zh: “你想去杰斐逊吗？”他说。

paragraphs.en: “Yes,” Jason said. “What’ll you charge me?”
paragraphs.zh: “是的。”杰生说。“你要收我什么钱？”

paragraphs.en: “Fo dollars.”
paragraphs.zh: “美元。”

paragraphs.en: “Give you two.”
paragraphs.zh: “给你两个。”

paragraphs.en: “Cant go fer no less’n fo.” The man in the car sat quietly. He wasn’t even looking at him. The negro said, “You want me er not?”
paragraphs.zh: “不能再少了。”车里的男人静静地坐着。他甚至没有看他。黑人说：“你想要我吗？”

paragraphs.en: “All right,” Jason said, “Get in.”
paragraphs.zh: “好吧，”杰生说，“上车吧。”

paragraphs.en: He moved over and the negro took the wheel. Jason closed his eyes. I can get something for it at Jefferson, he told himself, easing himself to the jolting, I can get something there. They drove on, along the streets where people were turning peacefully into houses and Sunday dinners, and on out of town. He thought that. He wasn’t thinking of home, where Ben and Luster were eating cold dinner at the kitchen table. Something—the absence of disaster, threat, in any constant evil—permitted him to forget Jefferson as any place which he had ever seen before, where his life must resume itself.
paragraphs.zh: 他走过去，黑人接过方向盘。杰生闭上了眼睛。我可以在杰斐逊那里得到一些东西，他告诉自己，让自己放松下来，我可以在那里得到一些东西。他们沿着街道继续前行，人们平静地走进房屋，享受周日的晚餐，然后驶出城镇。他是这么想的。他没有想到家，本和勒斯特正在厨房的餐桌上吃着冷晚餐。某种东西——没有灾难、威胁，没有任何持续的邪恶——让他忘记了杰斐逊这个他以前见过的地方，在那里他的生活必须重新开始。

paragraphs.en: When Ben and Luster were done Dilsey sent them outdoors. “And see kin you keep let him alone twell fo oclock. T.P. be here den.”
paragraphs.zh: 当本和勒斯特完成后，迪尔西将他们送到了户外。“请让你的亲戚今晚不要打扰他。蒂·皮在这儿。”

paragraphs.en: “Yessum,” Luster said. They went out. Dilsey ate her dinner and cleared up the kitchen. Then she went to the foot of the stairs and listened, but there was no sound. She returned through the kitchen and out the outer door and stopped on the steps. Ben and Luster were not in sight, but while she stood there she heard another sluggish twang from the direction of the cellar door and she went to the door and looked down upon a repetition of the morning’s scene.
paragraphs.zh: “是的，”勒斯特说。他们出去了。迪尔西吃完晚饭，清理了厨房。然后她走到楼梯脚下听了听，却没有任何声音。她穿过厨房，走出外门，停在台阶上。本和勒斯特不在视线范围内，但当她站在那里时，她听到地窖门的方向又传来一阵迟缓的声音，她走到门口，俯视着早上的场景的重复。

paragraphs.en: “He done it jes dat way,” Luster said. He contemplated the motionless saw with a kind of hopeful dejection. “I aint got de right thing to hit it wid yit,” he said.
paragraphs.zh: “他就是这么做的，”勒斯特说。他带着一种充满希望的沮丧注视着那把一动不动的锯子。“我没有合适的东西来击中它，”他说。

paragraphs.en: “En you aint gwine find hit down here, neither,” Dilsey said. “You take him on out in de sun. You bofe get pneumonia down here on dis wet flo.”
paragraphs.zh: “你在这里也没有被击中，”迪尔西说。“你在阳光下带他出去。在这湿漉漉的地板上，你一定会得肺炎。”

paragraphs.en: She waited and watched them cross the yard toward a clump of cedar trees near the fence. Then she went on to her cabin.
paragraphs.zh: 她等着，看着他们穿过院子，走向栅栏附近的一丛雪松树。然后她继续往自己的小屋走去。

paragraphs.en: “Now, dont you git started,” Luster said, “I had enough trouble wid you today.” There was a hammock made of barrel staves slatted into woven wires. Luster lay down in the swing, but Ben went on vaguely and purposelessly. He began to whimper again. “Hush, now,” Luster said, “I fixin to whup you.” He lay back in the swing. Ben had stopped moving, but Luster could hear him whimpering. “Is you gwine hush, er aint you?” Luster said. He got up and followed and came upon Ben squatting before a small mound of earth. At either end of it an empty bottle of blue glass that once contained poison was fixed in the ground. In one was a withered stalk of jimson weed. Ben squatted before it, moaning, a slow, inarticulate sound. Still moaning he sought vaguely about and found a twig and put it in the other bottle. “Whyn’t you hush?” Luster said, “You want me to give you somethin’ to sho nough moan about? Sposin I does dis.” He knelt and swept the bottle suddenly up and behind him. Ben ceased moaning. He squatted, looking at the small depression where the bottle had sat, then as he drew his lungs full Luster brought the bottle back into view. “Hush!” he hissed, “Dont you dast to beller! Dont you. Dar hit is. See? Here. You fixin to start ef you stays here. Come on, les go see ef dey started knockin ball yit.” He took Ben’s arm and drew him up and they went to the fence and stood side by side there, peering between the matted honeysuckle not yet in bloom.
paragraphs.zh: “现在，别开始了，”勒斯特说，“今天我和你的麻烦已经够多了。”有一个吊床，是用金属丝编织而成的桶形板条制成的。勒斯特躺在秋千上，但本却含糊其辞、漫无目的地继续前行。他又开始呜咽。“嘘，现在，”勒斯特说，“我打算打你一顿。”他向后靠在秋千上。本已经停止了动作，但勒斯特能听到他的抽泣声。“你安静点吗，呃不是吗？”勒斯特说。他起身跟了上去，发现本蹲在一个小土堆前。它的两端固定着一个装有毒药的蓝色玻璃空瓶。其中一根是一根枯萎的曼陀罗茎。本蹲在它面前，缓慢而含糊地呻吟着。他仍在呻吟着，模糊地寻找着，找到了一根树枝，把它放进了另一个瓶子里。“你为什么不安静？”勒斯特说：“你想让我给你一些让你不再抱怨的东西吗？我确实这么做了。”他跪下，突然将瓶子扫到身后。本停止了呻吟。他蹲下来，看着瓶子所在的小凹陷，然后当他吸满肺部时，勒斯特把瓶子带回到了视野中。“嘘！”他嘶声说道：“你别冲向贝勒！别这样。打球了。看到了吗？就在这里。如果你留在这里，你就准备开始吧。来吧，我们去看看他们开始敲球了。”他拉着本的手臂，把他拉了起来，他们走到栅栏旁，并肩站在那里，在尚未开花的缠结金银花之间凝视着。

paragraphs.en: “Dar,” Luster said, “Dar come some. See um?”
paragraphs.zh: “亲爱的，”勒斯特说，“亲爱的来一些。看到了吗？”

paragraphs.en: They watched the foursome play onto the green and out, and move to the tee and drive. Ben watched, whimpering, slobbering. When the foursome went on he followed along the fence, bobbing and moaning. One said.
paragraphs.zh: 他们看着四人打上果岭、出局，然后移至发球台并开球。本看着，呜咽着，流着口水。当四人继续前行时，他沿着栅栏跟着走，摇晃着，呻吟着。一说。

paragraphs.en: “Here, caddie. Bring the bag.”
paragraphs.zh: “给你，球童。把球包拿过来。”

paragraphs.en: “Hush, Benjy,” Luster said, but Ben went on at his shambling trot, clinging to the fence, wailing in his hoarse, hopeless voice. The man played and went on, Ben keeping pace with him until the fence turned at right angles, and he clung to the fence, watching the people move on and away.
paragraphs.zh: “嘘，班吉，”勒斯特说，但本继续摇摇晃晃地小跑，紧紧抓住栅栏，用嘶哑、绝望的声音哀号。那个人一边玩一边继续前行，本跟在他后面，直到栅栏转成直角，他紧抓住栅栏，看着人们走开。

paragraphs.en: “Will you hush now?” Luster said, “Will you hush now?” He shook Ben’s arm. Ben clung to the fence, wailing steadily and hoarsely. “Aint you gwine stop?” Luster said, “Or is you?” Ben gazed through the fence. “All right, den,” Luster said, “You want somethin to beller about?” He looked over his shoulder, toward the house. Then he whispered: “Caddy! Beller now. Caddy! Caddy! Caddy!”
paragraphs.zh: “现在可以安静点吗？”勒斯特说：“现在可以安静点了吗？”他摇了摇本的手臂。本紧紧抓住栅栏，持续地、嘶哑地哭泣。“你不停下来吗？”勒斯特说：“或者是你？”本透过栅栏凝视着。“好吧，丹恩，”勒斯特说，“你想听点什么吗？”他回头看向房子。然后他低声说道：“凯蒂！现在是贝勒。凯蒂！凯蒂！凯蒂！”

paragraphs.en: A moment later, in the slow intervals of Ben’s voice, Luster heard Dilsey calling. He took Ben by the arm and they crossed the yard toward her.
paragraphs.zh: 过了一会儿，在本缓慢的说话声中，勒斯特听到了迪尔西的呼唤声。他挽着本的手臂，他们穿过院子朝她走来。

paragraphs.en: “I tole you he warn’t gwine stay quiet,” Luster said.
paragraphs.zh: “我告诉过你，他不会保持安静，”勒斯特说。

paragraphs.en: “You vilyun!” Dilsey said, “Whut you done to him?”
paragraphs.zh: “你这个维云！”迪尔西说：“你对他做了什么？”

paragraphs.en: “I aint done nothin. I tole you when dem folks start playin, he git started up.”
paragraphs.zh: “我什么也没做。我告诉过你，当人们开始玩耍时，他就开始了。”

paragraphs.en: “You come on here,” Dilsey said. “Hush, Benjy. Hush, now.” But he wouldn’t hush. They crossed the yard quickly and went to the cabin and entered. “Run git dat shoe,” Dilsey said. “Dont you sturb Miss Cahline, now. Ef she say anything, tell her I got him. Go on, now; you kin sho do dat right, I reckon.” Luster went out. Dilsey led Ben to the bed and drew him down beside her and she held him, rocking back and forth, wiping his drooling mouth upon the hem of her skirt. “Hush, now,” she said, stroking his head, “Hush. Dilsey got you.” But he bellowed slowly, abjectly, without tears; the grave hopeless sound of all voiceless misery under the sun. Luster returned, carrying a white satin slipper. It was yellow now, and cracked and soiled, and when they placed it into Ben’s hand he hushed for a while. But he still whimpered, and soon he lifted his voice again.
paragraphs.zh: “你过来吧，”迪尔西说。“嘘，班吉。嘘，现在。”但他不会安静。他们快步穿过院子，来到小屋前，走了进去。“跑 git dat 鞋，”迪尔西说。“现在，别打扰卡林小姐。如果她说什么，就告诉她我抓住了他。继续吧，现在；我想你一定会做对的。”勒斯特出去了。迪尔西领着本走到床边，把他拉到她身边，她抱着他，前后摇晃，用裙子下摆擦着他流着口水的嘴。“嘘，现在，”她抚摸着他的头，“嘘。迪尔西抓住你了。”但他缓慢地、悲惨地吼叫着，没有流泪。阳光下所有无声的苦难所发出的庄严而绝望的声音。勒斯特回来了，手里拿着一只白色缎子拖鞋。现在它已经变黄了，又裂又脏，当他们把它放到本的手里时，他安静了一会儿。但他仍然呜咽着，很快他又提高了声音。

paragraphs.en: “You reckon you kin find T. P.?” Dilsey said.
paragraphs.zh: “你认为你能找到蒂·皮吗？”迪尔西说道。

paragraphs.en: “He say yistiddy he gwine out to St John’s today. Say he be back at fo.”
paragraphs.zh: “他说他今天要去圣约翰教堂。说他回来了。”

paragraphs.en: Dilsey rocked back and forth, stroking Ben’s head.
paragraphs.zh: 迪尔西前后摇晃着，抚摸着本的头。

paragraphs.en: “Dis long time, O Jesus,” she said, “Dis long time.”
paragraphs.zh: “耶稣啊，时间已经过去了，”她说，“时间已经过去了。”

paragraphs.en: “I kin drive dat surrey, mammy,” Luster said.
paragraphs.zh: “我可以开车去萨里，妈妈，”勒斯特说。

paragraphs.en: “You kill bofe y’all,” Dilsey said, “You do hit fer devilment. I knows you got plenty sense to. But I cant trust you. Hush, now,” she said. “Hush. Hush.”
paragraphs.zh: “你们杀了你们所有人，”迪尔西说，“你们确实伤了人性。我知道你们很有理智。但我不能相信你们。嘘，现在，”她说。“嘘。嘘。”

paragraphs.en: “Nome I wont,” Luster said. “I drives wid T. P.” Dilsey rocked back and forth, holding Ben. “Miss Cahline say ef you cant quiet him, she gwine git up en come down en do hit.”
paragraphs.zh: “不，我不会，”勒斯特说。“我和蒂·皮一起开车”迪尔西抱着本前后摇晃着。“卡琳小姐说，如果你不能让他安静下来，她就会站起来，然后下来，然后打。”

paragraphs.en: “Hush, honey,” Dilsey said, stroking Ben’s head. “Luster, honey,” she said, “Will you think about yo ole mammy en drive dat surrey right?”
paragraphs.zh: “嘘，亲爱的，”迪尔西抚摸着本的头说道。“勒斯特，亲爱的，”她说，“你会想想你在萨里开车的妈妈吗？”

paragraphs.en: “Yessum,” Luster said. “I drive hit jes like T. P.”
paragraphs.zh: “是的，”勒斯特说。“我开车就像蒂·皮”

paragraphs.en: Dilsey stroked Ben’s head, rocking back and forth. “I does de bes I kin,” she said, “Lawd knows dat. Go git it, den,” she said, rising. Luster scuttled out. Ben held the slipper, crying. “Hush, now. Luster gone to git de surrey en take you to de graveyard. We aint gwine risk gittin yo cap,” she said. She went to a closet contrived of a calico curtain hung across a corner of the room and got the felt hat she had worn. “We’s down to worse’n dis, ef folks jes knowed,” she said. “You’s de Lawd’s chile, anyway. En I be His’n too, fo long, praise Jesus. Here.” She put the hat on his head and buttoned his coat. He wailed steadily. She took the slipper from him and put it away and they went out. Luster came up, with an ancient white horse in a battered and lopsided surrey.
paragraphs.zh: 迪尔西抚摸着本的头，前后摇晃着。“我确实知道，”她说，“法律知道这一点。去吧，书房，”她说着站了起来。勒斯特溜了出去。本抓着拖鞋哭了。“嘘，现在。勒斯特已经去萨里郡了，带你去墓地。我们没有冒着危险，”她说。她走到挂在房间一角的一个用印花布窗帘制成的壁橱前，取出了她戴过的毡帽。“据人们所知，我们的情况变得更糟了，”她说。“无论如何，你是德劳德的智利人。我也是他的智利人，永远，赞美耶稣。在这里。”她把帽子戴在他头上，扣上他的外套扣子。他不断地哀号着。她从他手里接过拖鞋，收起来，然后他们就出去了。勒斯特出现了，牵着一匹古老的白马，骑着一匹破旧、不平衡的马车。

paragraphs.en: “You gwine be careful, Luster?” she said.
paragraphs.zh: “你要小心点，勒斯特？”她说。

paragraphs.en: “Yessum,” Luster said. She helped Ben into the back seat. He had ceased crying, but now he began to whimper again.
paragraphs.zh: “是的，”勒斯特说。她扶着本坐到后座。他已经停止哭泣，但现在他又开始抽泣。

paragraphs.en: “Hit’s his flower,” Luster said. “Wait, I’ll git him one.”
paragraphs.zh: “这是他的花，”勒斯特说。“等一下，我去给他买一个。”

paragraphs.en: “You set right dar,” Dilsey said. She went and took the cheek-strap. “Now, hurry en git him one.” Luster ran around the house, toward the garden. He came back with a single narcissus.
paragraphs.zh: “你把达尔设置对了，”迪尔西说。她走过去接过脸颊带。“现在，赶紧给他买一个。”勒斯特绕着房子跑向花园。他带着一朵水仙花回来了。

paragraphs.en: “Dat un broke,” Dilsey said, “Whyn’t you git him a good un?”
paragraphs.zh: “那东西坏了，”迪尔西说，“你为什么不给他一个好东西呢？”

paragraphs.en: “Hit de onliest one I could find,” Luster said. “Y’all took all of um Friday to dec’rate de church. Wait, I’ll fix hit.” So while Dilsey held the horse Luster put a splint on the flower stalk with a twig and two bits of string and gave it to Ben. Then he mounted and took the reins. Dilsey still held the bridle.
paragraphs.zh: “击中了我能找到的唯一一个，”勒斯特说。“你们星期五花了一整天的时间来破坏教堂。等等，我会解决问题的。”于是，当迪尔西抱着马时，勒斯特用一根树枝和两根绳子在花茎上固定了一块夹板，然后把它交给了本。然后他骑上缰绳。迪尔西仍然握着缰绳。

paragraphs.en: “You knows de way now?” she said, “Up de street, round de square, to de graveyard, den straight back home.”
paragraphs.zh: “你现在认得路了吗？”她说：“沿着街道，绕广场，到墓地，直接回家。”

paragraphs.en: “Yessum,” Luster said, “Hum up, Queenie.”
paragraphs.zh: “是的，”勒斯特说，“哼，奎妮。”

paragraphs.en: “You gwine be careful, now?”
paragraphs.zh: “你现在小心点吧？”

paragraphs.en: “Yessum.” Dilsey released the bridle.
paragraphs.zh: “是的。”迪尔西松开了缰绳。

paragraphs.en: “Hum up, Queenie,” Luster said.
paragraphs.zh: “哼，奎妮，”勒斯特说。

paragraphs.en: “Here,” Dilsey said, “You han me dat whup.”
paragraphs.zh: “在这里，”迪尔西说，“你给我带来了麻烦。”

paragraphs.en: “Aw, mammy,” Luster said.
paragraphs.zh: “噢，妈妈，”勒斯特说。

paragraphs.en: “Give hit here,” Dilsey said, approaching the wheel. Luster gave it to her reluctantly.
paragraphs.zh: “打这里，”迪尔西一边说，一边走近方向盘。勒斯特不情愿地把它给了她。

paragraphs.en: “I wont never git Queenie started now.”
paragraphs.zh: “我永远不会让奎妮现在就开始。”
